linkedin:4479291257.title: Offre de thèse CIFRE Janvier/Février 2027
linkedin:4479291257.desc: Pérennisation soutenable des systèmes de production : modélisation probabiliste hybride et anticipation des risques d’obsolescence Contexte et problématique Une part importante de l’outil industriel repose aujourd’hui sur des installations exploitées depuis plusieurs décennies. Ces moyens de production associent des équipements, composants, automatismes et logiciels dont la durée d’exploitation dépasse fréquemment celle de commercialisation ou de support. L’obsolescence constitue ainsi un risque important pour la continuité de production. Elle peut résulter d’évolutions technologiques, de l’arrêt d’une référence, de la raréfaction de pièces, de la disparition d’un fournisseur, de la fin d’un support ou de la perte de compétences. Sa maîtrise constitue un enjeu de disponibilité des installations, de souveraineté industrielle et d’utilisation raisonnée des ressources. Une installation industrielle comporte plusieurs milliers de références reliées entre elles au sein d’architectures techniques et de chaînes d’approvisionnement complexes. Les informations nécessaires à l’évaluation de leur pérennité sont dispersées entre bases de maintenance, référentiels techniques, données fournisseurs, historiques d’intervention et connaissances métier. Ces informations sont hétérogènes, évolutives et souvent incomplètes. Le module de diagnostic du logiciel OBSOLIO, développé par GreenTrack Genius, évalue actuellement l’obsolescence au moyen d’un scoring expert statique. La thèse vise à dépasser cette approche pour construire un modèle capable d’actualiser et d’anticiper le risque d’obsolescence à partir des données disponibles et des connaissances métier, tout en représentant explicitement l’incertitude et les mécanismes de propagation du risque. Question scientifique centrale Comment modéliser, propager et actualiser le risque d’obsolescence au sein d’une architecture industrielle multiniveau et de sa chaîne d’approvisionnement, en présence d’informations hétérogènes et incomplètes, afin de comparer de manière explicable des stratégies de pérennisation soutenable ? Verrou scientifique et approche proposée Le principal verrou scientifique concerne la propagation probabiliste d’un risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau, depuis le composant jusqu’à l’équipement et à la ligne de production, alors que l’état de connaissance sur les différents éléments du système est incomplet et variable. Une absence d’information sur une référence, un fournisseur ou une possibilité de substitution ne peut en effet être assimilée à l’absence de risque, ni être systématiquement considérée comme une situation défavorable. La modélisation devra donc distinguer autant que possible le risque déduit des informations disponibles de l’incertitude liée à l’incomplétude de ces informations. La recherche s’appuiera sur une approche hybride associant deux niveaux de représentation. 1. Représentation des connaissances et de l’architecture industrielle Un graphe de connaissances sera utilisé pour structurer les relations entre actifs, composants, nomenclatures, fournisseurs, références de substitution, historiques et événements d’obsolescence. Ce graphe aura pour fonction de représenter la structure du système étudié et les informations disponibles. Une question de recherche portera sur la manière de transformer ou d’exploiter cette représentation pour construire les dépendances pertinentes du modèle probabiliste. 2. Modélisation et propagation probabilistes Les réseaux bayésiens constitueront le cadre principal étudié pour agréger les connaissances expertes et les observations disponibles, représenter les dépendances entre facteurs et propager l’incertitude entre les différents niveaux du système. La dimension temporelle sera introduite lorsque les données disponibles permettent de caractériser l’évolution des variables et du risque. Les extensions dynamiques des réseaux bayésiens seront notamment étudiées pour représenter cette évolution et évaluer leur capacité à anticiper une situation d’obsolescence. Le travail portera en particulier sur les méthodes d’initialisation du modèle, l’intégration de connaissances expertes, l’apprentissage à partir des historiques et la robustesse de l’inférence en présence de données manquantes. Aide à la décision et pérennisation soutenable L’objectif est de dépasser le diagnostic pour comparer des stratégies de remédiation. Les réseaux bayésiens pourront être étendus sous forme de diagrammes d’influence, intégrant variables de décision et critères d’utilité. Plusieurs stratégies seront considérées : maintien en l’état, constitution ou mutualisation de stocks, substitution, reconditionnement, reconception partielle ou renouvellement. La pérennisation soutenable sera abordée comme un problème de décision multicritère prenant en compte au minimum : la disponibilité et le risque technique ; le coût de la stratégie ; son impact environnemental ; sa faisabilité industrielle et organisationnelle. L’objectif sera donc d’identifier la solution réduisant le risque d’obsolescence mais aussi de comparer les conséquences de différentes stratégies dans le contexte propre au système étudié. Validation et résultats attendus La validation reposera sur des données industrielles historiques : données de maintenance et d’équipements, informations fournisseurs, changements de références, événements d’obsolescence et autres données de cycle de vie disponibles sur les sites étudiés. Une validation rétrospective sera privilégiée. Elle consistera, lorsque les données le permettent, à reconstruire l’état d’information disponible à une date passée, à produire l’évaluation du risque correspondant, puis à comparer cette évaluation aux événements observés ultérieurement. Les résultats seront également comparés au scoring expert actuellement utilisé dans OBSOLIO afin de mesurer l’apport de la modélisation probabiliste en matière d’anticipation, de gestion des données manquantes et d’explicabilité. La thèse devra aboutir à trois résultats principaux : un modèle formel de représentation et de propagation probabiliste du risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau ; une méthode d’aide à la décision permettant de comparer des stratégies de pérennisation selon plusieurs critères ; un démonstrateur Python mettant en œuvre les modèles développés et permettant leur validation sur des cas industriels. Les contributions scientifiques porteront ainsi sur la représentation et la propagation d’un risque d’obsolescence dans des systèmes industriels complexes lorsque l’information disponible est distribuée, évolutive et incomplète. Les résultats auront vocation à alimenter le moteur algorithmique d’OBSOLIO, sans que le développement du logiciel constitue l’objet de la thèse. Profil recherché Le ou la candidate devra être titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master en génie industriel, ingénierie des systèmes, science des données, informatique industrielle ou domaine proche. De solides bases en probabilités, statistiques et modélisation sont attendues, ainsi qu’une bonne maîtrise de la programmation scientifique en Python. Une connaissance des réseaux bayésiens, des modèles graphiques probabilistes ou des méthodes de recherche opérationnelle constituera un atout. Le travail nécessitera également une capacité à comprendre des architectures industrielles complexes et à travailler avec les équipes de maintenance, méthodes, achats et ingénierie. Le profil recherché doit ainsi associer compétences en modélisation et intérêt pour les problématiques industrielles concrètes. Contact : Marc.Zolghadri@isae-supmeca.fr

linkedin:4478427322.desc: Job description: Ph.D. Cadidate (m/f/d) at the Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry The position is to be filled as soon as possible on a full-time or part-time basis for a fixed term of 36 months. Remuneration is based on the classification provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States (TV-L); placement in pay group E13 is possible, subject to the fulfillment of personal requirements. The Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry (IMB) is part of the Carl Gustav Carus Faculty of Medicine at TU Dresden. The institute’s research focuses on medical biometrics, bioinformatics, systems biology/medicine, including mathematical modelling, as well as medical informatics. In addition to these scientific activities, the IMB offers various services (e.g., consulting and education programs in the field of medical data science) for faculty and students at the Faculty of Medicine and the University Hospital. The position is part of the interdisciplinary research project “Virtual niche: Computational modelling and simulation of spatio-temporal dynamics of hematopoietic stem cells in their local microenvironment” funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). The core objective of the project is the development and application of a mathematical model that describes the spatio-temporal organization of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in their local growth environment within the bone marrow. The goal of gaining a better understanding of the underlying processes is of central importance both for open questions in basic stem cell biology and for future medical applications. Your responsibilities: Development of mathematical models to describe cellular dynamics Implementation of the models in a suitable programming environment Simulation of cellular dynamics within complex 3D structures Application of the computer model as a virtual bridge between in vitro and in vivo studies Systemic analysis and interpretation of experimental data in the context of complex biological interactions Close interdisciplinary collaboration with experimental teams at TU Dresden and external partner laboratories Your Profil: University degree (M.Sc., Diplom, or equivalent) in mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering (with biological/biotechnological focus) or a related field Very good or excellent academic record Strong interest in interdisciplinary work, particularly in the application of mathematical and computational methods in biology and medicine Solid programming experience (e.g. in the statistical software R or Python) Knowledge of (stem) cell biology and experience in mathematical modelling are advantageous Reliability, creativity, flexibility, and the ability to work well in a team A cooperative, self-motivated, and goal-oriented work style Very good English skills We offer: Compensation: Based on the TV-L Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States in pay grade E13 , plus an annual bonus, provided you meet the personal requirements Vacation: 30 days of paid vacation Professional Development: Extensive internal and external training and development opportunities to continuously strengthen your skills Company Culture: We value transparency, team spirit, and shared success. linkedin:4478501795.title: Promovendus digi-, data- en AI-competenties
linkedin:4478501795.desc: De zorg van morgen wordt steeds digitaler. Maar technologie werkt pas als zorgprofessionals ermee kunnen werken. Hoe leren studenten en professionals digi-, data- en AI-competenties? En hoe bereiden we hen voor op een snel veranderende digitale wereld? Dat onderzoek jij! Aantal uur: 28 • 36 uur per week Werklocatie: Beide locaties Amsterdam UMC Contractvorm: Bepaalde tijd Salaris: € 3.217 - € 4.077 Reageer tot en met: 2 november 2026 Wat ga je doen? Je combineert literatuuronderzoek met het ontwikkelen en evalueren van leertrajecten voor (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Je werkzaamheden bestaan uit: Je brengt de wetenschappelijke literatuur en de meest recente inzichten op het gebied van digi-, data- en AI-competenties en leren en ontwikkelen in kaart. Je schrijft een algemeen onderzoeksplan en werkt dit uit in deelstudies, inclusief de benodigde ethische goedkeuringen. Je onderzoekt modellen, methoden en technieken voor een leven lang ontwikkelen. Daarbij kijk je bijvoorbeeld naar transfer of training, simulatieleren en werkplekleren om tot schaalbare oplossingen te komen. Je ontwikkelt en evalueert leertrajecten, waaronder pilots, voor (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Je adviseert waar nodig projecten en programma's binnen Amsterdam UMC die aansluiten bij jouw onderzoek. Daarnaast schrijf je wetenschappelijke artikelen voor nationale en internationale tijdschriften. Je bundelt je onderzoeksresultaten uiteindelijk in een proefschrift en presenteert je bevindingen op nationale en internationale congressen. Ook draag je beperkt bij aan onderwijs en opleiden van studenten en medewerkers, voor zover dit aansluit bij jouw onderzoek. Wat neem je mee? We nodigen je uit om te solliciteren als je een van de volgende opleidingen hebt afgerond: Een (research)master onderwijskunde, met affiniteit met en bij voorkeur ervaring in de gezondheidszorg. Of: Een (research)master gezondheidswetenschappen, aangevuld met aantoonbare didactische ervaring of scholing. Daarnaast herken je jezelf in het volgende profiel: Je hebt aantoonbare affiniteit met onderzoek en ervaring met kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden. Je hebt interesse in digitalisering, data en AI in de zorg en in didactische principes zoals simulatieleren en werkplekleren, of je wilt je hierin verder verdiepen. Je bent analytisch sterk, zelfstandig en nieuwsgierig. Ook heb je het doorzettingsvermogen om een promotietraject succesvol af te ronden. Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Je kunt complexe onderwerpen helder uitleggen. Ervaring met lesgeven of begeleiden is een pré. Je werkt graag samen, maar kunt ook zelfstandig aan de slag. Wat bieden we jou? Je treedt in dienst bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Een contract voor de duur van 12 maanden, met de intentie te verlengen tot een totaal van vier jaar. Voor deze vacature geldt de Richtlijn Promovendi. Inschaling in salarisschaal OIO: € 3.217 tot € 4.077 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Daarnaast ontvang je 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering. Bereken hier jouw netto salaris. Mogelijkheid tot hybride werken, waarbij je minimaal twee dagen per week op locatie werkt. Vakantie-uren: 194,4 uur per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband en de mogelijkheid om uren bij te sparen. 100% OV-vergoeding. Kom je lopend, fietsend of met de auto? Dan ontvang je een vergoeding van €0,21 per km (voor de auto geldt een maximum van 40 km enkele reis). Kom je op de fiets? Maak gebruik van onze goede fietsregeling. Pensioenopbouw bij BeFrank, een modern, begrijpelijk en eerlijk geprijsd pensioen. Bekijk deze video met meer informatie over de indiensttreding bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Waar ga je werken ? Je werkt bij het Teaching & Learning Centre (TLC) van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de UvA, bij Amsterdam UMC, locatie AMC, aan de Meibergdreef. Je maakt deel uit van het onderzoeksteam, een van de vier teams binnen het TLC. Dit kleine team bestaat uit onderwijskundig onderzoekers en innovators die samenwerken aan onderwijsvernieuwing en onderzoek. Daarnaast werk je inhoudelijk samen met het projectteam dat de leerpaden voor digi-, data- en AI-vaardigheden binnen Amsterdam UMC ontwikkelt en in de praktijk brengt. Het TLC is het expertisecentrum voor hoger onderwijs van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de UvA. Het ondersteunt de opleidingen Geneeskunde en Medische informatiekunde bij het verzorgen van hoogwaardig onderwijs. Onderwijskundig adviseurs, medical educators, trainers, onderzoekers en innovators werken er samen aan het verbeteren van onderwijs en opleiden. Het TLC maakt deel uit van de kerntaak Onderwijs & Opleiden van Amsterdam UMC en draagt bij aan de ontwikkeling van studenten en (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Binnen het team heerst een open en samenwerkingsgerichte cultuur. Kennis delen en samen leren staan centraal. Je werkt ook nauw samen met onderzoekers van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de VU en met andere afdelingen binnen Amsterdam UMC. Zo draag je bij aan een groeiende community op het gebied van onderwijsonderzoek. Wat ga je onderzoeken? Je onderzoekt welke digi-, data- en AI-competenties huidige en toekomstige zorgprofessionals nodig hebben. Je brengt in kaart welke competenties al goed zijn ontwikkeld en waar nog hiaten of overlap bestaan. Op basis daarvan ontwikkel je een breed, evidence-based competentieraamwerk. Je doet voorstellen om deze competenties efficiënt te integreren in het continuüm van onderwijs en opleiden. Waar mogelijk evalueer je bestaande en nieuwe leerinterventies die aansluiten op (onderdelen van) het raamwerk. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar het directe leerrendement, maar ook naar de vraag of professionals de competenties op langere termijn behouden en toepassen. Je onderzoek sluit aan bij een groter project binnen Amsterdam UMC. Daarin ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en testen we al enkele jaren leerpaden voor verschillende doelgroepen. De ontwikkelde producten, zoals de ontwerpmethodiek, het eerste competentiemodel en het evaluatieproces, vormen de basis voor jouw onderzoek. Tegelijkertijd biedt deze context volop ruimte om nieuwe onderzoeksvragen te verkennen. Wil je alvast meer weten over de verschillende fases binnen het PhD-traject? Op deze pagina lees je hierover meer informatie. Laten we kennismaken De beoogde startdatum is zo snel mogelijk, in overleg. Heb je interesse? Stuur dan je motivatiebrief en cv, aangevuld met een publicatielijst indien relevant. De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken vindt plaats in de week van maandag 16 november 2026 . Tijdens deze gesprekken maak je kennis met de vice-decaan Onderwijs van de UvA, het hoofd van het TLC en de coördinerend onderzoeker van het onderzoeksteam. We vragen je om hier alvast rekening mee te houden. Heb je nog vragen? Voor inhoudelijke informatie over deze vacature kun je terecht bij Tom Broens , h oofd TLC, via t.h.broens@amsterdamumc.nl . Een referentiecheck en screening kunnen onderdeel zijn van de procedure. Lees hier wat dit inhoudt. Kom je bij ons in dienst, dan vragen we een VOG (Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag). Interne kandidaten krijgen, bij gelijke geschiktheid, voorrang op externe kandidaten. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

Experience combining behavioral analytics with advanced machine learning techniques to identify meaningful patterns in behavioral data will be highly valuable. This is a fixed-term internship of six months , offering the opportunity to work on cutting-edge machine learning research that contributes directly to game content and player experiences. You will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced environment, developing solutions with real-world impact across our products and services. The role is based in our Stockholm office and is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement. Responsibilities: Collaborate with researchers and engineers on projects aligned with your area of interest and expertise. Participate in the full research lifecycle, from problem definition and methodology exploration to implementation, experimentation, and evaluation. Document research outcomes and communicate progress and findings to team members and relevant stakeholders. Who You Are: Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field. Recent graduates with relevant backgrounds are also welcome to apply. linkedin:4479022782.desc: Job Description Are you interested in exploring the following questions? How are artificial intelligence (AI) and automation reshaping individuals' transitions to entrepreneurship? How do individuals' skills, experience, and technological readiness influence the types of businesses they create and their subsequent performance? How do these patterns vary across countries and institutional contexts? DTU Entrepreneurship invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship as part of an international research project entitled The New Landscape of Necessity Entrepreneurship: Understanding Entrepreneurial Transitions in an Era of AI- and Automation-Driven Labor Market Disruption . The project investigates how AI and automation reshape entrepreneurial transitions, with particular attention to individuals who start businesses following unemployment. The PhD candidate will join an international research team involving Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Professor Marc Gruber at École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland, and Professor John C. Dencker at Northeastern University, USA. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), the project combines large-scale surveys, Danish administrative registry data, and qualitative interviews across Denmark, Switzerland, and Greece. The position offers an opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge entrepreneurship research, work with rich international datasets, and collaborate with leading scholars in the field. Responsibilities And Qualifications Your primary responsibility will be to conduct high-quality research within the international project, with opportunities to develop your own research questions within its overall scope. Your tasks will include: Developing research questions and theoretical frameworks concerning entrepreneurship, human capital, AI, and labor market transitions. Applying quantitative and qualitative research methods to investigate entrepreneurial transitions and outcomes. Collecting, managing, and analyzing quantitative data, including large-scale surveys and Danish registry data. Contributing to the design and implementation of surveys and qualitative interviews in collaboration with international research partners. Preparing research papers for submission to leading international academic journals. Presenting research findings at international conferences and contributing to dissemination activities targeting policymakers and other stakeholders. Collaborating with researchers at DTU, EPFL, Northeastern University, and other project partners. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in entrepreneurship research and technological change. We expect you to have: A Master’s degree. A strong interest in developing quantitative research and analytical skills. Excellent written and spoken English communication skills. The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment. The following qualifications would be considered an advantage, but are not required: Experience working with large-scale datasets, registry data, or longitudinal data. Experience with statistical software such as Stata or R, and familiarity with econometric techniques, including regression analysis and panel data methods. Experience with survey design, qualitative interviewing, or mixed-methods research. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . Assessment The assessment of applicants will be conducted by Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, who will serve as the principal supervisor. We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is as soon as possible or as agreed with the successful candidate. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, DTU Entrepreneurship, Technical University of Denmark, at argnik@dtu.dk . You can read more about DTU Entrepreneurship at www.entrepreneurship.dtu.dk . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 8 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU Entrepreneurship is amongst the leading international entities in technology entrepreneurship and helps develop an entrepreneurial culture across DTU. As part of a dynamic and evolving ecosystem, we combine practice-oriented education and research in entrepreneurship with real start-up opportunities from all DTU departments. With rigorous research at its core, the Center builds the entrepreneurial capabilities of students, industry leaders, academics and policymakers to address unsolved problems, and together create new knowledge, methodologies and initiatives. linkedin:4479063185.title: Promovendus klinisch redeneren en AI: leren in een gesimuleerde zorgwereld
linkedin:4479063185.desc: Fascineert het je hoe artsen leren redeneren? En wil je meebouwen aan de toekomst van medisch onderwijs, met simulatie, virtuele patiënten en AI? Dan nodigen we je uit als promovendus om te onderzoeken hoe we klinisch redeneren kunnen trainen als de 'echte' patiënt niet altijd binnen handbereik is. Aantal uur: 28 • 36 uur per week Werklocatie: Locatie VUmc Contractvorm: Bepaalde tijd Salaris: € 3.217 - € 4.077 Reageer tot en met: 26 oktober 2026 Wat ga je doen? Je exploreert de literatuur op de huidige state-of-the-art rond bovenstaande onderwerpen. Je schrijft een algemeen onderzoeksplan en plannen voor deelstudies met bijbehorende ethische goedkeuringen. Je onderzoekt welke onderdelen van klinisch redeneren (zoals het toepassen van fundamentele kennis, het verzamelen van informatie, het afwegen van diagnoses en het formuleren van beleid) zich lenen voor welke vorm van simulatie, en welke taken juist de echte patiënt vragen. Je onderzoekt hoe AI, zoals LLM-gebaseerde chatbots, kan helpen bij het genereren van realistische casuïstiek op maat, het simuleren van patiënten en het geven van feedback op het redeneerproces, en hoe betrouwbaar en onderwijskundig effectief dat is. Je werkt hierbij samen met docenten en studenten, bijvoorbeeld in het Klinisch Trainingscentrum, de Living Library en de studentenpoli. Samen met onderwijskundigen en docenten in het Amsterdam UMC die al ervaring opdoen met LLM-gebaseerde chatbots in het onderwijs, ontwikkel en evalueer je (pilot)onderwijs voor coassistenten. Je verzamelt en analyseert data uit onder andere experimentele studies, met kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve methoden, en interpreteert de bevindingen in de context van het medisch onderwijs. Je schrijft wetenschappelijke artikelen voor (inter)nationale tijdschriften en brengt de resultaten uiteindelijk samen in jouw proefschrift. Je presenteert jouw bevindingen op nationale en internationale congressen en bouwt zo aan een sterk academisch profiel en netwerk. Je volgt onder andere cursussen vanuit de Doctoral School Amsterdam UMC die aansluiten bij het project en bij jouw eigen ambities, en krijgt de mogelijkheid om ervaring op te doen in het verzorgen van onderwijs en het begeleiden van studenten. Wat neem je mee? Je hebt een afgeronde (research)master in onderwijskunde, cognitieve psychologie, gezondheidswetenschappen, geneeskunde, biomedische wetenschappen, informatiekunde of een vergelijkbaar vakgebied; Je hebt affiniteit met onderzoek. Ervaring met onderzoek waarbij je gebruik hebt gemaakt van kwalitatieve en/of kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden is een pré; Interesse in klinisch redeneren, medisch onderwijs, simulatieleren en de rol van AI in de zorg en het onderwijs, en de nieuwsgierigheid om je hier verder in te verdiepen; Je bent analytisch sterk, zelfstandig en kritisch, en je hebt het doorzettingsvermogen om een promotietraject tot een goed einde te brengen; Je kunt complexe materie helder overbrengen; ervaring met onderwijs of begeleiden is een plus; Je bent een teamspeler die zowel zelfstandig als binnen een groot multidisciplinair team (artsen, psychologen, onderwijskundigen en technici) kan werken; Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels uitstekend, zowel schriftelijk als mondeling. Wat bieden we jou? Je treedt in dienst bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. De startdatum is zo snel mogelijk. Een contract voor de duur van 12 maanden, met de intentie te verlengen tot een totaal van vier jaar. Voor deze vacature geldt de Richtlijn Promovendi. Inschaling in salarisschaal OIO: € 3.217 tot € 4.077 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Artsen worden ingeschaald in salarisschaal 10: € 3.724 tot € 5.867 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Daarnaast ontvang je 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering. Bereken hier jouw netto salaris. Vakantie-uren: 194,4 uur per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband en de mogelijkheid om uren bij te sparen. 100% OV-vergoeding. Kom je lopend, fietsend of met de auto? Dan ontvang je een vergoeding van €0,21 per km (voor de auto geldt een maximum van 40 km enkele reis). Kom je op de fiets? Maak gebruik van onze goede fietsregeling. Pensioenopbouw bij BeFrank, een modern, begrijpelijk en eerlijk geprijsd pensioen. Bekijk deze video met meer informatie over de indiensttreding bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Waar ga je werken ? Je maakt deel uit van het team Onderzoek van Onderwijs binnen de Faculteit Geneeskunde VU. Daarnaast neem je actief deel aan het netwerk i.o. voor onderzoek van onderwijs binnen Amsterdam UMC. Amsterdam UMC Research BV Amsterdam UMC Research BV ondersteunt wetenschappelijk onderzoek zonder winstoogmerk. Hiermee voorzien we onderzoekers in alles wat ze nodig hebben om te kunnen excelleren. Zo bieden onze principal investigators (PI's) en projectleiders begeleiding op het gebied van projectbeheer, finance en human resources. Bij medisch-wetenschappelijke onderzoeksprojecten wordt daarnaast ook ondersteuning op juridisch vlak geboden. Bekijk de video voor meer informatie. Wat ga je onderzoeken? Klinisch redeneren is de kern van het artsenvak: het vermogen om uit het patiëntverhaal, de uitgevraagde klachten, het lichamelijk onderzoek en onderzoeksuitslagen de juiste diagnose en het juiste plan te destilleren. Het is geen losse vaardigheid, maar een samenspel van veel onderdelen: fundamentele (bio)medische kennis, het verzamelen van informatie, het afwegen van diagnoses en het opstellen van beleid. Tijdens de coschappen leren geneeskundestudenten dit door te observeren, te oefenen met medestudenten en simulatiepatiënten, maar bovenal door dit daadwerkelijk uit te voeren bij de patiënt. Maar juist die leeromgeving staat onder druk. Door o.a. hoge werkdruk, fusies van ziekenhuizen, beperkte financiële ruimte, uitplaatsing naar zelfstandige behandelcentra (ZBC’s) en verplaatsing van zorg naar de eerste lijn neemt de opleidingscapaciteit van coassistenten af. Daardoor is het voor coassistenten steeds lastiger om voldoende, gevarieerde en veilige oefenmomenten met echte patiënten te krijgen. Terwijl we juist die momenten nodig hebben om artsen goed op te leiden in klinisch redeneren. Simulatie en virtuele patiënten bieden een veelbelovend alternatief om studenten in de geneeskundeopleiding voor te bereiden op het zelfstandig zien van patiënten: studenten kunnen op hun eigen niveau veilig oefenen met een breed scala aan casuïstiek, zonder risico voor patiënten, en met directe feedback. AI maakt dat nu schaalbaar. Denk aan taalmodellen die realistische patiëntcasuïstiek genereren op maat van de student, die als virtuele patiënt een anamnese kan laten afnemen, of die als tutor kan meedenken en feedback geven op het redeneerproces zelf. Maar belangrijke vragen zijn nog onbeantwoord. Welke onderdelen van klinisch redeneren leer je goed in welke vorm van simulatie (van een virtuele patiënt achter een scherm, een simulatiepatiënt van vlees en bloed, tot een teamsimulatie met acteurs), en welke leer je het best bij een ‘echte’ patiënt? Hoe realistisch en betrouwbaar is de met behulp van AI gegenereerde casuïstiek? En hoe zorgen we dat studenten zowel leren klinisch redeneren mét AI als zélf kritisch blijven redeneren? Daar ga jij als promovendus onderzoek naar doen. Laten we kennismaken Let op: voeg bij je sollicitatie ook jouw publicatielijst mee aan het einde van jouw motivatiebrief of cv (indien relevant). De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken starten in de week van 26 oktober . Deze gesprekken worden gehouden met de vice-decaan onderwijs FdG VU en het hoofd onderzoek van onderwijs FdG VU. Heb je nog vragen? Voor inhoudelijke informatie over deze vacature kun je terecht bij Martine de Bruijne , vice-decaan onderwijs FdG VU, via mc.debruyne@amsterdamumc.nl . Een referentiecheck en screening kunnen onderdeel zijn van de procedure. Kom je bij ons in dienst, dan vragen we voor een aantal functiegroepen standaard een VOG (Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag). Bekijk wat het inhoudt en of het voor jouw functie van toepassing is. Interne kandidaten krijgen, bij gelijke geschiktheid, voorrang op externe kandidaten. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

linkedin:4479018891.title: PhD position: modeling menopause-related heart rhythm disorders
linkedin:4479018891.desc: Job Description Menopause induces profound electrical and structural changes in the heart, yet the mechanisms driving this transition, and the reasons it dramatically increases the risk of heart rhythm disorders in women, remain largely unexplored. In this PhD project, you will play a central role in uncovering these mechanisms by developing advanced, multi‑scale computational models of atrial electrophysiology. You will work with one of the most comprehensive and unique datasets available worldwide: high‑resolution intra‑operative electrical mapping data recorded directly from the human atria during cardiac surgery, combined with ECG, PPG, hormone profiles, and continuous vital signs. All data is collected within Erasmus MC, giving you direct access to clinicians, engineers, and the surgical team collecting the data. This means you will not rely on synthetic or incomplete datasets but you will build models grounded in rich, real-world physiology. Your task is to transform these multimodal datasets into patient‑specific “digital twins” that simulate how atrial electrophysiology evolves across the menopausal transition. You will design and calibrate mechanistic models at the cellular, tissue, and organ scale; develop numerical methods and optimization pipelines; and run large-scale simulations to reconstruct remodeling trajectories and identify the critical “breaking points” that lead to arrhythmias such as sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation. The mechanistic insights and model outputs you generate will directly feed into the women‑specific arrhythmia detection algorithms developed by our industrial partner. Your work will therefore have a clear translational pathway toward real‑world digital health solutions. Beyond modeling, you will contribute to algorithm development for arrhythmia prediction and collaborate closely with clinical researchers during patient recruitment and data collection. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys combining computational modeling, physiology, and real clinical data. Your work will directly advance women‑specific arrhythmia detection and care, making a scientific impact that is both academically significant and clinically meaningful. “What I enjoy most is seeing how mathematical models can reveal mechanisms that cannot be directly observed from data.” - team member The position will be available by Q4 2026. The project is funded by Health-Holland. Work environment You will conduct your research within the Translational Electrophysiology Unit of the Department of Cardiology at Erasmus MC. The group is internationally recognized for its work on cardiac electrophysiology and collaborates closely with the Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery and multiple research groups at TU Delft. You will join a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and collegial team of clinicians, engineers, and scientists who work together to understand and treat cardiac arrhythmias. The environment is dynamic, supportive, and rich in opportunities for scientific growth. Qualifications And Skills We are looking for a motivated researcher with: A MSc or MEng degree in Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Computational Science, or a related field. Strong interest in computational modeling, simulations, or mathematical physiology. Experience with dynamical systems, numerical simulation, or finite‑element–based modeling approaches is a strong plus. Programming experience (preferably Python, but other languages are also a plus). Affinity with clinical or patient‑related research. Excellent communication skills and ability to work in a multidisciplinary team. Strong analytical mindset and enthusiasm for scientific discovery. Terms of employment A full‑time, 4‑year PhD position. A gross monthly salary between € 3.217,- and € 4.077,- (scale OIO) based on a full-time workweek of 36 hours. A salary increase of 3.5% from May 2027, according to the collective labor agreement (CLA). Excellent fringe benefits, such as a 13th month that is already paid out in November and an individual travel expense package. Pension insurance with ABP. We take care of approximately 2/3 of the monthly contribution. Special benefits, such as an incompany physiotherapist and bicycle repairer. And there is also a gym where you can work on your fitness after work. A supportive team and excellent supervision. Opportunities to attend international conferences and courses. A dynamic research environment at the largest academic medical center in the Netherlands. More information Make this job your next career move! Apply now using the application button. For more information about the role, please contact Dr. Vehpi Yildirim, Department of Cardiology (mail (mailto:v.yildirim@erasmusmc.nl)or +31 (0)6 812 496 74), or Prof. Dr. Natasja de Groot, Department of Cardiology, Erasmus MC via mail (mailto:n.m.s.degroot@erasmusmc.nl).

linkedin:4468727081.title: Doctoral Researcher, MSCA Doctoral Network position “Electric solar wind sail mission design”
linkedin:4468727081.desc: MSCA Doctoral Network position “Electric solar wind sail mission design” We are now looking for two (2) Doctoral Researchers. This PhD topic is part of the “Electric solar wind sail doctors” (E-Sailors) network, funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network Programme. The E-Sailors network is designed to train the next generation of Electric solar wind sail (E-sail) scientists, developers and advocates. This particular Doctoral Researcher (DR) will work with in-orbit results of on-going missions, such as Foresail-1 p developed by Aalto University with the E-sail payload from the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI), as well as the DR will develop new and improved in-orbit E-sail experiments for future missions in lunar orbit and deep space. The DR will be enrolled at and hosted by Aalto University, Finland, with the main supervisor Jaan Praks, co-hosted by the FMI with the E-sail researcher Dr. Petri Toivanen. Research field : Space technology, payload development Supervisor : Jaan Praks Offered by : Aalto University, School of Electrical Engineering General Description Of Programme And Host The Electric solar wind Sail doctors (E-Sailors) is a challenge-based Doctoral Network that aims to bring Electric solar wind sail (E-sail) from low Earth orbit (LEO) demonstration missions to the operational environment of the solar wind. It is delivered by 8 universities in cooperation with FMI, where E-sail was invented, and 4 companies. E-sail is a highly innovative and potentially disruptive propellantless propulsion system. An operational E-sail consists of hair-thin and kilometres-long wires, or tethers, which are charged at a high voltage creating an electrostatic sheath (electric sail) which deflects solar wind particles and generates the propulsive effect in interplanetary environment. Successful and rapid development and deployment of the technology will ensure EU's leadership in the exploration and exploitation of deep space, the next commercial space frontier. The programme is designed to achieve the following training objectives for our doctoral researchers: Equip them with core scientific skills and specialised knowledge in designing experiments for demonstrating space technologies and developing space missions; Provide them with a wide range of transferrable skills, such as Open Science and FAIR, communicating science to public, advocacy, networking etc.; Develop their business and entrepreneurship skills, such as IPR management, preliminary business planning, pitching to investors, starting start-ups. Aalto University is a leading Finnish university combining science, technology, design, and business to foster innovation and multidisciplinary research. The Aalto Space Lab is a comprehensive facility dedicated to the development, integration, and qualification of small satellites and space payloads. The laboratory features an advanced electronics development environment equipped for precision soldering, calibration, functional testing, and sensor characterization. A dedicated cleanroom area supports the assembly and integration of flight hardware, ensuring high reliability and adherence to space standards. Adjacent to the electronics lab, the Space Technology Testing Laboratory provides an advanced thermal–vacuum facility that enables environmental testing of complete satellites and subsystems under simulated space conditions. This includes vacuum, thermal cycling, thermal balance, and outgassing testing, essential for qualifying hardware for launch and orbital operation. The Space Lab also offers access to a wide suite of engineering and simulation software for electronics design, spacecraft systems modelling, structural and thermal analysis, and mission performance verification. Together, these resources support the full development cycle—from early concept design and prototyping to environmental qualification and flight readiness. The Aalto Space Lab serves as a key hub for small satellite and payload research, education, and technology demonstration, supporting academic projects, collaborative research initiatives, and industrial partnerships that advance Finland’s growing role in space technology. Description Of Specific PhD Project Please indicate in your cover letter which of the two positions you are primarily interested in. Position 1: The E-Sailor 8 The E-Sailor 8 doctoral position focuses on developing advanced methods for E-sail tether deployment monitoring and safety, combining simulation, laboratory testing, and in-orbit validation. The candidate will create dynamical and photorealistic 3D models of the tether and spacecraft to support both engineering analysis and visual monitoring during deployment, working in coordination with the RT3D development led by E-Sailor 15. The research includes conducting laboratory and in-orbit experiments using data from the Foresail-1p mission, analysing tether dynamics, imaging, and operational behaviour. Based on these results, the doctoral researcher will propose and evaluate new deployment schemes and safety strategies, contributing to the reliability of future E-sail missions. The work will result in models and validated methods shared with the wider community to support ongoing and upcoming E-sail technology developments. Duration of the work contract and place of employment: The position is based at Aalto University (24 months) with collaboration at CrystalSpace (CS) (12 months), under the supervision of Jaan Praks (Aalto) and Jaan Viru (CS). Position 2: The E-Sailor 4 The E-Sailor 4 doctoral position focuses on the design and engineering of an electric sail (E-sail) payload system for nanospacecraft, with a particular emphasis on developing the payload for the ESTCube-LuNa mission. Building on previous demonstrations such as ESTCube-1, ESTCube-2, and Foresail-1p, the project aims to apply lessons learned to create a more capable and reliable E-sail payload. The work involves analysing previous mission data, defining requirements for new payloads, and designing the mechanical, electrical, and deployment subsystems for ESTCube-LuNa. E-Sailor 4 will also lead the development and testing of a prototype payload, performing functional and environmental tests to verify its performance and requirements for spacecraft integration. The research will result in three main publications covering lessons learned, design development, and prototype testing. In the final project phase, the doctoral researcher will spend 6 months at Spacecraft Anatomy (SA) to gain industrial experience in space hardware manufacturing and qualification. The project will deliver a E-sail payload prototype design and strengthen the technological foundation for future nanospacecraft missions using E-sail propulsion. Duration of the work contract and place of employment: The main supervisor of the DR at Aalto University, Finland (15 months) is Assoc. Prof. Jaan Praks. The DR will also be co-supervised by the E-sail inventor Petri Toivanen while working for 15 months at the FMI, Finland and by Dr. Iaroslav Iakubivskyi while working 6 months at Spacecraft Anatomy, Estonia. Additional details of the positions Starting date: The position is expected to start during 2026. Trial period: 6 months Target degree: Doctoral degree from Aalto University, Finland Approximate gross salary: The salary for a Doctoral Researcher at Aalto University is 3143 EUR per month, which will be adjusted according to the eligible allowances based on MSCA funding. The family allowance will be clarified with the selected candidate once their situation is defined. The salary at FMI is 2900-3200 EUR/month at the beginning of employment. The starting salary at Spacecraft Anatomy is approx. 2700 EUR/month, plus family allowance, if applicable. Requirements For PhD Position Master's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Space Technology, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or closely related field. Excellent command of written and spoken English. Research experience and independent work experience evident through technical projects, theses, publications, or technical reports. This includes the evidence of innovative thinking or novel approaches to technical problems, the ability to synthesize information from multiple sources to advance understanding and demonstrated curiosity and persistence in pursuing technical challenges. Strong academic and development track record with demonstrated proficiency in orbital mechanics and propagators (GMAT, STK, or similar), propulsion systems, spacecraft dynamics, space systems, space mission and environment analyses, cubesats, small spacecraft systems, space plasma physics, software development and version control (Git), simulation software development (experience in multiple fields are considered beneficial). Familiarity with simulation software and numerical methods and proficiency in programming languages (Rust, Python, MATLAB, C/C++, or similar) for simulation and data analysis. Experience in managing multiple concurrent tasks and priorities independently and track record of meeting project deadlines and delivering results without constant supervision. Proven ability to work autonomously on complex technical problems and demonstrated problem-solving skills in technical/engineering contexts. Leadership experience in terms of leading or significantly contributing to multi-month technical projects and taking initiative in research or development activities. Experience working with interdisciplinary and international teams while maintaining individual accountability, such as driving projects forward without extensive guidance. Example of at least one practical project completed within the deadline with minimal supervision, and evidence of self-motivation and proactive problem-solving. Please submit description of personal contributions and level of independence, project outcomes and impact, and references in terms of publications, theses, technical reports, simulations, analysis, code samples, or documentation (multiple references are considered beneficial). The above duties are not exhaustive; the PhD candidate may be required to undertake other tasks consistent with the role and the objectives of the E-Sailors Doctoral Network. Duties And Responsibilities Position 1: The E-Sailor 8 Undertake innovative and independent research on E-sail tether deployment monitoring, dynamics, and safety to enhance the reliability of future nanosatellite missions. Carry out literature reviews, requirement analyses, and theoretical studies on tether mechanics, deployment systems, and in-orbit monitoring approaches. Develop and validate numerical models of tether and spacecraft dynamics, and create photorealistic 3D visualizations to support monitoring and analysis of deployment behaviour. Adapt, develop, and learn new simulation, modelling, and imaging tools, including integration with real-time visualization frameworks such as RT3D. Plan and execute laboratory experiments to characterize tether deployment and verify model performance under controlled conditions. Contribute to in-orbit testing and data analysis activities related to the Foresail-1p mission, including image-based monitoring and interpretation of tether behaviour. Design and propose improved E-sail tether deployment schemes, safety mechanisms, and operational procedures for future missions. Document and communicate research progress through high-quality technical reports, scientific publications, and conference presentations. Collaborate closely with academic and industrial partners at Aalto University and CrystalSpace, while maintaining the ability to work independently and solve technical challenges proactively. Stay up to date with advances in spacecraft dynamics, tether technologies, and on-board imaging systems, integrating new insights into the research. linkedin:4476483317.title: PhD Position Video-based Hand Motion-tracking for Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis at TU Delft
linkedin:4476483317.desc: Are you passionate about human movement and developing clinical tools for understanding human movement disorders? Job Description Challenge: Over a quarter of a million people in the Netherlands alone have rheumatoid arthritis (RA) with a majority suffering from debilitating pain and inflammation that makes hand dexterity and work, at times, impossible. While anti-inflammatory and analgesic drugs are the main line of relief, new drugs and treatments are needed and being developed for long-term care. At the same time a major challenge in RA management is quantifying the effectiveness of treatments under real-world conditions. Change: We need technologies to measure and quantify changes in hand function due to daily life factors (sleep, stress, etc.…) and treatments/drugs in the home setting. These technologies would enable drug developers, physiotherapists and physicians to make objective and quantitative assessments regarding the effectiveness of treatments. Impact: Once we understand the effects of stressors and treatments on RA flare ups and hand function, clinicians will be able to more closely target treatments and plan daily routines that minimize pain and suffering from rheumatoid arthritis. We are seeking a PhD candidate for a 4-year contract to develop and apply computational models and video-based tools to capture hand movement and function with deployment in the home environment as the target. Furthermore, you will apply these tools to help us investigate the potential causes and timings of flare ups during patients’ daily lives. You will work primarily with video data, musculoskeletal models, and pose estimation algorithms. The models and algorithms you develop will be part of open source and data repositories affiliated with the broader research program and TU Delft’s commitment to Open Science. You will be an integral part of the ‘Care is coming home!’ program: a 5-year project executed by a large consortium consisting of 2 technical universities (TU Delft, UTwente), 6 hospitals (Amsterdam UMC, Erasmus MC, Leiden UMC, Maartenskliniek, Maastricht UMC, Radboud UMC), 13 companies (Able Human Motion, Biomex, Cue2Walk, DanuSports, Kinetic Analysis, Lode Holding, Madglove, ModelHealth, Moveshelf, Orikami, Sabender (Enterprising Company), Trinoma, VicarVision), 1 rehabilitation centre (Daan Theeuwes Centrum) and 5 patient organisations (Hersenletsel.nl, Hersenstichting, Parkinson Vereniging, ParkinsonNL, ReumaNederland). In total the program will encompass 9 PhDs and 5 postdocs to address the issue of translating health care to the home environment. This PhD position is hosted by the Biomechanical Engineering Department at TU Delft where you will be a part of both the Computational Biomechanics (Seth) and Neuromuscular Control (Mugge) Labs. In addition to research, there are many opportunities to develop your academic career by mentoring and teaching BSc/MSc students, presenting at international conferences, and participating in workshops/training and exchange programs abroad. Job requirements You Should Have MSc in engineering or similar discipline by the start date of the position Experience with mechanical modeling and simulation Experience in computer programming/scripting (e.g., C++, Python, Matlab, etc.) Experience collecting human experimental data (movement, video, or similar) Excellent written and oral communication skills in English The following aspects will help you stand out: Thriving in multidisciplinary environments Curiosity-driven and self-motivated working attitude Knowledge of biomechanical modeling, anatomy, vision-based motion capture, machine learning, control systems Keep in mind that this describes the background we imagine would best fit the role. If you do not meet all the requirements, but believe that you are up for the task, we absolutely want to hear your motivation and how you would fit! The PhD process is a learning experience, so let us know what you want to learn and develop as a PhD candidate. You can view the full job vacancy here. Application deadline: 21 October 2026

linkedin:4477594980.desc: About The Position The position is a 3-year doctoral research fellowship starting in 2027. The PhD candidate will be embedded in the welding and joining research activities of SFI FAST and will work closely with NTNU, SINTEF, and leading international industrial partners in the aluminium value chain. The PhD position focuses on understanding the influence of impurities coming from recycled Aluminium on the weldability of different alloys. These impurities can alter the weldability, microstructure, and performance of Aluminium welds compared to the reference alloy. Solidification and liquation cracking, pore formation, heat-affected zone softening, and degradation of corrosion resistance are some examples of possible challenges. However, the knowledge is limited about any of these possible changes. Therefore, the candidate needs to provide a thorough investigation of the welding process using conventional techniques and develop new methodologies. In addition, the welding procedure adoption to enhance the performance of the alloys based on their metallurgical characteristics shall be developed. Therefore, the candidate should have a great understanding of the welding process-microstructure-performance. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. You will be supervised by Professor Vahid Hosseini. About The Project SFI FAST (Future Aluminium Structures) is a national Centre for Research-based Innovation (SFI) funded by the Research Council of Norway and the aluminum industry. The Centre is led by NTNU in close collaboration with SINTEF and a broad consortium of 15 leading industrial partners across the aluminium value chain. FAST runs from 2026 to 2034 and represents one of Norway’s most ambitious long-term research initiatives within aluminium materials, manufacturing technologies, and circular economy. The primary objective of FAST is to establish the scientific and technological knowledge base required to enable the large-scale use of post-consumer scrap (PCS) aluminium in high-value, structural, and safety-critical products. FAST adopts a through-scale and through-process research methodology, integrating materials science, manufacturing processes, product and structural design, and lifecycle performance. A key outcome of FAST is the development of the FAST Virtual Lab, a digital framework combining experimental data, physics-based models, and data-driven methods to support design, manufacturing, and decision-making across aluminium value chains. Education and competence building are central pillars of FAST. The Centre will educate more than 18 PhD and postdoctoral researchers and over 100 MSc students, strengthening Norway’s international position in aluminium research and innovation. The two positions posted here will be among the first ones to start in the Centre. Please see the centre’s website: Future Aluminium Structures (FAST) - NTNU Duties of the position Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate Take part in the mandatory PhD research education programme Develop arc welding (GTAW and GMAW) and Friction stir welding for alloys with different impurity levels to minimize welding defects and improve mechanical and corrosion performance Develop knowledge in the influence of impurities on the weld’s physics, defects, microstructure, and performance Thermodynamic modelling of solidification and precipitation behaviour of recycled aluminium Development of weldability tests to quantify welding performance of Aluminium Alloys Advanced characterization of welded samples using Laser Confocal Microscopy, In-situ mechanical testing, SEM, FIB, and EBSD. Conduct and publish high-level research in peer-reviewed journals and international conferences Work closely with industrial and academic partners and participate in relevant SFI FAST activities, including mentoring and supervising MSc students Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information. You must have a relevant Master's degree in Mechanical engineering, Materials Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. You must have an academically relevant background within fusion and solid-state welding, welding metallurgy, and material characterization Documented strong background in: Experimental welding research Material characterization and testing Excellent written presentation skills and oral English language skills The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria Basic knowledge of robotic welding Knowledge of weld monitoring systems with focus on arc characteristics and thermal cycle analysis Knowledge of thermomechanical modelling of welding process Scandinavian language skills Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Highly motivated Able to work independently Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them Present and discuss your research with other professionals Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity Show curiosity and strong motivation for the subject Analyse data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed Keen interest in learning and working in teams Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities. We offer Exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment SFI FAST facilities, industrial network, and a joint PhD environment An exciting job with an important mission in society Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Working capital that can be used to implement the project Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. The employment period is 3 years. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). About The Application The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English. Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. linkedin:4479215663.desc: Career at WUR About Us Plenty of variety and challenges Pleasant working atmosphere Time for personal development Proper work-life balance Internationally leading Your job Have you ever wondered how we can ensure that climate mitigation and adaptation policies are fair, coherent, and effective? Are you interested in applying state-of-the-art impact evaluation techniques to analyze how climate policies affect land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity? Do you good communication skills in Spanish? Then this might be your next step! Climate change mitigation and adaptation in agriculture and forestry represent a “wicked problem”, shaped by uncertainty, conflicting objectives, institutional fragmentation and time pressure. While the EU has set ambitious climate targets for 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, progress in agriculture and forestry remains insufficient and current policy frameworks have not yet resulted in significant climate mitigation and adaptation results, or generated the systemic transformation needed. This PhD position is part of the EU-Horizon project “ Evidence-based pathways towards fair, coherent and effective climate policies for Europe’s agriculture and forestry (PolicyForClimate) ”, which will develop tools and frameworks to enable policymakers and other stakeholders to design fair, coherent, and effective climate mitigation and adaptation policies in the EU. The project will use AI-assisted evidence synthesis, a policy-lab approach, and embedded case studies to offer a continuously updated evidence base on policy impacts, trade-offs, synergies, and spillovers. Your research will focus on developing, applying, and validating a novel mixed-methods framework for ex-post impact evaluation of climate policies in forestry and agricultural landscapes. By combining state-of-the-art econometric techniques with qualitative participatory approaches, you will empirically analyze how climate policies have affected land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity metrics. This will require conducting systematic reviews on existing impact evaluation frameworks, run workshops and focus group discussions with various stakeholders, collect, combine, and analyze farm-level primary data and secondary spatially explicit data. Start date: February 2027. Your Duties And Responsibilities Include Conduct systematic literature reviews and workshops to develop a mixed-methods ex-post impact evaluation framework for climate policies; Apply rigorous econometric methods together with qualitative assessments, particularly from policy sciences, to evaluate the impact of specific climate policies on land cover, carbon, and biodiversity metrics; Conduct focus group discussions with various stakeholders in the EU to validate the proposed impact evaluation framework and results from the empirical analyses; Write research papers and present research findings at international academic conferences; Collaborate with our research partners and contribute to the dissemination of project results. You will work here You will be based at the Forest and Nature Conservation Policy Group (FNP) at Wageningen University . The FNP group focuses on the political, socio-economic and cultural dimensions of forests and nature. Our research addresses major challenges including biodiversity conservation, deforestation, forest transitions, climate change and landscape management in both the Global North and Global South. You will be jointly supervised by Dr. Jorge Sellare and Prof. Bas Arts from Wageningen University (WU-FNP), and by Dr. Dario Schulz (EFI) in the research group headed by Sven Wunder. linkedin:4472090457.title: PhD Position Continuum Two-Phase Flow Modelling of Piping in Dikes
linkedin:4472090457.desc: Develop advanced models to understand and predict piping and internal erosion in dikes. As a PhD researcher at TU Delft, you will connect fundamental fluid–soil interaction physics with computational modelling to contribute to safer flood defences. Job Description Internal erosion and piping are among the main failure mechanisms of clay–sand layered dikes and remain important challenges in flood risk management. Reliable numerical models can improve our understanding of how piping develops and help engineers assess and design safer, more reliable flood defence systems. In this PhD project, you will contribute to this challenge by advancing the modelling of particle transport and fluid–soil interaction in dikes. A key scientific challenge is to represent the complex interaction between soil particles and flowing water across different spatial and temporal scales, while keeping the models computationally efficient. The research builds on an Eulerian two-phase modelling approach previously applied to backward erosion piping. You will investigate how this approach can be further developed to capture the physical processes that govern pipe formation and progression, while connecting detailed modelling with larger-scale analyses. The goal of the project is to develop a robust and computationally efficient modelling framework that improves the prediction of piping in layered dikes. Your research will contribute to a better understanding of internal erosion and support the development of safer flood defence systems and more reliable flood risk assessments. Your Responsibilities As a PhD researcher, you will: Develop continuum-based two-phase models to predict internal erosion and pipe progression in clay-sand layered dikes. Derive constitutive modelling approaches from high-fidelity DNS-DEM data generated within the broader project consortium. Capture the multi-scale nature of pipe formation while maintaining computational efficiency, including the exploration of adaptive mesh refinement strategies. Disseminate research outcomes through scientific publications, conference presentations, and collaboration with researchers from relevant disciplines. Your work environment You will join the Offshore and Dredging Engineering group within the department of Maritime and Transport Technology of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. You will receive supervision and guidance while having the freedom to shape and develop your research. You will have access to well-equipped facilities, including: The hydraulic circuit. You will work in an open and collaborative environment where interdisciplinary teamwork, curiosity and scientific excellence are valued. The group works closely across fluid mechanics, soil mechanics, hydraulic engineering and ocean engineering, using various computational and experimental techniques, sharing knowledge and expertise to develop innovative solutions with meaningful societal impact. Please see our work for more information: Offshore and Dredging Engineering. Job Requirements You are highly motivated to translate fundamental flow and erosion physics into practically relevant scales through two-phase flow modelling. You are well organised, manage your time effectively and take initiative in a multidisciplinary research environment. You are results-oriented and enjoy working with researchers from different disciplines. Furthermore, you meet the following requirements: You have an MSc degree in a relevant field (Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Applied Physics, Process Technology, Civil Engineering or a closely related discipline) You have received training in multiphase flow physics, numerical methods, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), ideally complemented by application in your MSc thesis, research projects, or internships. Have excellent communication skills and command of English. Have affinity with teaching and guiding MSc students. Familiarity with Euler–Euler multiphase flow modelling and/or automatic mesh adaptation techniques is considered an advantage. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration. linkedin:4479244418.desc: Industrial PhD student: Kinetic modelling of catalytic hydrogen oxidation for hydrogen engines TRATON is a group of strong brands with a shared mission: transforming transportation together to create the future of sustainable transport solutions. Within TRATON, we include MAN, Scania, Volkswagen Truck & Bus, and International. As part of a global team of industry experts, you get to think bigger, experience more, and reach further. Together, we have the power to transform transportation - Let´s make a difference together. Introduction Join us as an industrial PhD student and contribute to the development of future hydrogen-fuelled heavy-duty vehicles by developing predictive kinetic models for catalytic hydrogen combustion. The research will bridge fundamental catalysis, experimental studies and engine-level simulations, with the long-term aim of enabling efficient hydrogen powertrains with ultra low emissions. Hydrogen internal combustion engines (H₂-ICE) with high-pressure direct injection offer high efficiency and power density but face challenges related to cold start and the need of carbon-based pilot fuels for ignition. Catalytic hydrogen oxidation over noble metals such as platinum could improve cold-start performance and enable hydrogen-only ignition concepts. Role Summary This role is a part of TRATON Group R&D, located in Södertälje, Sweden. The main focus of this Industrial PhD is the development and validation of kinetic models for hydrogen oxidation over noble-metal catalysts across a broad range of operating conditions and applications, including cold-start and in-cylinder conditions. You will also work closely with other PhD students and researchers to design and conduct relevant experimental studies supporting kinetic model development and validation, providing opportunities for hands-on experimental work in catalysis. The position will be part of PtHICE – Innovative ways to use platinum for zero emission hydrogen vehicles, a joint research project involving TRATON, Chalmers University of Technology, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Christian-Albrechts-University of Kiel, AVL List GmbH and Johnson Matthey. You will be employed by TRATON AB and affiliated with the Division of Chemical Engineering at Chalmers University of Technology, and work in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners. Job Responsibilities The work will involve all parts of a research project, from developing scientific hypotheses and analysing experimental data to kinetic model development, validation and application. Your main responsibilities will include: Develop and validate kinetic models for catalytic hydrogen oxidation based on experimental data, and apply them in 1D and 3D simulations under engine-relevant conditions, including cold start and catalytic-assisted hydrogen ignition. Collaborate with academic and industrial partners across experiments and modelling, and communicate research results through scientific publications and international conferences. Who You Are We welcome applicants from all backgrounds – your unique experience and perspectives is valuable to us. You should have an M.Sc. degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Engineering Physics, Applied Physics, or a related field, preferably with a background or strong interest in catalysis, chemical kinetics, reaction engineering or numerical modelling. You should be interested in understanding physical and chemical phenomena from experimental data and translating this knowledge into mathematical and numerical models. As a person, you are curious, energetic and collaborative, with a proactive mindset and a strong interest in learning and exploring new ideas. You enjoy working in a multidisciplinary team and contributing to a positive research environment. You should have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Swedish language skills are considered a merit but are not required. TRATON Offers We offer a dynamic and engaging workplace where collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement are part of everyday life. You will be part of a strong team environment that encourages knowledge sharing and close cooperation across functions. With a structured development plan and a wide range of training opportunities, TRATON supports your professional growth both locally and internationally. Benefits include access to our health center in mapor a wellness allowance, bonus, flexible working hours, and company car leasing. The group also arranges events for employees and their families, and for those living in Stockholm. We offer an inspiring and inclusive workplace with respect for the individual and great opportunities to shape your work and your future. As an Industrial PhD student, you will be an employee at TRATON AB, where you will be part of a team with industry experts and researchers in catalysis and simulation. Your time will be mainly based at TRATON R&D Sweden in Södertälje, while also spending some time at Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg as part of the PhD studies. Application We look forward to receiving your application, consisting of your CV and kindly ask you not to share a cover letter to ensure an efficient and unbiased recruitment process for all parties. The position is also subject to a successful security screening in accordance with TRATON’s standard recruitment procedures.
