indeed:1f22aaa5b32719ae.title: Doctoral Researcher in Interactive and Immersive Simulation of Animal Navigation in the Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group
indeed:1f22aaa5b32719ae.desc: Paygrade E13 TV-L Working Hours 100% (suitable for part-time) Institution Institute of Physics (School of Mathematics and Natural Sciences) Location Oldenburg (Oldb) Application Deadline 30.10.2026 First day of work 01.01.2027 Limited for 3 years About us The Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group at the University of Oldenburg invites applications for a three-year doctoral research position at the interface of computer science, physics, and biology. The project investigates how interactive and immersive simulation can help scientists explore, experiment with, and reason about computational models of animal navigation. Animals navigate using multiple environmental and sensory cues. Computational models allow researchers to investigate possible mechanisms, test hypotheses, and predict movement patterns. This PhD will develop and scientifically evaluate interactive approaches that make such models more accessible to systematic exploration, comparison, and interpretation. Virtual and mixed reality are promising approaches, alongside conventional desktop and potentially web-based interfaces. Research questions How can researchers interactively vary model parameters, assumptions, sensory cues, and competing navigation hypotheses? Under which conditions do immersive interfaces (VR/MR) offer advantages over conventional interfaces for exploring complex navigation simulations? How can interactive representations help connect individual simulated decisions and trajectories with population-level or large-scale movement patterns? How can the scientific value of different interaction techniques be evaluated in realistic research tasks? Your tasks Develop a research framework for visualizing and interacting with computational models of animal navigation. Design and implement methods to explore parameters, manipulate assumptions, compare hypotheses, and inspect simulated outcomes. Integrate existing or newly developed navigation models and simulation data into interactive environments, potentially using Unity, Unreal Engine, or other appropriate technologies. Design and conduct evaluations with researchers to assess how different interfaces support scientific exploration, interpretation, and reasoning. Collaborate closely with scientists in physics, biology, and computer science; document and disseminate results through scientific publications and presentations. Pursue an independent doctoral research project leading to a PhD. Your profile Required qualifications: Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Physics, Computational Biology, Engineering, Human–Computer Interaction, or a closely related discipline. Strong programming skills, for example in Python, C++, C#, or comparable languages. Experience in interactive software development, simulation, scientific computing, visualization, or related areas. Interest in computational modelling and in investigating scientific questions through software and empirical evaluation. Excellent written and spoken English; ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team. Advanced experience with machine learning methods Desirable qualifications Experience with VR/MR, Unity or Unreal Engine, 3D interaction, or immersive visualization. Knowledge of human–computer interaction, user studies, usability evaluation, or visual analytics. Experience with agent-based modelling, animal movement, navigation, ecological simulation, or trajectory analysis. Familiarity with reproducible research software, data pipelines, or scientific visualization. Possible additional application: science communication Methods developed for scientific research may also be adapted into accessible interactive demonstrations for public outreach, for example through VR/MR or web-based experiences at science events. This is a secondary opportunity rather than a separate educational-software development objective. We offer The Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group (www.quantbiolab.com) develops computational approaches to biological and physical systems and works in an international, interdisciplinary research environment. The position offers collaboration across disciplines, access to modern computational and immersive-visualization infrastructure, doctoral supervision, and opportunities for scientific publication and professional development. Employment conditions and benefits follow the applicable collective agreement (TV-L) and university policies, including annual leave, flexible working arrangements, and university health and sports programmes. Our standards The University of Oldenburg is dedicated to increase the percentage of female employees in the field of science. Therefore, female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. In accordance to § 21 Section 3 NHG, female candidates with equal qualifications will be preferentially considered. Applicants with disabilities will be given preference in case of equal qualification. Apply now Please send your application via e-mail by 30.10.2026 to ilia.solovyov@uni-oldenburg.de Please submit a single PDF with the following reference number QBL10 containing a cover letter explaining your research motivation and relevant experience, a CV, academic transcripts, a brief statement of research interests, a list of publications or software projects (if applicable), and contact details of at least two referees. Applications should be sent to Prof. Dr. Ilia Solov’yov. The application deadline and anticipated starting date will be announced in the final advertisement. Benefits at University of Oldenburg 30 days vacation Secure remuneration according to collective agreement Company pension scheme Further education opportunities Flexible working hours Health management Remote working Compatibility of career and family Support with childcare University Sports Centre Certificate Bicycle-friendly employer Corporate Benefits

indeed:e5946908878e240c.title: PhD Position Experimental Analysis of Boiling Instabilities in Advanced Nuclear Steam Generators
indeed:e5946908878e240c.desc: PhD Position Experimental Analysis of Boiling Instabilities in Advanced Nuclear Steam Generators Help determine operational limits of next-gen nuclear steam generators! Job description Advanced nuclear reactor designs like the high temperature gas cooled reactor or molten salt reactor offer certain advantages compared to traditional light water reactors. One such advantage is their potential to operate with a high thermal efficiency. This advantage stems from the fact that these reactors operate at much higher temperatures, enabling superheated steam generation. Traditional light water reactors utilize so-called U-tube steam generators in which saturated steam is produced. It is well known that such steam generators suffer from spontaneous oscillations of two-phase mass flow and pressure drop on the shell side. This phenomenon is well understood in light water reactors, allowing for safe and stable operation. However, these boiling instabilities are more severe in once-through helical steam generators, as the dryout point will shift rapidly up and down along the helical tubes. This oscillating behaviour can lead to thermal fatigue of the tube walls, which can ultimately result in mechanical failure. While this phenomenon is already complex enough in and of itself, it typically coincides with parallel channel instabilities. In this project, you will develop and build a laboratory steam generator set-up to study boiling instabilities in helical tubes. In the first year, you will help design and build the set-up along with a team of skilled technicians and an energetic supervisory team. Subsequently, you will study the characteristics of the boiling instabilities within the set-up and compare them to a numerical model. Your Working Environment You will join the Process & Energy (P&E) department at TU Delft’s Mechanical Engineering faculty.Our department works along the themes of Energy, Flow and Processes. You will work together with top researchers highly skilled in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics. Moreover, we collaborate with researchers from the Reactor Institute Delft. You will have opportunities for professional development through both technical and non-technical courses. We expect that as part of your PhD you will take the lead on interacting and collaborating with other researchers at TU Delft, with research groups at other universities, and with industry and other stakeholders. Furthermore, we expect that you have 2) A MSc. degree in either chemistry, physics or mechanical engineering or similar field. 3) Strong affinity with thermodynamics and transport equations. 4) A keen interest in the nuclear industry and its future roles in society. 5) An interest in transient modelling and analysis. 6) Good communication skills and the ability to be a team player in a highly multidisciplinary setting. indeed:4c348232035b73aa.desc: PhD Position Flexibility in Nuclear Power Can nuclear- and renewable energy play nice? Job description Both Europe and the Netherlands are committed to transitioning to a CO2-neutral economy by 2050. As part of this commitment, the Netherlands has built large-scale wind park, and a significant amount of energy comes from solar power as well. While wind and solar energy help to decarbonize power generation, it also comes at a cost. Due to the intermittent availability of wind and solar energy, grid congestion can occur (which means that the grid lacks sufficient capacity to handle demand or supply of electricity). Therefore, the grid must be carefully managed. In many countries, gas power plants help manage the grid. However, since natural gas counteracts decarbonization, the question arises: “which other technologies can help reduce grid congestion? Small modular reactors (SMR) - nuclear reactors below 300 MWe – may be able to operate flexibly to help counteract grid congestion. As such reactors have less inertia, they are better suited to load-following than large-scale nuclear power plants. Even so, their ramp rates are much lower than other technologies. Through smart design of the power cycle and the inclusion of thermal energy storage, ramp rates of SMR’s can be greatly enhanced. In this thesis project, you will design advanced power cycles with or without energy storage for SMR’s to enable enhanced load-following. Using numerical techniques, you will couple transient power cycle modelling with nuclear reactor modelling to analyse any feedback to the reactor. You will run different load-following scenarios to ascertain technologically feasible enhanced ramp rates. You will be assisted by an expert supervisory team during your PhD. As the Dutch Nuclear industry is growing rapidly, and the Dutch Government has announced a significant expansion of nuclear energy, your results may actively contribute to shaping the Dutch nuclear landscape. indeed:657a2f2f726c9aa2.title: PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN
indeed:657a2f2f726c9aa2.desc: Job requisition Id: 16967 Job type: PhD positions Contract hours min: 38 Contract hours max: 38 Location: Leiden Applying is possible until: 12 November 2026 Teaser Text The Faculty of Science and Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for candidates for a PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN ANA-KIN is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme. Over the past two decades, small-molecule kinase inhibitors have transformed cancer therapy, yet nearly all of them target the highly conserved ATP-binding site, which limits selectivity and allows resistance to emerge. ANA-KIN aims to train a new generation of interdisciplinary researchers capable of redefining kinase drug discovery beyond the ATP paradigm, by developing the experimental and computational tools, modular assays and workflows needed to systematically target non-conserved regulatory interfaces, such as kinase dimerization and substrate-binding sites. Proof-of-concept will be demonstrated on three representative kinases: EGFR, BRAF and the understudied “dark” kinase LTK. ANA-KIN brings together 11 beneficiaries and 9 associated partners across Europe and the USA, including Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (coordinator), University of Crete, Goethe University Frankfurt, Saarland University, EPFL, CNRS, Pompeu Fabra University, VIB, KU Leuven, INSERM and Leiden University, together with industrial partners such as AstraZeneca, Novartis, Servier and Skylight Therapeutics. The network combines chemical biology, structural biophysics (single-molecule FRET, cryo-EM, nanodiscs), AI-driven drug design and cell biology in an integrated learn–design–test loop. Twelve Doctoral Candidates (DCs) will each pursue an individual research project, benefit from co-supervision across institutions and sectors, carry out two research secondments at partner organizations, and follow a structured network-wide training program covering scientific, transferable, open-science and entrepreneurial skills. In this PhD project (DC10, Work Package 3 – Discovery), you will develop deep-learning architectures that integrate text-mined, cheminformatic, and biophysical descriptors to predict interface binding, allosteric signatures and resistance liabilities of kinase ligands. The models will learn jointly across peptide and small-molecule modalities and will be used to generate hybrid peptidomimetic design hypotheses. You will translate these models into consortium-wide prioritisation dashboards that support hit triage and analogue selection in the discovery campaigns of ANA-KIN, and work in close reciprocal feedback with DC9 (Saarland University) on structure-based and machine-learning pipelines. Model predictions will be validated prospectively with the experimental partners in the network. The expected results are a resistance-aware AI workflow for non-ATP interface ligands, accompanied by public models, datasets and interpretable feature maps, and prospective design case studies demonstrating improved optimisation trajectories. To reinforce structural grounding and experimental validation, you will carry out two secondments: at VIB (Belgium, Prof. Ruslan Efremov; 4 months) to extract structural classes and conformational features from cryo-EM data and use them to refine model constraints, and at Skylight Therapeutics (Belgium, Dr. Joshua Salafsky; 3 months) to test model predictions using second-harmonic generation (SHG)-based conformational profiling. The project will be supervised by Prof. Gerard J.P. van Westen (Leiden University), with Prof. Ruslan Efremov and Dr. Joshua Salafsky as co-supervisors. What you will do Conduct original and novel research in deep learning, AI, and cheminformatics for kinase drug discovery; Develop, benchmark and openly share models, datasets and decision-support dashboards following FAIR and open-science principles; Collaborate closely with experimental and computational DCs in the network, and carry out two research secondments abroad (VIB and Skylight Therapeutics, Belgium); Publish and present scientific articles at international journals and conferences; Participate in the ANA-KIN network-wide training events, schools and outreach activities; Contribute to educational activities; Write a dissertation. What you bring A MSc degree in Computer Science, AI, (Computational) Chemistry, Bioinformatics, Biopharmaceutical Sciences, or a relevant related field; Good knowledge of and experience with machine learning and deep-learning techniques (e.g. PyTorch); Good knowledge of and experience with cheminformatics and/or computational chemistry (e.g. RDKit, molecular descriptors, docking); Interest in structural biology, protein kinases and drug discovery; affinity with peptide or biophysical data is an advantage; Highly motivated to both perform foundational research and apply the developed methods to real-world problems; creative, ‘making things work’ mentality, independent, and communicative team player; Willingness to travel and to carry out research secondments at partner institutions abroad; Excellent programming skills (preferably Python); Good academic writing skills and interest in participating in educational activities; Excellent proficiency in English (oral and written). MSCA eligibility criteria At the date of recruitment, candidates must not have been awarded a doctoral degree; Mobility rule: candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the date of recruitment. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status are not taken into account. Where you will work Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research Our institute is a center of excellence for multidisciplinary research on drug discovery and development. Leiden University consistently ranks within the top-20 world-wide within the subject-based QS Ranking in Pharmacology and Pharmacy. At LACDR, we develop innovative scientific concepts in fundamental and translational research underlying the discovery and optimization of drugs, and personalized medicines. We aim to optimize the route to novel drugs that are both efficacious and safe, and therefore our research focuses on drug discovery and safety, bio-therapeutics, and systems biomedicine and pharmacology. State-of-the-art expertise and infrastructures ensure that we are strategically positioned in (inter)national collaborations, thus further strengthening the development of novel concepts and their application in a clinical and industry environment. Computational Drug Discovery Research in this group, headed by Gerard van Westen, focusses on computational methods integrated in different parts of the drug discovery process. More specifically, topics include innovative treatments for cancer, kinase and GPCR drug discovery, proteochemometrics, selectivity and polypharmacology modeling, allosteric modulation, drug resistance modeling, de novo molecular design, and novel methods in the domain of machine learning. For more information see: http://www.cddl.nl Research at our faculty The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from artificial intelligence, computer science, mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,700 staff and almost 6,000 students. We are located in the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry meet. For more information, see http://www.science.leidenuniv.nl . What we offer We offer a full-time appointment for 48 months as a Doctoral Candidate within the MSCA Doctoral Network ANA-KIN, starting late 2026. The appointment is initially for one year; after a positive evaluation of the progress of the research, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended for the remaining period. Salary ranges from € 3.204,- tot € 4.051,- gross per month (pay scale P in accordance with the Collective Labor Agreement for Dutch Universities). Leiden University offers an attractive benefits package with additional holiday (8%) and end-of-year bonuses (8.3%), training and career development. Our individual choices model gives you some freedom to assemble your own set of terms and conditions. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break. All our PhD students are embedded in the Leiden University Graduate School of Science. Our graduate school offers several PhD training courses at three levels: professional courses, skills training and personal effectiveness. In addition, advanced courses to deepen scientific knowledge are offered by the research school. As an ANA-KIN Doctoral Candidate you will also follow the network’s training program, including summer schools, workshops and an industrial immersion workshop, and your progress will be monitored by a Thesis Advisory Committee including an independent mentor. What we value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Inquiries about the research area can be made to Prof. Gerard van Westen, gerard@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. If you have any questions about the procedure, please contact Brigitte Kraakman, b.p.m.kraakman@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. To apply for this vacancy, please submit your application online via the blue button below. Please ensure that you upload the following additional documents quoting the vacancy number and “ANA-KIN DC10”: application letter (including a statement confirming that they meet the MSCA eligibility criteria) curriculum vitae a list of grades two references (who have agreed to be contacted) Only applications received no later than November 12th can be considered. The selection procedure will take place in November. Selected candidates may be invited for an interview in the last week of November / 1st week of December, during which you are kindly requested to be available. indeed:e650ea34576d82d0.desc: Job requisition Id: 16972 Job type: PhD positions Contract hours min: 38 Contract hours max: 38 Location: Leiden Applying is possible until: 30 November 2026 Teaser Text We are looking for PhD candidates interested in research at the intersection of machine learning (ML) and quantum many-body physics. They will work on the mechanics of ML and developing new ML approaches to challenging quantum problems, with a strong focus on making these approaches interpretable, reliable, and scalable. In this position, you will learn about state-of-the-art deep learning solutions as well as the challenges of understanding neural networks. You will be given increasing scientific freedom, supported by structured mentoring, including career development plans guided by your plans after the PhD. The starting date is flexible, the latest in November 2027. The position is set in the exciting, friendly, and interdisciplinary environment of the aQa (Applied Quantum Algorithms) group, which is a team of faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and students across the Leiden Institute of Physics (LION), the Leiden Institute for Advanced Computer Science (LIACS), the Leiden Institute for Chemistry (LIC), and the Leiden Mathematical Institute (MI) at the Leiden University. What you will do Conducting research on the mechanics of deep learning and applications of (interpretable, reliable, and scalable) ML in quantum sciences with scientific integrity and rigor under the supervision of Dr. Anna Dawid; Assisting in relevant teaching activities; Actively participating in regular group and one-on-one meetings; Co-supervising Bachelor and Master students; Co-organizing scientific events; Presenting your research results to the scientific community at international conferences and through publications. Where you will work The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. You will be part of the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS). LIACS offers the bachelor's programs in Computer Science and Data Science/Artificial Intelligence, as well as master's programs in Computer Science, ICT in Business and the Public Sector, Media Technology, and Science Based Business. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science What you bring Master’s degree in physics, computer science, or a closely related field; Strong interest in ML and motivation to make it interpretable and reliable; Knowledge of quantum physics and numerical methods for quantum systems or theory of deep learning is preferred; Good programming skills in Python; Proficient in spoken and written English; A team player who can communicate well across scientific fields and teams; Highly motivated and organized self-starter with an open mindset. indeed:9174580a55ea2141.title: PhD Researcher Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (1.0 FTE)
indeed:9174580a55ea2141.desc: Job requisition Id: 16924 Job type: PhD positions Contract hours min: 38 Contract hours max: 38 Location: Leiden Applying is possible until: 31 January 2027 Teaser Text PhD Researcher in “A Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Culture: Insights from Central Asia, the Middle East, North Africa, and Southeast Asia” ( Minaret Project ), 1.0 FTE. The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) invites applications for one PhD Researcher (1.0 FTE, 4 years) from September/October 2027 – September/October 2031 to join the Minaret Project, a HORIZON Unit Grant-funded interdisciplinary and transnational research initiative, which examines the interconnection between law, religion and governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies to promote democracy and good governance. The project brings together 11 universities with 15 PhD researchers across 3 work packages and 15 subprojects, with the applicant contributing to the subproject Neo-Imperialism and Constitutional Reform: The Global Dimension . This subproject examines to what extent international organizations and global governance actors act as neo-imperial forces shaping constitutional reform in North Africa and the Middle East. It will explore how donor-driven “rule of law” and “good governance” programs are developed, interpreted, and implemented in countries such as Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria. Particular attention will be paid to how the legal frameworks promoted by international actors relate to the government practices in these countries, and in particular to those embedded in local traditions and religious values. Drawing on policy-document analysis and elite interviews with a diverse range of actors -including international advisers, domestic policymakers, civil-society representatives, legal practitioners, religious scholars, and community leaders-, the study will investigate how transnational constitutional models are negotiated, adapted, resisted, or hybridized in practice. It will contribute to debates on postcolonial constitutionalism by examining the processes through which legal and governance norms circulate across borders, as well as the forms of influence, dependency, and agency that shape their adoption. Ultimately, the project seeks to develop a nuanced account of how external interventions affect perceptions of legitimacy, legal pluralism, and sovereignty in transitional Muslim-majority societies. What you will do The PhD researcher will join the Leiden-based Minaret team, working closely with two senior-researchers and two external mentors (one academic and one non-academic, associated with the project). The position provides the opportunity to conduct original empirical research on the underlying structures of constitutional reform in said countries, while also contributing to public engagement and the collaborative life of the project. All PhD researchers are required to undertake two secondments abroad with the project’s associated partners, one academic and one non-academic, of between two and six months' duration. This will not only enhance research capabilities but also equip the PhD researcher for academic and non-academic roles. Academic Research Conduct socio-legal and policy analysis with key stakeholders in selected countries. Write a doctoral dissertation and co-author academic publications based on qualitative research. Contribute to the project’s comparative framework within the subproject; within the work package (Imperial Genealogies and Constitutional Formation) and between the work packages. Communications & Engagement Present research findings at events organized by the research project, such as 3 summer schools and 4 training events. Willingness and ability to spend extended periods abroad for fieldwork and 2 secondments. Help organize international workshops, conferences, and events with academic and civil society partners. Contribute to project website and social media accounts. Where you will work The Faculty of Law is based in both Leiden and The Hague and, with over 7,000 students and approximately 600 staff members, is one of the largest law faculties in the Netherlands. The faculty is committed to innovative, multidisciplinary research and a constantly evolving curriculum that addresses key societal challenges. Our faculty is large enough to make an impact on both a national and international scale, yet small enough to offer a personal and engaging learning experience. In this way, we contribute every day to a safer and more sustainable world. Impact with law! For more information, please visit https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/law . The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) is part of the Leiden Law School. The VVI seeks to advance knowledge of the formation and functioning of legal systems in their social contexts, the impact of these systems on society and vice versa, their effectiveness in governance, and their contribution to development. The Institute adopts a socio-legal and global approach, doing research on law in the books and law in action in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Europe. VVI staff teaches several socio-legal thematic and regional courses for both Dutch and foreign exchange students. In addition, VVI provides PhD supervision, advisory services and training courses to policy makers and practitioners. For more information, see www.vvi.leidenuniv.nl . What you bring In our team, we are looking for someone who can work independently while also contributing to a collaborative environment. Since every position is unique, we will devote careful attention to your onboarding. If some aspects of the work are new to you, we will identify what support you need and develop a tailored plan for your professional growth. We do not expect candidates to already have all the qualifications listed below. Training will be provided in areas such as socio-legal studies, research methods, and the specificities of constitutional reform in the Middle East. That said, this position will be a good fit for you if you recognize yourself in many of the following: A MSc or LLM in Anthropology, Political Science, Law, International Studies, International Relations, Development Studies, or a closely related field; Demonstrated experience in conducting empirical research, ideally in the project’s country contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria); Experience working with (inter)national civil society actors; Knowledge of constitutional reform, especially in relation to religion, democracy, and governance; Familiarity with socio-legal literature and qualitative research methods; Ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary and international research team; Familiarity with one of the project’s country contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria) is an asset; Knowledge of written and spoken Arabic is strongly recommended. What we offer Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organisation is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development. You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organise through Healthy University. We also offer: An employment contract for the duration of four years. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities; A salary between €3204 - €4051 gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours) (PhD student); A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP; Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel; Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme; A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop and a mobile telephone. For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions What we value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. Leiden University aims to be an inclusive community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to develop to their full potential. Diversity in experiences and perspectives enriches our teaching and strengthens our research. High-quality education and research means inclusive education and research. Want to apply or find out more? If you want to apply straight away, click the application button. If you would like more information about what the job entails, please contact Dr. Nadia Sonneveld, at n.sonneveld@law.leidenuniv.nl. You can apply until 31 January 2027; To apply for this vacancy, please submit your application in English addressed to Dr. Nadia Sonneveld using the blue button at the top of this text. Interviews are scheduled in February-March 2027. Please include with your application the following: A cover letter stating your motivation for this position; A curriculum vitae; Transcripts from your bachelors and masters degrees; A major writing sample (i.e Master’s thesis, article, or other class paper); Names of 2-3 academic references. To help us get to know each other better, we follow a number of steps in the application procedure. For more information, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions In choosing between candidates, in case of equal suitability, preference will be given to internal candidates, women, the occupationally disabled and employees with a migration background. A pre-employment screening (references, diplomas, certificate of good conduct (VOG)) may be part of the selection procedure. Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. If you nevertheless choose to send us CVs, no rights can be derived from this. #LI-Hybrid Information at a Glance Faculty / Unit: Faculty of Law Contact with (Name + position): Dr. Nadia Sonneveld Contact Email address: n.sonneveld@law.leidenuniv.nl

indeed:ac61285ef558d09b.desc: Job Reference 455_26_CS_AHPC_R1 Position PhD Student linked to ERC Consolidator Grant (Processing-in-Memory) (R1) Closing Date Saturday, 31 October, 2026 Reference: 455_26_CS_AHPC_R1 Job title: PhD Student linked to ERC Consolidator Grant (Processing-in-Memory) (R1) About BSC The Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over 1000 staff from 60 countries. Look at the BSC experience: BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team. Context And Mission The Accelerators and Communications for HPC Group leads cutting-edge research and development around accelerators/coprocessors in HPC and high-performance networking. We collaborate closely with the major vendors in the topic for HPC: NVIDIA and Intel. We organize locally international events such as the PUMPS Summer School, PATC Courses on CUDA/OpenACC, and annual hackathons, and collaborate in the organization of related international conferences and workshops such as SC, IEEE Cluster, or AsHES. The group has been recently awarded one of the prestigious ERC Consolidator Grants. We are looking to cover a PhD Student positions to work on the new hot topic of processing-in-memory applied to Homomorphically Encrypted Deep Learning Inference. Prospective candidates may take a look at the following paper to get an initial idea of our focus: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.16139 Group Web Page: https://www.bsc.es/discover-bsc/organisation/scientific-structure/accelerators-and-communications-hpc Key Duties Drive research in the above-mentioned topic, under the supervision of the Group Manager and the mentorship of a postdoctoral researcher Requirements Education MS in a related field Essential Knowledge and Professional Experience Low-level C/C++ Additional Knowledge and Professional Experience At least 2 years experience working with Processing in Memory Competences Good English Level Conditions The position will be located at BSC within the Computer Sciences Department We offer a full-time contract (35h/week), a good working environment, a highly stimulating environment with state-of-the-art infrastructure, flexible working hours, extensive training plan, restaurant tickets, private health insurance, support to the relocation procedures Duration: Open-ended contract due to technical and scientific activities linked to the project and budget duration Holidays: 22 days of holidays + 6 personal days + 24th and 31st of December per our collective agreement Salary: we offer a competitive salary commensurate with the qualifications and experience of the candidate and according to the cost of living in Barcelona Starting date: 16/11/2026 Applications procedure and process All applications must be submitted via the BSC website and contain: A full CV in English including contact details A cover/motivation letter with a statement of interest in English, clearly specifying for which specific area and topics the applicant wishes to be considered. Additionally, two references for further contacts must be included. Applications without this document will not be considered. Development of the recruitment process The selection will be carried out through a competitive examination system ("Concurso-Oposición"). The recruitment process consists of two phases: Curriculum Analysis: Evaluation of previous experience and/or scientific history, degree, training, and other professional information relevant to the position. - 40 points Interview phase: The highest-rated candidates at the curriculum level will be invited to the interview phase, conducted by the corresponding department and Human Resources. In this phase, technical competencies, knowledge, skills, and professional experience related to the position, as well as the required personal competencies, will be evaluated. - 60 points. A minimum of 30 points out of 60 must be obtained to be eligible for the position. The recruitment panel will be composed of at least three people, ensuring at least 25% representation of women. In accordance with OTM-R principles, a gender-balanced recruitment panel is formed for each vacancy at the beginning of the process. After reviewing the content of the applications, the panel will begin the interviews, with at least one technical and one administrative interview. At a minimum, a personality questionnaire as well as a technical exercise will be conducted during the process. The panel will make a final decision, and all individuals who participated in the interview phase will receive feedback with details on the acceptance or rejection of their profile. indeed:5eb11acd652f501d.title: Phd candidate - Generative Agent-Based Modeling for Climate Policy Design
indeed:5eb11acd652f501d.desc: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About the Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main duties and responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants should submit a dossier including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About the University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián.

indeed:8b107218579ff8fe.title: Doktorandplats - statistiker inom tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården
indeed:8b107218579ff8fe.desc: Vid Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS) bedrivs världsledande forskning inom åldrande, demens, epidemiologi och vårdvetenskap. Forskningen sträcker sig från grundforskning på molekyl- och cellnivå till kliniska studier och forskning på samhällsnivå. Vid NVS genomför cirka en tredjedel av KI:s studenter sin utbildning på grund- och avancerad nivå. Institutionen med cirka 540 anställda och en omsättning på 530 miljoner miljoner år 2023, består av sju avdelningar och finns på Campus Flemingsberg och Campus Solna. Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård ansvarar för delar av läkarprogrammet. Inom forskarutbildning har vi en egen forskarskola i allmänmedicin. Vår primärvårdsforskning omfattar varierande projekt kring multisjuklighet, folksjukdomar som diabetes, nedsatt njurfunktion och psykisk ohälsa samt även pedagogiska projekt. Närmare 100 personer, av vilka cirka 30 doktorander, är anknutna till avdelningen. Vill du bidra till medicinsk forskning av toppkvalitet? Att vara doktorand innebär att vara antagen till en utbildning på forskarnivå (forskarutbildning) där man följer en individuell studieplan. En doktorand ägnar sig åt ett forskningsprojekt under handledning, kompletterat med kurser och andra lärandeaktiviteter. För en doktorsexamen krävs motsvarande fyra års utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid. Forskargruppen Doktorandtjänsten finns inom forskargruppen för STEADY-CAN (Stockholm Early Detection of Cancer Study) vid Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård, Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS). Gruppen består av kliniskt aktiva forskare, statistiker och doktorander som arbetar med tidig upptäckt av cancer, i nära samarbete med Regionalt cancercentrum Stockholm-Gotland och internationella samarbetspartners. Gruppen är involverad i flera pågående forskningsprojekt, inklusive utveckling av statistiska och maskininlärningsbaserade prediktionsmodeller, longitudinell analys av blodprovsdata och registerbaserade kohortstudier inom cancerepidemiologi. Du kommer att ingå i en tvärvetenskaplig grupp där statistiker, allmänläkare och epidemiologer arbetar nära varandra. I praktiken innebär det att du regelbundet diskuterar analysval med kliniker, förklarar statistiska metoder för personer utan statistisk bakgrund och själv lär dig om den kliniska vardagen i primärvården. Gruppen har regelbundna gemensamma analysmöten där du förväntas både ge och ta emot återkoppling på pågående arbete. Doktorandprojektet och doktorandens uppgifter Detta doktorandprojekt kombinerar traditionell statistisk modellering och maskininlärning i tillämpad forskning kring tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården. Projektet använder data från STEADY-CAN-kohorten, som omfattar över 2,7 miljoner vuxna i Region Stockholm med länkade laboratorie-, journal- och registerdata. Under doktorandutbildningen kommer kandidaten att få bred kunskap inom överlevnadsanalys, prediktionsmodellering, maskininlärning och hantering av stora registerbaserade datamängder. Vi söker en motiverad doktorand med god bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. Den framgångsrika kandidaten förväntas ta ett stort eget ansvar genom hela projektet, med stöd från handledarna. Detta innebär konstruktion av analysdatamängder, statistisk analys och implementering av maskininlärningsmetoder, författande av vetenskapliga artiklar samt deltagande i institutionens seminarier och i nationella och internationella konferenser. Vad erbjuder vi? En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. På KI får du träffa forskare med olika forskningsinriktningar som jobbar tillsammans. Det är det gränsöverskridande samarbetet som bidrar till KI:s världsledande position inom forskning. Som doktorand erbjuds du ett individuellt forskningsprojekt, en välutbildad handledare, ett stort utbud av valbara kurser och möjligheten att arbeta i en framgångsrik forskargrupp. Karolinska Institutet har samarbeten med framstående universitet över hela världen, vilket ger möjlighet till internationella utbyten. Som anställd doktorand får du en avtalsenlig lön, du får träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar och du får ersättning för läkarvård. Behörighetskrav för utbildning på forskarnivå För att delta i urvalet till en doktorandplats måste du styrka både det grundläggande (A) och det särskilda (B) behörighetskravet innan ansökningsperioden stänger. Det är ditt ansvar som sökande att styrka din behörighet genom att följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. A) Grundläggande behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det grundläggande behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: har avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå (magister- eller masterexamen), eller har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller har på annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.* Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. Utmärkta kunskaper i biostatistik och praktisk erfarenhet av överlevnadsanalys är meriterande. Tidigare erfarenhet av databehandling och statistisk analys är meriterande. indeed:1062a32bfdcba2bf.title: Thèse en IA, deep learning et Mathématiques appliquées
indeed:1062a32bfdcba2bf.desc: Offre de thèse – Méta-apprentissage robuste et efficace pour la segmentation d’images médicales Lieu : Toulouse INP / IRIT, Toulouse, France Durée : 3 ans — Début prévu : 1er septembre 2027 Date limite de candidature : 23 novembre 2026 Rémunération : environ 2 800 € Nous recherchons un candidat ou une candidate motivé(e) pour développer des méthodes de méta-apprentissage capables de s’adapter à de nouvelles tâches de segmentation d’images médicales à partir d’un nombre limité d’exemples annotés. Le projet se situe à l’interface de l’apprentissage profond, de l’optimisation et de l’imagerie médicale. Le projet s’articulera autour de trois axes de recherche : Optimisation du méta-apprentissage pour améliorer la stabilité des méthodes et réduire leur coût en calcul et en mémoire. Analyse des relations entre tâches médicales pour identifier les connaissances transférables et limiter les interférences entre tâches hétérogènes. Adaptation structurée et efficace des modèles pour faciliter l’apprentissage de nouvelles tâches avec peu de données annotées. La thèse sera dirigée par le Pr Lotfi Chaari (Toulouse INP / IRIT) , avec un co-encadrement assuré par Dr Amel Aissaoui (Toulouse INP / IRIT) et Dr Alena Kopanicakova (Université de Genève, Suisse) . Une cotutelle pourra être envisagée. Profil recherché : diplôme de master ou équivalent en informatique, intelligence artificielle, mathématiques appliquées, science des données ou dans un domaine connexe ; solides compétences en programmation, de préférence en Python/PyTorch ; intérêt marqué pour les aspects mathématiques et algorithmiques de l’apprentissage ; bonne maîtrise de l’anglais écrit et oral. Une expérience en méta-apprentissage, segmentation d’images, optimisation numérique ou imagerie médicale serait appréciée, sans être obligatoire. Important — Conditions d’éligibilité au programme BEST : les candidats doivent être titulaires de leur master à la date limite de candidature, ne pas déjà détenir de doctorat et ne pas avoir résidé ou exercé leur activité principale en France pendant plus de 12 mois au cours des 36 mois précédant la date limite de candidature. Un excellent dossier académique et un fort potentiel pour la recherche doctorale sont attendus. Conditions complètes : https://doctorat.univ-toulouse.fr/cofund-best Description complète du sujet et modalités de candidature : https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YbqYcot7dJgQsgSfN68Wf6HC6IyylZbEV36gyGo5uGY/edit?usp=sharing Pour candidater : déposez votre candidature sur https://edd-projets.utoulouse.fr/ et envoyez, en parallèle, votre CV détaillé et vos derniers relevés de notes à amel.aissaoui@irit.fr and Alena.Kopanicakova@unige.ch , avec pour objet : Application – PhD in Robust and Scalable Meta-Learning for Medical Image Segmentation . Lieu du poste : En présentiel

indeed:0dd0f018abac4a77.title: Two PhD positions SNSF project “Governing the Party: How the Chinese Communist Party Holds Itself Together”
indeed:0dd0f018abac4a77.desc: Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies (IAOS), Chair of Modern Chinese Studies Two PhD positions SNSF project “Governing the Party: How the Chinese Communist Party Holds Itself Together” 80 % Start of employment 1 March 2027, temporary The Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies (IAOS) at the University of Zurich is the largest centre for research and teaching on Asia in Switzerland. Within the IAOS, the Chair of Modern Chinese Studies (Prof. Dr. Jean Christopher Mittelstaedt) works on the ideological and institutional foundations of Chinese Communist Party governance. The Chair invites applications for two doctoral positions in the research project “Governing the Party: How the Chinese Communist Party Holds Itself Together”, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). The project “Governing the Party” (SNSF, 2027–2031) takes the Chinese Communist Party seriously as an organisation. The CCP holds that the Party “leads everything” (党是领导一切的), yet how an organisation of more than 100 million members governs itself remains poorly understood. The project uses the Party's institutions as its main analytical lens without setting its ideas aside: organisational routines and ideological work are studied together, as parts of the same form of governance. It belongs to the Chair's wider research on Party governance, which concentrates on the Party below the centre, from provincial Party committees to village branches and the institutions in which the Party is present. We welcome contemporary and historical projects on the Party since 1949, using archival, documentary, ethnographic or computational methods. The research is organised around four broad areas: Forming its people: how the Party recruits, trains, evaluates and promotes its members and cadres, and what organisational life means for them. Making and enforcing its rules: how the Party regulates itself, supervises its members and handles misconduct. Producing shared meaning: how ideology is produced, recombined and put into practice across institutions and levels. Extending its organisation: how the Party builds and runs its organisations in state organs, enterprises, universities, social organisations and other institutions. These areas are an orientation, not a list of predefined topics; what matters most is an original and feasible proposal. The Chair already hosts projects on Party organisations in private and technology firms, on the regulation of cadres' work style, and on the Party's promotion of an “autonomous knowledge system”. Proposals should address distinct questions. The SNSF project funds two doctoral candidates and one postdoctoral researcher. Several team members may work in the same area, provided their questions are distinct. Your responsibilities Develop and complete an independent doctoral dissertation within one of the project's four areas of research, under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Jean Christopher Mittelstaedt Develop, with guidance, large datasets from published Chinese-language sources for the dissertation, and contribute to the project's shared analytical framework Publish findings from the dissertation in peer-reviewed journals and contribute to co-authored outputs of the project Conduct fieldwork, archival or interview research where the dissertation requires it and conditions allow Take part in the research activities of the team and present work at conferences Enrol in a doctoral programme of the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences at the University of Zurich Assist with the organisation of workshops and with limited administrative tasks of the project Your profile An excellent MA degree (or equivalent) in political science, sociology, Chinese studies, history or a related discipline, completed by the start of employment Proficiency in modern Chinese sufficient to work independently with Chinese-language primary sources A serious interest in political institutions and organisations, and the ability to engage with theory in comparative politics, political sociology, organisation studies or the study of ideology Training in at least one of the following: qualitative or interpretive methods, quantitative methods, computational text analysis. We do not expect candidates to arrive with all of these: the willingness to acquire new methods matters more than a complete toolkit at the outset Excellent written and spoken English; German is an asset but not required The ability to work independently as well as in a team, and a commitment to a shared project over four years The University of Zurich is committed to equal opportunity and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, origin or background. Information on your application What we offer Salary in accordance with SNSF guidelines Temporary employment, 48 months The possibility of applying for an SNSF mobility grant for a research stay abroad of six to twelve months during the project Regular supervision within a small team working on a shared analytical framework Funding for fieldwork, archival research, conference travel and workshops Eligibility for SNSF supplementary measures, including flexibility grants for researchers with children Employment under the policies of the University of Zurich, with its benefits for staff (continuing education, the UZH and ETH Language Center, childcare through the kihz foundation, and others) Information on your application Please submit your application as a single PDF file through the UZH job portal. It should contain: Cover letter (max. 2 pages), stating which area of research your proposal addresses, your motivation and relevant skills, and your earliest possible start date CV Copies of your diplomas, including transcripts of records for your BA and MA degrees Research proposal (max. 3 pages, excluding bibliography) outlining how you propose to study your topic: the research question and its place within the chosen area, the sources you would use, your methods, and how the project could be completed within four years Two writing samples of max. 2,000 words each, one of them drawn from your MA thesis Names and contact details of two academic referees. Referees will be contacted only for shortlisted candidates Application deadline: 22 November 2026 Review of applications will begin after the closing date. Interviews with shortlisted candidates will be held online in the first half of December 2026, and we aim to make offers before Christmas. What we offer Work-Life Balance Flexible working models (such as part-time positions, mobile working, job-sharing) Childcare at the kihz foundation of UZH and ETH Learning and Development Wide range of continuing education courses of UZH and the Canton of Zurich Language Center run jointly with ETH Zurich Food Food and drinks at reduced prices in the UZH cafeterias Lunch-Check-card with UZH contribution Healthcare Special conditions on the Academic Sports Association ASVZ Free seasonal flu vaccinations Rest and relaxation at the quiet room in the university tower Discounts Private traffic: Carsharing, rent a vehicle, parking space Digitalization: Hardware, software, mobile phone subscriptions Conditions of Employment Policies of the UZH Most UZH staff are employed according to public law International Services Support for people from outside Switzerland Campuses Campuses Zurich City, Zurich Irchel, Oerlikon and Schlieren Sites Zurich West, Old Botanical Garden, Botanical Garden and Lengg Location Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies (IAOS), Chair of Modern Chinese Studies Rämistrasse 59, 8001 Zürich, Switzerland Further information Questions about the job Prof. Dr. Jean Christopher Mittelstaedt Chair of Modern Chinese Studies Working at UZH The University of Zurich, Switzerland's largest university, offers a range of attractive positions in various subject areas and professional fields. linkedin:4479783943.title: Doctoral Researcher in Humanoid Robotics, 3D Perception and Embodied AI
linkedin:4479783943.desc: Beschreibung Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Doctoral Researcher in Humanoid Robotics, 3D Perception and Embodied AI The Advanced Manufacturing Lab (am|z) at ETH Zurich, led by Prof. Markus Bambach, is seeking a highly motivated Doctoral Researcher to conduct research in humanoid robotics, 3D perception, and embodied artificial intelligence for autonomous manufacturing. The position is embedded in an interdisciplinary research project aiming to enable humanoid robots to perceive, understand, and interact with complex manufacturing environments using novel RGB-D sensing technologies. We are looking for a candidate with a strong background in robotics, computer vision, or machine learning who is passionate about developing intelligent robotic systems and translating scientific concepts into working solutions. The successful candidate will investigate novel approaches to robot perception, simulation-to-real transfer, and autonomous manipulation, contributing to the development of intelligent humanoid systems capable of performing complex manufacturing tasks. Project background The Advanced Manufacturing Lab at ETH Zurich investigates advanced robotic technologies for flexible, intelligent, and autonomous manufacturing. This Doctoral Researcher is part of a collaborative research project focused on developing intelligent humanoid robotic systems using next-generation, single-chip RGB-D sensing technologies. The project aims to integrate novel depth-sensing hardware with advanced perception algorithms, simulation environments, and learning-based robotic control to enable autonomous and collaborative manufacturing operations. Research Activities Span Several Interconnected Areas 3D simulation and synthetic data generation: Development of realistic manufacturing environments and simulation pipelines for generating annotated RGB-D data 3D semantic perception: Development of learning-based methods for object detection, segmentation, and scene understanding using RGB-D sensor information Sim-to-real transfer: Investigation of methods for transferring perception and manipulation capabilities from simulation to physical robotic systems Autonomous robotic manipulation: Integration of perception, planning, and control for robotic handling and assembly operations Collaborative humanoid robotics: Investigation of learning-based coordination strategies, including multi-agent reinforcement learning, for cooperative manufacturing tasks Language-guided robotic actions: Exploration of approaches that enable robots to interpret natural-language instructions and translate them into executable actions The project combines fundamental research with experimental validation using physical humanoid robotic platforms and real manufacturing scenarios. The doctoral research will focus on selected scientific challenges within these areas, with opportunities to contribute to the development of a fully integrated autonomous humanoid manufacturing demonstrator. Job Description Conduct independent scientific research in humanoid robotics, 3D perception, and learning-based robotic systems Develop and evaluate novel algorithms for RGB-D-based object detection, semantic segmentation, and 3D scene understanding Design and implement realistic robotic simulation environments and synthetic data generation pipelines for manufacturing applications Develop methods for improving the transfer of perception and manipulation capabilities from simulation to real-world robotic systems Design and implement data acquisition, annotation, processing, and evaluation workflows for synthetic and real RGB-D datasets Integrate perception algorithms with robotic manipulation, motion planning, and control frameworks Investigate learning-based approaches to autonomous robotic decision-making, with opportunities to explore multi-agent coordination and language-guided manipulation Implement, test, and validate developed methods on physical robotic and humanoid platforms Plan and conduct scientific experiments, establish quantitative benchmarks, and systematically evaluate the performance of developed methods Develop reproducible research software and contribute to shared software frameworks and experimental infrastructure Publish research findings in leading international robotics, computer vision, and machine learning conferences and journals Collaborate with researchers and industrial partners involved in the project and contribute to the supervision of student research projects Profile We are looking for a highly motivated and independent researcher with strong analytical and programming skills, scientific curiosity, and a passion for intelligent robotic systems. linkedin:4456264018.desc: Aalto University is a community of bold thinkers where science and art meet technology and business. We are committed to identifying and solving grand societal challenges and building an innovative future. Aalto has six schools with 14 000 students and a staff of 5000, of which more than 400 are professors. Our main campus is located in Espoo, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community. The Department of Computer Science is an internationally-oriented community and home to world-class research in modern computer science, combining research on foundations and innovative applications. With over 40 professors and more than 450 employees from 50 countries, it is the largest department at Aalto University and the leading computer science research unit in northern Europe. Computer science research at Aalto University ranks high in several international surveys (7th in Europe and 1st in the Nordics (NTU 2023); and 88th worldwide in Times Higher Education subject ranking 2025). We are now looking for a: Doctoral Researcher We are looking for a doctoral researcher(PhD student) with a strong background in probabilistic machine learning, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science, or a related field, and strong programming skills, to work on biology-informed machine learning for dynamical systems (see project description below). The position is based at the Department of Computer Science at Aalto University, Finland, within a research environment spanning the Computational Systems Biology group, the Finnish Centre for Artificial Intelligence (FCAI), and ELLIS Institute Finland. You will be supervised by Dr Julien Martinelli and Associate Professor Harri Lähdesmäki. The position offers a broad local research network in Bayesian machine learning and computational biology. Your network and team Dr Martinelli is an independent Research Fellow supported by an Academy Research Fellowship of the Research Council of Finland and develops Biology-Informed Machine Learning methods for biomedical applications. Associate Professor Lähdesmäki leads Aalto’s Computational Systems Biology group and has extensive expertise in Bayesian inference for biological systems. Project Description Ordinary differential equation (ODE) models provide interpretable descriptions of biological processes, but they are often incomplete: mechanisms may be only partly known, data are noisy and sparsely sampled, measurements vary across individuals and conditions, and some relevant biological states are unobserved. Purely data-driven models offer flexibility, but often ignore known biology and provide limited insight into uncertainty and mechanisms. These challenges motivate a broader Biology-Informed Machine Learning perspective [1]. The doctoral student’s thesis will focus on operationalising this perspective through the development of Biology-Informed Gaussian Processes (BioGPs). These are Bayesian dynamical models that combine known mechanistic components with flexible Gaussian process terms representing unknown or misspecified biology. Depending on the candidate’s interests, there may also be opportunities to connect this research with emerging foundation-model approaches for dynamical systems [2]. Key methodological questions shared across these directions include reliable uncertainty quantification, inference from heterogeneous trajectories, partial observability, and the integration of uncertain prior knowledge. A central goal will also be to go beyond trajectory prediction by coupling these approaches with methods for learning explicit, interpretable mechanistic ODEs, including their symbolic structure [3]. Lastly, recent work from the team includes nonparametric mixed-effect ODE models for population- and subject-specific dynamics [4], as well as GP-based approaches to modelling temporal single-cell data [5]. Selected references [1] J. Martinelli. “Position: Biology is the Challenge Physics-Informed ML Needs to Evolve”. In: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems. Vol. 38. OpenReview. 2025. [2] J. R. Hübers et al. “Foundation Inference Models for Ordinary Differential Equations”. In: Forty-third International Conference on Machine Learning. 2026. [3] C. Métayer, A. Ballesta, and J. Martinelli. “Data-driven discovery of digital twins in biomedical research”. In: Briefings in Bioinformatics 27.1 (2026), bbaf722. DOI: 10.1093/bib/bbaf722. [4] J. Martinelli et al. Bayesian Nonparametric Mixed-Effect ODEs with Gaussian Processes. 2026. arXiv: 2605.13088 [cs.LG]. [5] M. Y. Balik and H. Lähdesmäki. “Modeling Temporal scRNA-seq Data with Latent Gaussian Process and Optimal Transport”. In: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning. OpenReview. 2026. The focus of the PhD project will be the development of a physics-guided digital twin framework for magnesium alloys by integrating experimental characterization, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, precipitation modeling, and machine learning approaches to establish quantitative composition-process-structure-property relationships. Building upon recently developed machine-learning approaches for structure-property prediction in extruded magnesium alloys, the project aims to advance toward a next-generation Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework capable of predicting microstructure evolution and resulting mechanical properties across previously unseen processing conditions and material states. The candidate will work closely with interdisciplinary teams combining expertise in magnesium alloy development, thermomechanical processing, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, machine learning, and advanced experimental characterization. The objective of the project is to bridge the gap between purely data-driven materials modeling and mechanistic microstructure simulations by combining crystal plasticity, dynamic recrystallization, precipitation kinetics, and machine learning into a unified digital-twin framework. The resulting methodologies shall enable accelerated alloy and process design by leveraging experimentally validated physics-guided surrogate models with improved extrapolation capabilities beyond the limits of conventional machine-learning approaches. This work directly contributes to the digital transformation of materials development and manufacturing technologies for future lightweight engineering applications. linkedin:4479805921.desc: Vill du vara med och bidra till framtidens autonoma system som överträffar människors förmågor? Du kommer att tillhöra forskningsämnet maskinkonstruktion på avdelning produkt- och produktionsutveckling som tillhör institutionen för teknikvetenskap och matematik. Här bedrivs forskning inom produktutveckling, simuleringsdriven konstruktion, automation av arbetsmaskiner samt modellering & simulering. Forskargruppen består av fyra seniorer samt sex doktorander och har tillgång till relevant forskningsinfrastruktur. Forskargruppen samverkar även med andra universitet, institut och företag både nationellt och internationellt. Ämnesbeskrivning Maskinkonstruktion omfattar, för tekniska system, simuleringsdriven produktutveckling, modellering och simulering, produktutvecklingsmetodik samt produktinformationshantering. Modeller, metoder, processer och verktyg för utveckling av produkter är centrala för ämnet. Projektbeskrivning Doktorandprojektet syftar till att utveckla metoder och en modulär systemarkitektur för säker samverkan mellan autonoma terränggående arbetsmaskiner. Forskningen omfattar hur övergripande uppdrag kan brytas ned till prioriterade och samordnade maskinuppgifter, exempelvis navigering, materialhantering och inspektion. Särskilt fokus läggs på hur uppgifter kan omplaneras när omgivningen, maskinernas tillstånd eller kommunikationsförutsättningarna förändras. Projektet ska även utveckla säkerhetsfunktioner som upptäcker människor, hinder, kollisionsrisker och systemfel samt aktiverar lämpliga åtgärder, såsom omplanering, hastighetsbegränsning eller säkert stopp. Metoderna integreras i en gemensam arkitektur för planering, perception, styrning, kommunikation och säkerhet. Resultaten ska bidra till användbara metoder för kostnadseffektiv utveckling och validering av robusta, säkra och samverkande autonoma arbetsmaskiner. Arbetsuppgifter En doktorandtjänst innebär både teoretiskt och praktiskt arbete. Som doktorand tränas du i vetenskapligt arbete i form av publicering av vetenskapliga artiklar i tidskrifter och vid nationella och internationella konferenser. Du läser även obligatoriska och frivilliga doktorandkurser. Dessutom kan du få möjlighet att prova på lärarrollen. Som forskare arbetar du som en neutral part i många sammanhang vilket ger en fantastisk möjlighet att lära sig att driva utmanande utvecklingsprojekt. Arbetet kommer mer specifikt att innefatta utveckling av olika autonoma dellösningar (framförallt mjukvarumässiga) som implementeras, testas och demonstreras med hjälp av terrängfordonsforskningsplattformen AORO.
