linkedin:4479811873.title: PhD Student in Machine Design
linkedin:4479811873.desc: Would you like to contribute to the autonomous systems of the future—systems capable of exceeding human capabilities? You will join the research subject Machine Design at the Division of Product and Production Development, which is part of the Department of Engineering Sciences and Mathematics. Our research covers product development, simulation-driven design, automation of mobile machinery and modelling and simulation. The research group consists of four senior researchers and six PhD students and has access to relevant research infrastructure. The group also collaborates with universities, research institutes and companies, both nationally and internationally. Subject Description Machine Design encompasses, for engineering systems, simulation-driven product development, modelling and simulation, product development methodology and product information management. Models, methods, processes and tools for developing products are important for the research subject. Project Description The PhD project aims to develop methods and a modular system architecture for safe collaboration between autonomous off-road mobile machines. The research will investigate how high-level missions can be decomposed into prioritised and coordinated machine tasks, such as navigation, material handling and inspection. Particular attention will be given to replanning tasks when environmental conditions, machine states or communication conditions change. The project will also develop safety functions that detect people, obstacles, collision risks and system faults, and initiate appropriate responses such as replanning, speed reduction or a safe stop. The methods will be integrated into a common architecture for planning, perception, control, communication and safety. The results will contribute to practical methods for the cost-effective development and validation of robust, safe and collaborative autonomous mobile machinery. Duties A PhD position involves both theoretical and practical work. As a PhD student, you will receive training in scientific research, including publishing articles in scientific journals and presenting your work at national and international conferences. You will also take compulsory and elective doctoral courses and may have the opportunity to gain teaching experience. As a researcher, you will act as an independent party in many contexts, providing an excellent opportunity to learn how to manage challenging development projects. More specifically, the work will include developing autonomous subsystems, primarily software-based solutions, that will be implemented, tested and demonstrated using the AORO off-road vehicle research platform. Qualifications Applicants must hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in mechanical engineering, robotics, production engineering or a related field. You should have a strong interest in, curiosity about and passion for research. We attach considerable importance to personal qualities and individual suitability. Experience in kinematics, dynamics, programming, safety and CAD modelling is considered an asset. Knowledge of AI-assisted automation is particularly advantageous. Applicants must be proficient in spoken and written English. As teaching is conducted within Machine Design, experience in CAD is also considered an asset. The evaluation of candidates will take into account Luleå University of Technology’s employee policy and gender-equality objectives. For further information about doctoral studies in Machine Design, please see the general syllabus for third-cycle studies at the Faculty of Science and Technology. Further information The PhD position is a fixed-term, four-year appointment. Teaching and other departmental duties may be added, corresponding to no more than 20% of full-time employment. The position is based in Luleå, and the intended starting date is subject to agreement. linkedin:4479717292.title: PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN- NL
linkedin:4479717292.desc: The Faculty of Science and Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for candidates for a PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN ANA-KIN is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme. Over the past two decades, small-molecule kinase inhibitors have transformed cancer therapy, yet nearly all of them target the highly conserved ATP-binding site, which limits selectivity and allows resistance to emerge. ANA-KIN aims to train a new generation of interdisciplinary researchers capable of redefining kinase drug discovery beyond the ATP paradigm, by developing the experimental and computational tools, modular assays and workflows needed to systematically target non-conserved regulatory interfaces, such as kinase dimerization and substrate-binding sites. Proof-of-concept will be demonstrated on three representative kinases: EGFR, BRAF and the understudied “dark” kinase LTK. ANA-KIN brings together 11 beneficiaries and 9 associated partners across Europe and the USA, including Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (coordinator), University of Crete, Goethe University Frankfurt, Saarland University, EPFL, CNRS, Pompeu Fabra University, VIB, KU Leuven, INSERM and Leiden University, together with industrial partners such as AstraZeneca, Novartis, Servier and Skylight Therapeutics. The network combines chemical biology, structural biophysics (single-molecule FRET, cryo-EM, nanodiscs), AI-driven drug design and cell biology in an integrated learn–design–test loop. Twelve Doctoral Candidates (DCs) will each pursue an individual research project, benefit from co-supervision across institutions and sectors, carry out two research secondments at partner organizations, and follow a structured network-wide training program covering scientific, transferable, open-science and entrepreneurial skills. In this PhD project (DC10, Work Package 3 – Discovery), you will develop deep-learning architectures that integrate text-mined, cheminformatic, and biophysical descriptors to predict interface binding, allosteric signatures and resistance liabilities of kinase ligands. The models will learn jointly across peptide and small-molecule modalities and will be used to generate hybrid peptidomimetic design hypotheses. You will translate these models into consortium-wide prioritisation dashboards that support hit triage and analogue selection in the discovery campaigns of ANA-KIN, and work in close reciprocal feedback with DC9 (Saarland University) on structure-based and machine-learning pipelines. Model predictions will be validated prospectively with the experimental partners in the network. The expected results are a resistance-aware AI workflow for non-ATP interface ligands, accompanied by public models, datasets and interpretable feature maps, and prospective design case studies demonstrating improved optimisation trajectories. To reinforce structural grounding and experimental validation, you will carry out two secondments: at VIB (Belgium, Prof. Ruslan Efremov; 4 months) to extract structural classes and conformational features from cryo-EM data and use them to refine model constraints, and at Skylight Therapeutics (Belgium, Dr. Joshua Salafsky; 3 months) to test model predictions using second-harmonic generation (SHG)-based conformational profiling. The project will be supervised by Prof. Gerard J.P. van Westen (Leiden University), with Prof. Ruslan Efremov and Dr. Joshua Salafsky as co-supervisors. What You Will Do Conduct original and novel research in deep learning, AI, and cheminformatics for kinase drug discovery; Develop, benchmark and openly share models, datasets and decision-support dashboards following FAIR and open-science principles; Collaborate closely with experimental and computational DCs in the network, and carry out two research secondments abroad (VIB and Skylight Therapeutics, Belgium); Publish and present scientific articles at international journals and conferences; Participate in the ANA-KIN network-wide training events, schools and outreach activities; Contribute to educational activities; Write a dissertation. What You Bring A MSc degree in Computer Science, AI, (Computational) Chemistry, Bioinformatics, Biopharmaceutical Sciences, or a relevant related field; Good knowledge of and experience with machine learning and deep-learning techniques (e.g. PyTorch); Good knowledge of and experience with cheminformatics and/or computational chemistry (e.g. RDKit, molecular descriptors, docking); Interest in structural biology, protein kinases and drug discovery; affinity with peptide or biophysical data is an advantage; Highly motivated to both perform foundational research and apply the developed methods to real-world problems; creative, ‘making things work’ mentality, independent, and communicative team player; Willingness to travel and to carry out research secondments at partner institutions abroad; Excellent programming skills (preferably Python); Good academic writing skills and interest in participating in educational activities; Excellent proficiency in English (oral and written). MSCA eligibility criteria At the date of recruitment, candidates must not have been awarded a doctoral degree; Mobility rule: candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the date of recruitment. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status are not taken into account. Where you will work Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research Our institute is a center of excellence for multidisciplinary research on drug discovery and development. Leiden University consistently ranks within the top-20 world-wide within the subject-based QS Ranking in Pharmacology and Pharmacy. At LACDR, we develop innovative scientific concepts in fundamental and translational research underlying the discovery and optimization of drugs, and personalized medicines. We aim to optimize the route to novel drugs that are both efficacious and safe, and therefore our research focuses on drug discovery and safety, bio-therapeutics, and systems biomedicine and pharmacology. State-of-the-art expertise and infrastructures ensure that we are strategically positioned in (inter)national collaborations, thus further strengthening the development of novel concepts and their application in a clinical and industry environment. Computational Drug Discovery Research in this group, headed by Gerard van Westen, focusses on computational methods integrated in different parts of the drug discovery process. More specifically, topics include innovative treatments for cancer, kinase and GPCR drug discovery, proteochemometrics, selectivity and polypharmacology modeling, allosteric modulation, drug resistance modeling, de novo molecular design, and novel methods in the domain of machine learning. For more information see: http://www.cddl.nl Research at our faculty The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from artificial intelligence, computer science, mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,700 staff and almost 6,000 students. We are located in the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry meet. For more information, see http://www.science.leidenuniv.nl. What We Offer We offer a full-time appointment for 48 months as a Doctoral Candidate within the MSCA Doctoral Network ANA-KIN, starting late 2026. The appointment is initially for one year; after a positive evaluation of the progress of the research, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended for the remaining period. Salary ranges from € 3.204,- tot € 4.051,- gross per month (pay scale P in accordance with the Collective Labor Agreement for Dutch Universities). Leiden University offers an attractive benefits package with additional holiday (8%) and end-of-year bonuses (8.3%), training and career development. Our individual choices model gives you some freedom to assemble your own set of terms and conditions. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break. All our PhD students are embedded in the Leiden University Graduate School of Science. Our graduate school offers several PhD training courses at three levels: professional courses, skills training and personal effectiveness. In addition, advanced courses to deepen scientific knowledge are offered by the research school. As an ANA-KIN Doctoral Candidate you will also follow the network’s training program, including summer schools, workshops and an industrial immersion workshop, and your progress will be monitored by a Thesis Advisory Committee including an independent mentor. What We Value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Inquiries about the research area can be made to Prof. Gerard van Westen, gerard@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. If you have any questions about the procedure, please contact Brigitte Kraakman, b.p.m.kraakman@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. To apply for this vacancy, please submit your application online via the blue button below. Please ensure that you upload the following additional documents quoting the vacancy number and “ANA-KIN DC10”: application letter (including a statement confirming that they meet the MSCA eligibility criteria) curriculum vitae a list of grades two references (who have agreed to be contacted) Only applications received no later than November 12th can be considered. The selection procedure will take place in November. Selected candidates may be invited for an interview in the last week of November / 1st week of December, during which you are kindly requested to be available. Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. If you nevertheless choose to send us CVs, no rights can be derived from this.

linkedin:4478871053.title: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’
linkedin:4478871053.desc: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’ 1,0 FTE position for 4 years. The PhD candidate will be appointed for a period of 15 months. The appointment will be extended to 4 years when progress and performance are good. A PhD training program is part of the agreement. Vacancy number: FAC/BW/26087 The Project Can you help make energy data usable without giving away sensitive information? The energy transition in the Netherlands urgently requires upgrading of the electricity grid, for instance to accommodate solar panels, wind turbines, and electric vehicles. To efficiently plan and manage these upgrades, stakeholders such as grid operators, municipalities and energy communities need to share detailed data about electricity consumption, generation and grid operation. This data sharing however is prevented by concerns on the competitively sensitive nature and privacy of data, as it reveals detailed information about households, buildings and operational assets. Synthetic data generated by generative AI-models offers a promising alternative, but preserving statistical, temporal, and physical characteristics of real energy data while protecting sensitive information are major challenges. We are offering a PhD position in the SHARE project that addresses these challenges. Research challenges As a PhD candidate, you will develop methods for adaptive privacy protection of energy data , combining differential privacy, empirical privacy attacks and privacy–utility optimisation. Your research is part of the Adaptive Privacy and Legal Compliance work package in the SHARE project. More specifically, your challenges are to: Investigate how temporal patterns, spatial information, rare events and other distinctive features contribute to re-identification and inference risk. You will work with metrics such as uniqueness, entropy, attack success rates and time-series-specific indicators. Implement and study attacks such as membership inference, reconstruction, re-identification and attribute inference to understand where information leakage occurs in both original and synthetic datasets. Investigate methods that allocate stronger protection to sensitive components and lighter perturbation to lower-risk components, thereby preserving as much analytical utility as possible. Formulate privacy protection as an optimisation problem balancing formal privacy guarantees against statistical, temporal and physical utility requirements for energy-system applications. Collaborate closely with researchers at Radboud University, who develop physics-informed generative models for synthetic energy data, and investigate approaches such as differentially private training and post-generation privacy calibration. Work closely with distribution system operator Alliander and other consortium partners to evaluate whether the developed methods provide meaningful protection while retaining the information required for practical energy-system applications. Ultimately contribute to an open-source privacy layer for the SHARE toolbox. Requirements You hold, or will soon obtain, an MSc degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related discipline. You should have: a strong background in privacy-enhancing technologies, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity or statistical modelling; strong programming skills, particularly in Python; preferably, some familiarity with deep generative models (VAEs, GANs, diffusion models) and probabilistic modelling; good written and spoken English skills; knowledge of Dutch language preferred not mandatory. Salary The salary is determined in accordance with salary scale P of Appendix A of the Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities and ranges from € 3.204,-- gross per month upon commencement to € 4.051,-- gross per month in the fourth and final year, in case of full employment. The Open Universiteit provides good secondary benefits such as training, mobility, part-time employment and paid parental leave. Station The position is officially based in Heerlen. As part of the PhD project, you will mainly work at Radboud University in Nijmegen, where you will collaborate closely with the other researchers in the SHARE project. This setup enables close day-to-day collaboration with researchers working on machine learning, synthetic data and energy systems. You will be employed by Open Universiteit and supervised by Dr. Mina Alishahi as your primary supervisor, with Prof. dr. ir. Harald Vranken as co-supervisor. Information For more information about this vacancy you can contact: harald.vranken@ou.nl. Procedure Please apply to this position by sending an email to solliciteren@ou.nl, stating the vacancy number and including: your CV; a motivation letter; your MSc thesis or another representative piece of academic work, if available; contact details of two references. In your motivation letter, please briefly address the following three questions: Why are you interested in privacy-preserving machine learning and, in particular, this PhD project? Describe a research, thesis or programming project in which you worked with machine learning, privacy, cybersecurity, generative models or complex data. What was your own contribution? Provide a one-paragraph description of your MSc thesis, written for a reader outside your field. You will preferably start your employment on January 1st, 2027. Closing date: November 1st, 2026 Working at the Open University Working at the Open University means contributing to academic education for the most motivated students in the Netherlands and Flanders, as well as to scientific research with visible impact for people and society. With a broad range of bachelor’s and master’s programmes and short courses, the Open University makes lifelong learning accessible to everyone. There are no prior education requirements for bachelor’s programmes: anyone aged eighteen or older can enrol. Education is hybrid and flexible, available anytime and anywhere, at a pace that suits the student. The majority of the nearly 16,000 students combine their studies with work. This creates a valuable interaction: experiences and questions from professional practice enrich education and research and increase their societal relevance. It is therefore no coincidence that the Open University has ranked in the top three of the Dutch Keuzegids for universities for many years, and this year holds the number one position. In research, the university focuses on three central themes: healthcare, digitalisation and AI, and society and citizenship. Solutions to today’s challenges are sought across disciplinary boundaries and in collaboration with partners. The Open University employs approximately 800 staff members, has its main campus in Heerlen, and operates study centres in the Netherlands and Flanders. Its culture is people-centred, collaborative, and inclusive: an environment in which students, staff, and partners feel connected, with ample opportunities for personal development and a healthy work–life balance. Department of Computer Science You will be appointed within the Department of Computer Science of the Faculty of Science. The department’s research program “Towards high-quality and intelligent software” (2020–2025) consists of four research lines, focusing on: Techniques for quality assurance of software systems Software and computer system security, and privacy-by-design Responsible artificial intelligence, including methods and applications of AI Educational tools and computing education.

It is funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research (SSF) under a programme building research ties between Sweden and Taiwan, including opportunities for research visits among the participants. About Us RISE Research Institutes of Sweden AB is Sweden's research institute and innovation partner. In international collaboration with companies, academia, and the public sector, we contribute to a competitive business sector and a sustainable society. You will be part of the Cybersecurity unit at the department of Computer Science which is one of the largest technical cybersecurity groups in Sweden, conducting cutting-edge research on both fundamental and applied cybersecurity topics arising in AI, 6G, Internet of Things, etc. About The Role We are looking for a dedicated PhD student to strengthen our research in trustworthy multi-agent AI systems. Example research topics include evaluating the robustness of multi-agent systems under adversarial manipulation, designing secure and privacy-preserving multi-agent collaborative mechanisms, and verifiable decision-making under uncertainty and adversarial influence. You will be based in the RISE office at Kista, Stockholm for 4 years, and you will be enrolled as a doctoral student at a Swedish University. PhD education also involves participation in relevant university courses. Who are you? linkedin:4443351953.desc: Chez STMicroelectronics, nous sommes convaincus que la technologie est un moteur d’innovation et a un impact positif pour les entreprises, les personnes et la société. Bonnes capacités scientifiques (esprit critique, lecture d’articles) et compétences en programmation/outils numériques. Les résultats attendus de cette recherche sont la conception, le développement et la compréhension des performances des nouvelles architectures des qubits et de SET intégrant des matériaux avancés, capables de satisfaire les exigences du calcul quantique. Contact: carlos-augusto.suarezsegovia@st.com ST est fière d’être certifiée parmi les 17 entreprises mondiales « Global Top Employers 2025 » et d’être la première et unique entreprise de semi-conducteurs à recevoir cette distinction. linkedin:4473008608.title: PhD Position Sustainable Generative AI for Digital Sovereignty
linkedin:4473008608.desc: Join us for this PhD project in EU Horizon €8 million initiative, to transform how generative AI is deployed across Europe for a more sustainable, sovereign and resilient future. Job Description Generative AI is widely expected to become a central element of digital transformation. Its flexibility and adaptability give businesses in many sectors an opportunity to innovate rapidly, respond to changing conditions, and lower barriers to automation. For society to benefit from these advancements, organisations need to maintain control over sensitive information and critical decision-making tools. Reducing dependence on external providers strengthens digital autonomy, while more efficient ways of running AI help align technological progress with environmental and energy targets. By designing systems that are sustainable, sovereign, secure, and efficient at the same time, this PhD project will support Europe’s broader ambitions for responsible technological leadership. Position Overview: This PhD position is aimed at candidates with a Master’s degree in computer science/engineering, AI, data science, or related fields, with a strong interest in generative AI. The successful candidate will be based at the Department of Engineering Systems and Services (ESS) at Delft University of Technology under the supervision of Dr. Aaron Ding, Dr. Marcela Tuler de Oliveira, Prof. Dr. Marijn Janssen. This PhD project involves close collaboration with partners from the EU Horizon project, and candidates will have the opportunity to engage with interdisciplinary teams involved in the project. Key Responsibilities: To conduct an in-depth evaluation of existing foundation models to assess their suitability in the digital industries, automotive and healthcare domains. Design sustainable inference strategies and framework towards the computing continuum. Collaborate with experts from the f-inference consortium to design, develop, test and refine the design strategies and framework. Work independently and contribute collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team environment. Project Impact: This project will democratise the access to advanced Generative AI technologies through practical tools that help businesses, particularly SMEs, adopt state-of-the-art AI models. The outcomes are expected to enhance competitiveness, support sustainable innovation, and contribute to a more inclusive digital transition across Europe. Job Requirements MSc in computer science/engineering, AI, data science, or related fields. Strong analytical skills A strong interest in interdisciplinary research, and the use of AI in inter-oranisational context Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a dynamic, multidisciplinary environment. Excellent command of English TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Technology, Policy & Management The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information For more information about this vacancy, please contact Aaron Ding (aaron.ding@tudelft.nl). For more information about the application procedure, please contact Olivie Beek, HR-advisor (recruitment-tbm@tudelft.nl). Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 1 November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: your CV motivation letter official list of all courses followed during your BSc and MSc studies with grades your MSc thesis If the applicants are selected for an interview, they will be asked to provide contact details of two referees with their consent. The start date is flexible, but foreseen for summer/fall 2026. Screening starts as applications come in. You can address your application to Aaron Ding. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

linkedin:4479827428.title: CRUK Black Leaders in Cancer PhD Scholarship
linkedin:4479827428.desc: 🎓 PhD Opportunity | Artificial Intelligence in Childhood Leukaemia Research 🔬 Interested in using AI and data science to advance childhood cancer research? The Leukaemia Research Cytogenomics Group (LRCG) at Newcastle University is recruiting a PhD student through the Cancer Research UK (CRUK) Black Leaders in Cancer PhD Scholarship Programme, with applications now open for the 2027 intake. This exciting project will focus on developing and evaluating trustworthy synthetic healthcare data using statistical methods, machine learning and generative AI, drawing on a national dataset of more than 20,000 childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) patients. The research aims to support more robust, reproducible and privacy-conscious approaches to childhood leukaemia research, with the potential to improve our understanding of treatment pathways and patient outcomes. 🔬 Project focus: Developing and comparing statistical, machine-learning and generative AI approaches to synthetic healthcare data generation. Evaluating the preservation of clinically important patterns, treatment pathways and outcomes, including rare events such as relapse. Assessing data utility, privacy, fidelity, fairness and clinical validity. Exploring the use of synthetic data for methodological research, hypothesis generation and reproducible analysis. 🌍 What the scholarship offers: Fully funded 4-year PhD, including stipend and tuition fees (Home fee status). Mentoring and leadership development opportunities. Networking through Black in Cancer and the Windsor Fellowship. A supportive and diverse research environment. Opportunities for research placements and community engagement. 👩‍💻 Who should apply? We welcome applicants with backgrounds in statistics, data science, biostatistics, epidemiology, computer science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related quantitative disciplines. As part of the CRUK Black Leaders in Cancer Programme, we particularly encourage applications from talented Black students who are passionate about advancing cancer research and addressing inequalities in healthcare. 📍 Location: Newcastle University, UK 👨‍🏫 Primary Supervisor: Dr. Amir Enshaei 📅 Application deadline: 4 December 2026 🎓 Start: 2027 intake 🔗 Find out more and apply: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/cancer/training/studentships/cruk-black-leaders-phd/ For informal enquiries, please contact Amir Enshaei (Primary Supervisor). Join us in advancing AI-driven research to improve outcomes for children with leukaemia! #PhDOpportunity #PhDStudentship #BlackLeadersInCancer #CancerResearch #ArtificialIntelligence #MachineLearning #DataScience #ChildhoodLeukaemia #SyntheticData #NewcastleUniversity

linkedin:4479714389.title: Doktorandplats - statistiker inom tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården
linkedin:4479714389.desc: Vid Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS) bedrivs världsledande forskning inom åldrande, demens, epidemiologi och vårdvetenskap. Forskningen sträcker sig från grundforskning på molekyl- och cellnivå till kliniska studier och forskning på samhällsnivå. Vid NVS genomför cirka en tredjedel av KI:s studenter sin utbildning på grund- och avancerad nivå. Institutionen med cirka 540 anställda och en omsättning på 530 miljoner miljoner år 2023, består av sju avdelningar och finns på Campus Flemingsberg och Campus Solna. Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård ansvarar för delar av läkarprogrammet. Inom forskarutbildning har vi en egen forskarskola i allmänmedicin. Vår primärvårdsforskning omfattar varierande projekt kring multisjuklighet, folksjukdomar som diabetes, nedsatt njurfunktion och psykisk ohälsa samt även pedagogiska projekt. Närmare 100 personer, av vilka cirka 30 doktorander, är anknutna till avdelningen. Vill du bidra till medicinsk forskning av toppkvalitet? Att vara doktorand innebär att vara antagen till en utbildning på forskarnivå (forskarutbildning) där man följer en individuell studieplan. En doktorand ägnar sig åt ett forskningsprojekt under handledning, kompletterat med kurser och andra lärandeaktiviteter. För en doktorsexamen krävs motsvarande fyra års utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid. Forskargruppen Doktorandtjänsten finns inom forskargruppen för STEADY-CAN (Stockholm Early Detection of Cancer Study) vid Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård, Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS). Gruppen består av kliniskt aktiva forskare, statistiker och doktorander som arbetar med tidig upptäckt av cancer, i nära samarbete med Regionalt cancercentrum Stockholm-Gotland och internationella samarbetspartners. Gruppen är involverad i flera pågående forskningsprojekt, inklusive utveckling av statistiska och maskininlärningsbaserade prediktionsmodeller, longitudinell analys av blodprovsdata och registerbaserade kohortstudier inom cancerepidemiologi. Du kommer att ingå i en tvärvetenskaplig grupp där statistiker, allmänläkare och epidemiologer arbetar nära varandra. I praktiken innebär det att du regelbundet diskuterar analysval med kliniker, förklarar statistiska metoder för personer utan statistisk bakgrund och själv lär dig om den kliniska vardagen i primärvården. Gruppen har regelbundna gemensamma analysmöten där du förväntas både ge och ta emot återkoppling på pågående arbete. Doktorandprojektet och doktorandens uppgifter Detta doktorandprojekt kombinerar traditionell statistisk modellering och maskininlärning i tillämpad forskning kring tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården. Projektet använder data från STEADY-CAN-kohorten, som omfattar över 2,7 miljoner vuxna i Region Stockholm med länkade laboratorie-, journal- och registerdata. Under doktorandutbildningen kommer kandidaten att få bred kunskap inom överlevnadsanalys, prediktionsmodellering, maskininlärning och hantering av stora registerbaserade datamängder. Vi söker en motiverad doktorand med god bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. Den framgångsrika kandidaten förväntas ta ett stort eget ansvar genom hela projektet, med stöd från handledarna. Detta innebär konstruktion av analysdatamängder, statistisk analys och implementering av maskininlärningsmetoder, författande av vetenskapliga artiklar samt deltagande i institutionens seminarier och i nationella och internationella konferenser. Vad erbjuder vi? En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. På KI får du träffa forskare med olika forskningsinriktningar som jobbar tillsammans. Det är det gränsöverskridande samarbetet som bidrar till KI:s världsledande position inom forskning. Som doktorand erbjuds du ett individuellt forskningsprojekt, en välutbildad handledare, ett stort utbud av valbara kurser och möjligheten att arbeta i en framgångsrik forskargrupp. Karolinska Institutet har samarbeten med framstående universitet över hela världen, vilket ger möjlighet till internationella utbyten. Som anställd doktorand får du en avtalsenlig lön, du får träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar och du får ersättning för läkarvård. Behörighetskrav för utbildning på forskarnivå För att delta i urvalet till en doktorandplats måste du styrka både det grundläggande (A) och det särskilda (B) behörighetskravet innan ansökningsperioden stänger. Det är ditt ansvar som sökande att styrka din behörighet genom att följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. A) Grundläggande behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det grundläggande behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: har avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå (magister- eller masterexamen), eller har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller har på annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.* Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. *Om du anser dig ha motsvarande kunskaper ska du följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Bedömning av motsvarande kunskaper för grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. B) Särskilt behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det särskilda behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: - Intygar kunskaper i engelska (motsvarande Engelska B/Engelska 6 vid gymnasiet med godkänt betyg). Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan English language requirements for doctoral education. Kontroll av dokument Karolinska Institutet gör kontroll av dokumenten för att upptäcka förfalskningar. Karolinska Institutet förbehåller sig rätten att återkalla antagningsbeslut om förfalskningar eller oriktigheter påvisas. Inlämnande av falska handlingar är ett brott mot svensk lag och anses vara grund för rättsliga åtgärder. Färdigheter och personliga egenskaper Den sökande bör ha en gedigen bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. En examen i statistik/biostatistik eller matematisk statistik på avancerad nivå, t.ex. en masterexamen, är starkt meriterande. Utmärkta kunskaper i biostatistik och praktisk erfarenhet av överlevnadsanalys är meriterande. Tidigare erfarenhet av databehandling och statistisk analys är meriterande. Dessa erfarenheter ska företrädesvis vara från en medicinsk forskningsmiljö. Mycket goda kunskaper i statistisk programmering, företrädesvis i R, är avgörande för rollen. Erfarenhet av arbete med svenska registerdata är meriterande. Ett starkt intresse för medicinsk forskning i kombination med en passion för att tillämpa statistiska metoder för att besvara kliniskt relevanta forskningsfrågor är mycket önskvärt. Då STEADY-CAN-databasen, inklusive journal- och registervariabler och tillhörande beskrivningar, är på svenska är goda kunskaper i svenska i tal och skrift ett krav. Handledningen och det internationella samarbetet sker delvis på engelska, varför goda kunskaper även i engelska i tal och skrift också krävs. Den sökande ska ha god kommunikationsförmåga, vilket är avgörande för att samarbeta med tvärvetenskapliga team och effektivt presentera forskningsresultat. Vi lägger mycket stor vikt vid personliga egenskaper i denna rekrytering. Den idealiska kandidaten bör vara: Självständig, strukturerad och med stark analytisk förmåga. Flexibel och ivrig att lära. Denna roll innebär kontinuerligt lärande och anpassning till nya metoder och utmaningar. Öppen för konstruktiva synpunkter och förmåga att delta i balanserad, analytisk självreflektion. Kandidaten ska även trivas med att arbeta i team och samarbeta väl med teammedlemmar med olika akademisk bakgrund. Förklara i ditt personliga brev hur du uppfyller de nödvändiga färdigheterna och egenskaperna. Villkor Doktorandplatsen innebär en anställning som doktorand under maximalt 4 år på heltid. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen i rekryteringsverktyget Varbi. Använd knappen uppe till höger och följ anvisningarna. Vi ser gärna att din ansökan är skriven på engelska, men det går också bra att ansöka på svenska. Din ansökan ska innehålla dessa dokument: - Ett personligt brev och curriculum vitae - Eventuella examensarbeten och publikationer - Andra dokument som styrker de ovan efterfrågade färdigheter och egenskaper - Dokument som styrker det grundläggande behörighetskravet (se A ovan) - Dokument som styrker det särskilda behörighetskravet (se B ovan) Urval Urval bland behöriga sökande görs med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig forskarutbildning. En samlad bedömning av de sökandes meriter och lämplighet kommer att göras. Följande bedömningsgrunder tillämpas vid Karolinska Institutet: - Dokumenterade ämneskunskaper av betydelse för forskningsområdet - Analytisk skicklighet - Övriga dokumenterade kunskaper/erfarenheter som kan ha betydelse för aktuell forskarutbildning Alla sökanden kommer att få information när rekryteringen är slutförd. linkedin:4479154787.desc: Tecnun - Escuela de Ingeniería-Universidad de Navarra Tecnun-Escuela de Ingeniería , perteneciente a la Universidad de Navarra , se propone contribuir a la formación profesional, científica y humana de los futuros ingenieros. Desde su creación, en la primavera de 1961, mantiene un equilibrio entre la docencia, la investigación y el servicio a la sociedad, haciendo que estas actividades se complementen entre sí. Actualmente dispone de dos campus : la sede más antigua, ubicada en el campus universitario del Bº de Ibaeta, está integrada por los edificios de laboratorios, el edificio docente y de representación concluido en 1989, y un edificio multiuso, levantado en 1996. La otra sede se encuentra en el Parque Tecnológico de Miramón e integra las aulas y laboratorios de investigación de las áreas de Electricidad, Electrónica y Comunicaciones. Descripción de la oferta Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About The Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main Duties And Responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Requisitos Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants Should Submit a Dossier Including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About The University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián. indeed:b4d5926c58f63991.desc: The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI. The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions. Project description The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment. The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team. Description of the scientific environment The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ . This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk ) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk ) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam Who are we looking for? Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems. The PhD programme You can undertake the PhD programme as: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree. Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme Qualifications needed for the regular programme To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria: You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; You must work on the project full-time. Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality. Terms of employment in the regular programme Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years. Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network Disseminate research nationally and internationally Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project We are looking for the following qualifications: Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position Relevant educational background Relevant publications Relevant work experience Other relevant professional activities Good written and oral English language skills Application and Assessment Procedure Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. Please include : Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications ; Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; Publication list (if available); Names and contact details of three references. Application deadline: The deadline for applications is November 22 , 23:59 GMT +1 . We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements. The further process After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment. The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/. Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December Questions For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/. The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position. Vi søger svar og løsninger på fælles problemer og gør ny viden tilgængelig og nyttig for andre. indeed:70994ae299f9146b.title: Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology at the University of Oulu (Finland)
indeed:70994ae299f9146b.desc: The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are currently looking for a Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology to join research projects focusing on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), teacher education, and teachers’ professional development at the Faculty of Education and Psychology at the University of Oulu, Finland. The position is connected to two research projects: INTEGRATE – Training Teachers to Integrate EU Matters through GenAI-Supported Pedagogy and The Power of Teachers' Online Mentorship for AI Partnership (Power T/A) . The INTEGRATE project, funded by the Erasmus+ Programme under the Jean Monnet Teacher Training action, aims to empower pre-service and in-service teachers to integrate EU topics and values into everyday teaching through GenAI-supported pedagogy. The project develops and implements teacher education courses, online professional development modules, instructional materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities. The Power T/A project, funded by the Research Council of Finland, explores the integration of AI-based technologies into teacher mentorship and instructional activities. The project focuses on how AI technologies can support teachers’ professional development, particularly through online mentorship, and how teachers can develop the knowledge and skills needed for meaningful AI integration in education. About the job As a doctoral researcher, you will: Conduct doctoral research within the INTEGRATE (75%) and Power T/A (25%) projects, with a focus on GenAI, teacher education, and teachers’ professional learning. Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of GenAI-supported teacher education and professional development activities . Participate in the development and implementation of courses, online professional development modules, case-based learning materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities for teachers. Collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative research data related to the implementation and evaluation of project activities. Contribute to scientific publications and other research outputs arising from the projects. Collaborate with teachers, teacher educators, researchers, and national and international project partners. Present research findings at scientific conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results. In this role, you will become part of a dynamic and supportive research environment focusing on educational technology, teacher education, and the pedagogically meaningful and responsible use of artificial intelligence. Qualifications To succeed in the position, we expect from you: A Master’s degree in education, educational technology, educational psychology, or another relevant discipline. A strong interest in research on Generative AI, educational technology, teacher education, and EU matters and values. Proficiency in qualitative and/or quantitative research methods and the ability to apply these methods in educational research. Good IT and data analysis skills and an interest in using digital and AI-based tools in educational research. Fluent written and spoken English. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary and international research environments. Additional merits considered an advantage Familiarity with the Finnish K–12 education system and/or teacher education . Experience working with pre-service or in-service teachers . Experience in teaching, teacher education, professional development, or instructional design . Experience or demonstrated interest in AI/GenAI-supported teaching and learning . Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research data collection and analysis. Familiarity with technology-enhanced learning environments. Finnish language skills (not required but considered as an advantage). What we offer? The support of an experienced and enthusiastic project team of where you can share your expertise and grow as an expert. Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits. Development and career options of the big organization. Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us. Our Buddy Programme and Spouse Network support you and close-ones in settling into Oulu. We have a HR Excellence in Research -quality label which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers. Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, excellent education system, and competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu. Salary The position is fixed-term for three years as soon as possible or starting from January 2027. The salary will be based on the levels 2-4 of the demand level chart for teaching and research staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance will be paid (maximum of 50% of the job-specific component). Starting gross salary will be approx. 2300-2600 € per month (before taxes). A trial period of 6 months is applied in the position. How to apply? Interested? If yes, please apply by 15.11.2026 (23:59 Finnish local time) through our recruitment system. The application should be written in English and include the following: Cover letter CV following the guidelines of the Finnish Advisory Board on Research Integrity Certificates/Diplomas Contact information of two persons available for recommendation The eligible applicants fitting best in the profile expected for the position will be invited to an on-site or remote interview. All applicants will be notified during the selection process. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, such as people of different ages, genders and lingual, cultural or minority groups. Contact Information If you have any further questions, please contact D r. indeed:571be3fb97a6761d.title: Doctorat (H/F) en Web Sémantique et Intelligence Artificielle
indeed:571be3fb97a6761d.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Laboratoire d'Informatique, Signaux et Systèmes de Sophia Antipolis Type de Contrat CDD Doctorant Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 06903 VALBONNE Durée du contrat 36 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration 2300,00 € mensuel Date limite de candidature : vendredi 6 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Sujet De Thèse Dans le cadre du projet ANR DIVA, cette thèse se concentrera sur la modélisation sémantique et la représentation en graphes de connaissances de l’activité analytique des utilisateurs, ainsi que sur l’étude d’approches neuro-symboliques pour apprendre et raisonner sur ces représentations. L’objectif est ainsi de poser les fondations nécessaires à la prédiction de comportements et, à terme, au développement de mécanismes de recommandation et d’adaptation des visualisations explicables et contrôlables. Malgré des travaux importants sur la capture et la visualisation des traces d'activité des utilisateurs, les représentations existantes sont généralement propriétaires ou ad hoc [1], ce qui limite le raisonnement automatisé, l'interopérabilité et la réutilisation à long terme. Les graphes de connaissances (GC), fondés sur les normes du Web sémantique telles que RDF, RDFS et OWL, offrent une alternative prometteuse pour représenter l'activité des utilisateurs sous forme de données liées et riches sur le plan sémantique [3]. Ils permettent notamment de structurer et intégrer des données d'activité hétérogènes, tout en fournissant des mécanismes standardisés d'interrogation et de raisonnement. Cette représentation constitue ainsi un support pertinent pour l'application de méthodes d'IA visant à identifier des comportements analytiques et à en prédire l'évolution, tout en conservant une représentation explicite et interprétable des connaissances. S'appuyant sur des travaux antérieurs (par exemple, UI2Ont [4] et DIVA [5], et des ensembles de données ouverts sur l'activité des utilisateurs [6], cette thèse de doctorat vise à développer des modèles sémantiques et des approches neuro-symboliques pour la représentation et l'analyse de l'activité utilisateur. Elle s'articule autour des objectifs suivants : Modélisation sémantique de l'activité de l'utilisateur : Développer un cadre unifié, fondé sur des vocabulaires RDF, pour représenter l'activité multimodale de l'utilisateur sous forme de GC, en intégrant et structurant les données hétérogènes générées lors de l'exploration visuelle, notamment les interactions de l'utilisateur, le suivi du regard et les verbalisations. Découverte et prédiction du comportement exploratoire de l'utilisateur : Étudier des méthodes neuro-symboliques permettant d'exploiter les GC pour découvrir et prédire des comportements exploratoires, en combinant apprentissage automatique et raisonnement symbolique afin d'identifier des modèles comportementaux interprétables. Raffinement dynamique et validation des modèles comportamentaux : Étudier des méthodes de raffinement incrémental des modèles et règles comportementaux au cours de l'exploration, et évaluer leur qualité, leur interprétabilité et leurs capacités prédictives dans différents scénarios d'utilisation. Plan de travail : La thèse débutera par une revue de l’état de l’art, suivie du développement et de la validation du modèle sémantique et des pipelines de construction des graphes de connaissances. Les travaux porteront ensuite sur la découverte et la prédiction des comportements exploratoires à l’aide de méthodes neuro-symboliques, puis sur leur raffinement dynamique et incrémental. Les approches développées seront évaluées sur des données réelles et donneront lieu à des publications scientifiques ainsi qu’à des contributions open source. Les livrables attendus sont : L1. Modèle sémantique et extension de DIVA-O pour l’activité utilisateur multimodale. L2. Pipeline de construction et d’enrichissement des graphes de connaissances. L3. Méthodes neuro-symboliques pour la découverte et la prédiction des comportements exploratoires. L4. Méthodes de raffinement dynamique des modèles comportementaux. L5. Évaluation expérimentale des modèles et méthodes proposés. L6. Publications scientifiques et ressources open source. Références Bibliographiques [3] H. Paulheim and F. Probst, “A Formal Ontology on User Interfaces – Yet Another User Interface Description Language?,” 2011. [4] H. Paulheim and F. Probst, “UI2Ont—A Formal Ontology on User Interfaces and Interactions,” in Semantic Models for Adaptive Interactive Systems, T. Hussein, H. Paulheim, S. Lukosch, J. Ziegler, and G. Calvary, Eds., London: Springer, 2013, pp. 1–24. doi: 10.1007/978-1-4471-5301-6_1. [5] A. Menin and C. Faron, “DIVA: An Ontology-based Approach to Model User Activity within Visualization Systems,” in SAC 2026 - 41st ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing, Thessaloniki, Greece, Mar. 2026. doi: 10.1145/3748522.3779893. [6] S. Mohseni, A. Pachuilo, E. H. Nirjhar, R. Linder, A. Pena, and E. D. Ragan, “Analytic Provenance Datasets: A Data Repository of Human Analysis Activity and Interaction Logs,” Jan. 16, 2018, arXiv: arXiv:1801.05076. doi: 10.48550/arXiv.1801.05076. Votre Environnement de Travail Cette thèse est accueillie par le laboratoire I3S du CNRS à l’Université Côte d’Azur. Plus précisément, le/la doctorant(e) rejoindra l’équipe Wimmics (Inria, Université Côte d’Azur, CNRS, I3S), qui mène des recherches à l’interface entre intelligence artificielle et Web, notamment autour des graphes de connaissances, de la représentation et du traitement sémantique des données, et des méthodes d’IA pour les données du Web. Cette thèse s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet ANR JCJC DIVA, qui vise à étudier comment l’activité des utilisateurs avec des systèmes de visualisation interactifs peut être capturée, représentée et exploitée afin de mieux comprendre et, à terme, accompagner leurs processus d’analyse. Le projet part du constat que les interactions des utilisateurs avec les visualisations constituent une source riche d’information sur leurs processus analytiques, leurs stratégies et leurs objectifs, mais que les approches existantes reposent souvent sur des représentations ad hoc, limitant leur interopérabilité, leur réutilisation et le raisonnement automatisé [1], [2]. DIVA vise ainsi à développer des approches sémantiques et neuro-symboliques pour représenter l’activité des utilisateurs et identifier des comportements analytiques à partir de leurs traces d’interaction avec le système, des données biometriques, ainsi que des verbalisations sur leur raisonnement. Références [1] K. Xu, A. Ottley, C. Walchshofer, M. Streit, R. Chang, and J. Wenskovitch, “Survey on the Analysis of User Interactions and Visualization Provenance,” Comput. Graph. Forum, vol. 39, no. 3, pp. 757–783, 2020. [2] F. Yanez, C. Conati, A. Ottley, and C. Nobre, “The State of the Art in User‐Adaptive Visualizations,” Comput. Graph. Forum, vol. 44, Dec. 2024, doi: 10.1111/cgf.15271.  Description de l'entreprise CS, filiale du groupe Sopra Steria, est un acteur technologique de référence dans la conception, l’intégration et l’exploitation de systèmes critiques. En rejoignant CS, vous intégrez une entreprise humaine et innovante. Nous livrons bien plus que des systèmes, nous bâtissons la confiance. Nous allons au-delà des besoins exprimés, nous préparons les défis de demain. Plus que de simples experts, nous façonnons l’innovation. Explorer, observer, sécuriser l’espace de demain. Description du poste Nous recrutons un(e) Stagiaire Ingénieur(e) de pré-thèse pour mener des trava ux sur la détection de lacs et rivières par télédétection avec quantification d'incertitudes pour rejoindre notre Business unit Espace au sein de notre agence Space Processing & Intelligence spécialisée dans le traitement et l’hybridation des données spatiales . Vos missions Issu de la collaboration entre l’Agence Space Processing & Intelligence et le CS RESEARCH LAB, votre stage vous permet d’intégrer tout à la fois l’équipe R&D projet des Hydronautes et l’équipe de chercheurs en fusion de données incertaines du Lab’ ! Le stage s’inscrit dans le cadre de nos projets hydro qui consistent à faire le suivi des ressources en eau. Pour ces projets la détection des pixels en eau est un produit critique qui conditionne notamment l’estimation de la surface en eau, du volume en eau ou encore la largeur des rivières et donc l’estimation de leur débit. De nombreux indicateurs différents peuvent être associés à cette segmentation des pixels en eau. Ils peuvent faire intervenir de l’apprentissage, se reposer sur diverses bandes spectrales, et identifier directement ou indirectement l’eau, le tout avec une incertitude variable selon les indicateurs. Dans ce cadre votre mission consiste à : Réaliser un état de l’art du domaine Constituer un jeu de données permettant de mener et valider les expériences de façon rigoureuse Développer et/ou réunir différents indicateurs de la présence de pixel en eau Étudier, proposer, et mettre au point un cadre permettant de fusionner des indicateurs sous incertitude dans le but de fournir un produit de détection des pixels en eau accompagné d’un intervalle de confiance Échanger avec les porteurs des applications aval pour leur proposer des méthodes d’exploitation de ces produits (pixels en eau, intervalle de confiance) conformément à leurs besoins Restituer vos expériences, résultats et analyses à travers un rapport, des présentations, et un code documenté. L'environnement technique Python (paquets scientifiques et de traitement d’images) Pytorch GDAL QGIS Les plus de ce stage Le stage s’intègre directement dans nos projets tels que le France2030 StockWater. Il pourra ouvrir la voie à un sujet de Thèse. L’encadrement sera fait en étroite collaboration entre l’Agence Space Processing & Intelligence - forte connotation applicative sur la thématique gestion des ressources en eau par télédétection- et une équipe de recherche au sein du CS REASEARCH LAB expertise en probabilité imprécise Le CS RESEARCH LAB réunit des chercheurs (dont HDRs) et s’attaque à des problématiques transverses à l’échelle du groupe notamment au travers de thèses CIFRE.
