indeed:9f7c4781399f6306.title: PhD Candidate in Network Modelling for Food Safety and Regulatory Decision-Making
indeed:9f7c4781399f6306.desc: PhD Candidate in Network Modelling for Food Safety and Regulatory Decision-Making Job description Maastricht University’s School of Business and Economics, in collaboration with Sciensano, the Belgian institute for health and a leading public-health research organisation, is looking for a PhD candidate in Network Modelling for Food Safety and Regulatory Decision-Making. Sciensano brings established expertise in food safety, food contaminants, exposure assessment, risk analysis, and scientific evidence generation for public authorities. The collaboration connects methodological research at Maastricht University with Sciensano’s policy-facing work supporting food safety assessment and risk-manager decision-making at Belgian and European levels. The position focuses on the development of new multi-layer network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data. The aim is to support evidence generation for contaminant risk assessment, food safety monitoring, and regulatory decision-making. The PhD candidate will conduct original methodological research while working in close connection with public-health and regulatory questions. The project offers a distinctive opportunity to develop rigorous computational models in a setting where scientific evidence, regulatory judgement, and societal impact are closely connected. The project This PhD project develops new multi-layer network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data. The project addresses an open methodological challenge: how to specify, estimate, validate, and interpret network models that can support evidence generation for contaminant risk assessment and regulatory decision-making. The project focuses on the development of network-based models for analysing complex relationships in food safety data, including information relevant to contaminants, consumption patterns, exposure assessment, and regulatory prioritisation. The methodological contribution lies in developing models suited to this type of heterogeneous and relational data, rather than simply applying existing algorithms to a new domain. The work builds on Sciensano’s established activities in food safety, exposure assessment, and contaminant risk analysis. Sciensano’s work supports science-based policy, legislation, and decision-making by risk managers at Belgian and European levels. This collaboration gives the project a strong societal and institutional grounding, while preserving a clear methodological research ambition. The precise modelling choices and empirical focus will be developed as part of the PhD trajectory, in close dialogue with the supervisory team and Sciensano researchers. The candidate will be supervised by a team from Maastricht University’s School of Business and Economics and Sciensano, combining SBE’s methodological expertise with Sciensano’s expertise in food safety, while drawing on both institutions’ experience with regulatory decision-making. The candidate will: develop new network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data; work on model specification, estimation, validation, interpretation, uncertainty assessment, and robustness analysis; analyse heterogeneous data relevant to food safety, contaminants, consumption patterns, exposure assessment, and regulatory decision-making; investigate how network models can support contaminant risk assessment, monitoring prioritisation, and evidence generation for food safety authorities; implement computational methods in reproducible research workflows; publish research in international peer-reviewed journals and present findings at academic conferences; collaborate with researchers from Maastricht University, Sciensano, and relevant academic or policy-facing partners; complete a doctoral dissertation within the agreed timeframe. Candidate profile We are looking for a candidate with a strong quantitative and computational background who is motivated to develop rigorous modelling approaches for societally relevant regulatory questions. The candidate should have: a completed or near-completed master’s degree in a relevant field, such as computer science, data science, applied mathematics, statistics, econometrics, operations research, physics, computational social science, systems science, or a related quantitative discipline; demonstrated experience with programming for data analysis or computational modelling, preferably in Python, R, Julia, or a comparable language, and willingness to further develop skills in writing reproducible, modular, and maintainable research code; a foundation in at least one relevant methodological area, such as network modelling, statistical learning, machine learning, probabilistic modelling, complex systems, or computational modelling, together with the ability and motivation to develop the specialised network-modelling expertise required for the project; an interest in structured, relational, and heterogeneous data; the ability to formulate research questions with both methodological and applied relevance; strong analytical skills and the capacity to work independently; strong written and spoken English communication skills, preferably at C1 level or higher according to the CEFR, with the ability to explain technical concepts to interdisciplinary academic, public-health, and policy-facing audiences; ability and willingness to work in an interdisciplinary environment involving methodological, food-safety, public-health, and regulatory expertise. Experience with food safety, contaminant risk assessment, exposure assessment, nutrition, toxicology, public health, or regulatory science is welcome but not required. Domain-specific knowledge can be developed during the project in collaboration with Sciensano. A strong technical profile and an interest in food safety decision-making are more important. The starting date is negotiable, but ideally the position would start in January 2027. Employment conditions At Maastricht University, the PhD candidate will work in an international, open, and engaged academic environment. The position offers: a 18-month contract, 1.0 FTE, with the prospect of a 2,5 year extension based on mutual satisfaction; a gross monthly salary between €3,204 and €4,051, based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week; 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus; 29 vacation days, based on full-time employment, four additional days off, and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours; flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home; supervision by researchers from Maastricht University and Sciensano; the opportunity to develop new methodology in network modelling, computational analysis, and structured food-safety data; close collaboration with Sciensano, a public-health institute with established expertise in food safety, exposure assessment, contaminant risk analysis, and scientific evidence generation for public authorities; access to doctoral training, research seminars, methodological expertise, and professional-development opportunities; opportunities to publish in international journals and present at academic conferences; an interdisciplinary research environment combining methodological rigour with public-health and regulatory relevance; a solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities; an inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe. Find out more about the PhD journey at Maastricht University, from starting your research to completing your PhD and beyond. As a PhD candidate, you will be automatically enrolled in one of our Graduate Schools. Find out more about our Graduate Schools. Further information For questions about the scientific content of the project, the research environment, or the collaboration between Maastricht University and Sciensano, please contact: Rui Jorge Almeida via rj.almeida@maastrichtuniversity.nl Mirjana Andjelkovic via Mirjana.Andjelkovic@sciensano.be For questions about the application procedure or employment conditions, please contact: Miranda Van den Beuken via miranda.vandenbeuken@maastrichtuniversity.nl Application procedure Applications should include: a motivation letter describing the candidate’s interest in the position and fit with the project; a curriculum vitae; transcripts or a list of completed courses and grades; a writing sample, such as a master’s thesis, research paper, or technical report; if available, examples of programming, modelling, or data-analysis work; the names and contact details of at least two academic referees. In the motivation letter, candidates are encouraged to explain how their methodological background could contribute to the development of multi-layer network models for food safety and regulatory decision-making. Prior experience in food safety or public health is not required, but candidates should be willing to engage with domain experts and policy-facing research questions. indeed:381efab6d31ee7c3.desc: The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field. Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed. Introduction Are you eager to shape the next generation of chips using atomically thin materials? In this PhD position, you will develop 2D nanomaterials and devices for more energy-efficient sensing and computing. The project will be undertaken within the NanoComputing Research Lab in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), at the heart of Europe’s leading semiconductor region. Job Description In this PhD position, you will investigate 2D materials as a platform for next-generation sensing and computing devices. You will develop growth recipes for 2D materials and fabricate and characterize devices that could contribute to emerging energy efficient brain-inspired computing hardware. What you'll contribute to Specifically, you will: develop metal-organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) growth recipes for large-area 2D materials, such as MoS₂ and WSe₂, with controlled defect densities; optimize transfer processes to integrate the grown 2D materials onto target device substrates, enabling heterogeneous integration; develop scalable fabrication processes in the TU/e cleanroom (NanoLab@TU/e) for device arrays, including sensors and transistors; engineer metal–semiconductor and dielectric interfaces to improve device performance; characterize materials and devices, and work with circuit designers to link material properties to device and circuit performance; publish your results in leading journals and present them at international conferences; supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s student projects. Your research environment You will join the NanoComputing Research Lab (NanoComputing Research Lab), in the Integrated Circuits group of the Department of Electrical Engineering at TU/e. You will be supervised by Dr. Abhishek Singh Dahiya (project leader) and Prof. Aida Todri-Sanial. You will have access to TU/e’s state-of-the-art cleanroom and characterization facilities. indeed:6ee888ca78bfb861.desc: About the position 3-year 100% PhD position is available at the Department of Pediatric Research, OUS Rikshospitalet for a highly motivated and skilled PhD student on a project funded by South-Eastern Norway Regional Health Authority. The position is available from 23rd November 2026. Neonatal cholestasis is a condition with impaired bile flow causing accumulation of bile acids and bilirubin, liver damage and debilitating pruritus. Reduction in bile to the intestine results in malabsorption, reduced weight gain, vitamin deficiency and changes in microbiota. Both genetic and environmental factors can result in cholestasis. About the Department / Research Group Professor Runar Almaas (Pediatric hepatology) at PFI, OUS is leading the project. The PhD candidate will be supervised by him and by Co-supervisor Barbora Smolkova (PhD) and senior researcher Gareth Sullivan. The group is using induced pluripotent stem cells for making liver organoids and a major part of the work will be related to this model. Oslo University Hospital is a workplace with great diversity. We believe this is crucial for solving our tasks in the best possible way. We want this diversity to be reflected among the applicants for our positions, and we encourage all qualified candidates, regardless of background, to apply! Key information Application deadline: 15.11.2026 Employer: Oslo universitetssykehus HF Town/city: Oslo Title: PhD Position Positions: 1 Full-time/part-time: Full-time Employment type: Contract Percentage of full-time: 100 Webcruiter ID: 5194655530 Start date: 23.11.2026 End date: 09.11.2029 Social sharing : Share on x Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook Share by email Duties and responsabilities What Tasks and Responsibilities Are Associated with the Position? To reveal mechanisms of cholestasis and pruritus and to investigate novel potential treatments we are using liver organoids derived from disease-specific induced pluripotent stem cells. iPSC-derived liver organoids are a unique model that can mimic key features of the human liver and can be used to study liver development and disease. In these project liver organoids will be used for studying protein trafficking, effect of modulating factors and potential drugs. Qualifications Master degree (or equivalent) in medicine, biomedicine, biotechnology, or molecular biology Good practical skills in various extraction, quantification, and analysis of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) and proteins including qRT-PCR, ddPCR, and Western blotting are advantages Skills and prior experience in cell cultivation and handling is an advantage experience in other relevant molecular biology techniques including gene editing using CRISPR/Cas9 technology, next-generation sequencing, etc is an advantage Experience in scientific writing / presentation is an advantage Good written and oral communication skills in English Practical Information We request that relevant documentation be attached to the application. Please note that all documents should be in English or a Scandinavian language. Personal qualities We are looking for a highly dedicated, reliable and highly motivated candidate with great working capacity We expect scientific curiosity and understanding about the nature of scientific thinking You have a strong interest in completing your tasks in structured way. You are able to design, plan, perform, and analyze experiments in an innovative way The candidate is expected to work together with engineers and other scientists in a team. Ability to work independently, but with good communication skills is preferred. We can offer 100% position for three years granted Ambitious project and interesting scientific topic. An emerging and rapidly developing area of research Training in advanced methods and models. Encouraged supervision and cooperation team A friendly and international environment A favorable pension arrangement and attractive welfare arrangements In accordance with the OUS’s equal opportunities policy, we invite applications from all interested individuals regardless of gender or ethnicity Address: Oslo universitetssykehus HF, Rikshospitalet, Sognsvannsveien 20, 0372 Oslo, Norway Open directions (in new tab) Contacts Runar Almaas Head of Department Phone: +4741321932 About the employer Oslo University Hospital is a highly specialized hospital in charge of extensive regional and local hospital assignments. The hospital has a nationwide responsibility for a number of national and multi-regional assignments, and has several national centers of competence. Oslo University Hospital is responsible for approximately 50 percent of all medical and health care research conducted at Norwegian hospitals, and is a significant role player within the education of a large variety of health care personnel.

indeed:b6dd9f7887240a5d.title: PhD Research Intern
indeed:b6dd9f7887240a5d.desc: Job description Company and benefits Social Impact & Sustainability Job ID 41745 Join the leader in entertainment innovation and help us design the future. At Dolby, science meets art, and high tech means more than computer code. As a member of the Dolby team, you’ll see and hear the results of your work everywhere, from movie theaters to smartphones. We continue to revolutionize how people create, deliver, and enjoy entertainment worldwide. To do that, we need the absolute best talent. We’re big enough to give you all the resources you need, and small enough so you can make a real difference and earn recognition for your work. We offer a collegial culture, challenging projects, and excellent compensation and benefits, not to mention a Flex Work approach that is truly flexible to support where, when, and how you do your best work. Internship: Development and On-Device Deployment of an Autoregressive Model for Real-Time Speech Restoration and Dialog Enhancement Start: Open Duration: 3 months (full-time) or 6 months (part-time) Location: Stockholm Speech restoration and dialog enhancement are critical components in modern audio experiences, especially in noisy environments or legacy content with degraded quality. Current systems often rely on non-causal, server-side models that require full audio context, limiting their use in real-time or on-device applications. With recent advances in autoregressive language modeling and efficient deep learning deployment, there is growing potential to develop low-latency, high-quality speech enhancement systems that operate in real time and even on consumer devices. This internship aims to design and implement an autoregressive, large language model (LLM)-based architecture for speech restoration and dialog enhancement. The model will be trained to reconstruct clean speech from degraded inputs by leveraging both acoustic and linguistic context. It will be evaluated against Dolby’s current best multimodal system, focusing on perceptual quality, intelligibility, and latency. A key objective is to explore the feasibility of deploying the model on-device through techniques such as model compression, quantization, pruning, and compilation using modern inference frameworks. Candidate requirements Master’s or Ph.D. student in Machine Learning, Signal Processing, Computer Science, or a related field. Hands-on experience with PyTorch. Interest in model optimization for edge deployment using tools such as Triton Inference Server, ONNX, TensorRT, or similar frameworks. Prior experience in this field is a plus. Experience fine-tuning LLMs is a plus. Knowledge of audio-language modeling is a plus. Dolby Hiring Entity: Gävlegatan 12A 113 30 Stockholm, Sweden

indeed:3f0926cce4ced4b9.title: Doctoral student in Industrial Design with focus on strategic design
indeed:3f0926cce4ced4b9.desc: Lund University was founded in 1666 and is repeatedly ranked among the world’s top universities. The University has around 46 000 students and 8 500 staff based in Lund, Helsingborg and Malmö. We are united in our efforts to understand, explain and improve our world and the human condition. Lund University welcomes applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We regard equality, equal opportunities and diversity as a strength and an asset. Description of the workplace The position is located in the division of Industrial Design at the Department of Design Sciences at LTH, Lund University. Design Sciences is an interdisciplinary department that integrates design, technology, and people in its research and education. As a doctoral student you will become part of an interdisciplinary research environment and work alongside doctoral students, senior researchers and teaching staff within Industrial Design and the wider Department of Design Sciences. Being a doctoral student As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. You will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree. More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. Subject and project description Research in Industrial Design investigates how design shapes and responds to technological, environmental and societal change. It develops and critically examines design knowledge, methods and practices, with the aim of understanding how design can contribute to meaningful and responsible transformation. Our research combines scientific and artistic approaches and is often conducted in collaboration with academic, industrial and public-sector partners as well as communities and third-sector organizations. The research environment encompasses sustainable design; emerging technologies and AI; design strategy, management and innovation; design practice and methods; and critical and participatory perspectives on design and design education. This doctoral position has a particular focus on strategic design. The research will investigate how design can operate as a strategic capability in organizations and society and contribute to processes of innovation, transformation and value creation. Possible areas of inquiry include how design capabilities are developed and embedded in organizations; the role of design and design approaches in enabling organizational change; design in complex settings; systemic design; and user and citizen engagement in strategic design processes. The research may also investigate futures-oriented approaches, including designerly ways of navigating complex and uncertain societal, technological and environmental conditions. Within this overall research area, the doctoral student will develop and refine the specific research direction and project in dialogue with the supervisors. The project is expected to combine theoretical inquiry with empirical research and may incorporate experimental, participatory or practice-based design approaches where relevant. Work duties You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme. You will develop and conduct an independent doctoral research project. Your work will include formulating research questions, reviewing and developing relevant theoretical perspectives, designing and conducting empirical studies, analysing research material, communicating findings through academic publications and conferences, and completing a doctoral thesis. You will also be expected to participate actively in the research environment of the Division of Industrial Design and the Department of Design Sciences and to engage with relevant academic and external research partners. Additional duties include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours). The position requires regular on-site presence at Lund University in Lund to carry out the work and participate fully in the research environment. Qualifications To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below. Admission requirements A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Industrial Design if the applicant has: at least 30 higher education credits relevant to the subject area, of which at least 15 credits must be at an advanced level, or an in-depth study of at least 20 higher education credits at an advanced level relevant to the subject area, or a degree in fine arts, engineering, Master's or Magister's degree relevant to the subject area. Additional requirements In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: Knowledge and skills relevant to industrial design and to the proposed area of doctoral research. Ability to to independently formulate and address research problems. Analytical skills and the ability to engage critically with theoretical perspectives and empirical material. Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. Other qualifications (advantages) For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications: Experience of conducting empirical, practice-based or participatory research. Experience of interdisciplinary or multidisciplinary work. Experience of managing complex projects involving multiple actors or perspectives. Experience of using design methods and practices as part of research or inquiry. Experience of collaboration with academic, industrial, public-sector or other societal actors. Experience of communicating research or complex design work to different audiences. Consideration will also be given to the applicant's ability to take initiative, work independently, collaborate with others, and develop and complete a long-term research project. We offer Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. More about working at Lund University on lu.se. About the employment The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting on 2027-01-01 or soon after. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§. More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. Other This doctoral position is funded by the Ingvar Kamprad Design Foundation (IKDF). How to apply Applications must be written in English and include: CV A cover letter describing your reasons for wishing to undertake a PhD in Industrial Design, your interest in this position, and how your academic, professional and/or personal experiences have shaped your research interests and prepared you for doctoral studies. Copies of degree certificates and transcripts confirming that you meet the general and specific admission requirements; A research statement (maximum 1,500 words) describing the research questions, problems or phenomena within Strategic Design that you are interested in exploring, why you consider them important, and how you might approach investigating them. The statement is intended to demonstrate your research interests and ability to formulate a potential direction for doctoral research; it is not expected to constitute a fully developed research proposal. A portfolio or selection of work samples demonstrating relevant design, research, or professional work. These may include design projects, research projects, publications or other written work, collaborative or community-based projects, or other work relevant to the position. For collaborative work, clearly describe your own role and contribution. Contact information for three references and Any other documents you wish to be considered. We welcome your application. LTH is Lund University’s Faculty of Engineering. At LTH we educate people, build knowledge for the future and work hard for the development of society. We create space for brilliant research and inspire creative advancements in technology, architecture and design. We have nearly 12,000 students. Every year, our researchers – many of whom work in world-leading profile areas – publish around 100 theses and 2 000 scientific findings. In addition, a number of research results and degree projects are transformed into innovations. Together we explore and create – to benefit the world. We kindly decline all sales and marketing contacts. indeed:fa75a4e8504b1c03.title: AstraZeneca-Funded Non-Clinical PhD Studentship (Fixed Term): Physics-Guided Representation Learning for Drug Discovery
indeed:fa75a4e8504b1c03.desc: Applications are invited for a four-year, AstraZeneca-funded PhD studentship in the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics, commencing in October 2027. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by Prof Sergio Bacallado (University of Cambridge), Dr Dino Oglic (AstraZeneca), and Dr Jon Paul Janet (AstraZeneca). The studentship offers an opportunity to conduct cutting-edge research at the interface of statistical machine learning, molecular simulation and drug discovery. Project description The project, entitled Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection , aims to develop novel machine-learning methods for predicting molecular binding affinities and supporting decision-making in drug discovery. Free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations provide valuable information about how strongly candidate drug molecules bind to their biological targets, but these calculations are computationally expensive. This project will investigate how machine-learning models can extract richer information from FEP data and experimental measurements, combining physical principles with modern representation-learning techniques. The research will involve developing and evaluating new statistical and machine-learning methods, with access to both public benchmark datasets and AstraZeneca's industrial drug-discovery expertise and data. Candidate requirements Applicants should have, or expect to obtain, a first-class or upper second-class honours degree (or equivalent), normally following four years of university study. We welcome applicants with backgrounds in Mathematics, Statistics, Machine Learning, Scientific Computing, or any closely related discipline. Experience with computational chemistry would be desirable but is not essential . We particularly welcome applications from candidates with strong mathematical or machine-learning backgrounds who are interested in applying their expertise to problems in drug discovery. Funding The studentship provides funding for four years , covering a maintenance stipend and University tuition fees at the UK/Home rate. The studentship is open to candidates eligible for Home-fee status. International candidates may also be considered, provided that additional funding can be secured through scholarships or other approved funding schemes to cover the difference between Home and international tuition fees. This difference cannot be covered through student self-funding. Training and supervision The student will benefit from joint academic and industrial supervision, participating in the research activities of the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics and collaborating closely with AstraZeneca researchers to gain exposure to industrial applications of artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical development. How to apply Applications must be submitted through the University of Cambridge Postgraduate Applicant Portal , selecting the course PhD in Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics : https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/mapmpdpms/apply Applicants should indicate Dr Sergio Bacallado as their proposed supervisor and use the following project title: Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection. Applications should include the supporting documentation required by the University, including academic transcripts, a CV, two references, and the relevant research summary and reasons for applying. The deadline for applications is 6 January 2027 (23:59 UK time) . Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview in January 2027 . Informal enquiries about the project are welcome and may be addressed to Dr Sergio Bacallado at sb2116@cam.ac.uk . The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

linkedin:4481206916.desc: Funded PhD Position in Multi-Agent AI and Distributed Optimization for Resilient Cyber-Physical Systems. Universidad Rey Juan Carlos, Móstoles, Madrid, Spain. What the position offers The position combines three years of competitive funding with scientific supervision and opportunities to develop original research connecting AI and Operations Research in a competitive international environment. linkedin:4479945503.title: PhD Candidate in AI Driven MAC Control for Integrated Terrestrial NTN 6G Networks
linkedin:4479945503.desc: About The Position Are you motivated to pursue a doctoral degree and contribute to cutting-edge research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and next-generation wireless communications like 6G? The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU has a vacancy for a PhD candidate in AI‑Driven & Self-healing MAC Control for Integrated Terrestrial-NTN 6G networks. The position is fully funded and will run for four years (100 % employment), including teaching duties. Your immediate leader is the Head of the Communication Technology Unit at the department of Information Security and Communication Technology. The workplace will be located in Trondheim. About The Project Future 6G and beyond communication systems are expected to integrate terrestrial cellular networks with non-terrestrial platforms, including Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellites, High Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS), and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). While such integrated networks can provide ubiquitous connectivity and improved resilience, they also introduce significant challenges due to highly dynamic radio environments, heterogeneous backhaul infrastructures, mobility, resource constraints, and service disruptions. The core research focuses on the MAC layer and its techniques – the candidate will design, implement and evaluate an AI-driven MAC-control framework that self‑heals in integrated terrestrial-NTN (LEO, HAPS, UAV) 6G networks. The work will be hands-on and system-oriented; a closed-loop, verifiable prototype will be built, tested under realistic degradations and examined for different metrics such as latency, reliability, fairness and SLA‑violation. For example, the candidate will do some of the tasks including: AI-driven Link Adaptation and MAC control – develop AI-based mechanism that proactively anticipate and respond to rapidly changing conditions in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (LEO satellites, HAPS, and UAVs) and to cascading radio access networks (RAN) failures/degradations. AI-Driven self-healing MAC – develop algorithms and techniques at the MAC layer for fast anomaly detection, failure prediction, autonomous recovery, and performance resilience. Service-aware MAC layer techniques – develop novel MAC-layer mechanisms that integrate queueing theory, traffic modelling, machine learning, and network-performance prediction for improving latency, reliability and fairness to support mission‑critical services. The proposed algorithms and mechanisms will be implemented and validated on the B5G Lab infrastructure at the IIK department, NTNU. The lab provides industry‑grade 5G equipment, open‑source RAN stacks, programmable OpenFlow/P4 switches and AI‑Boxes for fast inference, together with NetFPGA/DAG hardware for sub‑millisecond failure detection and a Timeseries‑DB/Grafana monitoring platform for closed‑loop testing. One or multiple satellite ground stations (e.g., Starlink, OneWeb) will be installed and connected to the core network soon to support NTN testing. Duties of the position Complete all the doctoral courses work, a condition to obtain the doctorate degree Carry out high‑quality research within the scope described above Publish enough scientific results in recognized venues and contribute to research disseminations Actively participate in the Networking Research Group and its activities Engage in international activities (conferences, research stays at foreign educational institutions) Teach and support learning activities in courses related to communications and networking Required Selection Criteria You must have a relevant master’s degree in wireless communications and mobile networks, computer networks and distributed systems, telecommunication engineering, computer science with a networking focus, or equivalent, with a strong background in theory, ML/AI, and mathematics Your master’s degree must correspond to a five-year Norwegian degree, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level Master students can still apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position, and no later than 1st of August 2027 You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background (not worse than C), you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. A scientific proposal (max. 1000 words / 3 pages) You must meet the requirements for admission to the PhD program in Information Security and Communication Technology. The following tests can be used as such documentation: TOEFL: 600 (paper-based test), 92 (Internet-based test). IELTS: 6.5, with no section lower than 5.5 (only Academic IELTS test accepted). CAE/CPE: grade B or A PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”. The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNU's guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria High skills in applied mathematics, problem mathematicalising and solving Practical experiences with networked systems and multi-vendor softwarized environments Experience with 5G radio access and core testbeds including open-source solutions Relevant publications and dissemination will be considered an advantage Experience in teaching, preferably on master level Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian language Personal characteristics We Are Seeking Applicants Who Are Highly motivated by fundamental research of practical relevance Well organized and have interest beyond their own research Capable to work independently with clear goals and plans to achieve them Eager to present and discuss their research with other professionals Eager to disseminate research results in both local and international venues In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal suitability, as well as motivation, in terms of the qualifications specified in the advertisement. We offer An exciting job with an important mission in society Access to the B5G Lab’s state‑of‑the‑art infrastructure Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD program in Information Security and Communication Technology within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral program throughout the period of employment. About Tilburg University Tilburg University is the university in the humanities and social sciences. With leading research and inspiring education, we contribute to the interpretation and, where possible, solutions to current societal issues, from climate change to digitalization Our community is personal, engaged, and small-scale. On our green, compact, and vibrant campus there is room for encounter, collaboration, reflection, and personal growth. Read more about Tilburg University. Working at Tilburg University means working in an inclusive team with attractive employment conditions. About the Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences (TSHD) Research and education at the Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences (TSHD) focuses on humans, technology, culture, and their interactions in a globalizing digital society. linkedin:4480963636.title: PhD Position in Accountable and Responsible AI
linkedin:4480963636.desc: Are you eager to conduct high-impact research spanning computer science, economics, law, and the creative industry—while living in Amsterdam, a dynamic city renowned for its high-quality life and its thriving AI and creative sectors? Working at the UvA Join Us! A fully funded four-year Ph.D. position is available in the Complex Cyber Infrastructure research group at the University of Amsterdam. As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes deeply embedded in our society, the urgency to warrant its responsible and accountable use is increasing. Examples include the control that creative industry actors need to manifest when using AI pipelines in the (moving) image industry. This PhD project aims to focus on the emerging field of Accountable and Responsible AI, with the goal of advancing knowledge and practice at the intersection of AI research, creative industry practices, and societal regulatory expectations. Two projects underpin this position: SafeGenAI – a creative industry endeavour to enable creative industry actors to safely use GenAI tools; and LLM4LM – a large consortium addressing the legal-tech challenges in cross-organisational multi-domain agentic solutions. The candidate will not only have a chance to contribute to shaping the next generation AI systems within the creative industry and logistics practices, but also potentially to design more transparent, fair, and compliant ones with evolving societal and regulatory expectations. The successful candidate will be embedded in a team that will help transfer fundamental research results into the creative industry and legal practices, respectively. Moreover, they will be working closely with the supervision team, as well as the other PhD students and postdocs in the research group. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do In this context, you will investigate the following key challenges: Opacity in GenAI inferencing: How can the inferencing and reasoning processes of GenAI systems be made sufficiently transparent and traceable to support accountability in high-stakes professional contexts? AI legal compliance-by-design: How can GenAI systems be built to satisfy the requirements of the regulations such as the EU AI Act — including transparency, human oversight, and risk management — while remaining practically useful in domain-specific workflows? SMEs lack the expertise to navigate complex regulatory environments: How can domain-specific structured knowledge be integrated into GenAI systems to ground their outputs, reduce hallucination, and support trustworthy decision for non-expert users? What We Ask Of You Your experience and profile: MSc in CS, AI or a closely related field. Strong interest in Interest in finance and financial services is a plus.; previous experience in these fields is a plus. Enthusiasm for the research process: studying research papers, solving complex problems, applying creative thinking, evaluation, reflection and disseminating findings via writing and oral presentations. The ability to critically analyse abstract models as well as concrete implementations. The ability to work individually as well as effectively in a team Fluency in written and spoken English This Is What We Offer You A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD Candidate is applicable.. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. We also have an extensive secondary benefits package. Your place at the UvA You will work in this team The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. The mission of the Informatics Institute (IvI) is to perform curiosity-driven and use-inspired fundamental research in Computer Science. The main research themes are Artificial Intelligence, Computational Science and Systems and Network Engineering. Our research involves complex information systems at large, with a focus on collaborative, data driven, computational and intelligent systems, all with a strong interactive component. The Complex Cyber Infrastructure (CCI) group is part of the Informatics Institute at the University of Amsterdam. CCI focuses on the complexity of human-made systems on all scales. Cyber Infrastructure is rapidly evolving from relatively simple fixed components to programmable and virtualized objects with many degrees of freedom, owned, operated and governed by different entities in multiple administrative domains interacting on the Internet. Harnessing this complexity in a transparent, trustable way for safe and secure data processing is a major research topic that defines the focus of CCI research. The challenges are addressed by combining methods and results from research into sustainable and sovereign distributed data processing, programmable networks, policy reasoning and normative control, and software (language) engineering. Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam. About The Faculty Of Science Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, whether it concerns elementary particles, the birth of the universe, or how the brain functions. The Faculty has a student population of approximately 8,000 students, as well as 1,800 staff members working in education, research, or support services. Important to know Your application & contact If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application. You can apply online via the red button. We accept applications until and including 15 November 2026. We plan to organise multiple rounds of interviews. Therefore, due to time sensitivity the vacancy will be closed if a suitable candidate is selected before 15 November 2026. Applications should include the following information (all files besides your cv should be submitted in one single pdf file): a detailed CV including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience; a letter of motivation; a list of publications; the names and email addresses of two references who can provide letters of recommendation. A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure. (for details: national knowledge security guidelines). Only complete applications received within the response period via the link below will be considered. If you have any questions or do you require additional information? Please contact: Dr. Ana Oprescu, Assistant Professor Complex Cyber Infrastructure, a.m.oprescu@uva.nl Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion As an employer, the UvA maintains an equal opportunities policy. We value diversity and are fully committed to being a place where everyone feels at home. We nurture inquisitive minds and perseverance and allow room for persistent questioning. With us, curiosity and creativity are the prevailing culture. Studies show that women and members of underrepresented groups only apply for jobs if they meet 100% of the qualifications. Do you meet the educational requirements but not yet all of the requested experience? The UvA encourages you to apply anyway.

linkedin:4481217444.title: PhD in Energy-Efficient Sensors and Computing Hardware from 2D Materials
linkedin:4481217444.desc: Introduction Are you eager to shape the next generation of chips using atomically thin materials? In this PhD position, you will develop 2D nanomaterials and devices for more energy-efficient sensing and computing. The project will be undertaken within the NanoComputing Research Lab in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), at the heart of Europe’s leading semiconductor region. Job Description In this PhD position, you will investigate 2D materials as a platform for next-generation sensing and computing devices. You will develop growth recipes for 2D materials and fabricate and characterize devices that could contribute to emerging energy efficient brain-inspired computing hardware. What You'll Contribute To Specifically, you will: develop metal-organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) growth recipes for large-area 2D materials, such as MoS₂ and WSe₂, with controlled defect densities; optimize transfer processes to integrate the grown 2D materials onto target device substrates, enabling heterogeneous integration; develop scalable fabrication processes in the TU/e cleanroom (NanoLab@TU/e) for device arrays, including sensors and transistors; engineer metal–semiconductor and dielectric interfaces to improve device performance; characterize materials and devices, and work with circuit designers to link material properties to device and circuit performance; publish your results in leading journals and present them at international conferences; supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s student projects. Your research environment You will join the NanoComputing Research Lab (NanoComputing Research Lab), in the Integrated Circuits group of the Department of Electrical Engineering at TU/e. You will be supervised by Dr. Abhishek Singh Dahiya (project leader) and Prof. Aida Todri-Sanial. You will have access to TU/e’s state-of-the-art cleanroom and characterization facilities. What we're looking for A master’s degree in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field, with a solid foundation in semiconductor materials and device physics, and prior experience in the growth of nanomaterials (preferably 2D materials using CVD), nanofabrication processes such as atomic layer deposition, lithography, etching etc., and 2D material transfer process. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field. A research-oriented attitude. Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and mentor bachelor/master’s students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About Us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. Job Description Are you ready to shape the future of autonomous maritime security? We are looking for a highly motivated and talented PhD Candidate to spearhead advanced research on the FoilDrone system—an innovative, future-proof maritime surveillance concept. Project Context & Mission Maritime domain awareness is a critical global priority. Traditional surveillance options face major trade-offs: airborne drones offer high speed but suffer from critically low endurance (6 to 22 hours), while unmanned surface vessels (like the Saildrone) boast long endurance but travel at very low speeds (3 to 5 knots) and cannot see over the horizon. The FoilDrone system bridges this market gap by combining an aerial Vertical Take-Off and Landing (VTOL) rotating-wing sailplane with a submerged, tethered hydrofoil. completely eliminating propulsion power consumption during operations. You will take the design from conceptual idea towards physical implementation through independent research, simulation and experimentation. Your core duties will include: Advanced Multi-Body Dynamics & Control: Deepen and expand simulation models linking the aerial vehicle to the submerged hydrofoil via a flexible tether. Refine independent controllers to ensure stability during critical transitions (transit, deployment, sailing, and recovery). Aerodynamic & Hydrodynamic Optimization: Investigate the complex interactions of fixed wing drone, cabels, and hydrofoils. Optimize aerodynamic and hydrodynamic efficiencies across varying sea states and wind disturbances. Experimental Validation: Translate theoretical models into physical hardware. Collaborate with technical staff and student teams to design wind-tunnel experiments, tow-tank tests, and open-water flight trials to validate structural integrity, deployment mechanisms, and control strategies. Position PhD in AI enabled prediction of pollen season magnitude for next generation forecasting Employer University of Birmingham Birmingham - research that matters At Birmingham, you’re free to pursue your own independent research, while building the skills and confidence to make an impact on global society. A platform for significant, pioneering research, Birmingham is a hub for innovation, delivery and academic rigour. We focus on global issues, with a collaborative, cross-disciplinary culture. Combined with modern facilities and academic expertise, it’s an approach that shapes and inspires all our teaching, creating and learning. Homepage: https://www.birmingham.ac.uk Location Birmingham, United Kingdom Sector Academic Relevant divisions Atmospheric Sciences (AS) Biogeosciences (BG) Type Full time Level Student / Graduate / Internship Salary A fully funded 3.5-year PhD studentship, including a tax-free stipend at the UKRI rate (currently £21,805 per year for 2026/27), tuition fees, and £8,000 for research and training. International applicants are eligible to apply, with international tuition Preferred Education Master Application deadline 6 January 2027 Posted 19 October 2026 Job Description PROJECT HIGHLIGHTS Work directly with the UK Met Office on next-generation operational pollen forecasting Develop novel AI and machine-learning methods to predict pollen season magnitude months in advance Join an interdisciplinary team spanning environmental science, mathematics and artificial intelligence Overview Understanding and forecasting airborne pollen is essential for improving operational environmental prediction across the UK. While daily pollen forecasts have improved substantially in recent years, one of the greatest remaining challenges is predicting the overall magnitude of each pollen season. For example, total birch pollen concentrations can vary by a factor of eight between consecutive years, driven by complex interactions between previous-season pollen production, meteorological conditions during the preceding summer, and weather during the flowering season itself. These processes remain poorly understood and are not currently represented within operational forecasting systems. This project will harness a unique UK-wide pollen reanalysis (2000–2025), developed by the UK Met Office under the stewardship of Co-I Lucy Neal, together with long-term pollen observations and meteorological datasets, to develop next-generation machine learning approaches for predicting seasonal pollen magnitude. The resulting models will improve understanding of the environmental drivers of interannual variability while providing practical tools to enhance the operational Met Office NAME pollen forecast. With only 8 active regulatory-grade pollen monitoring sites across the UK, equivalent to approximately one site per eight million people, long-term pollen observations are extremely sparse. The pollen reanalysis provides an unprecedented spatially and temporally complete dataset for developing and validating artificial intelligence methods. The student will investigate how biological memory, antecedent weather conditions and environmental variables combine to determine pollen production, developing interpretable machine learning models capable of predicting seasonal severity months in advance. This PhD will be embedded in a vibrant interdisciplinary research environment at the University of Birmingham, combining expertise in environmental science, artificial intelligence and applied mathematics. Joint supervision from Environmental Sciences, the School of Mathematics, and the UK Met Office will provide outstanding training in machine learning, environmental modelling and operational forecasting. The research will directly address a major limitation in current pollen forecasting systems, delivering new scientific understanding alongside AI tools with clear operational impact for the UK Met Office and wider environmental forecasting community. linkedin:4478618248.desc: Temporary contract | 14+22(+12) months | Belval Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a Research and Technology Organization (RTO) active in the fields of materials, environment and IT. By transforming scientific knowledge into technologies, smart data and tools, LIST empowers citizens in their choices, public authorities in their decisions and businesses in their strategies. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? You will be part of the LIST Materials Research and Technology department, where you will carry out your work in the Quantum Materials Group, led by Dr. Florian Kaiser. Quantum technologies have the potential to revolutionise the world in many aspects. Quantum colour centres in in wide bandgap semiconductors have recently emerged as a promising platform, since they can incorporate quantum systems, which can be scaled up by industrial processing. Along these lines, we have recently shown that individual colour centres can be integrated into silicon carbide nanophotonic waveguides with little-to-no degradation of spin-optical coherences. These finding define the strategy for developing a scalable quantum technology architecture. Our strategy is to use multiplexed and integrated colour centres for quantum communication tasks. Key here is to generate entanglement between colour centres based on spin-photon entanglement, as well as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. With this milestone demonstration, we strive to kickstart subsequent developments towards a quantum internet architecture. The objective of this PhD thesis is to support our work towards optical interference between colour centres, i.e., Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. The initial part of this thesis comprises setting up our new optical cryostat platform, which is based on a combination of standard confocal microscopy, and interferometry. In the second step, you will benefit from our ongoing activities towards quantum photonic silicon carbide chips in which we generate colour centres in fibre-coupled waveguides. You will determine the ideal pulsed excitation schemes for colour centres, considering spectral, temporal and polarization filtering. Subsequently, you will characterise the photon quality depending on experimental parameters, and implement initial two-photon inteference experiments outside of the cryostat, followed by a fully-on-chip demonstration inside the cryostat. If time permits, this project can be further extended to the generation of entanglement between two colour centre chips located in two different cryostats. Is Your profile described below? linkedin:4480265095.desc: About The Position A fully-funded PhD position in modelling marine larval dispersal and spatial population genetics and demography is available at the Department of Biology, Norwegian University of Science & Technology (NTNU) under the supervision of Associate Professor Scott Burgess. NTNU’s Department of Biology hosts internationally leading research activity in ecology, evolutionary biology, physiology, marine science and technology, and cell & molecular biology. As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia. About The Project The PhD position is aligned with a research program that has the overall aim of providing new understanding of the processes that affect marine larval dispersal and gene flow, how we measure it with genetic data, and how we use that information to predict the genetic and demographic responses of spatially structured marine populations to environmental variation and change. Specifically, the primary focus of the PhD will be to understand how complex coastlines, ocean circulation, and biology (e.g., reproductive systems and phenology, larval behavior and survival) interact to affect the spatial structure of the genetic and demographic properties of marine populations. There is flexibility, and an expectation, for candidates to develop their own line of research within this broad scope. For example, projects could focus on combining simulations using spatial-genetic-demographic individual based models (e.g., using the software SLiM), machine learning approaches, and genomic data to estimate larval dispersal distances from the spatial structure of genetic genealogies across the genome, and the genetic relatedness among individuals; or develop and use biophysical models (hydrodynamics + particle tracking) to understand the demographic and genetic dynamics of marine metapopulations and adaptation to environmental change. The PhD position provides an exciting opportunity to gain broad experience and expertise working at the interface of population genetics and demography, oceanography, and computer science. It will provide broad training in research skills, and will suit a candidate who is curious and is motivated to undertake high-level research to gain skills in computational methods and software tools to understand large, complex biological data. The position will be hosted within a dynamic international research group based at NTNU, with strong links to local and international collaborators. There will be opportunities for conference and workshop participation. The project supervisor will be Associate Professor Scott C. Burgess (Department of Biology, NTNU). Your immediate leader will be the head of department. Duties of the position Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate. Learn and apply advanced statistical and computational methods to analyze genetic data generated from simulations, outputs from biophysical models, or empirical genomic data to answer questions in spatial population genetics and marine metapopulation dynamics. Contribute to generating and managing reproducible computer code and workflows. Produce a high-quality PhD thesis, comprising of manuscripts suitable for publication in international peer-reviewed journals. Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Produce presentations for research dissemination. Contribute to building a collaborative and interactive local and international research team. Undertake teaching and other professional activities, as agreed with the Department of Biology. Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty’s Doctoral Programme. In particular, your previous education must be equivalent to a five-year Norwegian degree programme. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis. This corresponds to an undergraduate Bachelor degree and typically a 2-year Master’s degree. You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. Good oral and written communication and presentation skills in English. You must have a relevant background in ecology or evolution. You must have strong quantitative and computational skills. linkedin:4473616098.title: PhD position (all genders) in Computational Neuroscience and NeuroAI
linkedin:4473616098.desc: Main tasks Over the past decades, neuroscience has made remarkable progress in characterizing the architecture of biological neural networks. We now possess increasingly detailed descriptions of synaptic connectivity, cellular composition, laminar organization, mesoscale topology, and large-scale connectomes across multiple species. Across these diverse levels of organization, common structural principles have begun to emerge, including modularity, core-periphery organization, asymmetric reciprocity, and multi-scale network organization. Yet, despite this wealth of anatomical knowledge, a fundamental question remains unresolved: how do these structural features shape neural computation? Which aspects of biological connectivity are essential for flexible, robust, and adaptive information processing, and which are simply byproducts of development or evolution? This PhD project aims to bridge this gap by combining computational and network neuroscience with artificial intelligence to investigate how biologically inspired connectivity principles influence computation in recurrent neural networks. Research Environment The Institute of Computational Neuroscience is a small, active and internationally diverse group working at the interface of computational neuroscience, network science, neuro-inspired artificial intelligence and clinical neuroscience. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by Prof. Claus C. Hilgetag and Dr. Fatemeh Hadaeghi. About The Project A central methodological framework will be recurrent neural networks and reservoir computing models. Our goal is to uncover how biological wiring and functional organization can inform artificial neural network design and to translate these insights into models that operate effectively with low-precision (binary or ternary) weights. Main Aims Are To Explore bio-inspired backbones for unimodal temporal learning Develop modular and core-periphery architectures for multimodal learning Explore Scalability and real-world application. The work will involve close interaction with a strong computational and network neuroscience team at our institute. The position provides substantial scope for scientific initiative and intellectual ownership. The successful candidate may also contribute to the development of related research proposals and future funding applications. The position is funded through third-party research funding, comprises 65% of the regular weekly working hours, and provides the opportunity for obtaining the academic qualification of a PhD. linkedin:4480247952.desc: About The Position Digitalization and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming society, and the integration of AI into the maritime industry represents a digital shift that will redefine today’s operations. The maritime industry is increasingly embracing AI, enabling a broad digital transformation. At the same time, the use of AI introduce new cybersecurity challenges that need to be understood and addressed to enable secure and trustworthy AI technology. This PhD project will investigate cybersecurity challenges associated with the development and use of AI in the maritime domain. The project will have an interdisciplinary approach, combining insights from information security, artificial intelligence, maritime operations, and data engineering. The research may address cybersecurity risks related to the data used to develop AI models, the models themselves, or their integration and use in maritime applications. Relevant research topics may include cybersecurity risks related to training data and AI models, data poisoning and manipulation, privacy and confidentiality, secure data sharing, and methods for assessing the security and trustworthiness of maritime AI technology. The specific research questions and methodological approach will be further developed based on the candidate’s background and interests, relevant maritime AI use cases, and collaboration with industry partners. This position offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of cybersecurity, AI, and maritime operations in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners.
