linkedin:4482113481.desc: Job Description Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering? Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells , a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF). Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data. In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The group is part of the Catalysis Theory Center (CatTheory), which provides a strong infrastructure and computational facilities, including the Niflheim supercomputer with GPU nodes at DTU Physics. Responsibilities And Qualifications The successful candidate must have an MSc in physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or related areas, as well as a strong interest in atomistic modelling and machine learning for sustainable energy solutions. The candidate must display good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, be innovative and able to work both independently and in cross-disciplinary teams, as well as with international academic collaborators and industrial partners. Successful candidates must document: Experience with atomistic simulations & density functional theory (e.g. GPAW, VASP, ASE) Python programming skills Preferably, experience with machine-learning interatomic potentials (e.g. MACE, NequIP, or similar) Preferably, knowledge of solid oxide cells, oxide materials, electrochemistry or catalysis Preferably, experience with high-performance computing and Linux environments Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . Assessment You will be assessed against the responsibilities and qualifications stated above and the following general criteria: Atomistic modelling and DFT experience Python programming experience Machine learning experience Knowledge of materials science, electrochemistry or catalysis Communication skills We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is from 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Alexander Bagger ( alexbag@dtu.dk ). You can read more about DTU Physics at https://physics.dtu.dk/ . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. This project aims to create a new generation of injectable therapeutic hydrogels that combine beneficial probiotics and bacteriophages to simultaneously eradicate bacterial infections and promote tissue regeneration. With a strong translational focus, the project seeks to advance these living therapeutic systems toward clinically relevant solutions for wound infections and antimicrobial resistance. Your tasks You will contribute to the development of injectable, self-healing biomaterial-based hydrogels for the local delivery of probiotics and bacteriophages to wound sites. Your work will involve: Design and synthesis of injectable hydrogel systems Encapsulation and controlled delivery of probiotics and bacteriophages Engineering and characterization of phage-based antimicrobial strategies against pathogenic bacteria and biofilms Characterization and optimization of hydrogel properties and biological functionality Evaluation of tissue regeneration and the therapeutic potential of living therapeutics Elucidation of mechanisms of action and investigation of antimicrobial resistance evolution Your profile We are looking for a highly motivated and curious candidate with: A Master's degree in Biomaterials, Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, Microbiology, Molecular Biology, Chemistry, or a related field Strong interest in antimicrobial resistance, biomaterials, microbiology, or phage therapy Experience in one or more of the following areas: Microbiology and bacterial culture / Biofilm research / Biomaterials and hydrogels / Molecular biology or synthetic biology / Bacteriophages Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to an interdisciplinary team Previous experience with phages, hydrogels, wound healing models, or antimicrobial testing is advantageous. Our offer A highly international and multidisciplinary research environment Access to state-of-the-art research infrastructure Scientific training spanning microbiology, biomaterials engineering, phage biology, and translational biomedical research Close collaboration with leading bacteriophage experts at ETH Zurich and opportunities to work across disciplines A stimulating work environment within one of Switzerland's leading research institutions Attractive employment conditions according to Empa regulations The position is available from November 2026 or after negotiation with a duration of four years. We live a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities - that's what counts. We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

linkedin:4482112695.title: Doktorand i arbetsintegrerat lärande (AIL) med fokus på palliativ vård
linkedin:4482112695.desc: Högskolan Väst drivs av att göra skillnad. Genom vår utbildning och forskning vill vi bidra till innovation, en positiv samhällsutveckling och en hållbar värld. Vi är en modern högskola under stark utveckling och att samverka med omvärlden är prioriterat för oss. Högskolan Väst har ett av landets högsta söktryck och en hög andel av studenterna etablerar sig på arbetsmarknaden. Högskolan har 13 000 studenter och över 700 anställda. Vårt attraktiva campus ligger centralt i Trollhättan och är en plats där kunskaper, idéer, kulturer och människor möts. Vi jobbar aktivt för en inkluderande arbetsmiljö med jämställda förhållanden och sätter värde på de kvaliteter som mångfald tillför verksamheten. Vi som arbetar på Högskolan Väst gör skillnad varje dag. Vill du också det? Doktorand i arbetsintegrerat lärande med inriktning mot palliativ vård. Högskolan Väst söker nu en doktorand i arbetsintegrerat lärande till ett Kamprad-finansierat projekt inom forskningsgruppen NormAIL på Institutionen för hälsovetenskap. Centrala kunskapsområden i avhandlingsarbetet är arbetsintegrerat lärande (AIL), vårdvetenskap och virtual reality (VR). Du intresserar dig för frågor om hur VR kan användas vid utbildning i palliativ vård för personal inom demensvård inom kommunal vård- och omsorg. Projektet fokuserar på hur digitala lärmiljöer kan stödja kompetensutveckling och bidra till att stärka personalens förmåga att möta komplexa vårdsituationer i den dagliga verksamheten. Det kan exempelvis handla om: • Hur VR och AI kan användas vid utbildning i palliativ vård för personer med demens inom kommunal vård- och omsorg. • Hur lärande inom palliativ vård påverkar vård och omsorg för personer med demens. • Hur utbildning med stöd av VR och AI påverkar bemötande av personer i livets slut. • Hur ett vetenskapligt förhållningssätt påverkar personal i kommunal vård och omsorg. Doktorandens vetenskapliga arbete i projektet Doktorandens vetenskapliga arbete kommer att genomföras inom ramen för ett forskningsprojekt med fokus mot palliativ vård i demensvård, inom kommunal vård och omsorg. Projektet tar sin utgångspunkt i de förändrade villkor som kommer med en åldrande befolkning och en pågående förskjutning av vården från slutenvård till kommunal vård och omsorg. Projektet undersöker hur virtual reality i kombination med en avatar kan stödja lärande och kompetensutveckling hos personal på ett särskilt boende för personer med demenssjukdom. En central fråga är hur denna form av lärande kan integreras i personalens arbete och hur erfarenheter från vårdpraktiken kan tas till vara. Doktorandprojektet syftar till att bidra till utvecklingen av framtidens utbildningsinsatser inom kommunal vård och omsorg, med särskilt fokus på palliativ vård och demensvård. Genom forskning med hög samhällsrelevans förväntas projektet generera kunskap som kan stärka kvaliteten i vården för äldre personer med komplexa vårdbehov. Projektet ska också bidra med kunskap om förutsättningarna för arbetsintegrerat lärande när ny teknik används för kompetensutveckling inom vård och omsorg. Ämnesområde: Arbetsintegrerat lärande (AIL) Forskningsmiljö: Som doktorand vid institutionen för hälsovetenskap tillhör du forskarutbildningen inom AIL vid Högskolan Väst. Du blir verksam i en stark doktorand- och forskningsmiljö som ger möjlighet att förena perspektiv på lärande i arbetslivet med vårdvetenskapliga frågor inom palliativ vård och demensvård. Arbetsuppgifter: Forskarutbildningen innebär, förutom deltagande i forskarutbildningens kurser och andra aktiviteter, genomförande av ett självständigt avhandlingsarbete. Som doktorand ägnas anställningstiden framför allt åt forskarutbildning. En doktorand får dock i begränsad omfattning arbeta med utbildning och administration. Sådant arbete får, innan doktorsexamen har avlagts, inte omfatta mer än 20 % av full arbetstid (Högskoleförordningen 5 kap 2§). Eventuell institutionstjänstgöring (20 %) genomförs huvudsakligen inom undervisningsfältet omvårdnad/vårdvetenskap. Behörighetskrav: För att kvalificera sig för anställning som doktorand krävs att två behörighetskrav är uppfyllda: 1) grundläggande behörighet och 2) särskild behörighet. Grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå har den som: har avlagt examen på grund- och avancerad nivå, fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. Särskild behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå i arbetsintegrerat lärande har den som har: Examen på avancerad nivå med relevans för forskarutbildningsämnet arbetsintegrerat lärande. Examensarbete omfattande minst 15 hp på avancerad nivå eller annat skriftligt arbete av motsvarande karaktär och omfång. Behörighetskraven kan uppfyllas av studier i Sverige eller utomlands. För denna anställning krävs dessutom: God förmåga att kommunicera muntligt och skriftligt på svenska och engelska. Meriterande för anställningen är följande kvalifikationer: Examen inom vårdvetenskap/omvårdnad Utbildning och arbetslivserfarenhet inom demensvård/ palliativvård Erfarenhet av VR och AI i kontexten lärande och/eller vård Tidigare vetenskaplig publicering Bedömningsgrunder: Urval bland sökande ska göras med hänsyn till förmågan att tillgodogöra sig forskarutbildningen, vilket avser vetenskaplig kvalitet på tidigare arbeten samt förslag på avhandlingsinriktning, ämnets relevans och genomförbarhet i förhållande till arbetsintegrerat lärande (AIL). Vid bedömningen av projektets genomförbarhetgenomförbarhet kommer även sökandens kunskap och kompetens inom vårdvetenskap, demens, palliativ vård och VR/AI att väga tungt. Under punkt 3 i Allmän studieplan för utbildningen på forskarnivå i Arbetsinegrerat Lärande Dnr 2021/159 kan du läsa mer om behörighetskrav och bedömningsgrunder. Varaktighet och anställningsvillkor: En anställning som doktorand ska gälla tillsvidare, dock längst till en viss tidpunkt och aldrig längre tid än ett år efter avlagd doktorsexamen. Den första anställningen får gälla högst ett år. Anställningen får förnyas med högst två år i taget. Anställningen motsvarar fyra års heltidsstudier under maximalt åtta år (Högskoleförordningen 5 kap 7§). Ansökan Ansökan görs digitalt via Högskolan Västs rekryteringsverktyg Varbi via högskolans webbplats. Ansökan ska bestå av: CV/Meritförteckning Personligt brev innehållande: Intresse för forskningsämnet Tidigare erfarenhet av det föreslagna forskningsämnet och dess forskningsmetoder och vetenskapliga teorier Motiv till att bedriva forskarstudier Examensbevis för kandidat- och masternivå Examensarbete på avancerad nivå Kursförteckning/transcript över alla terminer för kandidat- och masterexamen på originalspråk samt i översättning En kort vetenskaplig reflektion (max två sidor exkl. referenser) med utgångspunkt i den projektbeskrivning som presenteras i utlysningen. Texten ska behandla och problematisera projektets övergripande syfte och ambition att bidra till utvecklingen av framtidens utbildningsinsatser inom kommunal vård och omsorg, med särskilt fokus på palliativ vård för personer med demenssjukdom. Reflektionen ska även beskriva hur ett arbetsintegrerat lärande kan stödja kompetensutveckling och bidra till att stärka personalens arbete samt hur projektet kan bidra till kunskapsutveckling inom AIL. Övriga handlingar som sökanden vill åberopa. Godkända skrivspråk gällande uppsatser, examensbevis, betyg och andra relevanta dokument är skandinaviska språk och engelska, eller översättningar till dessa språk. Vid översättning bifogas även originaltext. Om du har pågående studier på avancerad nivå kan du ansöka och därefter komplettera din ansökan med godkänt examensarbete, giltigt examensbevis och andra behörighetsdokument för sista dagen för ansökan. Din ansökan ska vara Högskolan Väst tillhanda senast 2026-11-11 . De underlag som inte kan skickas digitalt märks med ref.nr R 2026/170 och skickas till: HR-avdelningen Högskolan Väst 461 86 Trollhättan Sverige Institutionen för hälsovetenskap eftersträvar jämställdhet och mångfald inom samtliga yrkesgrupper. Vi välkomnar sökande med olika etniska och kulturella bakgrunder. För oss är det självklart med ett inkluderande arbetsklimat och att våra medarbetare kan kombinera arbete med ett aktivt föräldraskap. Välkommen med din ansökan! Vi undanber oss all direktkontakt med bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag samt försäljare av rekryteringsannonser.

Eva Mennigen. The International Research Training Group “Risks and Pathomechanisms of Affective Disorders” (IRTG 2773) is funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). It is a structured international graduate program conducted in cooperation between the Technical University (TU) Dresden and the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at King’s College London. The successful candidate will receive comprehensive supervision by an experienced scientific team, including participation in a structured curriculum. This curriculum covers topics from developmental neuroscience, child and adolescent as well as adult psychiatry, clinical and cognitive psychology, and in particular computational science. Using repeated clinical, neuroimaging, genetic, immunological, and behavioural data, we will model latent dimensions of risk and resilience and examine their developmental trajectories in relation to the clinical manifestation of affective disorders. linkedin:4482148186.desc: Some features of our web site require JavaScript to function properly. Please enable JavaScript in your browser. Position PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on ML-methods in climate modelling Employer The Department of Meteorology, Stockholm University The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. You can read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology. Homepage: https://www.su.se/english/divisions/department-of-meteorology Location Stockholm, Sweden Sector Academic Relevant divisions Atmospheric Sciences (AS) Ocean Sciences (OS) Type Full time Level Student / Graduate / Internship Salary Open Preferred Education Master Application deadline 3 November 2026 Posted 21 October 2026 Job Description Project description Clouds and their responses to varying environmental conditions are particularly important determinants of current climate and future climate change. However, the resolution of a typical climate model is far too coarse to explicitly represent processes of relevance to cloud formation. Those processes therefore need to be parameterized, or represented as functions of large-scale state variables. Such sub-grid scale parameterizations are associated with large uncertainties, and are also computationally expensive. This project focuses on novel ways to bridge between micro- and global scales, to improve climate model accuracy, efficiency and generalizability, and leverage modern computer architecture. We will explore the use of machine learning (ML) models trained on combinations of observational data and high-resolution simulations, as alternatives to empirical parameterizations of essential, unresolved sub-grid scale processes related to turbulence, cloud formation and aerosol-cloud interaction. The tasks will include deriving and training data-driven models, coupling them to a large-scale climate model, evaluating the results against observations and traditionally parameterized models, and using the ML-enhanced model to estimate climate-relevant quantities like cloud radiative effects and forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with data scientists within the Swedish e-Science Research Centre, and contribute to development of methods with applicability also beyond climate science. The successful candidate will thereby develop their skills in atmospheric science and climate modelling, but also in data science and machine learning, and in communicating and collaborating within and across disciplines. Qualification Requirements In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be fulfilled before admission to the programme. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. The specific entry requirements additionally require a minimum of 90 higher education credits in any of the fields of meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry; and at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics as well as a degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. At least 60 higher education credits of these courses must be on the second-cycle level. In addition, proficiency in English language, equivalent to English B in Swedish high school, is required. The specific entry requirements may also be fulfilled by a person who has otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. General syllabus for doctoral studies in atmospheric science and oceanography. Selection The selection between candidates who meet the entry requirements will be made with reference to their ability to benefit from the training. However, the fact that an applicant is deemed able to transfer credits from previous training or professional experience may not alone give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Admission decisions are made in accordance with current delegation policies. The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme. Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University. About The Employment Starting date as per agreement. We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %). A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. Contact For more information about the project, please contact professor Frida Bender, frida.bender@misu.su.se. For more information about the PhD programme, please contact the study director, Associate Professor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. indeed:108485d5b3bd8949.desc: Login and apply The Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology, School of Computing The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in the field of Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data at the School of Computing on the Kuopio campus. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application by 17 November 2026. Role and salary The demand for minerals required for energy transition and digitalisation is expanding mining faster than our ability to understand its impacts. MINE-THE-GAP (website), funded by the European Research Council (ERC), combines satellite imagery, mining data reports, and AI to map mining activities and their impacts worldwide and provide the information needed for more transparent and sustainable mining. We are seeking three motivated Doctoral Researchers (PhD Students) to join the project, each leading their own thesis on mapping different aspects of mining. As part of the MINE-THE-GAP team, you will, as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), have the opportunity to apply your data science and programming skills to a global sustainability challenge and to become an expert in handling large Earth observation datasets and scalable AI. We offer three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in a research group with strong international visibility. You will receive hands-on training in the processing of large Earth observation and spatial datasets, as well as in scalable AI methods, developing highly sought-after skills for careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations. The position provides opportunities for international collaboration and research visits abroad through an extensive network of partner institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Monash University Indonesia, and the University of Melbourne. You will benefit from close supervision, mentoring, and a supportive team environment, along with dedicated funding for conference participation, workshops, and scientific publications. One Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will be recruited for each of the following three research topics: mining land use: semantic segmentation of satellite images to map mining areas (e.g., open pits, waste rock piles, tailings dams) mining waste: predicting terrain height changes from radar and optical satellite image time series to estimate mining waste minerals and commodities: image classification with multispectral and hyperspectral data to identify the minerals and commodities of mining sites. Within your chosen research topic, you will build, train, and validate scalable deep learning and computer vision models using large, multi-modal Earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, LiDAR, hyperspectral). You will work closely with the principal investigator, Victor Maus, postdoctoral researchers, and international collaborators, publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to open science. Your main duty as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for the doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). The positions will be filled for a fixed term due to the Doctoral Researcher’s (PhD Student’s) own doctoral dissertation work and studies. A trial period is applied to all new members of the staff. The salary of the position is determined in accordance with the salary system for Finnish universities. The salary comprises two components: a job-related salary element and a personal salary element. For a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), the job-related salary element is based on levels 2–4 of the job requirement level chart for teaching and research staff depending on the stage of the applicant’s doctoral research and postgraduate studies. The personal salary element is 6–50% of the job-related salary element. At the beginning of the employment, the total salary will be approximately EUR 2,710–2,845 /month. Our requirements and expectations We require you to be eligible for postgraduate studies; i.e., to hold a Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Geoinformatics, Statistics, or a related field) awarded by a university or by a university of applied sciences, or to have completed an applicable study programme abroad which in the awarding country gives eligibility for corresponding postgraduate education meet the student admission criteria for the LUMETO doctoral programme (Doctoral Programme in Science, Forestry and Technology, website) have a good command of written and spoken English. Students in the final stages of their Master’s degree may also apply provided that they complete their degree and deliver a copy of their degree certificate to the faculty by 15 December 2026. Applicants who do not yet have the right to pursue postgraduate studies at the University of Eastern Finland are not required to apply for study rights at the application stage. If the applicant is selected for the position and applies for postgraduate study rights, the selection will be conditional until the right to pursue postgraduate studies in the faculty’s doctoral programme has been granted. The application for postgraduate study rights is submitted through the Studyinfo (Opintopolku) service. Other requirements good programming skills (e.g., Python/R) interest in machine learning and spatial data. The following will be considered an advantage experience with machine learning or deep learning (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) or strong motivation to learn these skills experience with Earth observation or geospatial data, desirable, but we encourage anyone with a strong willingness to learn to apply experience with cloud computing or collaborative software development (e.g., GitHub) is also welcome. Your benefits You will have access to the university’s staff benefits, including the opportunity for flexible multi-location work excellent opportunities for professional development and continuous learning extensive occupational health care a broad selection of staff training staff discount on lunch in our campus restaurants, as well as on a range of other services affordable sports services. Please read more in the Work at UEF section on our website. You will have an opportunity to work in meaningful as part of our international, creative, participatory and inclusive academic community. Enjoy your life in Finland! Known for its cleanliness, welfare know-how, modern technology and superb education system, Finland is an exotic and safe country to work in. Please visit the Life in Finland section on our website to learn more. How to apply? Submit your application by using our electronic application form no later than 17 November 2026 by 23:59 (midnight) Finnish time (UTC+2). Please note that you must include the following appendices in your application CV (Template for CV, TENK web page) a list of publications (Instructions, Research Council of Finland Web page) copies of your academic degree certificates / diplomas, and copies of certificates / diplomas relating to your language proficiency, if not indicated in the academic degree certificates/diplomas a transcript of records a motivation letter (max. 1 page) describing your interest in the position and research project, your background, as well as your career aspirations and your motivation for engaging in doctoral-level research. External evaluation will be used in the recruitment process. If your degree certificate is not in English, Finnish, or Swedish, you must provide official English translations of your degree certificate documents. indeed:3c2ed42fbb9af34b.title: PhD Position F/M Detecting Dangerous Browser Extensions to Protect the Security and Privacy of Web Users
indeed:3c2ed42fbb9af34b.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Doctorant A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle Inria is the French National Institute for Research in Digital Science, of which the Inria Côte d'Azur University Center is a part. With strong expertise in computer science and applied mathematics, the research projects of the Inria Côte d'Azur University Center cover all aspects of digital science and technology and generate innovation. Based mainly in Sophia Antipolis, but also in Nice and Montpellier, it brings together 47 research teams and nine support services. It is active in the fields of artificial intelligence, data science, IT system security, robotics, network engineering, natural risk prevention, ecological transition, digital biology, computational neuroscience, health data, and more. The Inria Center at Université Côte d'Azur is a major player in terms of scientific excellence, thanks to the results it has achieved and its collaborations at both European and international level. Contexte et atouts du poste The PhD position is funded by the French National Research Agency (ANR). It is part of Aurore Fass' ANR JCJC project "EXPELLIARMUS: Disarming Dangerous Browser Extensions to Protect the Security and Privacy of Web Users". EXPELLIARMUS, aims to develop methods to "disarm" dangerous extensions to better protect the security and privacy of Web users. More specifically, it will detect, understand, and mitigate dangerous browser extensions through an interdisciplinary approach combining computer science, human factors, and legal analysis. EXPELLIARMUS will deliver a systematic taxonomy of dangerous extension behaviors, open-source datasets and detection tools, as well as actionable recommendations for users, browser vendors, developers, and regulators. The PhD student will be part of the research team led by Dr. Nataliia Bielova (https://www-sop.inria.fr/members/Nataliia.Bielova/index.html) at the Inria Centre at Université Côte d’Azur at the French Riviera. The PhD student will be supervised by Dr.-Ing. Aurore Fass (https://aurore54f.github.io/). Note that a PhD in France typically lasts 3 years. Mission confiée Context on Browser Extension Security Given the central role of the Web in our daily lives and its overall impact on society and economy, it is crucial that Web pages and browser extensions assure the security and privacy of their large user base. Browser extensions have become an integral part of the modern Web ecosystem. The most popular desktop browser Chrome lists 280k browser extensions [1] (totaling almost 3 billion active users) in its official gallery, the Chrome Web Store [2]. Browser extensions enable users to enhance and customize their browsing experience: typically, extensions offer additional functionality to Web users, such as ad blocking (e.g., AdBlock), grammar checks (e.g., Grammarly), or password management (e.g., LastPass). To operate, browser extensions need elevated privileges compared to Web pages. Browser extensions can access sensitive user data, such as cookies or browsing history, and they can interact with arbitrary websites and other extensions [3, 4, 5]. While a compromised or malicious Web page is in itself troublesome, a malicious or vulnerable browser extension is much more powerful, as an attacker can leverage an extension's elevated privileges to cause more harm [3]. In particular, browser extensions can exfiltrate sensitive user data [6], track users online [7], or propagate unwanted software [8]. Detecting such threats at scale remains a challenge, as the extension ecosystem is particularly large, diverse, and continuously evolving. Limitations of existing work Abundant prior work attempted to detect some classes of dangerous extensions [9], e.g., malicious [10], vulnerable [3], or fingerprintable extensions [11]. However, related works have major limitations. Existing works analyze only hundreds of extensions [12], are outdated (e.g., 2012–2015 [8, 13, 14, 15]), have limited scalability and necessitate significant manual effort [16, 4], lack a clear characterization of what a dangerous behavior is [14]; and finally, only a small minority thereof is open source, as we have highlighted in [10]. Besides, existing machine learning-based detectors are opaque, they lack interpretability and explainability. It is therefore critical to design automated, large-scale, and reliable security and privacy analyses of browser extensions that have the potential to be deployed in the real world. Chrome Web Store. https://chromewebstore.google.com [3] Aurore Fass , Dolière Francis Somé, Michael Backes, and Ben Stock. DoubleX: Statically Detecting Vulnerable Data Flows in Browser Extensions at Scale. In ACM CCS, 2021. Code repository: https://github.com/Aurore54F/DoubleX [4] Dolière Francis Somé. Empoweb: Empowering web applications with browser extensions. In IEEE S&P, 2019. [5] Jianjia Yu, Song Li, Junmin Zhu, and Yinzhi Cao. [7] Michael Weissbacher, Enrico Mariconti, Guillermo Suarez-Tangil, Gianluca Stringhini, William Robertson, and Engin Kirda. Ex-ray: Detection of history-leaking browser extensions. In ACSAC, 2017. In USENIX Security, 2012. [13] Nav Jagpal, Eric Dingle, Jean-Philippe Gravel, Panayiotis Mavrommatis, Niels Provos, Moheeb Abu Rajab, and Kurt Thomas. Principales activités Objectives of the PhD The broad objective of this PhD is to develop new automated tools to detect dangerous browser extensions , with a specific focus on malicious extensions. While the majority of prior work focuses on Chrome, we also want to study dangerous extensions on other browsers, such as Firefox and Edge, since we showed that the same malicious extensions can be published on multiple galleries [1]. Objective 1 : Generate a large-scale dataset of browser extensions. Establish a systematic and comprehensive taxonomy of dangerous browser extension behaviors. Objective 2 : Design novel, automated, and explainable methods to detect dangerous browser extensions, combining JavaScript static and lightweight dynamic analyses, predictive machine learning, and Large-Language Models. Provide interpretable and continuously adaptable detection models. Objective 3 (in collaboration with a postdoctoral researcher, to be recruited): Assess how different stakeholders (i.e., platform maintainers, developers, and users) understand and manage the underlying security and privacy risks of browser extensions. Keywords : Web Security & Privacy, Browser Extensions, Dangerous Behavior Detection, Code Analysis, Applied Machine Learning, (Human Factors). Bereich Institut für Oberflächenforschung Standort Geesthacht Aluminium and magnesium alloys are key to lighter vehicles, aircraft, drones and consumer goods but only if they are safe and durable, reliably protected against corrosion. Chemical conversion coatings are one of the most effective and commercially successful ways to do this. They protect the metal and help paint adhere to it. Yet finding better, environmentally friendly formulations is still largely a matter of trial and error. The number of possible formulations is virtually infinite, so we do not test them one by one. At the Department of Electrochemistry and Big Data, we run a robotic high-throughput testing platform combined with machine learning for AI-assisted discoveries. We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a PhD student in the quickly developing field of high-throughput and robotic experimentation in materials science. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply. Your tasks Develop and validate experimental methods for the accelerated screening of chemical conversion treatment formulations Translate these methods into automated high-throughput workflows on our existing robotic testing platform Work side by side with our computational scientists to build large, machine-readable datasets for AI-assisted discovery Uncover the mechanisms behind effective adhesion promotion and corrosion protection, and turn them into design rules for next-generation coatings Publish your results in leading journals, present at international conferences, write project reports, and contribute to open, FAIR datasets Your profile A completed master's degree in chemistry, electrochemistry, materials science, computational materials science or a related field Solid experimental skills in chemical laboratories and confidence in quantitative data analysis using appropriate software Experience with corrosion protection, including chemical conversion coatings for light alloys (Mg, Al or Zn) Experience with electronic lab notebooks, FAIR data, databases or machine learning Curiosity about automation and AI, and motivation to work at the interface of experiment and computation Very good English, knowledge of the German language is preferred but not mandatory, we support language learning Content-related enquiries regarding this position can be directed to Sviatlana.Lamaka@hereon.de. indeed:39c1cab975bc3e35.desc: Vacature ID: 16964 Functie categorie: PhD-posities Aanstellingsomvang in uren min: 38 Aanstellingsomvang in uren max: 38 Standplaats: Leiden Solliciteren kan tot en met: 11 januari 2028 The Institute of Environmental Sciences CML and Faculty of Science is looking for: PhD Researcher Excited to explore how population decline and changing demographic structures redefine urban planning, where and what we decide (not) to build, and what this means for resource demand and the environment? Key responsibilities The primary objective of this PhD project is to advance understanding of how spatial population distribution, demographic change (including aging population and smaller households), and urban form jointly shape future resource demand and GHG emissions. The project will evaluate core trade-offs, balancing the efficiency gains of urban density against the rise in vacant buildings and underutilized infrastructure caused by regional depopulation. Ultimately, the research will inform urban and regional development strategies to minimize net land take and GHG emissions, while catering to the needs of changing populations across the rural-urban continuum. As a PhD researcher on this project, you will: Develop high-resolution activity demand models for the building energy and transport sectors under future spatially refined European demographic projections. Integrate demand projections with material flow and life-cycle models to quantify future energy requirements, material intensity, and GHG emissions. Evaluate adaptive re-use and circular strategies for vacant buildings and underutilized transport infrastructure in depopulating or aging regions. Design integrated spatial planning scenarios that combine built environment transformations with transport infrastructure investments to support low resource and emission development pathways across population change and urban/rural contexts Where you will work Leiden University is situated between Amsterdam (36 km) and The Hague (15 km) and was founded in 1575, making it the oldest university in the Netherlands. It houses around 35,000 students originating from 112 nationalities, facilitated by approximately 8,000 staff. indeed:fa906069b66eb67d.title: PhD Candidate in Cell-Matrix Interactions in Dynamic Hydrogels
indeed:fa906069b66eb67d.desc: PhD Candidate in Cell-Matrix Interactions in Dynamic Hydrogels Welcome to Maastricht University! Join us in developing cell-instructive and adaptive supramolecular biomaterials. In this PhD project, you will investigate how the molecular organization, mechanics, dynamics, and presentation of biological signals within hydrogels influence cell behavior. You will then help extend these principles toward living materials in which engineered cells actively modify their surrounding matrix. PhD Candidate in Cell-Matrix Interactions in Dynamic Hydrogels Discover how dynamic supramolecular matrices instruct cells and how cells can, in turn, reshape and improve the material around them Our goal: To establish predictive relationships between supramolecular hydrogel design and cell response, and to use these insights to create adaptive materials with two-way communication between cells and their matrix. Your colleagues: You will join the BioMatt group of Dr. Matthew Baker (https://merlninstitute.com/discover-merln/departments-and-groups/research-groups/biomatt-polymeric-biomaterials). The BioMatt group is part of MERLN’s Department of Instructive Biomaterials Engineering (IBE), which develops biomaterials that actively interact with and guide biological systems. Within this environment, BioMatt combines molecular and polymer design with cell biology and tissue engineering to create dynamic materials for biomedical applications. Working at MERLN means joining an international network of researchers from approximately 25 nationalities and a collaborative community spanning biomaterials, chemistry, mechanobiology, tissue engineering, biofabrication, microbiology, and cell biology. You will work in newly renovated laboratories with access to state-of-the-art facilities and close scientific support from colleagues across the SupraValent team. What you do This position leads the cell–matrix interaction and mechanobiology line within the ERC Consolidator project SupraValent. You will use both design and use established hydrogel platforms and processing workflows from the team to determine how material properties are sensed by cells and how cells feed back on their environment. You will: Design and create supramolecular hydrogels with control over biofunctionalization via peptide cues Establish robust 2D and 3D cell-culture workflows in supramolecular and dynamically reinforced hydrogels. Determine how stiffness, stress relaxation, network architecture, and dynamic covalent reinforcement influence cell adhesion, morphology, mechanotransduction, phenotype, and matrix production. Investigate how the molecular-scale presentation and accessibility of cell-adhesive or other bioactive ligands affect cellular responses, including cases where bulk material properties are closely matched. Study reciprocal cell–matrix interactions, including cell-mediated remodeling, deposition of extracellular matrix, and changes in hydrogel structure or mechanics over time. Work closely with team members to evaluate engineered cells within hydrogel environments and determine whether their activity can controllably build, reinforce, functionalize, or remodel the material. Contribute to experimental design, data analysis, publications, conference presentations, and supervision of students within the multidisciplinary BioMatt team. The project will initially use well-defined cells and previously created materials and will develop toward novel materials designs with engineered living-material concepts in collaboration. Specific cell types and biological questions will be selected according to the strongest mechanistic opportunities and collaborations. Are you ready to connect molecular material design with cell function? Then we would love to meet you. Scientific background Cells respond not only to the chemical composition and stiffness of their extracellular matrix, but also to its viscoelasticity, molecular organization, ligand presentation, and capacity to change over time. These variables are difficult to control independently in conventional hydrogels. SupraValent combines reversible benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxamide (BTA) self-assembly with covalent and dynamic-covalent modification to create materials whose mechanics, dynamics, and functionality can be adjusted after assembly. The project has established a growing molecular toolbox and hydrogel platforms with tunable stress relaxation, self-healing, reinforcement, and processing behavior. The next challenge is to determine how to make these material features more biologically meaningful. This PhD project will move beyond simple viability testing to resolve how cells sense local and bulk properties, how these cues influence mechanotransduction and matrix production, and how cellular activity changes the material over time. In the later phase, the candidate will work towards a central SupraValent concept: living cells that do more than survive within a hydrogel, instead actively contributing to its construction, reinforcement, or functional adaptation. This fully funded 4-year PhD position offers training at the interface of supramolecular and polymer chemistry, mechanobiology, cell biology, and biomaterials, while remaining embedded in a highly collaborative research environment. Key references Hafeez et al. Advanced Materials 2023, 35, 2207053. https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.202207053 Hafeez et al. Advanced Materials 2023, 35, 2301242. https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.202301242 Ruiter et al. Advanced Science 2022, 9, 2200543. https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202200543 Rijns et al. JACS 2024, 146, 17539–17588. https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.4c02980 What you bring We are interested in the combination of experience, motivation, and perspective you would bring. The ideal candidate is a careful and curious experimental scientist who wants to understand cell–material interactions on a molecular scale. You are comfortable 1) working with cells, interested in quantitative analysis, or 2) molecularly designing and characterizing soft polymer materials. In the project you should be excited to learn both as part of the PhD trajectory. Furthermore, you bring: An MSc (or equivalent) in Biomaterials, Polymer Chemistry, Tissue Engineering, Cell Biology, Biotechnology, Bioengineering, or a closely related field. Candidates with an equivalent research qualification from an educational system without a separate Master’s degree are also encouraged to apply; eligibility will be assessed individually Substantial hands-on experience with either mammalian cell culture or biomaterials design acquired through an MSc thesis, extended research project, or relevant research position, including (cell culture) aseptic technique, experimental planning, and reliable maintenance of cell-based assays or (biomaterials) polymer functionalization, soft matter characterization, hydrogel formation. Experience studying cells in contact with biomaterials, hydrogels, extracellular-matrix models, or other engineered microenvironments. Direct experience with 3D cell culture or cell encapsulation is highly desirable. Interest in mechanobiology and in relating cell behavior to material properties such as stiffness, stress relaxation, ligand presentation, or remodeling. Prior rheology or mechanical-characterization experience is helpful but not required. The ability to document experiments clearly, analyze data critically, troubleshoot protocols, and communicate across disciplinary boundaries. Experience with extracellular-matrix deposition, cell-mediated remodeling, engineered cells, microbial culture, or engineered living materials is considered an advantage, but is not required. Excellent command of scientific English (minimum CEFR level C1), as English is the working language of the group. Availability to start the position on short notice is highly desirable; however, the start date remains flexible for highly qualified applicants. What we offer At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer: A 12-month contract (1,0 FTE) with the prospect of a 3 year extension based on mutual satisfaction. A gross monthly salary between € 3.204 and € 4.051 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus. 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours. Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas. A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with. A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities. An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe. About the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML) FHML is committed to health in the broadest sense: from molecule to human, and from healthcare to prevention. We train healthcare professionals and researchers through innovative educational programs and conduct groundbreaking research in health and well-being. As part of Maastricht UMC+ (MUMC+), our international and interdisciplinary community forms a unique collaboration between university and academic hospital, where education, research, and care come together. About MERLN Research Institute MERLN (Institute for Technology-Inspired Regenerative Medicine) within FHML develops new technologies for the repair, regeneration, and in vitro modeling of tissues and organs. Within MERLN, the Department of Instructive Biomaterials Engineering (IBE) uses materials science and engineering to design biomaterials for applications ranging from medical devices and scaffolds for regenerative therapies to predictive in vitro models. By controlling material chemistry, structure, mechanics, and biological functionality, IBE researchers create systems that actively interact with and guide biological processes. The department brings together expertise in polymeric, inorganic, supramolecular, and bioactive materials at the interface of chemistry, engineering, and regenerative medicine. Interested? Please submit: CV Cover letter explaining your motivation and relevant experience Names and contact details of two referees The selection process consists of two interviews: one conducted online and one on-site. During the on-site interview, candidates will be asked to give a presentation, followed by individual meetings with team members. For more information about the scientific content of the position, contact Dr. Matthew Baker via m.baker@maastrichtuniversity.nl. Apply now via the button below. We look forward to getting to know you! About Maastricht University At Maastricht University, we collaboratively seek solutions to help move the world forward. We do this with 23,300 students and 5,400 employees across 5 regional locations, 6 faculties, and more than 70 research institutes. We encourage you to push boundaries and discover new opportunities for yourself and the world around you. Together, we can find the answers for tomorrow. The vacancy is open to internal and external candidates. In case of equal qualifications, internal candidates will be prioritized. indeed:d2db4a63698d39ad.title: PhD Position: Multisynaptic Plasticity in Dendrites
indeed:d2db4a63698d39ad.desc: Employment 0.8 - 1.0 FTE Gross monthly salary € 3,204 - € 4,051 Required background Research University Degree Organizational unit Faculty of Science Application deadline 08 November 2026 Are you an enthusiastic young scientist with a Master's degree in a neuroscience-related field? And would you like to figure out how plasticity at multiple synapses is coordinated within dendrites? Then you have a part to play as a PhD candidate in our research team. Put your ideas to the test at our green campus and push your boundaries in an internationally friendly environment. Synaptic plasticity is considered to be the foundation of brain adaptation and learning. Multiple signalling pathways have been identified that are underlying synaptic plasticity of single synapses, depending on induction protocol and cell type. However, linking these molecular pathways to behavioural adaptation and learning turned out to be difficult. Under physiological conditions in vivo, multiple synapses will be activated simultaneously and plasticity pathways will inherently interfere. In this PhD project, we will use a combination of single cell electrophysiology, advanced microscopy techniques and novel biosensors to examine molecular pathways underlying multisynaptic plasticity in dendrites of hippocampal CA1 neurons in brain slices. Research in the Wierenga lab focuses on the formation and plasticity of inhibitory synapses and the interactions between inhibitory and excitatory synapses within dendrites. In this project, you will use two-photon glutamate uncaging in hippocampal slices to induce synaptic plasticity at multiple spines and you will exploit novel biosensors to study interactions between molecular pathways within the dendrite. Furthermore, you will explore how these interactions are affected by neuromodulators. Pilot experiments with four spine stimulation have shown that large calcium signals emerge within the dendritic shaft that continue even after the stimulation has ended, and that there are at least two modes of spine growth that seem to be regulated independently. The research has the following objectives: To determine how calcium release from internal stores contributes to dendritic calcium signals. To investigate how PKA and PKC activity interacts with calcium signals. To assess if these interactions can explain the two modes of spine growth. To examine when and where molecular signalling molecules (aka retrograde messengers) are produced. Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time. Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate . At Radboud University, I can fully focus on expanding my expertise while learning from my peers and mentors. Noemí Segura-Solé PhD candidate in Microbial Ecology Read Noemí's story Does this sound like you? You are a highly motivated, enthusiastic, critical, creative and team-oriented young scientist with a particular interest in neuroscience. You have a Master's degree in life sciences, biology, biomedical sciences or a related discipline, and an interest in intracellular signalling and optical recording methods. You have experience in advanced microscopy and/or single cell (patch clamp) electrophysiology in living brain tissue. Ideally, you can program (in Matlab, Python or a similar environment), but if not, you will learn. You take initiative and are eager to learn. You can work independently, but you also enjoy interacting within a group. You are fluent in English (written and spoken) and have good communication skills. You demonstrate integrity and positivity and motivate others to do the same. What we offer you We will give you a temporary employment contract (0.8 FTE 5- year contract - 1.0 FTE 4- year contract) of 1.5 years, after which your performance will be evaluated. If the evaluation is positive, your contract will be extended by 2.5 years (4-year contract) or 3.5 years (5-year contract). You will receive a starting salary of €3,204 gross per month based on a 38-hour working week, which will increase to €4,051 from the fourth year onwards (salary scale P). You will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8,3% end-of-year bonus. You will receive extra days off. With full-time employment, you can choose between 30 or 41 days of annual leave instead of the statutory 20. Additional employment conditions Work and science require good employment practices. Radboud University's primary and secondary employment conditions reflect this. You can make arrangements for the best possible work-life balance with flexible working hours, various leave arrangements and working from home. You are also able to compose part of your employment conditions yourself. For example, exchange income for extra leave days and receive a reimbursement for your sports membership. In addition, you receive a 34% discount on the sports and cultural activities at Radboud University as an employee. And, of course, we offer a good pension plan. We also give you plenty of room and responsibility to develop your talents and realise your ambitions. Therefore, we provide various training and development schemes. Where you will be working Our research team is a diverse team of international scientists broadly interested in the role of inhibitory synapses in the brain at the molecular, cellular and systems levels. We use a combination of two-photon microscopy, electrophysiology and molecular techniques to study formation and plasticity of inhibitory synapses in organotypic and acute brain slices from mice. We are particularly interested in the interactions between excitatory and inhibitory synapses within dendrites during synaptic plasticity, in brain development and in neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative diseases. The Wierenga lab is embedded within the Donders Centre for Neuroscience (DCN) at the Faculty of Science of Radboud University (Nijmegen, Netherlands). DCN is part of the world-renowned Donders Institute for Brain, Cognition and Behaviour, a world-class interfaculty neuroscience institute with a lively and interactive culture housing more than 800 researchers devoted to understanding the mechanistic underpinnings of the brain. Excellent, state-of-the-art research facilities are available for the broad range of neuroscience research that is being conducted at the Donders Institute. The Donders Institute has been assessed by an international evaluation committee as 'excellent' and recognised as a 'very stimulating environment for top researchers, as well as for young talent'. The Donders Institute fosters a collaborative, multidisciplinary and supportive research environment with a diverse international staff. English is the lingua franca at the Institute. Faculty of Science The Faculty of Science (FNWI), part of Radboud University, engages in groundbreaking research and excellent education. In doing so, we push the boundaries of scientific knowledge and pass that knowledge on to the next generation. We seek solutions to major societal challenges, such as cybercrime and climate change and work on major scientific challenges, such as those in the quantum world. At the same time, we prepare our students for careers both within and outside the scientific field. indeed:78d78f7c4093e093.title: PhD in supramolecular interactions in organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors
indeed:78d78f7c4093e093.desc: The Department of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry bridges science and engineering to create sustainable solutions for society. By combining expertise in molecules, materials, and processes, we drive innovations that address global challenges in energy, circularity, health and future technology. Through world-class research, interdisciplinary collaboration, and strong industry partnerships, we educate engineers and scientists who turn scientific discoveries into technologies with lasting societal impact. Together, we create chemistry for a better world. Introduction Are you fascinated by how molecular-scale interactions determine the real-world performance of functional materials? In this PhD project, you will study a new class of materials that find application in future technologies ranging from neuromorphic computing and bioelectronics to energy storage. Are you ready to help unravel the inner workings of these fascinating materials by investigating them during operation? Job Description Your research In your PhD project, you will uncover how intermolecular interactions and supramolecular morphology govern the functionality of organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Bridging the fields of OMIECs and supramolecular chemistry, you will investigate these relationships through in-depth operando characterization. OMIECs are soft materials that conduct both electrons and ions, highly promising for applications ranging from energy storage and solar fuels to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing. However, electrons, ions, solvent and the molecular structure all reorganize during operation, making it difficult to disentangle how molecular-scale interactions ultimately determine macroscopic function. You will develop characterization methods and experimental setups to probe intermolecular interactions as OMIECs operate. Spectroelectrochemistry will be a key tool; developing operando cells, setups, and experiments that enable you to discern dynamic spectral signatures of molecular packing. By following changes in supramolecular organization during electrochemical doping, your work will reveal how doping affects supramolecular organization. You will also determine how supramolecular packing governs doping efficiency and dynamics, linking morphology to device-relevant properties, by studying varied samples of available supramolecular building blocks. These fundamental insights will provide a supramolecular knob for tuning material functionality, thereby introducing new ways to control material behavior. The key outcome of your research is a mechanistic framework describing the bidirectional interplay between OMIEC doping and supramolecular interactions. Building on this framework, you will ultimately design switchable supramolecular OMIEC systems in collaboration with other researchers, targeting applications in in-material computing. Beyond these systems, your fundamental insights will contribute to the general development of next-generation computing and adaptive bioelectronics. Your environment and support As a member of the Optoelectronic Mixed Conductors group at the Department of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry, you will conduct your research under the supervision of Prof. Tom van der Pol. Your project is highly interdisciplinary, with opportunities to collaborate with researchers across the department. You will become part of a broad and vibrant scientific community, including the Institute for Complex Molecular Systems. At TU/e and within the Optoelectronic Mixed Conductors group, curiosity-driven research and personal development go hand in hand. You will have the freedom to pursue ambitious scientific questions while receiving the guidance and support needed to develop your own ideas and expertise. Your supervisory team will support you in developing the skills, confidence, and scientific perspective needed to uncover the mechanisms that govern OMIECs and to shape your own path as a researcher. Job Requirements We are looking for an enthusiastic self-motivated researcher who holds an MSc degree in chemistry, physics, material science, or equivalent . Experience with functional material characterization is essential, and spectroscopy or electrochemistry is preferred. Prior experience with organic semiconductors, supramolecular chemistry, or operando characterization is highly valued. You possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills and enjoy hands-on experimental research. You are curious, creative, and eager to develop new experiments, setups, knowledge, and skills. You enjoy working in an interdisciplinary team and you actively seek opportunities to collaborate. You are motivated to contribute to teaching and supervision of students. You are excellent in spoken and written English. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. indeed:87ab46d57952069d.title: PhD Position in Digital Twins for Flood-Resilient Infrastructure
indeed:87ab46d57952069d.desc: PhD Position in Digital Twins for Flood-Resilient Infrastructure Develop and implement a Digital Twin that strengthens our ability to protect critical infrastructure against flooding. Job description Current and future impact of flooding to critical infrastructure (e.g. dikes, bridges) is a major concern worldwide. Unfortunately, the management of flood-prone structures is extremely challenging because underlying processes are complex and uncertain. If our capacity to anticipate flood-induced impacts on infrastructure does not improve, societal and economic consequences are likely to be unsustainable. Digital Twins (DTs) offer a promising opportunity to combine recent advances in modelling, data assimilation and machine learning. However, for DTs to support the management of flood-prone infrastructure, they must be effectively integrated with flood-risk modelling. The scientific challenge is to develop methods that enable Digital Twins to leverage multiple models, datasets and computational techniques to improve predictive capacity in real flood-risk contexts. FlooDT (Digital Twin for flood-resilient infrastructure management) is a prestigious and ambitious project funded by NWO. It aims to develop a new methodological framework to exploit the capability of DTs for managing flood risk “from climate prediction to structure protection”. TU Delft is leading the project and a consortium that involves multiple universities (e.g. ETH Zurich, Univ. Polytechnica of Catalunya) and stakeholders (e.g. Deltares, Rijkswaterstaat). The project has also the support of the TU Delft Digital Competence Centre (DCC). For this unique project we are seeking a motivated and talented PhD candidate for a 4-year appointment. In your role you will: Develop functional modules for Digital Twins, such as risk analysis, scenario modelling and processing of monitoring data. Develop hybrid (physics based/machine learning) modelling for flood risk. Apply and validate the Digital Twin functionalities for simplified representation of infrastructure (first) and real case studies (second). Implement the developed functionalities into end users' platforms. Co-organise workshops and co-coordinate stakeholder engagement (e.g. regular meetings, presentations, visits). You will join the FlooDT team and the Flood Risk and Hydraulic Structures section, a collaborative and international team where curiosity, interdisciplinary research and scientific excellence are valued. Our section closely collaborates with the other sections within the Department of Hydraulic Engineering, other departments within our Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geoscience and many research groups around the world. We offer strong support for your professional growth, including mentoring, training, and ample opportunities for international collaboration and networking. This position will open doors to exciting career opportunities in both academia and the future-facing companies that are shaping the next generation of digital technologies. Job requirements We are looking for an excellent, enthusiastic and inquisitive computational researcher who enjoys working in an international and multidisciplinary environment. You have: A MSc degree in Civil Engineering, Computer Science or Hydro-informatics (or in a related discipline). Demostrated experience in numerical modelling, hydrodynamic simulation and data management. Scientific and/or practical knowledge of machine learning. Excellent programming skills (e.g. in Python, SQL, Java, PyTorch, etc.). A critical, creative and pro-active approach to research, with distinctive problem-solving skills. Proven experience with writing scientific reports/publications. Confidence/willingness in engaging with partners and stakeholders. Excellent command of English (oral and written). Previous internship experience with non-academic institutions is desiderable. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences The Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences (CEG) is committed to outstanding international research and education in the field of civil engineering, applied earth sciences, traffic and transport, water technology, and delta technology. Our research feeds into our educational programmes and covers societal challenges such as climate change, energy transition, resource availability, urbanisation and clean water. Our research projects are conducted in close cooperation with a wide range of research institutions. CEG is convinced of the importance of open science and supports its scientists in integrating open science in their research practice. The Faculty of CEG comprises 28 research groups in the following seven departments: Materials Mechanics Management & Design, Engineering Structures, Geoscience and Engineering, Geoscience and Remote Sensing, Transport & Planning, Hydraulic Engineering and Water Management. & Geosciences.
