indeed:e39a93e4a84369ed.title: PhD Candidate in Complex Networks
indeed:e39a93e4a84369ed.desc: Job requisition Id: 16991 Job type: PhD positions Contract hours min: 38 Contract hours max: 38 Location: Leiden Applying is possible until: 24 November 2026 The Mathematical Institute (MI) of Leiden University and the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS) are looking for a PhD Candidate in Complex Networks to commence at the earliest possible date and no later than April 2027. The project investigates how structural properties observed in complex networks can be understood and modeled using mathematically tractable network models. The research will combine theoretical modeling with computational and data-driven investigation of real-world networks, with a particular emphasis on understanding how features such as spatial structure, clustering, heterogeneity, and connectivity shape network behavior. Possible research directions include, but are not limited to, network science, spatial network modeling, random graph models, and data-driven methods for network analysis. We welcome candidates with an interest in real-world network data as well as in developing and analyzing mathematical models of complex networks. The precise balance between theoretical, computational, and data-driven work will depend on the candidate’s background and interests. The position will be co-supervised by dr. Moritz Otto (MI) and dr. Akrati Saxena (LIACS). Michel Mandjes (MI) will act as promotor. Academic excellence is the main selection criterion. What you will do Conducting complex networks research at the intersection of mathematics and computer science. Writing a publication-based PhD thesis. Engaging in a limited number of teaching and supervision activities. Where you will work The PhD candidate will be employed at the Mathematical Institute and also be affiliated with the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science and AI (LIACS). In particular, the candidate will become part of the Leiden AlFa (Algorithmic Fairness: https://alfa.liacs.nl ) group and the Probability research group , and collaborate closely with the Network Science group. Both the research groups and the institutes are highly international and feature a mix of disciplinary and cultural backgrounds. There are plenty of additional opportunities for other types of interaction and collaboration, for example, at the Faculty of Science through the Leiden Complex Networks Network (LCN2) and nationally through the Dutch Network Science Society . The Mathematical Institute focuses on four key research themes: Algebra, Geometry, and Number Theory; Analysis and Dynamical Systems; Probability; and Statistics and Data Science. There is extensive collaboration between these themes. For more information about the Mathematical Institute, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/mathematics . LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: http://www.cs.leiden.edu What you bring A university degree* in mathematics, computer science or a closely related field. Knowledge in an area of research related to network science/complex networks, e.g., graph theory, probability, random graphs, complex systems, or topological data analysis. Programming experience, preferably in Python, and willingness to develop strong computational skills (please mention your level of proficiency and knowledge of other programming languages in your CV). Strong motivation for academic research. Good English communication skills. The ability to work independently and in a team. You live and are officially registered as resident in The Netherlands or are willing to relocate upon starting the position. * Candidates who expect to complete their Master’s degree by early spring 2027 are also encouraged to apply. What we offer We offer a full-time position for initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the thesis, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended by a further three years. A salary starting from € 3.204,= to € 4.051,= gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours, Payscale P) A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP; Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel; Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme; If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands; A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop and a mobile telephone. For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions What we value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Only applications received via the university’s application tool by 24 November 2026 can be considered. Please send us Your CV and full academic transcripts (bachelor’s and master’s) A short cover letter of at most 2 pages detailing your motivation to apply for the position A recent writing example (paper or thesis) that you are proud of and that reflects your academic writing skills Names and contact details of at least one person who has agreed to be contacted for an academic reference (there is no need to send letters) In case of doubt or questions about the suitability of your research interest for this position, feel very welcome to reach out to dr. Moritz Otto (m.f.p.otto@math.leidenuniv.nl) or dr. Akrati Saxena (a.saxena@liacs.leidenuniv.nl), before formally applying. If you have any questions about the application procedure, please contact hr@math.leidenuniv.nl. Interviews are expected to take place from 1 December 2026. indeed:3d3fa3e14f6de554.title: PhD in Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models
indeed:3d3fa3e14f6de554.desc: The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field. Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed. Introduction Are you interested in the communication networks behind modern AI systems? Would you like to combine mathematical modeling with experiments on programmable network hardware to make AI infrastructure faster and more energy-efficient? In this PhD project, you will develop models and orchestration methods for the networks that connect GPUs during large language model inference. Are you our next PhD candidate in high-performance AI networking? Job Description Your research challenge Large language models rely on powerful computing infrastructure to generate responses. When inference is distributed across multiple GPUs, these devices must continuously exchange intermediate results. Network congestion and communication overhead can therefore limit performance and increase energy consumption, even when substantial computing resources are available. In the project Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models (COIL) , you will investigate how analytical network models can support the design and operation of AI clusters. The project combines network performance modeling, optimization, and experimental research, giving you the opportunity to connect mathematical foundations with practical challenges in AI infrastructure. You will develop fast, composable analytical models using Network Calculus, a mathematical framework for analyzing communication networks. These models will capture interactions between inference traffic, network architecture, and mechanisms such as flow control and congestion feedback. They will provide bounds on communication latency and buffer requirements, complemented by energy estimates based on measurement-calibrated power models. Building on these models, you will explore how architectural choices—including network topology, link bandwidth, and parallelization strategies—affect performance and energy consumption. You will develop tools that help cluster designers evaluate promising configurations efficiently. You will also investigate how the models can guide runtime decisions, such as workload placement, prioritization, routing, or resource reservation. A focused prototype will demonstrate how model-informed decisions can improve the operation of an existing network. Experimental validation will be an integral part of your research. You will use measurements from AI infrastructure and conduct reproducible experiments on programmable networking testbeds. Technologies of interest include Ethernet-based AI networks, emerging Ultra Ethernet mechanisms, P4-programmable switches, and SmartNICs. Finally, you will evaluate the results from the testbeds on real AI infrastructure in collaboration with our partner SURF. Through this combination of theory, software development, and experimentation, you will contribute to more responsive and energy-efficient AI infrastructure. The project also offers opportunities to share your findings with networking standardization communities and to release research tools and experimental results openly. An interdisciplinary and international environment You will conduct your research under the main supervision of Prof. Lisa Maile who leads the Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) lab. NoMaD is part of the Electronic Systems group in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your supervision will also include partners from the Advanced Models by Open Research and Engineering (AMOR/e) Lab of Computer Science and the Model-Based Design Lab from Electrical Engineering. The position is funded through the EuroTech programme, which promotes research collaboration between leading technical universities across Europe. As part of this project, you will collaborate closely with Prof. Georg Carle and his research group on Network Architectures and Services at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) . As part of this collaboration, you will spend six-month in Munich with the group at TUM , where you will gain hands-on experience with programmable network hardware and reproducible experimental infrastructure. Job Requirements Essential qualifications A master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. A strong mathematical background, demonstrated by excellent performance in mathematically rigorous courses, additional mathematics electives, a mathematics minor or specialization, or substantial mathematical work in a thesis or research project. Good programming skills and an interest in developing research software and experimental tools. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, initiative, and creativity. An interest in high-performance networking and AI infrastructure, and motivation to apply mathematical methods to computer networks and distributed systems. A strong team spirit and enthusiasm for working in an international, collaborative, and socially engaging environment. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Willingness to spend at least six months at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) as part of the project. Desirable qualifications A solid foundation in computer networks or distributed systems. Experience with Network Calculus, network simulation, mathematical optimization, or GPU communication. Experience with programmable networking technologies, such as P4 or SmartNICs. Selection procedure Interviews and a scientific presentation will be part of the selection procedure. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. The Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) Lab develops mathematical models, tools, and protocols for reliable and efficient communication networks. Its research connects formal analysis with practical implementation, covering technologies such as Time-Sensitive Networking, Ultra Ethernet, and beyond-5G networks. Applications range from connected vehicles and industrial automation to large-scale AI infrastructure. By combining analytical methods with simulation and hardware experiments, the lab translates theoretical insights into practical network designs and resource-management solutions. NoMaD is part of the ES group, which develops methods for designing electronic, embedded, and cyber-physical systems with predictable performance, timing, reliability, and energy consumption. With about 12 full-time and 5 part-time professors and ~45 post-docs, PhDs, and EngD students, the group’s expertise spans model-driven engineering, system architectures, software, and digital circuits. This provides an interdisciplinary environment for your research, connecting network modeling and optimization with broader challenges in computing and system design. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed. Information Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to know more? Please contact the hiring manager Prof. Lisa Maile, l.t.maile@tue.nl. Visit our website for more information about the application process. You can also contact Kevin Caris, HR advisor, k.t.caris@tue.nl. Curious to hear

indeed:67083d1df6a1d6ad.title: PhD in Multifunctional Polymer Composites
indeed:67083d1df6a1d6ad.desc: The Department of Mechanical Engineering department conducts world-class research aligned with the technological interests of the high-tech industry in the Netherlands, with a focus on the Brainport region. Our goal is to produce engineers who are both scientifically educated and application-driven by providing a balanced education and research program that combines fundamental and application aspects. We equip our graduates with practical and theoretical expertise, preparing them optimally for future challenges. Introduction Are you inspired to push the limits of polymeric materials for lighter and smarter defense platforms? Join us to develop a new generation of 3D-printed composite panels that shield electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact. Job Description We are offering 2 PhD positions within project VALOR, an ambitious, interdisciplinary collaboration between academia, industry and government partners. The project aims to develop a new generation of lightweight composite panels that both shield sensitive electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact events, helping to make defense platforms safer and more resilient. Naval ships, drones and military vehicles increasingly depend on electronic radar, communication and navigation systems that must be protected against electromagnetic interference and radar detection . Today, this is mostly done with metals, which block practically all wave power with only a thin layer. However, they add weight, corrode, and reflect electromagnetic waves, making platforms easier to detect. Project VALOR tackles this challenge by merging two fields that have so far been developed separately: absorption-based electromagnetic shielding and impact-resistant sandwich structures . By combining 3D-printed architected nanocomposite materials with predictive modelling into one integrated design strategy, the project will construct a design framework for panels that are able to both carry loads and absorb electromagnetic waves, with a performance that can be tailored to specific (defense) applications. Your role We are recruiting two PhD candidates who will work as a team throughout the project, i.e. from material screening to design and testing of larger scale panel demonstrators. Both candidates will conduct a combination of experimental and numerical work and collaborate closely with industrial partners within the consortium. More specifically: PhD 1 focuses on mechanics and manufacturing : 3D printing nanocomposite lattice materials, fabricating composite facesheets, conducting mechanical tests, constructing and validating mechanical finite element models. PhD 2 focuses on electromagnetic testing and design : formulating polymer nanocomposite materials and characterizing their electromagnetic behaviour, designing and testing absorbing architected nanocomposite structures, conducting electromagnetic shielding simulations. Your team and network You will join the Processing and Performance of Materials section in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at TU/e. The group has around 20 PhD and post-doctoral researchers working on how processing, structure and properties connect in polymers and polymer-based composite materials. The group is known for its integrated experimental-numerical approach to tailor the performance of these materials. You will have access to state-of-the-art computational facilities and laboratories dedicated to rheology, polymer processing (incl. additive manufacturing) and mechanical testing. You will be supervised by Frederik Van Loock (project leader), Ruth Cardinaels and Tom Engels. indeed:082beca7b290bfb0.title: PhD Research Fellow in Structured Vision-Language Models
indeed:082beca7b290bfb0.desc: Integreat -Norwegian Centre for Knowledge-driven Machine Learning Boks 1072 Blindern, 0316 Oslo Om jobben Lagre favoritt Stillingstittel PhD Research Fellow in Structured Vision-Language Models Type ansettelse Vikariat, heltid 100% Antall stillinger 1 Arbeidsspråk Engelsk Søk senest onsdag 18. november About the position Integreat - the Norwegian Centre for Knowledge-driven Machine Learning is seeking a motivated PhD candidate to join our interdisciplinary research centre at the University of Oslo, Norway. You will be part of a dynamic group of early career researchers, supervised by senior experts, collaborating across disciplines to tackle fundamental challenges through innovative methods, theory and critical analysis. The fellowship period is 3 years. A fourth year may be considered, and it will involve 25 % of other career-promoting work. Other career-promoting work may consist of teaching, supervision, and/or research assistance. This is dependent upon the qualifications of the applicant and the current needs of the Department of Informatics Starting date from January 2027 and upon individual agreement thereafter. A candidate may be appointed to only one PhD Research Fellowship at the University of Oslo. About Integreat See the video for more information about Integreat. Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/-_I52cJHiW4 About Integreat Integreat - Norwegian Centre for Knowledge-driven Machine Learning is a Centre of Excellence, funded by the Research Council of Norway (2023-33). Integreat has two branches, one in Oslo (University of Oslo, UiO) and one in Tromsø (UiT The Arctic University of Norway). Machine learning is the mathematical and computational engine of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and therefore it is a fundamental force of technological progress in our increasingly digital, data- and algorithm-driven world. Integreat develops theories, methods, models, and algorithms that integrate general and domain-specific knowledge with data, laying the foundations of next generation machine learning. We do this by combining the mathematical and computational cultures, and the methodologies and theories, of statistics, logic, language technology, ethics and machine learning, in new and unique ways. Focus of Integreat is to develop groundbreaking methods and theories, and therefore solving fundamental problems in science, technology, health and society. Integreat draws on the research strengths of researchers and students from the departments of Mathematics, Informatics, Philosophy, and the Oslo Centre for Biostatistics and Epidemiology at UiO, the Norwegian Computing Centre (NR) and the ML group at UiT, with members from the departments of Physics and Technology, Mathematics and Statistics, and Computer Science. Project description Vision-language models (VLMs) can name what is in a picture, but they often miss what is happening in it. Shown a park scene, a model may list "a dog", "a Frisbee" and "a park" and still fail to say that the dog is leaping to catch the Frisbee mid-air. The same gap shows up when a model misreads a symbolic painting or gives a vague description of a medical image. More training data does not close this gap, because the models have no explicit representation of how the objects in a scene relate to each other. This project gives VLMs that representation. You will develop panoptic scene graphs, in which every object and background region in an image becomes a node and the edges encode spatial, semantic and relational context. The graphs are built from superpixels rather than the fixed square patches used in standard vision transformers. Superpixels follow object boundaries, so the nodes of the graph are meaningful from the start. The project builds directly on our recent work on superpixel tokenization for vision transformers (ECCV Workshops 2024, NeurIPS 2025). The scene graph is then fused with a large language model (LLM), and the two parts inform each other. The LLM guides which objects and relations the vision model should focus on, and the graph grounds the LLM's answers in what is actually in the image, which reduces hallucination. Because a scene graph has the same form as a knowledge graph, it also opens the way to graph-based visual retrieval-augmented generation (graph visual RAG), where a model links what it sees to external knowledge before it answers. The aim is a new class of VLMs that reason over images instead of only describing them. Such models would be more accurate, more explainable (each answer can be traced to nodes and edges in the graph) and more useful where deep understanding matters. Examples include a robot that follows an instruction such as "place the red mug next to the laptop onto the top shelf", a medical system that reasons about the relations between structures in an X-ray, and a self-driving car that anticipates how pedestrians and vehicles will interact. As a PhD fellow on the project, you will contribute to: develop superpixel-based panoptic segmentation models built on modern transformer architectures design methods that predict relations between segmented regions and generate panoptic scene graphs fuse scene graphs with LLMs for visual question answering and grounded reasoning, including graph visual RAG publish and present your results at leading machine learning and computer vision venues Project supervisors: Professor Adín Ramírez Rivera at the Department of Informatics, UiO, in collaboration with Benjamin Ricaud and Filippo Maria Bianchi at UiT The Arctic University of Norway. Working language: English. What skills are important in this role? The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition to be among Europe’s leading communities for research, education and innovation. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this, and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials. Qualification requirements: Master’s degree or equivalent in computer science, machine learning, data science, mathematics, statistics, electrical engineering, or a related field. Foreign completed degree (M.Sc.-level) corresponding to a minimum of four years in the Norwegian educational system. Experience in scientific programming. Desired qualifications: Proficiency in scientific programming (e.g., Python) Proficiency in deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch) Background in machine learning, mathematics, linear algebra, and statistics Experience in creating, adapting, or training modern, token-based transformer architectures Experience working with image / vision models Experience in creating or adapting large language models (LLMs) and interfacing them with other models Familiarity with image segmentation Familiarity with Scene Graph Generation Familiarity with LLM fine-tuning and alignment Knowledge of graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (Graph RAG) Understanding of probabilistic modelling and information-based regularizers Strong scientific writing skills Language requirement: Good oral and written communication skills in English English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/ EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements: https://www.mn.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/regulations.html#toc8 Grade requirements: The norm is as follows: the average grade point for courses included in the Bachelor’s degree must be C or better in the Norwegian educational system the average grade point for courses included in the Master’s degree must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system the Master’s thesis must have the grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system The purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. For more information see: Supplementary Regulations at the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences to the Regulations for the Degree of Philosophiae Doctor (PhD) at the University of Oslo - The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences Personal skills We are looking for candidates who are curious, motivated to learn, and interested in tackling challenging scientific questions. You should be able to work independently while also contributing actively to collaborative research activities and the broader research community. Integreat brings together researchers from different disciplines, institutions, and career stages. We value openness to new perspectives, effective communication, and a willingness to engage across disciplinary boundaries. We are looking for candidates who contribute positively to a supportive, inclusive, and respectful research environment. Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal qualifications. We need different perspectives in our work Integreat is committed to equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging, guided by our INTEGREAT principles (Integrity, Non discrimination, Tact, Environment, Gratitude, Respect, Empathy, Accountability, Transparency). We embed these values in practice through inclusive hiring and structured evaluations, targeted mentoring and career development, and flexible work arrangements and accommodations to ensure everyone can thrive and contribute. We particularly welcome applications from women and gender minorities who are underrepresented in STEM, as well as applicants with immigrant backgrounds, disabilities, non linear career paths, or career breaks. We will take career interruptions and diverse career trajectories into account during evaluation. If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps, we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian). The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. From the salary, 2% is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund A unique research environment with multiple opportunities to develop research themes at the forefront of modern science A friendly, inclusive, and collaborative international working environment that values diverse perspectives Access to a strong network of top-level national and international collaborators A reliable and generous pension agreement, along with strong public benefits Comprehensive welfare schemes supporting both personal and professional well-being Full access to public health services through membership in the National Insurance Scheme A vibrant academic environment with an active and supportive research community Structured career development programmes at the faculty level and an individual professional development plan throughout the postdoctoral period Mentoring and support structures tailored to early-career researchers Flexible working conditions, with understanding for different life situations and family responsibilities Research mobility funds supporting short research stays and international collaboration Family-friendly surroundings in Oslo and Tromsø, with rich opportunities for culture, nature, and outdoor activities A clear institutional commitment to gender equality and diversity, with dedicated initiatives and networks for women in science Integreat provides a researcher training programme, INTREF - the Integreat Young Researchers’ Forum - a fellow driven initiative offering scientific training, transferable skills worksh

indeed:486ce38a242db4e0.title: PhD Student Positions on Networked Physical AI Multi-Agent Systems
indeed:486ce38a242db4e0.desc: The Networked Systems Lab of the Universidad Miguel Hernández (UMH) de Elche (Spain) offers several fully-funded PhD positions in Networked Physical AI Multi-Agent Systems. Successful candidates will work in an internationally recognized research group with extensive collaborations in academia and industry, publish in top-tier journals and conferences, contribute to active projects (and proposals) and have opportunities for international collaborations. The Networked Systems Lab (formerly UWICORE laboratory) is internationally-recognized for its research on wireless networking for connected and automated mobility and smart manufacturing. The laboratory is actively involved in EU and national projects, standardization and R&D contracts with industrial partners. Some of the PhD projects will be carried out in collaboration with industrial partners in the US. The laboratory is located in the Mediterranean coast of Spain (Elche) and is part of the Department of Communications Engineering of the Universidad Miguel Hernández (UMH) and of the Institute for Engineering Research (I3E) of Elche. Tasks Future Physical AI systems will be characterized by large populations of autonomous embodied agents – including collaborative robots and connected autonomous vehicles– operating in shared physical environments. Unlike today's agentic AI systems, which primarily execute predefined workflows in structured and well-defined digital environments, future Physical AI agents will have to perceive, reason and act under unstructured and continuously evolving real-world conditions and objectives. This calls for a fundamental rethinking of how agents interact, requiring intelligence and semantic and task-oriented networking to be co-designed so that agents can collaboratively construct meaningful representations of the physical world, reason over existing (shared) context and knowledge, and adapt their networking and interactions to efficiently accomplish individual and collective tasks. Our lab is offering several PhD positions on research at the intersection of Physical AI, multi-agent systems, and 6G networks. The research will focus on developing solutions that enable autonomous agents to perceive, reason, network, and collaborate effectively in dynamic real-world environments. The research may also include interactions between embodied agents and agents at the 6G edge-cloud continuum infrastructure, as well as AI-network-control co-design. Research will initially be framed in collaborative mobile robotics and connected automated mobility, while developing scientific foundations that generalize to a broader range of cyber-physical systems. Specific research topics will be discussed during the interviews, and they can be co-defined with selected candidates based on their background, expertise, and research interests. The positions are for three years and will start as soon as possible. The positions are fully funded according to the Spanish PhD employment scheme and include full social security benefits. Requirements Candidates should hold (or be close to completing) a Master’s degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical, Electronic, or Telecommunications Engineering (or related disciplines). Strong interest or experience in one or more of the following topics is required: Artificial Intelligence, Physical AI, autonomous systems (e.g., mobile robotics and connected and automated vehicles), multi-agent systems, networking, 6G. Candidates should have good programming skills (e.g., C++ and/or Python) as well as good theoretical foundations and strong critical thinking skills. Experience with popular machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) or simulation environments is considered a plus, but not required. Previous research experience or publications are positively considered but are not required. Good English writing and speaking skills as well as curiosity, self-motivation, and team-working attitude are essential.

indeed:e4e54c248c25e1dc.desc: Are you excited to push the boundaries of artificial intelligence in nuclear technology? Join us as a doctoral student to explore the advanced frontier of AI-driven nuclear safeguards and enhance global nuclear safety and security. About us The Reactor Physics, Modelling and Safety group at Chalmers develops advanced methods for modelling, simulation, monitoring and safety analysis of current and next-generation nuclear reactors. In this doctoral research, you will investigate an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework to enable transparency in ANN models and their predictions for SNF inspection, bridging high-performing machine learning with transparent nuclear verification. indeed:19dede2a5e2307a5.title: Doctoral Student in Environmental Bioengineering
indeed:19dede2a5e2307a5.desc: Doctoral Student in Environmental Bioengineering 100%, Zurich, fixed-term The Environmental Microfluidics Group of Prof. Roman Stocker in the Institute of Environmental Engineering is seeking a dynamic and motivated doctoral student with an engineering background for a project on how bacterial chemotaxis accelerates plasmid transfer, including the spread of antibiotic resistance. The position is funded by a recently awarded SNSF grant, and the project is a joint effort with Prof. Jonasz Slomka at the University of Warsaw. This position will be based in the laboratory of Prof. Roman Stocker. Project background Bacterial conjugation, the contact-dependent transfer of plasmids between cells, speeds up bacterial evolution and is a major route for the spread of antibiotic resistance in the environment, which in turn poses a global health threat. Aquatic environments are full of microscale chemical hotspots, such as the nutrient-rich 'phycosphere' around phytoplankton and sinking marine particles, and chemotactic bacteria are known to find and accumulate rapidly at these locations. This project will test the hypothesis that this accumulation enhances plasmid spreading in the environment, contributing to a cutting-edge view of the role of antibiotic resistance in nature. The project seeks to study when, where and how strongly this enhancement operates across different chemical hotspots, fluid flows and bacterial strains, and what it means for the spread of antibiotic resistance among aquatic bacteria. Job description This is a primarily experimental PhD at the interface of engineering and microbiology. The student will: Design, build and characterize new instrumentation to couple existing chemotaxis assays to controlled shear systems. This includes mechanical design, 3D ing, control systems and integration with a fluorescence microscope. Run chemotaxis and conjugation experiments with bacterial donors and recipients of plasmids and a range of chemoattractants, with the opportunity to learn and use advanced techniques such as flow cytometry and plate-reader-based plasmid transfer quantification. Image and track fluorescently labeled bacteria and chemical plumes in shear flow, and analyze the data with quantitative image- and data-analysis pipelines. Test clinically relevant bacteria and freshwater (e.g. lake) bacteria, to assess the potential for chemotaxis-driven spread of resistance in the environment. Contribute data to mathematical models of plasmid spread. Profile We are looking for a hands-on, skilled and curious engineer who loves to build new tools and is interested in using them to answer fundamental scientific questions. Ideal candidates hold an MSc degree in bioengineering, mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electrical engineering, environmental engineering, physics or a related discipline, and have some (not necessarily all) of the following skills: Practical experience in prototyping and manufacturing, for example CAD, 3D ing, machining (strongly preferred). Experience with control systems and instrumentation, for example motor control, sensors, microcontrollers, and automation or data-acquisition code (Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW or similar) (preferred). Openness to gain experience in the microbiology laboratory: bacterial cultures, sterile technique, plate readers and flow cytometry. Familiarity with microscopy, image analysis, fluid mechanics or microfluidics (beneficial but not necessary). Fluency in English (oral and written), enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary and international team, and the drive to pursue scientific excellence (required). You will be guided by Prof. Roman Stocker and by members of his lab with extensive experience in microbiology, experimental techniques and environmental processes. You will have the opportunity to work in a cutting-edge, fast-paced research environment, interact with researchers from many different disciplines (engineers, physicists, microbiologists, oceanographers, chemists, mathematicians), gain technical experience across diverse research approaches and interact with world-class collaborators. indeed:1b75053d8368598d.title: PhD position NCCR Genesis: combining remote and in-situ life detection techniques
indeed:1b75053d8368598d.desc: NCCR Genesis: background The Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) and the Division for Space Research and Planetary Sciences (WP) at the University of Bern invite applications for a PhD position in the frame of the new NCCR Genesis. The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect unambiguous traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress. Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch. Our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups. Project description Are we alone in the universe? The search for life beyond the Earth is one of the most fascinating endeavours that humankind has embarked upon. Recent years have seen tremendous progress in instrumentation, laboratory experiments and theories on the origin of life. This PhD project will investigate for the first time the combination of remote life sensing techniques using circular spectro-polarimetry with in situ laser-based mass spectrometry measurements, both designed for the detection or signatures of life. The work will mainly involve experiments in the lab, using cell cultures of a range of strains (including anaerobic cultivation of microorganisms) and various classes of organic molecules relevant to Solar System environments. These studies will be complemented by targeted field measurements of soil material containing microorganisms and low abundant organics that are relevant candidates for extinct/extant life on Mars or in the icy moons of the solar system. The results of this endeavour will reveal the potential of combining life detection methods at different scales that will be key to define optimal strategies for future life-detection missions, such as the planned ESA L4 mission to Enceladus or future NASA mission to Mars. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team with expertise spanning astrophysics, microbiology, biomedicine and engineering. The new group member will have the opportunity to gain unique experience in dual-use instrumentation applicable to both space exploration and medical diagnostics. Profile We are looking for a creative and motivated candidate, a team player, with a MSc degree in physics, chemistry, or biology. Willingness to learn microbiological techniques is essential; prior wet lab experience is an asset. No prior expertise in optics is required; training will be provided, though a basic understanding of polarization, vacuum technology and/or mass spectrometry is a plus. Excellent oral and written skills in English are a requirement. What we offer The position is based at the Centre for Space and Habitability, which strives to investigate key questions in space sciences through interdisciplinarity. The team collaborates tightly with various national and international partners. This includes for example the Microbiology Laboratory of the University of Neuchâtel where the lab measurements on microorganisms will be conducted. Laser-based mass spectrometry on organics will be conducted at the Space Research and Planetary Sciences division of the University of Bern, which is closely collaborating with colleagues at NASA Ames Research Center, USA. The city of Bern is well known for its quality of life, cultural richness and beautiful surroundings offering plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities. The position is funded for a period of 4 years. The annual gross salary is competitive, ranging from CHF 50,042 in the first year to CHF 53,263 in the final year. Ample funding for travel, publications and computing resources will be available. Child allowance and maternity/paternity leave are offered. Assistance with visa procedures is available for international candidates. Additionally, the CSH offers career advice, mentorship, and teaching opportunities. Application and Contact Questions about the position? Queries should be addressed to: Prof. Dr. Brice-Olivier Demory (brice-olivier.demory@unibe.ch) and PD Dr. Andreas Riedo (andreas.riedo@unibe.ch) who will jointly supervise the PhD student. Questions about the application? Applications are invited from all nationalities and should consist of a 2-page cover letter detailing your interest in joining the group and in the PhD topic a CV official transcripts of your Bachelor's and Master's degrees, as well as contact details of three referees (references will only be requested for short-listed candidates) Application materials should be submitted in a single PDF file to info.csh@unibe.ch with "NCCR Genesis PhD1 position" in the subject line. The review of the applications will start immediately and will continue until the position is filled.

linkedin:4481323334.desc: Unternehmensbeschreibung Bei Bosch gestalten wir Zukunft mit hochwertigen Technologien und Dienstleistungen, die Begeisterung wecken und das Leben der Menschen verbessern. Unser Versprechen an unsere Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeiter steht dabei felsenfest: Wir wachsen gemeinsam, haben Freude an unserer Arbeit und inspirieren uns gegenseitig. Willkommen bei Bosch. Die Robert Bosch GmbH freut sich auf deine Bewerbung! Stellenbeschreibung Die industrielle Automatisierung steht an einem Wendepunkt. Foundation Models bieten eine beispiellose Generalisierung und Anpassungsfähigkeit – doch ihr Einsatz in realen Produktionsumgebungen bedeutet, sich harten Randbedingungen stellen zu müssen: Latenzen im Mikrosekundenbereich, deterministisches Verhalten, funktionale Sicherheitszertifizierungen und Legacy-Infrastrukturen, die sich nicht ohne Weiteres ersetzen lassen. Zu deinen Aufgaben gehört die Untersuchung, wie Foundation Models in der industriellen Realität nutzbar werden. Hierfür entwickelst du innovative Anpassungs-, Validierungs- und Deployment-Methoden. Du bringst diese Modelle in die Fertigung, die Prozessindustrie und in cyber-physische Systeme, wobei du Latenz, Determinismus und Sicherheit als nicht verhandelbare Größen berücksichtigst. Außerdem widmest du dich den Kernfragen, wie Foundation Models eine begrenzte, vorhersagbare Leistung erbringen können, ohne an Fähigkeiten einzubüßen. Du erarbeitest Lösungen, wie sich Foundation Models mit etablierten industriellen Sicherheits- und Automatisierungsstandards (z. B. IEC 61131, IEC 61508) vereinbaren lassen. Nicht zuletzt erweiterst du Brownfield-Automatisierungsplattformen um die Fähigkeiten von Foundation Models und schaffst so neue Möglichkeiten für die Industrie. linkedin:4481390454.desc: About The Position NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim. This position will be in Gjøvik, Norway. At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world. You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here. Video: https://youtu.be/Xt-yHCN5QS0 Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network CAPTURE, collaborate with academic, healthcare, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on wireless endoscopy. As part of the CAPTURE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting. The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027. Your immediate leader will be the unit leader of Colourlab. About The Project The CAPTURE project is an EU-funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to advancing wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) through developments in computer vision and artificial intelligence. The project aims to improve image-based diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment by developing methods that reduce clinicians’ workload, enhance imaging quality, and support more accurate and timely diagnoses. CAPTURE combines research with a strong focus on doctoral training, preparing a new generation of researchers to work at the interface of technology and medicine. The consortium brings together expertise from academia, industry, and hospitals, ensuring that the research is both scientifically rigorous and clinically relevant. The project focuses on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), reflecting its growing prevalence in Europe. As many of the methods developed have broader applicability, the project will also consider other gastrointestinal diseases. These goals will be achieved through the recruitment and training of 15 doctoral candidates in an international and intersectoral environment, providing interdisciplinary expertise across the technical, clinical, and applied aspects of WCE. Duties of the position Automated approaches for pathology detection using WCE are generally based on recent AI models. These models often result in black-box decisions. For a clinician to use these systems, the basis for diagnostic decision should be clearly explained. The PhD candidate will help develop explainable AI (XAI) methods for automated diagnostic decision systems to enhance the explainability and actionability of their predictions for doctors. The candidate will also evaluate the generated explanations with medical doctors to assess their relevance, usefulness, and importance in clinical settings. Key responsibilities Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above Academic publications and popular science dissemination Participate in the Colourlab research group Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person across the CAPTURE partner institutions and contribute to CAPTURE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures. Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to Robert Gordon University, UK and Technical University of Darmstadt, Germany. Close collaboration with hospitals for assessing methods developed in PhD project Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must have experience with computer vision and machine learning. You must have excellent programming skills in Python with exposure to popular deep learning libraries like PyTorch or Tensorflow. At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible. You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information. You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, electrical engineering or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis. Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position. You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. You must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment (short stays such as holidays are not taken into account). The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria Preference may be given to candidates with: Experience with computer vision, medical image processing, self-supervised learning or learning in low-data regimes. Experience with statistical signal processing and pattern recognition will be counted positive. Experience with pretrained representation models, transfer learning and xAI. Knowledge of robustness analysis in computer vision applications. Knowledge of explainable AI, uncertainty estimation, calibration, out-of-distribution detection, adversarial robustness, or causal analysis. Experience with causal inference, counterfactual explanations, or uncertainty quantification in deep learning Evidence of scientific writing, publications, a strong master's thesis, research software, or relevant open-source contributions. Excellent analytical and communication skills. Ability to work in an international and interdisciplinary environment. Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Show strong motivation for research and a willingness to engage deeply with challenging scientific questions. Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them. Present and discuss your research with other professionals. Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback. Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity. Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject. Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions. Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed. Communicate, present, and collaborate effectively, including explaining technical ideas clearly and presenting research results to interdisciplinary audiences and project partners. Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities. We offer An exciting job with an important mission in society Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As an employee in Norway, the successful candidate will normally be a member of the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme, which provides access to public healthcare and social security benefits in accordance with applicable legislation and regulations. As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. This will cover the MSCA Living Allowance and Mobility Allowance. In addition, a family allowance may be provided in accordance with MSCA regulations. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. The employment period is 3 years. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Computer Science within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The successful applicant must devote full working time to the project and the doctoral training programme. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed. About The Application The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. linkedin:4482478560.desc: At STMicroelectronics, we believe in the power of technology to drive innovation and make a positive impact on people, businesses, and society. As a global semiconductor company, our advanced technologies and chips form the hidden foundation of the world we live in today. When you join ST, you will be part of a global business with more than 115 nationalities, present in 40 countries, and comprising over 50,000 diverse and dedicated creators and makers of technology around the world. Developing technologies takes more than talent: it takes amazing people who understand collaboration and respect. People with passion and the desire to disrupt the status quo, drive innovation, and unlock their own potential. Embark on a journey with us, where you can innovate for a future that we want to make smarter and greener, in a responsible and sustainable way. Our technology starts with you. YOUR ROLE Since 2000, wide-bandgap materials, especially silicon carbide, have been progressively introduced into power electronic circuits. Owing to their higher critical electric field compared with silicon, high-voltage unipolar devices such as Schottky diodes and MOS transistors have been developed, replacing silicon bipolar devices, including fast bipolar diodes and IGBTs, with significantly reduced switching losses. The resulting improvement in power efficiency reduces cooling requirements and enables a smaller overall system footprint, making the adoption of wide-bandgap devices particularly advantageous in applications with stringent constraints on size and weight, such as spacecraft and avionics. For these applications, high tolerance to cosmic rays is obviously expected. On the ground, higher power efficiency is also crucial for electrical vehicle deployment as it increases driving range, and for smart-grid applications that require very high voltage devices (> 2000V). Here again, cosmic ray robustness, especially neutrons, is essential to meet the very low failure rates expected in the automotive sector and to avoid complex maintenance in smart-grid applications. Since 2004, cosmic rays impact on silicon carbide devices has been extensively studied. In addition to the well-known single event burnout (SEB), also observed in silicon power devices, silicon carbide devices have been shown to exhibit a new cumulative degradation mechanism reported as single-event leakage current (SELC). No consensus has yet been reached within the scientific community regarding its cause. In This Context, You'll Be Responsible For Defining models to be implemented in cosmic-ray simulations for silicon carbide devices. Performing simulations on existing diode structures to validate the simulation setup. This activity will benefit from an ongoing study engaged with the french national center for space studies (CNES), which will provide with heavy-ion robustness results from different diode structures. Studying the reverse characteristics of damaged diodes and request analyses (either electrical or structural ones) to understand the mechanisms involved. Simulating new diode structures to improve cosmic-ray robustness. Thesis location STMicroelectronics Tours RADIAC team at IES (University of Montpellier) Your Skills & Experiences Master degree in semiconductor physics, condensed-matter physics, or particle-matter interaction, B2 English level and finite-elements simulation experience would be appreciated. linkedin:4482462486.title: PhD in Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models
linkedin:4482462486.desc: Introduction Are you interested in the communication networks behind modern AI systems? Would you like to combine mathematical modeling with experiments on programmable network hardware to make AI infrastructure faster and more energy-efficient? In this PhD project, you will develop models and orchestration methods for the networks that connect GPUs during large language model inference. Are you our next PhD candidate in high-performance AI networking? Job Description Your research challenge Large language models rely on powerful computing infrastructure to generate responses. When inference is distributed across multiple GPUs, these devices must continuously exchange intermediate results. Network congestion and communication overhead can therefore limit performance and increase energy consumption, even when substantial computing resources are available. In the project Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models (COIL) , you will investigate how analytical network models can support the design and operation of AI clusters. The project combines network performance modeling, optimization, and experimental research, giving you the opportunity to connect mathematical foundations with practical challenges in AI infrastructure. You will develop fast, composable analytical models using Network Calculus, a mathematical framework for analyzing communication networks. These models will capture interactions between inference traffic, network architecture, and mechanisms such as flow control and congestion feedback. They will provide bounds on communication latency and buffer requirements, complemented by energy estimates based on measurement-calibrated power models. Building on these models, you will explore how architectural choices—including network topology, link bandwidth, and parallelization strategies—affect performance and energy consumption. You will develop tools that help cluster designers evaluate promising configurations efficiently. You will also investigate how the models can guide runtime decisions, such as workload placement, prioritization, routing, or resource reservation. A focused prototype will demonstrate how model-informed decisions can improve the operation of an existing network. Experimental validation will be an integral part of your research. You will use measurements from AI infrastructure and conduct reproducible experiments on programmable networking testbeds. Technologies of interest include Ethernet-based AI networks, emerging Ultra Ethernet mechanisms, P4-programmable switches, and SmartNICs. Finally, you will evaluate the results from the testbeds on real AI infrastructure in collaboration with our partner SURF. Through this combination of theory, software development, and experimentation, you will contribute to more responsive and energy-efficient AI infrastructure. The project also offers opportunities to share your findings with networking standardization communities and to release research tools and experimental results openly. An interdisciplinary and international environment You will conduct your research under the main supervision of Prof. Lisa Maile who leads the Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) lab. NoMaD is part of the Electronic Systems group in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your supervision will also include partners from the Advanced Models by Open Research and Engineering (AMOR/e) Lab of Computer Science and the Model-Based Design Lab from Electrical Engineering. The position is funded through the EuroTech programme, which promotes research collaboration between leading technical universities across Europe. As part of this project, you will collaborate closely with Prof. Georg Carle and his research group on Network Architectures and Services at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) . As part of this collaboration, you will spend six-month in Munich with the group at TUM , where you will gain hands-on experience with programmable network hardware and reproducible experimental infrastructure. Job Requirements Essential qualifications A master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. A strong mathematical background, demonstrated by excellent performance in mathematically rigorous courses, additional mathematics electives, a mathematics minor or specialization, or substantial mathematical work in a thesis or research project. Good programming skills and an interest in developing research software and experimental tools. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, initiative, and creativity. An interest in high-performance networking and AI infrastructure, and motivation to apply mathematical methods to computer networks and distributed systems. A strong team spirit and enthusiasm for working in an international, collaborative, and socially engaging environment. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Willingness to spend at least six months at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) as part of the project. Desirable Qualifications A solid foundation in computer networks or distributed systems. Experience with Network Calculus, network simulation, mathematical optimization, or GPU communication. Experience with programmable networking technologies, such as P4 or SmartNICs. Selection procedure Interviews and a scientific presentation will be part of the selection procedure. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About Us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. The Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) Lab develops mathematical models, tools, and protocols for reliable and efficient communication networks. Its research connects formal analysis with practical implementation, covering technologies such as Time-Sensitive Networking, Ultra Ethernet, and beyond-5G networks. Applications range from connected vehicles and industrial automation to large-scale AI infrastructure. By combining analytical methods with simulation and hardware experiments, the lab translates theoretical insights into practical network designs and resource-management solutions. linkedin:4482478648.title: PhD - Benchmarking Robotic Tactile Sensors
linkedin:4482478648.desc: The Manipulation and Touch Lab at Imperial College London has funding to support a home PhD student on the topic of Benchmarking Contemporary Tactile Sensors . The project will be supervised by Dr Ad Spiers, an Associate Professor of Robotics and Machine Learning. The Manipulation and Touch Lab is part of the Intelligent Systems and Networks research group and the Imperial Robotics Forum. Project Summary: Increasing interest in robotic manipulation has led to recent an explosion in the variety of (commercial and experimental) tactile sensing platforms, which vary in transduction techniques, fabrication methods and processing approaches. While all sensors have their pros and cons, there is currently no clear documentation to allow these sensors to be directly compared, particularly when diverse use cases are considered. Comparative benchmarking has become an important topic in robotic manipulation within the last decade or so, leading to such efforts as the YCB object set, COMPARE ecosystem and NIST task boards. Clearly, a similar effort would be beneficial for tactile sensing, though the scope and details of such benchmarks are currently unclear. The developments of relevant and rigorous sensor tests will be the focus of this PhD, which will be actualised via high-precision robotic test equipment and access to multiple tactile sensors from various manufacturers. We anticipate this research to generate protocols and datasets that will be shared with the international robotics research community, as we have done with our past research outputs. The Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Imperial has a long and proud history of world-class research and innovation. It ranked the 1st in the UK (Engineering) in REF 2021 based on the proportion of world-leading research (4*). Funding: The PhD studentship is fully funded for and includes home-level tuition fees, a tax-free stipend for three and a half years at the UKRI London rate (approximately £23,805 per year for 2026/27), and support for research expenses and travel to conferences. The post is only open to home applicants. Qualifications: Applicants are expected to hold either a Bachelor’s (2:1 or higher) and Master’s (Merit or higher) or Integrated Master’s (Merit or higher) in relevant subjects.
