linkedin:4474186348.desc: Chez STMicroelectronics, nous sommes convaincus que la technologie est un moteur d’innovation et a un impact positif pour les entreprises, les personnes et la société. En tant qu’acteur mondial des semiconducteurs, nos technologies de pointe et nos composants électroniques sont invisibles mais au cœur du monde d’aujourd’hui. Rejoindre ST, c’est intégrer une entreprise internationale riche de plus de 115 nationalités, présente dans 40 pays, et rassemblant plus de 50 000 talents passionnés et engagés, tous unis par la volonté de créer et d’inventer la technologie de demain. Innover demande bien plus que des compétences techniques : cela nécessite des personnes inspirantes, qui savent collaborer avec respect et enthousiasme. Des collaborateurs animés par la passion, prêts à remettre en question le statu quo, à faire avancer l’innovation et à révéler leur plein potentiel. Venez vivre cette aventure avec nous et contribuez à construire un futur plus intelligent et plus durable, en alliant responsabilité et innovation. Notre technologie commence avec vous. In the context of silicon power devices for automotive applications, improving current conduction and reducing on-state resistance inevitably increase power density, leading to greater self-heating. The Safe Operating Area (SOA) of a power MOSFET, which defines the safe operating limits of the device, is typically constrained by thermally driven mechanisms. In this framework, a detailed understanding of the electro-thermal behavior of the device is essential to identify weak points across the power die and ensure reliable operation under both static and dynamic conditions. This PhD will focus on developing and validating a coupled electro-thermal simulation workflow capable of predicting local self-heating, current crowding, and SOA limits in silicon power MOSFETs. In particular, the candidate will investigate electro-thermal models and methodologies available in TCAD and will evaluate realistic thermal boundary conditions by combining 2D and 3D simulations. The work will also explore simplified thermal network representations, based on thermal resistances and capacitances, to reproduce the thermal behavior of power MOSFETs. In addition, the study will also consider operation at gate voltages only slightly above threshold, where power MOSFETs may become thermally unstable and exhibit current crowding, generating localized hot spots. In this context, the candidate will explore the feasibility, advantages, and implementation of integrating a multiphysics environment such as COMSOL to couple device-level and chip-level simulations, with the aim of predicting hot-spot formation and thermal runaway conditions. The candidate will work in close collaboration with the IM2MP laboratory in Marseille. About Your Missions Conduct an in-depth literature review on electro-thermal phenomena in silicon power MOSFETs and on the associated simulation approaches. Develop and validate a coupled electro-thermal simulation workflow. Study the models and methodologies available in TCAD to analyze self-heating, current crowding, and Safe Operating Area (SOA) limits. Evaluate realistic thermal boundary conditions by combining 2D and 3D simulations, as well as simplified thermal network representations. Explore the integration of a multiphysics environment such as COMSOL to couple simulations at the device level and at the chip level. About You Master’s degree in semiconductor physics, electronics engineering, or a related field. A strong interest in numerical simulation and the study of electro-thermal phenomena. Good command of scientific English and the ability to write clear and well-structured technical documents. Initial experience with Sentaurus or COMSOL would be appreciated. linkedin:4481386406.desc: Are you excited to push the boundaries of artificial intelligence in nuclear technology? Join us as a doctoral student to explore the advanced frontier of AI-driven nuclear safeguards and enhance global nuclear safety and security. About Us The Reactor Physics, Modelling and Safety group at Chalmers develops advanced methods for modelling, simulation, monitoring and safety analysis of current and next-generation nuclear reactors. Combining expertise in reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, nuclear safeguards, diagnostic techniques and machine learning applied to nuclear technology, the group conducts both fundamental and applied research in collaboration with national and international partners across academia and industry. We are part of the Division of Subatomic, High Energy and Plasma Physics, at the Department of Physics and Astronomy, offering a dynamic and stimulating working environment. About The Research Project Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models are powerful tools for Spent Nuclear Fuel (SNF) safeguards inspection. However, their architectural and optimization complexity renders them black boxes, posing a challenge when making critical decisions, such as classifying SNF as either consistent or inconsistent with declared information. In this doctoral research, you will investigate an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework to enable transparency in ANN models and their predictions for SNF inspection, bridging high-performing machine learning with transparent nuclear verification. Who We Are Looking For The following requirements are mandatory: To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree (masterexamen) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree (magisterexamen) of 60 credits* in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or equivalent. You have strong written and verbal communication skills in English. You have background/experience in at least one of the following areas: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Explainable AI, Reactor Physics, Nuclear Safeguards. You have a solid background in computational methods and strong programming skills (e.g., in Python). You thrive in a collaborative environment and take responsibility for your work. You have a strong analytical mindset and enjoy complex challenges. for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted. What You Will Do Conduct doctoral research focused on exploring, testing, and evaluating an Explainable AI (XAI) framework for Spent Nuclear Fuel (SNF) safeguards inspection. Integrate various XAI methods and study semantic layers to aggregate predictions into actionable explanations for safeguards inspectors. Leverage XAI insights to guide ANN model architectures, optimize training strategies, and strengthen model robustness. Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate research results through peer-reviewed journal publications and conference presentations. Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Nuclear Engineering. The position generally also includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours. Contract terms The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start. Moreover, the VUB is a member of EUTOPIA , an alliance of like-minded European universities, all ready to reinvent themselves. 2 - Position description The Faculty of Engineering , Department Applied Mechanics , Research Group Thermodynamics and Fluid Mechanics is looking for a PhD-student with a doctoral grant . More concretely your work package, for the preparation of a doctorate , contains: We offer a full-time PhD position in the framework of the ERC Starting Grant project “Energising the future with clean plasma-based technologies” (ESCAPADE, proposal number 101302707). Plasma-assisted combustion (PAC) offers a promising pathway towards cleaner and more efficient combustion of sustainable fuels. However, progress towards industrial deployment is limited by the absence of predictive computational tools capable of capturing the complex interactions between plasma discharges, chemistry, and flame dynamics. ESCAPADE addresses this challenge by developing an innovative multi-physics simulation framework that combines first-principles modeling, machine learning, reduced-order techniques, and computational fluid dynamics. The project will deliver the next generation of predictive tools for the design and optimization of low-emission combustion systems operating with both sustainable and conventional fuels. The FLOW research group at the VUB has a strong expertise in both fundamental and applied research topics related to the modelling of thermal-fluid systems, with applications in aeronautics (unsteady aerodynamics, flow control), aerospace (atmospheric re-entry, aerospace plasmas) and energy (wind energy, bioenergy, hydrogen, heat networks, combustion). Since 2021, FLOW joined forces with the ATM research group at ULB, working in similar fields of expertise, to create the VUB-ULB Joint Research Group BRITE (Brussels Institute for Thermal-fluid Systems and clean Energy, https://brite-research.be ). Plasma-assisted combustion combines non-equilibrium plasma discharges with combustion processes to improve ignition, flame stability, and pollutant emissions for sustainable fuels. While detailed state-to-state plasma-combustion models provide an unprecedented description of the underlying physics, their computational cost remains prohibitively high for multidimensional simulations and industrial applications. This PhD project aims to develop the next generation of computational tools for plasma-assisted combustion by combining detailed state-to-state kinetic modelling, mechanism reduction, and physics-informed machine learning. The researcher will contribute to the development of advanced plasma-assisted combustion simulation codes capable of explicitly modelling plasma discharges, non-equilibrium chemistry, and combustion processes across a wide range of operating conditions. A key objective of the project is the development of novel reduction methodologies for large state-to-state kinetic mechanisms containing hundreds to thousands of species and reactions. Building upon recent advances such as plasma-directed relation graph techniques (P-DRGEP), principal component analysis, and machine-learning-based lumping strategies, the PhD candidate will construct high-fidelity reduced-order models that preserve the essential plasma-combustion interactions while significantly reducing computational costs. The developed methodologies will be integrated into in-house plasma-assisted combustion solvers and validated against experimental benchmark datasets generated by leading international partners of the project. Emphasis will be placed on ammonia/hydrogen combustion systems, which are emerging as key carbon-free fuels for future energy and propulsion applications. The resulting reduced models will enable direct integration of detailed plasma chemistry into advanced CFD environments, including DNS and LES simulations of realistic combustion systems. References Rekkas-Ventiris, G., Giuntini, L., Sabia, P., Sorrentino, G., & Bellemans, A. (2026). Numerical investigation of plasma-assisted MILD combustion of ammonia using a hybrid modeling approach. Fuel , 406 , 136751. Rekkas-Ventiris, G., Gomez, A. D., Deak, N., Kincaid, N., Pepiot, P., Bisetti, F., & Bellemans, A. (2024). A novel machine learning based lumping approach for the reduction of large kinetic mechanisms for plasma-assisted combustion applications. Combustion and Flame , 260 , 113252. The research will focus on developing oxide-ion synaptic transistors and integrating them into neuromorphic chips to implement neural networks directly in hardware. The successful candidate will work at the interface of iontronic devices, microfabrication and neuromorphic electronics, progressing from individual artificial synapses to functional arrays and hardware demonstrations. These devices use controlled oxygen-ion motion to tune and store their electrical conductance, enabling analog in-memory computing. The research will combine device fabrication, electrical characterization and programming with the implementation and validation of neural networks for low-power edge computing. The position offers hands-on training in advanced fabrication and measurement techniques and close collaboration with partners working on microelectronics, algorithms and system integration. Characterize synaptic devices and arrays, assessing conductance modulation, programming speed, retention, endurance, variability and energy consumption. Develop automated electrical measurements and programming protocols to address devices and set synaptic weights, including thermally assisted programming with integrated micro-heaters. Implement and validate analog computing operations and neural-network functions in device arrays, linking measured device properties to computational accuracy and energy efficiency. Collaborate with IMB-CNM and UOC on circuit and system integration, contributing to hardware demonstrations for satellite navigation (GNSS) signal processing and intelligent IoT nodes. linkedin:4473919984.title: Industrial PhD position: Superconducting Qubit Control
linkedin:4473919984.desc: Your role This is a position for one industrial PhD student in Göteborg Sweden. As a part of the position, you will be enrolled as a student in the research school of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology (WACQT) at Chalmers University of Technology. At Chalmers, your research will contribute to the development of a quantum computer based on superconducting circuits by optimising the microwave control signals. At Saab you will become a part of a team that develops new concepts and studies future technologies. Here, you will apply your deep technical expertise in support of future radar systems. This is a fulltime position with Saab. During the time of enrolment in the graduate school, you will spend 80% of your time towards the PhD studies at Chalmers, and the remaining 20% working with Saab internal projects. Background Quantum computers (QCs) are currently being researched and developed by many actors worldwide, with ever increasing performance in terms of qubit counts, coherence times, and gate fidelities across several different modalities. Among the QC modalities, superconducting circuits have perhaps enjoyed the largest development efforts and are also the quantum computing research platform at Chalmers University of Technology, under development within the WACQT programme. Qubit control in superconducting circuits which involves, e.g., state preparation, gate operations, and readout, is implemented with microwave pulses. When scaling up for fault-tolerant quantum computing, the complex quantum mechanical systems must be able to correct for a multitude of error sources. Due to known and unknown characteristics of the quantum system, such as unwanted coupling, cross-talk, non-linearities, control signal overlap etc., errors will disturb the sensitive qubit states. It has been shown that leakage errors may be reduced significantly by careful design of the microwave signals to improve single-qubit and two-qubit gate fidelities, state preparation, and readout. Optimisation of the control signals is a crucial tool in moving towards fault-tolerant quantum computing that will require large qubit counts and high-fidelity operations. Research project This research project will be to study techniques to enhance the performance of QCs based on superconducting circuits by optimising the control system of the qubits. The research activities will focus on designing the microwave control signals. The optimal control routines will be experimentally tested and evaluated on state-of-the-art quantum computing devices. Primarily, you will study techniques of waveform optimisation for the qubit control signals, such as hardware adaptive microwave pulse design. The goals of this research are novel methods that improve total fidelities by optimising the control of state preparation, logical gates, and state readout. The research outcome should support an accelerated development of large-scale, fault-tolerant QCs. The project will balance both experimental and theoretical aspects of qubit control. On the one hand, pulse design requires detailed modelling of the quantum mechanical system dynamics, including multiple error sources and characteristics that are specific to the particular device. To validate the system models and estimate unknown model parameters, there will also be research activities regarding system characterisation on the experimental quantum computing device. Your profile You shall have strong background in mathematics and physics, for example a Master’s degree in Engineering Physics (Civilingenjör Teknisk Fysik), with an interest in modelling of and working experimentally with complex technical research questions. We believe that a Master’s level education in quantum mechanics is important. You should be curious and excited to be working with new technologies and be comfortable working independently. Particular merits for the position include: Experience in working with quantum computing technology and superconducting circuits Experience in working with experimentally with microwave systems Good communication skills, in direct communication and writing Experience in working with high level programming languages, such as Matlab or Python This position requires that you pass a security vetting based on the current regulations around/of security protection. For positions requiring security clearance additional obligations on citizenship may apply. About WACQT: Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology WACQT is a 12-year research effort aiming at developing and securing Swedish expertise within quantum computing and simulation, quantum communications, and quantum sensing. A large part is devoted to develop a quantum computer that can solve problems far beyond the reach of the best conventional supercomputers. Time: 2018 – 2030 Funder: Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation Budget: 1.4 billion SEK plus cofounding Universities: Chalmers University of Technology (coordinator), Lund University, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm University, Linköping University, University of Gothenburg. https://wacqt.se What you will be a part of Explore a wealth of possibilities. Together, we achieve the extraordinary, each bringing our unique perspectives. Your part matters. Saab designs, manufactures and maintains advanced systems in aeronautics, weapons, command and control, sensors and underwater systems. Saab is headquartered in Sweden. linkedin:4464669716.desc: Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain. In our research group, we design mechanically robust, multi-responsive polyurethane elastomer with backbone-integrated molecular switches. Our aim is to move beyond conventional stimuli-responsive materials, which merely switch between predetermined states, toward life-like materials that genuinely learn: Forming memories, consolidating them over time, selectively forgetting, and adapting their behavior through experience, all while retaining commercial-grade mechanical properties. In this PhD project, you will synthesize and characterize semi-crystalline polyurethane elastomers containing backbone-integrated photo-, halo-, and thermochromic molecular switches, and investigate how their interactions can be engineered to produce quantifiable memory and learning behaviors. Your tasks Synthesize libraries of single-, dual-, and triple-switch polyurethanes (Stenhouse salt, DASA, and Spiropyran) via copolymerization and post-polymerization functionalization, and validate backbone integration by NMR, GPC, DSC, DMA, tensile testing, UV-Vis spectroscopy, and pump probe characterization. Design and characterize synergistic switching cascades (collaborative, competitive, and interdependent pathways) using time-resolved and spatially resolved spectroscopy, patterned illumination, and pH/thermal stimuli. Develop and validate logic maps for memory formation, consolidation, and selective forgetting, and translate these into training-recall-forgetting cycles on physical polymer films and bilayer actuators. Contribute to integrating learning materials into soft robotic bilayer actuators and, together with the wider team, demonstrate behavioral adaptation in autonomous soft robots. Collaborate with international partners Your profile The candidate should have a strong background in Organic Chemistry, Polymer Chemistry, Materials Science, or a closely related field. We are looking for a highly motivated, curious person who enjoys working at the interface of synthetic chemistry, materials science, and soft robotics, who is comfortable in a multidisciplinary, collaborative environment. The PhD candidate needs to be highly proficient in spoken and written English and hold a Master's degree. S/he will participate in writing scientific publications and presenting data at national and international scientific conferences. Previous experience in one or more of the following areas is required: Polymer/polyurethane synthesis and characterization Molecular switches (e.g., photochromic, halochromic, or thermochromic systems) Standard analytical methods (NMR, UV-Vis, FTIR, and related techniques) Thermomechanical characterization of polymers (DSC, DMA, tensile testing) Experience with soft actuators or soft robotic systems is a plus but not required. linkedin:4482173810.title: PhD Candidate in Complex Networks- NL
linkedin:4482173810.desc: The Mathematical Institute (MI) of Leiden University and the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS) are looking for a PhD Candidate in Complex Networks to commence at the earliest possible date and no later than April 2027. The project investigates how structural properties observed in complex networks can be understood and modeled using mathematically tractable network models. The research will combine theoretical modeling with computational and data-driven investigation of real-world networks, with a particular emphasis on understanding how features such as spatial structure, clustering, heterogeneity, and connectivity shape network behavior. Possible research directions include, but are not limited to, network science, spatial network modeling, random graph models, and data-driven methods for network analysis. We welcome candidates with an interest in real-world network data as well as in developing and analyzing mathematical models of complex networks. The precise balance between theoretical, computational, and data-driven work will depend on the candidate’s background and interests. The position will be co-supervised by dr. Moritz Otto (MI) and dr. Akrati Saxena (LIACS). Michel Mandjes (MI) will act as promotor. Academic excellence is the main selection criterion. What You Will Do Conducting complex networks research at the intersection of mathematics and computer science. Writing a publication-based PhD thesis. Engaging in a limited number of teaching and supervision activities. Where you will work The PhD candidate will be employed at the Mathematical Institute and also be affiliated with the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science and AI (LIACS). In particular, the candidate will become part of the Leiden AlFa (Algorithmic Fairness: https://alfa.liacs.nl) group and the Probability research group, and collaborate closely with the Network Science group. Both the research groups and the institutes are highly international and feature a mix of disciplinary and cultural backgrounds. There are plenty of additional opportunities for other types of interaction and collaboration, for example, at the Faculty of Science through the Leiden Complex Networks Network (LCN2) and nationally through the Dutch Network Science Society. The Mathematical Institute focuses on four key research themes: Algebra, Geometry, and Number Theory; Analysis and Dynamical Systems; Probability; and Statistics and Data Science. There is extensive collaboration between these themes. For more information about the Mathematical Institute, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/mathematics. LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: http://www.cs.leiden.edu What You Bring A university degree* in mathematics, computer science or a closely related field. Knowledge in an area of research related to network science/complex networks, e.g., graph theory, probability, random graphs, complex systems, or topological data analysis. Programming experience, preferably in Python, and willingness to develop strong computational skills (please mention your level of proficiency and knowledge of other programming languages in your CV). Strong motivation for academic research. Good English communication skills. The ability to work independently and in a team. You live and are officially registered as resident in The Netherlands or are willing to relocate upon starting the position. Candidates who expect to complete their Master’s degree by early spring 2027 are also encouraged to apply. What We Offer We offer a full-time position for initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the thesis, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended by a further three years. A salary starting from € 3.204,= to € 4.051,= gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours, Payscale P) A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP; Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel; Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme; If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands; A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop and a mobile telephone. For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions What We Value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Only applications received via the university’s application tool by 24 November 2026 can be considered. Please send us Your CV and full academic transcripts (bachelor’s and master’s) A short cover letter of at most 2 pages detailing your motivation to apply for the position A recent writing example (paper or thesis) that you are proud of and that reflects your academic writing skills Names and contact details of at least one person who has agreed to be contacted for an academic reference (there is no need to send letters) In case of doubt or questions about the suitability of your research interest for this position, feel very welcome to reach out to dr. Moritz Otto (m.f.p.otto@math.leidenuniv.nl) or dr. Akrati Saxena (a.saxena@liacs.leidenuniv.nl), before formally applying. If you have any questions about the application procedure, please contact hr@math.leidenuniv.nl. Interviews are expected to take place from 1 December 2026.

linkedin:4472327025.desc: Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 16 000 students and 5 200 employees, including 446 professors. Our campus is in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community. The School of Chemical Engineering is one of the six schools of Aalto University. It combines natural sciences and engineering in a unique way. We are now looking for a DOCTORAL RESEARCHER IN CHEMICAL ENGINEERING for a funded position in an industrial collaboration project together with Neste Oyj, related to development of dynamic trickle bed reactor models . The project duration is four years, during which you are expected to finalize your PhD degree. Your role and goals Trickle bed reactors are in a central position in many refinery operations, both in traditional oil refining as well as treatment of novel bio-based feedstocks. Trickle bed operations have been studied from many angles, including fluid flow models, chemical kinetics, and mass transfer. Despite these, there is still a need for dynamic models of trickle bed reactors with both industrial and scientific importance. Your task would be to develop such models based on literature, in collaboration with an industrial partner. You should: Collect and critically analyze relevant literature Build and analyze models for predicting dynamic trickle bed reactor operations, including material and energy balances, reaction kinetics, mass and heat transfer, phase equilibria, fluid flow, and process control and operation Collaborate with other members of the research group and external partners to achieve project goals Present research findings at conferences and publish results in peer-reviewed journals Your network and team You will be working in the Chemical Engineering research group lead by professor Ville Alopaeus. Chemical Engineering research group is part of Department of Chemical and Metallurgical Engineering in the School of Chemical Engineering at Aalto University. Currently the research group consists of around 15 researchers in various roles related to research and teaching. Your Experience And Ambitions We are looking for motivated and research-oriented candidates with curious engineering mindset, good communication and collaboration skills and good understanding about mechanistic process modeling principles, phase equilibria, reaction engineering, heat and mass transfer, and fluid dynamics. A Master’s degree in Chemical Engineering, or related field is required. Applicants must fulfill the eligibility and admission criteria for Aalto Doctoral Programme in Chemical Engineering. Doctoral studies at Aalto University take approximately four years . You can find more information about Aalto’s doctoral program and its requirements here: https://www.aalto.fi/en/programmes/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-chemical-engineering What We Offer We offer a fixed term contract initially for 2 years. During the first 6 months you must apply and receive a right to study in the Doctoral Programme in Chemical Engineering. After a successful evaluation by the end of the first 2 year contract, the contract will be extended. Extension contract is typically based on the progress evaluation, revised project plan and available funding. The starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is about 3140 €/month (gross). The contract includes Aalto University occupational healthcare benefits. We value work-life balance and well-being in all aspects of life. The primary workplace will be the Otaniemi Campus in Espoo, Finland. Life on the revitalized campus is vibrant, featuring stunning architecture, tranquil nature, and a variety of cafes, restaurants, and services, all complemented by excellent public transportation connections. We offer great possibilities for competence development and learning. We constantly keep learning to find the most impactful ways to empower – and invest in – our people. Join us! To apply, please submit your application including your through our recruitment site (click "Apply now!”) latest at 23.59pm (EET) 30th October 2026 . The application material should include: Motivation letter (maximum one page) CV and possible proofs of scientific activity (publications, conference papers etc.) A certified copy of master´s degree certificate and an official transcript of records Any other supporting documents, such as recommendation letters Please note: Aalto University’s employees should apply for the position via our internal HR system Workday (Internal Jobs) by using their existing Workday user account (not via the external webpage for open positions). If you are a student or visitor at Aalto University, please apply with your personal email address (not aalto.fi) via Aalto University open positions Note that only submissions through the online recruitment system are accepted. linkedin:4482467388.title: PhD in Multifunctional Polymer Composites
linkedin:4482467388.desc: Introduction Are you inspired to push the limits of polymeric materials for lighter and smarter defense platforms? Join us to develop a new generation of 3D-printed composite panels that shield electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact. Job Description We are offering 2 PhD positions within project VALOR, an ambitious, interdisciplinary collaboration between academia, industry and government partners. The project aims to develop a new generation of lightweight composite panels that both shield sensitive electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact events, helping to make defense platforms safer and more resilient. Naval ships, drones and military vehicles increasingly depend on electronic radar, communication and navigation systems that must be protected against electromagnetic interference and radar detection . Today, this is mostly done with metals, which block practically all wave power with only a thin layer. However, they add weight, corrode, and reflect electromagnetic waves, making platforms easier to detect. Project VALOR tackles this challenge by merging two fields that have so far been developed separately: absorption-based electromagnetic shielding and impact-resistant sandwich structures . By combining 3D-printed architected nanocomposite materials with predictive modelling into one integrated design strategy, the project will construct a design framework for panels that are able to both carry loads and absorb electromagnetic waves, with a performance that can be tailored to specific (defense) applications. Your role We Are Recruiting Two PhD Candidates Who Will Work As a Team Throughout The Project, I.e. From Material Screening To Design And Testing Of Larger Scale Panel Demonstrators. Both Candidates Will Conduct a Combination Of Experimental And Numerical Work And Collaborate Closely With Industrial Partners Within The Consortium. More Specifically PhD 1 focuses on mechanics and manufacturing: 3D printing nanocomposite lattice materials, fabricating composite facesheets, conducting mechanical tests, constructing and validating mechanical finite element models. PhD 2 focuses on electromagnetic testing and design: formulating polymer nanocomposite materials and characterizing their electromagnetic behaviour, designing and testing absorbing architected nanocomposite structures, conducting electromagnetic shielding simulations. Your team and network You will join the Processing and Performance of Materials section in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at TU/e. The group has around 20 PhD and post-doctoral researchers working on how processing, structure and properties connect in polymers and polymer-based composite materials. The group is known for its integrated experimental-numerical approach to tailor the performance of these materials. You will have access to state-of-the-art computational facilities and laboratories dedicated to rheology, polymer processing (incl. additive manufacturing) and mechanical testing. You will be supervised by Frederik Van Loock (project leader), Ruth Cardinaels and Tom Engels. Job Requirements PhD 1 – Mechanics and manufacturing We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious researcher with the following qualifications: A master’s degree (or equivalent) with excellent grades in Mechanical Engineering with a specialization in mechanics of materials / solid mechanics. A strong interest in combining experimental work with numerical modelling. Enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary team and with industrial and defense partners. A research-oriented mindset: critical thinking is your second nature. Good communication skills and fluency in English, both spoken and written (C1 level). Experience with one or more of the following areas is a plus: mechanical characterization of polymer-based materials, finite element simulations of mechanical behaviour of polymer-based materials, 3D printing of polymers, polymer and composite processing. PhD 2 – Electromagnetic testing and design We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious researcher with the following qualifications: A master’s degree (or equivalent) with excellent grades in Engineering (Mechanical or Electrical), Materials Science or Applied Physics, with a specialization in materials. A strong interest in combining experimental work with numerical modelling. Enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary team and with industrial and defense partners. A research-oriented mindset: critical thinking is your second nature. Good communication skills and fluency in English, both spoken and written (C1 level). Experience with one or more of the following areas is a plus: electromagnetic characterization of polymer-based materials (e.g. vector network analysis, waveguide measurements), electromagnetic simulations (e.g. full-wave finite element modelling), 3D printing and processing of polymers. Why Join? Work within the multidisciplinary Processing and Performance of Materials group Work at the forefront of advanced materials research in collaboration with industry leaders. Combine material formulation, characterization, and computation in a multidisciplinary team. Get trained to use cutting-edge experimental and numerical simulation facilities. Contribute to the development of advanced multi-functional and 3D printed composite panels that make defense platforms more safe and resilient. Work in an international working environment and present your work at international conferences. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About Us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. The Department of Mechanical Engineering department conducts world-class research aligned with the technological interests of the high-tech industry in the Netherlands, with a focus on the Brainport region. Our goal is to produce engineers who are both scientifically educated and application-driven by providing a balanced education and research program that combines fundamental and application aspects. We equip our graduates with practical and theoretical expertise, preparing them optimally for future challenges. Information Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to know more? Please contact the hiring manager Frederik Van Loock, f.v.loock@tue.nl. Visit our website for more information about the application process. You can also contact HRServices.me@tue.nl. Curious to hear more about what it’s like as a PhD candidate at TU/e? Please view the video. Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page. Application We invite you to submit a complete application by using the apply button. The application should include a: Cover letter in which you describe your motivation and qualifications for the position. Curriculum vitae, including a list of your publications and the contact information of three references. Kindly note that we may reach out to references at any stage of the recruitment process. We recommend notifying your references upon submitting your application. Complete overview of grades obtained (bachelor & master degree). Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. We give priority to complete applications. We look forward to receiving your application and will screen it as soon as possible. The vacancy will remain open until the position is filled. Please note You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. linkedin:4476199948.title: PhD position Secure multi-stakeholder 6G orchestration
linkedin:4476199948.desc: Join the Dutch 6G flagship project to help shape the future of communications. Job Description Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge. 6G services will no longer run in a single place. They will be built from software functions that are placed, scaled, and moved across devices, base stations, edge sites, and central clouds, often owned and operated by different parties. This PhD project designs, builds, and evaluates the management and orchestration (MANO) systems that make this multi-stakeholder continuum secure and dependable. The research question is how orchestration can decide across infrastructure that cannot be fully trusted. The project addresses how hardware roots of trust are discovered, allocated, and carried across migration, how a node is attested continuously while it serves traffic, how split AI workloads are placed without exposing model or data across trust boundaries, and how orchestration decisions are made auditable. The work extends open-source orchestration platforms and is validated on FNS experimental infrastructure in collaboration with industrial partners. You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. Fostering a highly collaborative and friendly atmosphere, we will give you all the support you need to develop and grow. Moreover, as a valued member of the FNS consortium, you can collaborate with various partners in pursuit of integrating your AI/ML techniques into the various 6G PoCs and demos. Job requerements Become part of an expansive ecosystem shaping the development of 6G. You will benefit from training in 5G and beyond networks, AI, and software development. Plus, you will gain exclusive access to (1) a state-of-the-art testbed where theory meets real-world application, and (2) an ecosystem that cultivates entrepreneurial endeavours. Are you ready to challenge yourself? We're seeking candidates who have, or are about to receive, a Master-of-Science degree in a relevant computer science discipline and who like to combine theory with practice. Proficiency in English is essential, as you'll collaborate within a diverse, international community. For more details on our admission requirements, please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/opleidingen/phd/admission. We’ll evaluate based on your academic record, interviews, and possibly assignments. While a strong background in the field is crucial, what matters as well is your creative flair, motivation, and above all, your passion for comprehensive research! TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context. At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration. Challenge. Change. Impact! Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact dr. Nitinder Mohan, via n.mohan@tudeft.nl. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 1 Nov 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: CV Motivational letter Copies of your BSc and MSc degrees and transcripts. You can address your application to dr. Nitinder Mohan. Applications will be evaluated as they come in,so please apply as soon as possible. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services. Recruitmentcode 6Gflagship

indeed:511d3a537d1ec7ab.title: Master's Theses "Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence for Cyber Security"
indeed:511d3a537d1ec7ab.desc: The AIT Austrian Institute of Technology is Austria’s largest Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) . We aim to transform scientific excellence into innovation with impact. Together with our partners, we develop technologies and solutions for a sustainable, resilient, and digitalised future, strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and technological sovereignty. Our international teams combine cutting-edge research with strong implementation expertise to create measurable value for industry and society. Our Center for Digital Safety & Security invites applications for master’s theses at our location in Vienna (Giefinggasse, 1210). At the Center for Digital Safety & Security, we conduct research into a wide range of key technologies such as distributed IT systems, the Internet of Things (IoT), cybersecurity, data science, artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain technologies, quantum and photonic technologies, wireless systems (6G) and digital solutions for crisis and disaster management. Our Research Field Cyber Security , which forms part of the Cyber Security & Communication Technologies Competence Unit, specialises in applied research in the field of digital security and is pioneering the development of highly innovative concepts, algorithms and systems for anomaly detection, cyber-threat analysis, penetration testing and cryptography. Using our groundbreaking technologies, we simulate modern ICT and OT infrastructures as well as cyber-attacks. Master's Theses "Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence for Cyber Security" CENTER FOR DIGITAL SAFETY & SECURITY We are looking for motivated and enthusiastic master’s students to join our team for a period of six to eight months . The ideal candidate has a solid background and a strong interest in one or more areas relevant to cyber security, such as (1) data science and data analysis, (2) software development and systems engineering, or (3) machine learning and artificial intelligence. You will work closely with our senior researchers to further develop and enhance open-source solutions for areas such as log-data analysis for intrusion detection, cyber threat intelligence processing, and the dynamic provisioning of complex IT infrastructures. Guided by our interdisciplinary team, you may apply modern data-driven methods to process, analyse, and interpret log data for indications of cyber attacks. Alternatively, you may focus on natural language processing (NLP) techniques and large language models (LLMs) for the automated processing and analysis of cyber threat intelligence feeds. As a cyber security enthusiast, you will contribute directly to our projects, academic publications, and open-source code bases , helping to strengthen the European cyber security ecosystem . You will further develop your scientific research skills and have the opportunity to exchange ideas with leading experts and experienced researchers in the field. You will gain first-hand insights into how a research organisation collaborates with customers and industry partners to address real-world cyber security challenges. Your qualifications as an Ingenious Partner: Master’s student at an Austrian university in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field. Basic knowledge of relevant technologies and methods in the Cyber Security area. A conscientious, independent working style and a high degree of reliability. For prototype development, experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage, depending on the specific thesis topic: Python-based implementations, including data structures, machine learning libraries, mathematics, and statistics Security monitoring technologies, technical artefacts of cyber attacks, and their analysis Log data analytics, data science methods, and data visualization techniques A good understanding of common network protocols, Linux operating systems, and their application in modern enterprise environments Linux user-space and kernel-space development, including C programming and kernel internals Automated deployment and system integration, including system design, C, Python, Linux scripting, and Ansible Application of large language models (LLMs) and artificial intelligence (AI), including evaluation harnesses, prompting strategies, and their application in cyber security Strong interest in applied research questions and real-world challenges from industry High level of motivation and a collaborative, team-oriented mindset. Good written and spoken English and German skills What to expect: Duration of the internship: 6-8 months Start date: There is flexibility concerning the start-date A remuneration of EUR 1.379,60 gross per month for 20 hours per week. In addition to our company benefits, we offer flexible working conditions and work experience in a highly innovative environment. As a research institution, we are familiar with the supervision and implementation of final theses and are looking forward to supporting you accordingly. At AIT, we create an inclusive and family-friendly working environment that promotes equal opportunities and actively strengthens diversity across our workforce and in leadership positions. Among other initiatives, we are committed to increasing the proportion of women in our company and therefore particularly welcome applications from female applicants. Please submit your complete application documents online, consisting of your CV, a cover letter, relevant certificates (transcript of records), as well as a proof of identity. Apply now!

indeed:3c4faa1ef2a706fd.title: Doctoral Researcher, SmartSpaces project, Centre for Wireless Communications
indeed:3c4faa1ef2a706fd.desc: The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are now looking for a Doctoral Researcher to join the Centre for Wireless Communications unit at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering, University of Oulu. The Centre for Wireless Communications (CWC) counts about 250 experts working in four research groups. The research topics are selected to create scientific knowledge and engineering solutions with high impact, to train professionals and to enable resilient, sustainable, and secure connectivity and networks. The vision is to stay among world leading academic communities, and conduct research on wireless communications and technologies for future 6G networks. About the job The doctoral researcher will contribute to the SmartSpaces project, funded by the Research Council of Finland in collaboration with research partners at Rice University, USA. The research will focus on enabling wireless systems to sense and interpret their surroundings and provide secure, efficient spatial awareness services. Particular emphasis will be placed on mathematical modelling, optimization, and algorithm development for integrated sensing and communication. Topics of interest include: RF radar signal processing Backscattering Resource allocation and scheduling. Query-driven and task-oriented sensing. Machine learning for adaptive sensing and network operation. Combining RF and acoustic sensing to improve spatial awareness. Secure and trustworthy sensing, including authentication and resilience against eavesdropping, spoofing, and jamming. Efficient representations of sensed environments, including compact digital twins and the management of sensing information. The main duties of a doctoral researcher are related to undertaking original academic research in several of the above topics towards the award of a joint doctoral degree, accompanied by the publication of results in high-impact journals and conference venues, and thorough, transparent, and insightful collaboration with the whole research team. Who are you? You are required to have: A master’s or equivalent degree in Electrical and Communications Engineering, Computer Sciences, or related fields, with top grades. Skills and motivation for doctoral studies. Excellent verbal and writing communication skills in English. Additionally, to succeed and enjoy the position, you are expected to have: A strong background in Mathematics Excellent programming skills Aptitude for working both independently and as part of a team Aptitude for developing strong productive relationships At least one of the following prerequisite skills: wireless communications/networking convex optimization signal processing machine learning RF radars You must apply for the right to study for a doctoral degree at the beginning of your employment in accordance with the requirements of the University of Oulu Graduate School (UniOGS). What we offer The support of an experienced and enthusiastic team with whom you can share your expertise and grow as an expert. Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture, and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits. Development and career options of the big organization. Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us. Our Buddy Programme and Spouse Network support you and your close ones in settling into Oulu. We have an HR Excellence in Research -quality label, which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers. Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, an excellent education system, and a competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu. Salary The position is fixed-term for 3 years, starting as soon as possible. The salary will be based on the levels 2-4 of the demand level chart for teaching and research staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance will be paid (a maximum of 50 % of the job-specific component). The starting gross salary will be approximately 2800-2900 € per month (before taxes). A trial period of 6 months is applied to the position. How to apply? Interested? If yes, please apply by October 31, 2026 (23:59 Finnish local time) through our recruitment system. The application should be written in English and include the following: CV List of publications (if applicable) Motivation letter (1-page description of the motivation and suitability for the position, and more importantly, the specific research interests and how would you tentatively address them) During the recruitment process, be prepared to provide the details of 1-2 persons available for recommendation as well as the copies Master’s or equivalent Diploma and transcript of records. The application period has been extended to October 31. The initial application deadline was on October 13. Contact Information If you have any further questions, please contact Associate Professor Onel Alcaraz López (Onel.AlcarazLopez@oulu.fi). indeed:7cac406dea563321.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Doctorant A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle The Inria Saclay-Île-de-France Research Centre was established in 2008. It has developed as part of the Saclay site in partnership with Paris-Saclay University and with the Institut Polytechnique de Paris . The centre has 40 project teams , 27 of which operate jointly with Paris-Saclay University and the Institut Polytechnique de Paris; Its activities occupy over 600 people, scientists and research and innovation support staff, including 44 different nationalities. The team is bi-localized, hosting at CREST (on the Polytechnique campus) but working from Criteo HQ in Paris once a week. Mission confiée Agentic systems are increasingly present: agents make decisions or tasks. They may interact for that with other agents, which opens the possibility of collaboration, but also potentially of collusion. This was observed in the past in algorithmic pricing systems. Un avis ministériel défavorable pour un poste affecté dans une ZRR aurait pour conséquence l’annulation du recrutement. Politique de recrutement : Dans le cadre de sa politique diversité, tous les postes Inria sont accessibles aux personnes en situation de handicap. Contacts Équipe Inria : FAIRPLAY Directeur de thèse : Loiseau Patrick / patrick.loiseau@inria.fr L'essentiel pour réussir The successful candidate should have high motivation for research work and a taste for societal and security questions. A propos d'Inria Inria, l'institut national de recherche dans les sciences et technologies du numérique, est en appui de l’État pour les stratégies nationales de recherche et d’innovation du numérique en tant qu'Agence de programmes. Ensemble, nous explorons des domaines clés comme l'intelligence artificielle, la cybersécurité, l’informatique quantique, le Cloud, la transformation numérique de la santé, les jumeaux numériques ou encore les technologies numériques pour la défense. Notre objectif : l’impact scientifique, technologique et industriel au service de la souveraineté numérique de la France.

indeed:a8d436a0acb63dc1.title: PhD Student
indeed:a8d436a0acb63dc1.desc: Ihre Aufgaben Your tasks Design and perform multielectrode in vivo electrophysiological recordings from the inferior colliculus of the Mongolian gerbil. Develop and validate computational and data-driven models of auditory information processing and optogenetically evoked neural responses. Integrate experimental measurements into a digital-twin framework and assess model generalization, uncertainty and biological plausibility. Design and optimize sound-processing algorithms that map acoustic signals to spatial and temporal optical stimulation patterns, and benchmark their performance in vivo and in silico. Collaborate with experimental neuroscientists and engineers; present and publish scientific findings and contribute to interdisciplinary project meetings. Ihre Qualifikationen Your qualifications Completed MSc or equivalent in neuroscience, biomedical/electrical engineering, biology, physics or a related field. Enthusiasm for in vivo electrophysiology. No prior in vivo experience is required; full training in electrophysiological techniques will be provided. Good programming skills (preferably MATLAB/Python) and experience in signal processing, scientific computing or machine learning. Strong analytical skills, curiosity about biological systems and enthusiasm for developing experimental and computational research. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary, international team; very good written and spoken English. Knowledge of auditory neuroscience, PyTorch/JAX or computational neuroprosthetics is an advantage but not a prerequisite. Wir bieten We offer A scientifically ambitious PhD project at the interface of in vivo electrophysiology, computational modeling and optogenetic neurotechnology for future hearing restoration. Close interaction with teams at IAN and EKFZ-OT developing optical cochlear implants, with access to complementary experimental, computational and engineering expertise. An internationally connected Göttingen Campus research environment, opportunities for doctoral training at the Göttingen Graduate Center for Neuroscience, Biophysics and Molecular Biosciences. Support for scientific publications, professional development and participation in collaborative research networks and training academies. Employment and social benefits in accordance with the applicable TV-L regulations; final contract conditions to be specified. Weitere Informationen This PhD project is funded by CAIMed (Lower Saxony Center for AI and Causal Methods in Medicine) and will contribute to the Göttingen program developing optical cochlear implants for future hearing restoration. The goal is to establish an experimentally grounded digital twin of the auditory system and use it to generate, optimize, and benchmark sound-coding strategies for optogenetic stimulation of the auditory nerve. Combining in vivo electrophysiology, computational neuroscience, and generative modeling, the project investigates how acoustic signals can be transformed into spatiotenporal light patterns for stimulation via the optical cochlear implant under development at IAN and EKFZ-OT. Your application Please submit a cover letter describing your motivation and relevant research experience, a CV, academic certificates/transcripts, and contact details of two referees via the UMG application portal. Please indicate relevant programming projects or publications where applicable. We look forward to receiving your application! Travel and application expenses cannot be reimbursed.

indeed:cce5ef3ac11b72e7.title: PhD Researcher (m/f/d): Understanding climate risks to global food security
indeed:cce5ef3ac11b72e7.desc: PhD Researcher (m/f/d): Understanding climate risks to global food security Tasks Investigate feedback mechanisms and processes behind acceleration in extreme weather trends Design targeted climate model experiments and analyse large ensembles to test conditions under which tail-specific feedbacks are triggered Apply explainable AI (XAI) and other advanced statistical methods to uncover non-linear interactions between physical drivers of extremes Evaluate how well climate models represent these tail processes against observations and reanalysis Investigate drivers, statistics and impacts of record-breaking events in current and future climates, in collaboration with the other group members Publish in leading journals, present at international conferences Help organise group events Co-supervise PhD students Profile Essential Master's degree (or equivalent) in climate science, atmospheric science, physics, geosciences, environmental science, statistics or a related field Programming skills (e.g. Python, R) and experience handling gridded or time-series data Strong motivation for independent, interdisciplinary research Good command of written and spoken English Advantageous Experience with climate model output, reanalysis data or extreme event analysis Knowledge of extreme value statistics, compound events or time-series methods Experience with agricultural modelling and agricultural datasets Experience with machine learning or causal methods Previous research experience, e.g. a Master's thesis in a related topic Our offer The position will begin on the 1st of January 2027 though some flexibility in start date is possible. Remuneration will follow the standard PhD salaries given in the Max Planck Society which correspond to 65% of EG 13 TvöD (Bund). The position includes 31 days of annual leave. We also offer attractive and family-friendly flextime and options for remote work. Additional benefits include an employer subsidy for public transport, access to training opportunities within the Max Planck Society, as well as language and health courses. The successful candidate can apply for admission to our graduate school “International Max Planck Research School for Modeling the Anthropocene”. The Max Planck Society is committed to employing more individuals with disabilities and especially encourages them to apply. We are also committed to encouraging diversity and actively challenging biases based on gender, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion and other components of identity. We were honored with the TOTAL E-QUALITY award for the first time in 2023 for our commitment. The Max Planck Society supports the compatibility of family and career and is certified according to the "berufundfamilie" (“job and family”) audit. Your application should include: A cover letter A CV of no more than 3 pages A summary of research interests with max. 2 pages If applicable a list of relevant scientific, peer-reviewed publications related to the position or a copy of the candidate’s MA/MPhil/MSc thesis Contacts of two referees Any relevant certificates Position remains open until filled. About us The Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (MPI-GEA) was founded in summer 2022 and is a dynamically growing, highly-interdisciplinary and international research institution. The research focuses on modeling and analyzing the interrelationships between biophysical and human-made systems, looking from the deep past to the future. The institute examines how humanity has driven the emergence of the Anthropocene – the period in which human activities began significantly impacting our planet’s climate and ecosystems – and identifying potential intervention points towards a more sustainable future. The Carl Zeiss Stiftung Independent Research Group on High-End Climate Risks (CZS-HECR) at MPI-GEA works towards an end-to-end understanding of worst-case climate outcomes, from unprecedented and compounding extremes to their societal impacts. The group combines fundamental physical process understanding rooted in climate physics and Earth System analyses, targeted climate model experiments, advanced statistics, including machine-learning- and explainable AI to deliver usable climate risk estimates under current and future climates for core societal sectors such as health, food, energy and finance. indeed:e7f51da5f36bf7d1.title: PhD Researcher (m/f/d): Economic Impacts from Complex Climate Risks
indeed:e7f51da5f36bf7d1.desc: PhD Researcher (m/f/d): Economic Impacts from Complex Climate Risks Tasks Investigate the economic impacts of extreme, record-breaking and compounding weather extremes Develop novel statistical methods to integrate extreme weather events and their complex interaction into empirical damage functions and / or integrated assessment modelling frameworks Apply and/or develop agent-based economic models to investigate impacts from compounding weather extremes Apply causality tools and advanced statistical methods to disentangle drivers of worst case climate impacts Write and publish your research as a doctoral thesis and papers in international journals Present results at conferences and group events, and take part in training such as Summer Schools and Workshops Profile Essential Master's degree (or equivalent) in climate science, atmospheric science, physics, geosciences, mathematics, statistics or a related field Good knowledge of atmospheric dynamics and climate variability Programming skills (e.g. Python) and experience with analysing large climate datasets Strong motivation for independent research Good command of written and spoken English Advantageous Experience with climate observations, reanalysis and climate model output Experience with standard statistical modelling techniques Familiarity with causal inference, explainable AI and machine learning techniques Interest in the link between climate variability and societal impacts Our offer The position will begin on the 1st of January 2027 though some flexibility in start date is possible. Remuneration will follow the standard PhD salaries given in the Max Planck Society which correspond to 65% of EG 13 TvöD (Bund). The position includes 31 days of annual leave. We also offer attractive and family-friendly flextime and options for remote work. Additional benefits include an employer subsidy for public transport, access to training opportunities within the Max Planck Society, as well as language and health courses. The successful candidate can apply for admission to our graduate school “International Max Planck Research School for Modeling the Anthropocene”. The Max Planck Society is committed to employing more individuals with disabilities and especially encourages them to apply. We are also committed to encouraging diversity and actively challenging biases based on gender, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion and other components of identity. We were honored with the TOTAL E-QUALITY award for the first time in 2023 for our commitment. The Max Planck Society supports the compatibility of family and career and is certified according to the "berufundfamilie" (“job and family”) audit. Your application should include: A cover letter A CV of no more than 3 pages A summary of research interests with max. 2 pages If applicable a list of relevant scientific, peer-reviewed publications related to the position or a copy of the candidate’s MA/MPhil/MSc thesis Contacts of two referees Any relevant certificates Position remains open until filled. About us The Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (MPI-GEA) was founded in summer 2022 and is a dynamically growing, highly-interdisciplinary and international research institution. The research focuses on modeling and analyzing the interrelationships between biophysical and human-made systems, looking from the deep past to the future. The institute examines how humanity has driven the emergence of the Anthropocene – the period in which human activities began significantly impacting our planet’s climate and ecosystems – and identifying potential intervention points towards a more sustainable future. The Carl Zeiss Stiftung Independent Research Group on High-End Climate Risks (CZS-HECR) at MPI-GEA works towards an end-to-end understanding of worst-case climate outcomes, from unprecedented and compounding extremes to their societal impacts. The group combines fundamental physical process understanding rooted in climate physics and Earth System analyses, targeted climate model experiments, advanced statistics, including machine-learning- and explainable AI to deliver usable climate risk estimates under current and future climates for core societal sectors such as health, food, energy and finance. Doctoral researchers join an interdisciplinary team, and a broad international network are provided with highly competitive research conditions including generous support for travel and research visits.
