indeed:d95f63657731785c.title: PhD: new methodologies for RSV infection and immunity
indeed:d95f63657731785c.desc: Bilthoven Universitair Master 36 uur Schaal 8 / €3.333 - €4.457 (bruto) Onderzoek / wetenschap, Medisch / verzorging Solliciteer voor 9 november 2026 Dit ga je doen Are you an MSc graduate in viro-immunology and keen to help replace traditional animal testing? As a PhD researcher within a new European consortium, you will advance, standardize, and qualify a cutting-edge human cell-based model to evaluate RSV immunity. Working alongside leading scientists and regulators across Europe, you will deepen your expertise in advanced methodologies like single-cell RNA sequencing while shaping non-animal approaches in vaccine research. This role offers a clear path to complete your PhD thesis, publish high-impact literature, and build an international network at the intersection of science and public health. Developing Advanced Human Epithelial Models for RSV Traditionally, research into respiratory virus infection and immunity has relied on small animal models and in vitro cultures of immortalized cell lines. Bridging these experimental systems, differentiated primary human epithelial cell culture models are gaining ground, but their use in vaccine research remains limited due in part to a lack of immunological components and standardization of these models. We have recently developed a novel virus neutralization model for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). This virus causes considerable morbidity and mortality in infants and older adults, and first-generation preventive strategies have recently become available. Our novel neutralization model builds upon the previously established air–liquid interface respiratory epithelial transwell model, which includes functional multiciliated and mucus-producing goblet cells. Your responsibilities Within a new European consortium, you will apply the RSV neutralization model as a use case to advance its standardization and qualification as a new approach methodology (NAM) in collaboration with regulatory partner institutes in the UK and Germany. In addition, you will dive deeper into the possibilities of this model to provide insights into population variability as well as viral escape mutants. With this project, you will contribute to the implementation of novel in vitro methodologies that will increase our understanding of antiviral mucosal immunity and reduce the need for animal experiments. Your role will involve: Co-design of a standardization plan for the RSV neutralization model, in collaboration with (regulatory) consortium partners, including technical transfer of the model to partner sites. Performing extensive cell culture work including viral infections at BSL-2/ML-II biosafety level, aimed at standardization and further exploration of the RSV neutralization model. Various molecular biological and virological techniques, including (confocal) microscopy, virus titration, RT-qPCR, single-cell RNA sequencing and multiplex immunoassays. Systematic literature reviewing of available and ongoing studies related to the use of in vitro models of respiratory viral infection and immunity. Analyze and interpret data, publish in peer-reviewed scientific journals, present the results in the institute as well as at (inter-)national conferences and prepare a PhD thesis based on your findings. Participate in a team of virologists, immunologists, bioinformaticians and regulators at RIVM and collaborating institutes to share and discuss the results of your studies. About the RIVM department The Center for Immunology of Infectious Diseases and Vaccines (IIV) at RIVM serves as the government's knowledge center in the field of immunology of infectious diseases and vaccines. The core mission of IIV is to provide information and advice on vaccine effectiveness, vaccination strategies, and immune responses to infectious diseases, supporting government policy and informing the public. Research at IIV focuses on optimizing the effectiveness and safety of current and future vaccination programs, immunosurveillance, age-related efficacy of immune responses, and identifying correlates of protection. Within IIV, the Department of Immune Mechanisms - Immunological Models (IIM) employs immunological models to support the core mission of IIV. You will be part of IIM, an international, dynamic, and highly motivated team of approximately 20 scientists and technicians at various stages of our careers, united by a strong drive to advance immunological research for the benefit of public health. We combine expertise in virology, immunology, and bioinformatics, and we believe in the power of collaboration and teamwork. About the PhD programme The intended start date is February 1st, 2027. The PhD programme lasts four years. Your appointment is initially for one year. At the end of the first year, an evaluation takes place according to the standard procedure. If this evaluation is positive, the appointment will be extended by three years. During the PhD research, your salary is set as follows according to Functiegebouw Rijk (FGR): First year: €3,333.81, according to scale 8, step 0. Second year: €3.741,48, according to scale 8, step 5. Third year: €3.984,50, according to scale 8, step 7. Fourth year: €4.132,76, according to scale 8, step 8. How to apply and more information You can address your application to IIM manager Jørgen de Jonge. Do you have any questions before applying? Please contact project leader Puck van Kasteren (+316 311 423 91), she is more than happy to answer your questions. We look forward to hearing from you. In the event of substantial interest in this vacancy, we may invite a larger group of candidates for a short 15-minute online interview, including a brief pitch and two or three predefined questions Dit krijg je Schaal 8 €3.333 - €4.457 (bruto) Arbeidsovereenkomst voor bepaalde tijd 4 jaar 36 uur Het salaris is gebaseerd op een werkweek van 36 uur. Dit bieden we nog meer Naast het salaris ontvang je een Individueel Keuzebudget (IKB). Het IKB bestaat uit geld (16,50% van je bruto jaarsalaris) en tijd. Met het IKB maak jij de keuzes die bij jou passen en kun je een deel van je arbeidsvoorwaarden zelf samenstellen. Je kunt er bijvoorbeeld voor kiezen om een deel van je maandinkomen te laten uitbetalen wanneer jij dat wenst. Ook kun je dit budget omzetten in verlof en andersom of besteden aan fiscaal vriendelijke doelen. De Rijksoverheid hecht sterk aan persoonlijke groei en loopbaanontwikkeling en biedt daarvoor tal van mogelijkheden. Dit vragen wij Your profile To be successful in this position, you bring the following knowledge and experience: An MSc in biomedical sciences, biology, medicine, or a related discipline, preferably focused on infection and immunity. Background in infection and immunity or a related field, preferably with previous experience in cell culture work and virological methods (such as titration or neutralization assays). Strong analytical capacity to systematically review literature, interpret multifaceted datasets, and translate findings into rigorous scientific publications and your PhD thesis. High autonomy and initiative to independently plan, drive, and adapt your daily research activities. Clear communication skills in English, allowing you to articulate research outcomes effectively to diverse audiences. A collaborative mindset to align naturally with an international, multidisciplinary team of scientists, regulators, and laboratory technicians. Bij het RIVM hebben we één van de beste cao's van Nederland, namelijk die van de Rijksoverheid. Hier kom je te werken Over RIVM RIVM: deskundig, betrouwbaar en onafhankelijk Als Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu (RIVM) zijn we een deskundige, betrouwbare en onafhankelijke adviseur voor overheid, professionals en burgers. Ons doel: een gezonde bevolking en een duurzame, veilige en gezonde leefomgeving. We bewaken gezondheid, ziekten, de kwaliteit van de leefomgeving én het milieu. indeed:3dc56e9b5dcf865c.title: PhD Position: Safe Planning and Decision-Making under Uncertainty for Long-Horizon Robot Autonomy
indeed:3dc56e9b5dcf865c.desc: PhD Position: Safe Planning and Decision-Making under Uncertainty for Long-Horizon Robot Autonomy Join TU Delft and the EU-funded OPERA consortium. Push the frontier of general-purpose AI for robotics and tackle the fundamental tension between long-horizon reasoning and real-time safety guarantees. Job description Robots that operate for long periods among people must plan beyond the next few seconds while staying safe. They need to predict how their surroundings and the people in them will evolve, know how reliable these predictions are, and adapt their plans when the predictions fail. In the EU-funded OPERA project, TU Delft contributes to General-Purpose AI for robotics by developing methods that combine fast, reactive behavior with more deliberate reasoning, planning, and decision-making. In this PhD position, you will develop planning and decision-making methods that let robots act safely and reliably over long time horizons when their knowledge of the environment and of the people around them is incomplete. The research sits at the intersection of model-based planning and control and learning-based models, and addresses the trade-off between safety, performance, and real-time computation. You will formulate the methods and analyze their guarantees and failure modes. This research is connected to OPERA's tasks on GPAI-powered planning and decision-making, on long-term reasoning in human-centered environments, and on adaptive human-robot and robot-environment interaction. Depending on your background, the work may draw on optimal control and model predictive control, motion planning, probabilistic modeling and estimation, or learning-based methods. The emphasis is on methods with a clear formulation and well-understood failure modes, validated in simulation and on real robots. You will work in the Cognitive Robotics Department at TU Delft under the supervision of Prof. Robert Babuška and Dr. Laura Ferranti, and you will be embedded in the Reliable Robot Control Lab (https://r2clab.com/). You will collaborate with OPERA partners across Europe on simulation, perception, and the OPERA open-source toolbox. Job requirements The ideal candidate for this PhD position has a strong background in control, optimization, or motion planning and is motivated by the question of how robots can plan safely and reliably over long time horizons. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds who want to work at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. You have: An MSc degree in Systems and Control, Robotics, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. A strong interest in safe planning and decision-making for robots, at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. A passion for rigorous, theoretically grounded research, combined with an eagerness to validate ideas in simulation and on real robots. Strong analytical and mathematical skills, in particular in optimization, probability and statistics, and dynamical systems. Excellent communication skills and proficiency in English (written and verbal), as required for academic publication and international collaboration. You are particularly encouraged to apply if you have experience in one or more of the following areas: Hands-on experience implementing optimization-based planners or controllers (e.g., model predictive control with acados or CasADi) in C++ or Python. Safe or robust control and planning under uncertainty. Learned dynamics or prediction models, model-based reinforcement learning. Uncertainty quantification, probabilistic or Bayesian modeling, state estimation. Long-horizon or hierarchical planning, prediction of human or multi-agent behavior. Real-robot deployment with ROS or ROS 2. As part of OPERA, you will travel to meet and collaborate with the project’s European partners and attend regular consortium meetings. We particularly encourage applications from women and other underrepresented groups, as we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive research environment. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Mechanical Engineering From chip to ship. From machine to human being. From idea to solution. Driven by a deep-rooted desire to understand our environment and discover its underlying mechanisms, research and education at the ME faculty focusses on fundamental understanding, design, production including application and product improvement, materials, processes and (mechanical) systems. ME is a dynamic and innovative faculty with high-tech lab facilities and international reach. It’s a large faculty but also versatile, so we can often make unique connections by combining different disciplines. This is reflected in ME’s outstanding, state-of-the-art education, which trains students to become responsible and socially engaged engineers and scientists. We translate our knowledge and insights into solutions to societal issues, contributing to a sustainable society and to the development of prosperity and well-being. That is what unites us in pioneering research, inspiring education and (inter)national cooperation. . Do you want to experience working at our faculty? These videos will introduce you to some of our researchers and their work. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3059 - €3881 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information For more information, please reach out to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska [l.ferranti@tudelft.nl, r.babuska@tudelft.nl] Please do not use LinkedIn and other channels for applications or inquiries. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 15 November 2026 upload the following documents: A letter of motivation explaining why you are the right candidate for this project An updated cv Exam transcipts from your Bachelor and Master A copy of your MSc thesis, or draft MSc thesis (or a link to access it) You can address your application to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: #EUfunded This is an EU funded project, named OPERA, with project number 101298363, within program HORIZON/HORIZON-CL4-2025-04-DIGITAL-EMERGING-07 You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services. Faculty/Department: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering Salary range: €3059 - €3881 Hours per week: 38-40 FTE: 1,0 Submission is possible until: 15 Nov 2026 ID job: 3993

indeed:eee1df7ef95dc80a.title: PhD Candidate (MSCA) in multiscale ejector design and optimization within high temperature heat pumps
indeed:eee1df7ef95dc80a.desc: Career Vacant positions Job vacancy PhD Candidate (MSCA) in multiscale ejector design and optimization within high temperature heat pumps About the position SINTEF Energy is announcing two PhD candidate positions within the field of thermal engineering and industrial heat supply utilizing High Temperature Heat Pumps (HTHPs). Both positions are within the frame of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN). The candidate will be employed by the Energy Use Department to carry out the doctoral project described below, enrolled by the doctoral program at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), and have supervisors at both SINTEF and DTU Construct. About the project The activity is coordinated within the HeatMinds MSCA-DN by Brunel University in London, UK. The HeatMinds project is officially launched in October 2026 and holds a consortium of 18 partners across Europe. This integrated project aims to conduct collaborative research while training fifteen doctoral candidates to make a step change in accelerating the development and deployment of industrial HTHPs to support the decarbonization of heat supply in the process industry. Supported by leading universities, research centres, and industrial actors, advanced models and design tools will be developed that contribute to the advancement of these efforts. HeatMinds will tackle highly connected research questions, namely what are the optimum and sustainable cycle arrangements, component designs, and supporting energy policy frameworks? HeatMinds will establish a roadmap for deploying IHTHP technology to support the decarbonisation of several key industries. The other project partners recruiting PhD students are Brunel University (UK), City St. Georges University (UK), University of Seville (Spain), Technical University of Denmark, and SINTEF Industry. One of the PhD projects hosted by SINTEF Energy is titled “Multiscale design and optimization of ejectors integrated within novel IHTHP architectures” and addresses the potential for improved energy efficiency achieved by using ejectors. The project also addresses the coupled and multiscale challenges associated with optimal design and integration, and focuses on the use of natural working fluids. On the one hand, the analysis and design of optimal heat pump cycles is typically carried out using simple lumped or one-dimensional models. On the other hand, accurate component performance and design requires more detailed analysis methods, such as CFD, that present a challenge for how complex and coupled systems should be designed. This project includes elements of: Evaluation of two-phase ejector component integration strategies within high temperature heat pump applications, considering system constraints and ejector performance trade-offs. Component design and optimization using computational fluid dynamics. Exploration of multi-fidelity and multiscale modelling methods that may include surrogate modelling approaches for coupled cycle analyses. Evaluation of proposed efficient reduced-order ejector performance models that could be directly implemented to ejector dimensioning tools and/or automation algorithms. Comparison to experimental test results. SINTEF Energy, along with the partners in HeatMinds, hold significant experience and expertise in the analysis, design, and experimental testing of two-phase ejectors integrated in refrigeration and heat pump applications. DTU Construct additionally has an extensive track record working with two-phase flow, turbomachinery, and design optimization. The work will be conducted in close collaboration with SINTEF colleagues as well as with HeatMinds partners. The project includes an international secondment to Danfoss (Denmark), to gain practical insight into industrial R&D for ejector components and systems. Duties of the position Publish scientific articles and contribute to dissemination activities. Engage in collaboration and secondment with HeatMinds partners. Participate in relevant conferences, workshops, and training activities. Be flexible and prepare to adjust to activities and project focus as the PhD project progresses if needed. Complete the doctoral education. Participate actively in the relevant SINTEF Energy research groups’ activities. Required selection criteria You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree[JD1.1]. Master’s students in their final year can apply, but the degree must be completed and documented before 1 January 2027. Strong academic record (average grade B or better) or demonstrated research potential Must meet the admission requirements for the PhD program at DTU Construct. Please see https://www.dtu.dk/english/education/phd for more information for specific requirements for the PhD program at DTU Construct. Excellent written and spoken English. MSCA Mobility Rule: At the time of employment, the candidate must not have lived, worked, or studied in Norway for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date of the position. The appointment is to be made in accordance with SINTEF’s guidelines for recruitment positions and the academic regulations set by DTU Construct. Background (mandatory) Strong mechanical engineering fundamentals with a focus on thermal and fluid flow phenomena Foundations of computational fluid dynamics, numerical methods, and heat and mass transfer Thermodynamic cycle analysis Fundamentals of programming Additional background that will be valued in the selection process: Optimisation methods and/or surrogate modeling for component and system design Multiphase flow and phase change modelling Familiarity with experimental methods and model validation Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently and take initiative. Plan and carry out research systematically. Collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Show strong motivation and curiosity for the subject. Communicate clearly and constructively with colleagues. Emphasis will be placed on personal suitability and motivation for the position. We offer An exciting and challenging research project within an international MSCA Doctoral Network with excellent opportunities to collaborate within international research groups and industry. A dynamic, creative, and inclusive working environment. Access to cutting edge facilities and interdisciplinary training. Career development and mentoring through the HeatMinds network. Salary and conditions The employment period is three years, funded through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network Grant HeatMinds. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. About the application The application must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter). Curriculum vitae. Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale. Names and contact information of two references. Applications without the required documentation will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, disability, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. indeed:f69c43fe8d37ed10.title: CDTNet PhD Fellow
indeed:f69c43fe8d37ed10.desc: Job Description Summary For this position, we are looking for a talented and ambitious doctoral candidate to join CDTnet, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to transforming cardiovascular medicine through Digital Twins. Digital Twins are personalised virtual models that combine biomedical data, artificial intelligence, physiological modelling, and clinical knowledge to improve the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of cardiovascular disease. Through CDTnet, 15 doctoral candidates will work at leading universities, hospitals and industry partners across Europe while receiving world-class interdisciplinary training. This fully-funded three-year position will be hosted in Oslo, Norway with secondments in Norway, Spain and the UK. GE Healthcare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world. Job Description Project Description Heart valve disease affects millions of people worldwide and relies heavily on medical imaging for diagnosis, treatment planning and patient follow-up. Echocardiography is the most widely used imaging technique for assessing valve function, but the development of reliable artificial intelligence tools for image analysis is often limited by the availability of large, high-quality, annotated datasets. Creating and annotating such datasets is expensive and time-consuming, creating a significant barrier to innovation. This project will investigate how generative artificial intelligence can be used to improve the assessment of mitral valve diseases in particular mitral regurgitation. The doctoral candidate will develop novel methods analysing different echocardiography data modalities such as b-mode or colorflow and investigate how generating synthetic echocardiographic images can support automated image analysis tasks, such as valve segmentation and the assessment of mitral valve regurgitation. Attention will be given to understanding how patient-specific information can be incorporated into generative models to improve accuracy, consistency and clinical relevance. Working at the interface of artificial intelligence, medical imaging and cardiovascular medicine, the candidate will evaluate how generated synthetic data can improve the performance and robustness of machine-learning models when compared with training approaches utilising real world data alone. The project will make use of both proprietary clinical datasets and publicly available resources. Ultimately, the developed methods will be integrated into clinical software and evaluated as part of a prospective study of automated mitral valve assessment. The project provides a unique opportunity to contribute to the next generation of AI-enabled cardiac imaging technologies within a leading industrial research environment, while benefiting from close collaboration with academic and clinical partners across Europe. Planned Secondments Oslo University Hospital, Norway (3 months): retrospective analysis of mitral valve regurgitation and validation of automated assessment methods. IDIBAPS, Barcelona, Spain (2 months): design and implementation of a prospective clinical study for automated mitral valve assessment. King's College London, United Kingdom (2 months): investigation of how mechanistic cardiovascular models can complement machine-learning approaches. Desirable Project-Specific Qualifications and Skills We are looking for a highly motivated and solution-oriented applicant with a strong machine learning background. The ideal candidate will have: Master’s degree (equivalent to a minimum of 120 ECTS credits) preferably in machine learning, computer science, statistics, applied mathematics/electrical engineering. Other degrees can also be considered given that the candidate has formal competence in machine learning and/or image analysis/computer vision. Foreign completed degrees (M.Sc.-level) must correspond to a minimum of four years in the Norwegian educational system A solid background in modern deep learning, machine learning, mathematics, linear algebra, and/or statistics is also required Solid knowledge and documented experience with programming in Python and relevant machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) Fluent oral and written communication skills in English Experience with medical image analysis and echocardiography is a plus Inclusion and Diversity GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer where inclusion matters. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. Behaviors We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership – always with unyielding integrity. Total Rewards Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support. #LI-MG1 Additional Information Relocation Assistance Provided: No

indeed:d7e7291c97dddf0b.title: PhD Candidate (MSCA) in optimal high temperature heat pump control
indeed:d7e7291c97dddf0b.desc: Career Vacant positions Job vacancy PhD Candidate (MSCA) in optimal high temperature heat pump control About the position SINTEF Energy is announcing two PhD candidate positions within the field of thermal engineering and industrial heat supply utilizing High Temperature Heat Pumps (HTHPs). Both positions are within the frame of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN). The candidate will be employed by the Energy Use Department to carry out the doctoral project described below, enrolled by the doctoral program at Brunel University (UK), and have supervisors at both SINTEF and Brunel. About the project The activity is coordinated within the HeatMinds MSCA-DN by Brunel University in London, UK. The HeatMinds project is officially launched in October 2026 and holds a consortium of 18 partners across Europe. This integrated project aims to conduct collaborative research while training fifteen doctoral candidates to make a step change in accelerating the development and deployment of industrial HTHPs to support the decarbonization of heat supply in the process industry. Supported by leading universities, research centres, and industrial actors, advanced models and design tools will be developed that contribute to the advancement of these efforts. HeatMinds will tackle highly connected research questions, namely what are the optimum and sustainable cycle arrangements, component designs, and supporting energy policy frameworks? HeatMinds will establish a roadmap for deploying IHTHP technology to support the decarbonisation of several key industries. The other project partners recruiting PhD students are Brunel University (UK), City St. Georges University (UK), University of Seville (Spain), Technical University of Denmark, and SINTEF Industry. One of the PhD projects hosted by SINTEF Energy is titled “Advanced Control Strategies for Dynamic Operation of High-Temperature Heat Pump Systems”. The project will address the challenges related to optimal control of high temperature heat pumps and their integration within dynamic industrial processes. This project includes elements of: Investigation and development of novel or advanced control algorithms such as model predictive control (MPC) and reinforcement learning (RL) for high-temperature heat pump systems. Investigation and development of control strategies for high-temperature heat pump systems that achieve near-optimal operation using simple control elements (self-optimizing control). Evaluation of proposed control strategies in integrated scenarios within the context of industrial decarbonization and energy system flexibility. Demonstration and evaluation of proposed control strategies in a pilot-scale laboratory system. SINTEF Energy, along with the partners in HeatMinds, hold significant experience and expertise in the analysis, design, and experimental testing of high temperature heat pumps, as well as advanced control methodologies for energy systems. Brunel University additionally has an extensive track record working with control strategies and algorithms. The work will be conducted in close collaboration with SINTEF colleagues as well as with HeatMinds partners. The project includes an international secondment to the German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Low Carbon Industrial Processes to gain practical insight into high temperature heat pump control methods realized in modern experimental facilities. Duties of the position Publish scientific articles and contribute to dissemination activities. Engage in collaboration and secondment with HeatMinds partners. Participate in relevant conferences, workshops, and training activities. Be flexible and prepare to adjust to activities and project focus as the PhD project progresses if needed. Complete the doctoral education. Participate actively in the relevant SINTEF Energy research groups’ activities. Required selection criteria You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree[JD1.1]. Master’s students in their final year can apply, but the degree must be completed and documented before 1 January 2027. Strong academic record (average grade B or better) or demonstrated research potential Must meet the admission requirements for the Mechanical Engineering PhD program at Brunel University. Excellent written and spoken English. MSCA Mobility Rule: At the time of employment, the candidate must not have lived, worked, or studied in Norway for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date of the position. The appointment is to be made in accordance with SINTEF’s guidelines for recruitment positions and the academic regulations set by Brunel University. Background (mandatory) Mathematical modeling, simulation, and analysis of dynamic thermal systems Thermodynamic cycle analysis Control theory and PID controller tuning Proficiency in scientific programming (MATLAB/Python) Additional background that will be valued in the selection process: Advanced control algorithms including MPC and/or RL Heat pump and/or thermal management system analysis and design Familiarity with optimisation methods (e.g. gradient-based methods) Familiarity with plantwide control procedures (e.g. self-optimizing control) Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently and take initiative. Plan and carry out research systematically. Collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Show strong motivation and curiosity for the subject. Communicate clearly and constructively with colleagues. Emphasis will be placed on personal suitability and motivation for the position. We offer An exciting and challenging research project within an international MSCA Doctoral Network With excellent opportunities to collaborate within international research groups and industry. A dynamic, creative, and inclusive working environment. Access to cutting edge facilities and interdisciplinary training. Career development and mentoring through the HeatMinds network. Salary and conditions The employment period is three years, funded through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network Grant HeatMinds. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale. Names and contact information of two references. indeed:d3dca7eac4345e07.title: PhD position in Development and Implementation of Advanced HIV-1 reservoir diagnostics for a Biomedical laboratory scientist
indeed:d3dca7eac4345e07.desc: Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required. The research group The project is based within the research team of Maarten van de Klundert, which is part of senior professor Anders Sönnerborgs activities at the department of Medicine, Huddinge, Centrum of Infectious Medicine – Clinical Infectious Disease. The team has a strong research focus on HIV-1. The PhD position is based at ANA Futura Laboratory, Campus Flemingsberg, a modern and international research environment with access to advanced infrastructure and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration. The position will be closely integrated with the clinical microbiology laboratory at Karolinska University Laboratory, the National Reference Laboratory for HIV-1 and Retroviruses. You will work in a collaborative environment involving researchers with complementary expertise in molecular virology, HIV-1 immunology, and bioinformatics. The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student The PhD position is part of the national Graduate School: Biomedical Laboratory Scientists for Excellence – Future Educators in Health and Medical Care, (BioLabX). Therefore, only graduated Biomedical laboratory scientists are eligible to apply for the position In this doctoral project, you will investigate the HIV-1 reservoir in clinical samples from people living with HIV-1. It is closely connected to an ongoing clinical cohort at Department of Infectious Diseases, Karolinska University Hospital, and combines established clinical sampling with molecular and bioinformatic analyses of HIV-1 proviruses. You will establish and optimise workflows for the analysis of HIV-1 proviral DNA to characterise HIV-1 proviral sequences with respect to genetic diversity, viral subtype, drug-resistance mutations, hypermutation, and other sequence features. For data analysis, you will use advanced bioinformatics and phylogenetic analysis. You will also be involved in biobanking of all incoming samples, and later characterise immunological characteristics of selected study participants, for instance by FACS analysis, ELIspot assays, assessing HIV reactivation and more. In addition to mandatory courses specific to the PhD education at Karolinska Institutet, the BioLabX program includes a shared course package consisting of two subject-specific doctoral courses. The program also comprises a seminar series, workshops, and annual retreats that are mandatory for the doctoral students. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment full of expertise and curiosity. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. As a doctoral student you are offered an individual research project, a well-educated supervisor, a vast range of elective courses and the opportunity to work in a leading research group. Karolinska Institutet collaborates with prominent universities from all around the world, which ensures opportunities for international exchanges. You will be employed on a doctoral studentship which means that you receive a contractual salary. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care. B) Specific eligibility requirement You meet the specific eligibility requirement for doctoral/third-cycle/PhD education if you: Show proficiency in English equivalent to the course English B/English 6 at Swedish upper secondary school. Follow the instructions on the web page English language requirements for doctoral education. Verification of your documents Karolinska Institutet checks the authenticity of your documents. Karolinska Institutet reserves the right to revoke admission if supporting documents are discovered to be fraudulent. Submission of false documents is a violation of Swedish law and is considered grounds for legal action. (A) and (B) can only be certified by the documentation requirement for doctoral education. Skills and personal qualities The successful candidate is required to have: A strong interest in HIV research, molecular virology and translational biomedical research. Good analytical skills and an ability to interpret experimental and quantitative data. Excellent ability to speak, read and write in English. A degree in Biomedical Laboratory Science or an equivalent degree The following qualifications are desirable: Experience of experimental laboratory work in molecular biology, microbiology, virology or a related field. Experience with DNA and RNA sequencing, especially NGS and phylogeny. Basic programming and/or bioinformatic experience, for example in R, Python or related tools, and working in linux environments. Experience working with immunological methods and assays, such as PBMC isolation, FACS, ELIspot, intracellular cytokine staining (ICS) etc. It is considered an advantage to have some knowledge of Swedish. Particular emphasis will be placed on the applicant's motivation for doctoral studies, scientific curiosity and analytical ability. Terms and conditions The doctoral student will be employed on a doctoral studentship maximum 4 years full-time. Application process Submit your application and supporting documents through the Varbi recruitment system. Use the button in the top right corner and follow the instructions. We prefer that your application is written in English, but you can also apply in Swedish. Your application must contain the following documents: A personal letter and a curriculum vitae Degree projects and previous publications, if any Any other documentation showing the desirable skills and personal qualities described above Documents certifying your general eligibility (see A above) Documents certifying your specific eligibility (see B above) Selection A selection will be made among eligible applicants on the basis of the ability to benefit from doctoral education. The qualifications of the applicants will be evaluated on an overall basis. Karolinska Institutet uses the following bases of assessment: Documented subject knowledge of relevance to the area of research Analytical skill Other documented knowledge or experience that may be relevant to doctoral studies in the subject. All applicants will be informed when the recruitment is completed. KI applies a salary scale when setting salaries for doctoral students. indeed:0fd2cac2461f2f09.title: Doctoral student in Web and Emerging Applications Security
indeed:0fd2cac2461f2f09.desc: Join a world-leading research environment at the Chalmers Security and Privacy Lab and help shape the future of web, software, and AI security. As a doctoral student, you will contribute to cutting-edge cybersecurity research while working closely with internationally recognized researchers. This position offers an excellent opportunity to develop as an independent researcher and make an impact on secure and trustworthy digital systems. Software is often the root cause of vulnerabilities in modern computing systems. We develop principled concepts and mechanisms to ensure robust security and privacy for software. You will be supervised by Prof. Andrei Sabelfeld (Wallenberg Scholar and recipient of awards from ERC, SSF, VR, WASP, Google, Amazon, Facebook, and OpenAI, as well as the Chalmers Doctoral Supervisor of the Year award). About us The Department of Computer Science and Engineering, a joint department of Chalmers and the University of Gothenburg, spans the breadth of computing disciplines. Our internationally visible research, strong industry links and diverse environment create a collaborative setting where ideas grow into real impact. At the division of Computing Science, we advance secure and trustworthy software and systems, spanning foundations, programming languages, tools and practical methods that help shape dependable digital infrastructures. About the research project You will contribute to one of our research projects on Web and Emerging Applications Security. Our research tracks include: • Web application crawling and security scanning (Black Widow, Black Ostrich, and Spider-Scents) • Security and privacy of browser extensions (FakeX and CodeX) • JavaScript server-side sandboxing (SandTrap) • Data minimization in Trigger-Action Platforms (minTAP and LazyTAP) • Security and privacy of agentic and AI-integrated systems (ongoing research area) Promotional video of our research on securing web applications Who we are looking for The following requirements are mandatory: To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a closely related field Strong written and verbal communication skills in English Documented research interest and/or achievements in cybersecurity and/or privacy Ability to work independently and analytically to solve complex research problems for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted. The following experience will strengthen your application: A Master's thesis or research-oriented project in language-based security, web security, or systems security Experience with program analysis, formal methods, or AI/LLM-based systems Publications, open-source security tools, or participation in security competitions (CTFs) and bug bounty programs What you will do Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate School of Computer Science and Engineering Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours Conduct research within one of the tracks above Design, implement, and evaluate security analysis tools and prototypes, such as crawlers, scanners, sandboxes, data minimizers, and extension analyzers Publish and present results at cybersecurity venues Contract terms The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start. The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years. A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026). Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn. What we offer As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about working at Chalmers and our benefits for employees. A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg. Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg. Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence. We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities. If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in. Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here. Application procedure The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files. CV Personal letter A brief introduction about yourself and your track record. A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position. A brief description of your future goals and research focus. Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts. Documented evidence of relevant work, if available, such as (links to) research papers, project reports, and software repositories. Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form. A background check may be conducted as part of the application process. Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview. We welcome your application no later than November 27, 2026. For questions, please contact: Professor Andrei Sabelfeld andrei@chalmers.se We look forward to your application! *** Chalmers declines to consider all offers of further announcement publishing or other types of support for the recruiting process in connection with this position. *** Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. Through global commitment and entrepreneurship, we foster an innovative spirit, in close collaboration with wider society. Chalmers was founded in 1829 and has the same motto today as it did then: Avancez – forward.

indeed:91431de0cc91ef3d.title: PhD position in the field of nonlinear vibrational metamaterials
indeed:91431de0cc91ef3d.desc: Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain. The Laboratory for Acoustics/Noise Control is an international team of scientists and engineers active in the fields of vibroacoustics, environmental acoustics, and psychoacoustics. The diverse research topics rely on extensive numerical models and a broad range of experimental equipment for noise and vibration measurements. Mechanical waves and vibrations are traditionally controlled using linear devices with fixed properties. In this PhD project, the student will explore a new generation of nonlinear resonators whose dynamic behaviour changes with vibration amplitude, enabling functionalities that are not achievable with conventional designs. The research will combine mechanical modelling, finite-element simulations, prototype development, and experimental testing. The goal is to develop efficient models and design rules for nonlinear metamaterials capable of adaptive vibration isolation, frequency conversion, and non-reciprocal wave propagation. The successful candidate will work within a collaborative Swiss-French project involving Empa, ETH Zurich, and LAUM. Your tasks As doctoral candidate within this project you will work on highly nonlinear building blocks for vibrational metamaterials. Specific tasks to achieve the challenging results include Develop analytical and numerical models for strongly nonlinear resonators exhibiting nonlinear stiffness, damping, and inertia effects. Design, simulate, and optimize novel resonator concepts based on inertia amplification, bilinear stiffness, and multi-degree-of-freedom dynamics. Manufacture and experimentally characterize resonator prototypes using vibration testing, laser vibrometry, and modal analysis techniques. Investigate nonlinear phenomena such as internal resonances, frequency conversion, bifurcations, and nonlinear energy transfer. Create reduced-order models and efficient simulation tools for the design of nonlinear metamaterials and wave-control devices. Disseminate research results through publications in leading journals, presentations at international conferences, and collaboration with project partners at ETH Zurich and the Université du Mans. Your profile If you recognize yourself in the story below, then you have the profile that fits the project and the research group: I have a master degree in engineering, physics or mathematics, obtained no longer than four years ago and performed above average in comparison to my peers. I am proficient in written and spoken English. During my courses or prior professional activities, I have gathered some experience with at least one of the following: structural and/or nonlinear dynamics, numerical modelling techniques (finite element method), or experimental methods in acoustics. I have a profound interest for these topics. As a researcher I perform research in a structured and scientifically sound manner. I read technical papers, understand the nuances between different theories and implement and improve methodologies myself. In frequent reporting, varying between weekly to monthly, I show the results that I have obtained and I give a well-founded interpretation of those results. I iterate on my work and my approach based on the feedback of my supervisors which steer the direction of my research. It's important for me to work as an active team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and being inspired by my colleagues. During my PhD I want to grow towards more independence, e.g. representing the research group on project meetings and conferences. I see these events as an occasion to disseminate my work to an audience of international experts and research colleagues, and to learn about the larger context of my research and the research project. Our offer We offer a fully funded 4-year PhD position at Empa. The candidate will also be enrolled as a PhD student at the ETH Zürich, co-supervised by Dr. Paolo Tiso. The core of the PhD project will be conducted at Empa with at least one research secondment in Le Mans and intense collaboration with the Chair in Nonlinear Dynamics at ETHZ. Besides ample occasions to develop yourself in a scientific and/or industrial direction offered by the research group, further doctoral training for PhD candidates is provided in the framework of the Doctoral School. Starting date is February 2027 or upon mutual agreement. You stay in a vibrant environment centrally in Europe. Empa has its main campus in Dübendorf, located close to Zürich and 20 minutes by tram from Zurich International Airport. Zurich is one of the cities with the highest quality of life worldwide, welcoming to non-German speaking people and with ample opportunities for social, cultural, and outdoor activities. We foster a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities. Our commitment is documented in our Diversity Action Plan and refers to specific goals, which are implemented and further developed on a regular basis. You don't meet every single requirement? We are aware that particularly women and individuals from minority backgrounds often hesitate to apply unless they meet every requirement. However, we also value motivation, commitment and a willingness to learn. If you see yourself in this role, we would love to receive your qualified application, even if you don't meet 100% of the requirements. We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered. David Heusser, HR Partner

linkedin:4481626382.desc: This is NTNU NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim. At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world. You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here. (Video unable to load from YouTube. Accept cookie and refresh page to watch video, or click here to open video) About The Position We have a vacant 100% PhD position in the MRI Physics Group at the Department of Physics, NTNU. The project is an interdisciplinary collaboration between the MRI Physics Group and the X-ray Physics Group at the Department of Physics. In the MRI Physics Group, we aim to improve image quality in medical imaging for diagnostic purposes and neuroscience research. Accurate and sensitive imaging is crucial for diagnosis, research, and monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases such as Multiple Sclerosis, Alzheimer's disease, and ALS. Among other techniques, we use functional MRI (fMRI), which is a method for measuring brain activity and connectivity between nerve cells. MRI measurements can be affected by magnetic field inhomogeneities, resulting in geometric distortion and signal loss in the images. The aim of the project is to investigate the potential of using Implicit Neural Representation (INR), a class of neural networks, for reconstructing MR images directly from MR signals. By incorporating a physical model of the MR signal into the training of the INR network, we aim to compensate for the effects of magnetic field inhomogeneities in the reconstructed images. Initially, this approach will be applied to functional MRI of the spinal cord, based on data acquired using a high-field MRI system (7 Tesla). NTNU hosts Norway's first, and currently only, 7T MRI system for clinical use and research. We will also investigate the broader potential of INR-based image reconstruction for various MRI applications, including industrial applications in geology. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. Duties of the position Simulate MRI data and model disturbances arising from various physical sources Develop, implement and train INR models for MRI time-series data Analyze functional MRI data of the spinal cord Present research findings in written form through academic publications Present research findings orally and participate in international conferences Assist with teaching activities Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must have a relevant Master's degree in physics, mathematics, biomedical engineering, computer science or equivalent. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than 31 August 2027. You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. Weitere Forschungsrichtungen umfassen die sichere kollaborative Datenverarbeitung und die Entwicklung praxistauglicher datenschutzwahrender Lösungen für verteilte Gesundheitsumgebungen. linkedin:4482887356.desc: Job Description Summary For this position, we are looking for a talented and ambitious doctoral candidate to join CDTnet, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to transforming cardiovascular medicine through Digital Twins. Digital Twins are personalised virtual models that combine biomedical data, artificial intelligence, physiological modelling, and clinical knowledge to improve the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of cardiovascular disease. Through CDTnet, 15 doctoral candidates will work at leading universities, hospitals and industry partners across Europe while receiving world-class interdisciplinary training. This fully-funded three-year position will be hosted in Oslo, Norway with secondments in Norway, Spain and the UK. GE Healthcare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world. Job Description Project Description Heart valve disease affects millions of people worldwide and relies heavily on medical imaging for diagnosis, treatment planning and patient follow-up. Echocardiography is the most widely used imaging technique for assessing valve function, but the development of reliable artificial intelligence tools for image analysis is often limited by the availability of large, high-quality, annotated datasets. Creating and annotating such datasets is expensive and time-consuming, creating a significant barrier to innovation. This project will investigate how generative artificial intelligence can be used to improve the assessment of mitral valve diseases in particular mitral regurgitation. The doctoral candidate will develop novel methods analysing different echocardiography data modalities such as b-mode or colorflow and investigate how generating synthetic echocardiographic images can support automated image analysis tasks, such as valve segmentation and the assessment of mitral valve regurgitation. Attention will be given to understanding how patient-specific information can be incorporated into generative models to improve accuracy, consistency and clinical relevance. Working at the interface of artificial intelligence, medical imaging and cardiovascular medicine, the candidate will evaluate how generated synthetic data can improve the performance and robustness of machine-learning models when compared with training approaches utilising real world data alone. The project will make use of both proprietary clinical datasets and publicly available resources. Ultimately, the developed methods will be integrated into clinical software and evaluated as part of a prospective study of automated mitral valve assessment. The project provides a unique opportunity to contribute to the next generation of AI-enabled cardiac imaging technologies within a leading industrial research environment, while benefiting from close collaboration with academic and clinical partners across Europe. Planned Secondments Oslo University Hospital, Norway (3 months): retrospective analysis of mitral valve regurgitation and validation of automated assessment methods. IDIBAPS, Barcelona, Spain (2 months): design and implementation of a prospective clinical study for automated mitral valve assessment. King's College London, United Kingdom (2 months): investigation of how mechanistic cardiovascular models can complement machine-learning approaches. Desirable Project-Specific Qualifications And Skills We are looking for a highly motivated and solution-oriented applicant with a strong machine learning background. The ideal candidate will have: Master’s degree (equivalent to a minimum of 120 ECTS credits) preferably in machine learning, computer science, statistics, applied mathematics/electrical engineering. Other degrees can also be considered given that the candidate has formal competence in machine learning and/or image analysis/computer vision. Foreign completed degrees (M.Sc.-level) must correspond to a minimum of four years in the Norwegian educational system A solid background in modern deep learning, machine learning, mathematics, linear algebra, and/or statistics is also required Solid knowledge and documented experience with programming in Python and relevant machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) Fluent oral and written communication skills in English Experience with medical image analysis and echocardiography is a plus Inclusion and Diversity GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer where inclusion matters. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. Software-defined and programmable networking is a key enabling technology for cloud-native and AI-native 6G networks, supporting greater scalability, flexibility, automation, and efficient resource utilization. Cross-layer and cross-domain programmability, across the control and data planes and from RAN to core, is expected to be a defining characteristic of 6G systems, which are currently being developed and standardized. In this context, data plane programming capabilities in next-generation mobile networks can bring significant benefits with regards to network slicing and multi-tenancy, dynamic traffic engineering, offloading network functions to hardware accelerators, etc. Specifically, this PhD project, conducted in collaboration with Ericsson, the leading mobile communications equipment manufacturer, will investigate data-plane programmability in next-generation mobile networks, with a particular focus on cloud-native and AI-native Radio Access Networks (RAN). The candidate will investigate research challenges including, but not limited to, the specification and implementation of common abstraction layers for heterogeneous programmable data planes, mechanisms for data-plane multitenancy and modularization, and programmable radio resource management, with an emphasis on intelligent and adaptive control. The research is conducted within the scope of the Future Network Services (FNS): the 6G flagship project for the Netherlands where 60 leading ICT businesses, mobile operators, semiconductor manufacturers and research institutions, have united to spearhead the development of specific aspects of 6G: Software antennas, AI-driven networking, and groundbreaking 6G applications. You will be embedded in the MNS group. The group focuses its research on the fundamental architectural problems that arise from the interconnection of systems and of data flows. linkedin:4482491624.desc: Job Description Are you interested in developing innovative robotic systems that can adapt their mechanical properties to interact safely and effectively with their environment? Do you have a background in robotics, mechatronics, and control, and enjoy combining mechanical design with hands-on experimental research? At DTU Electro, you will have the opportunity to develop and validate novel robotic technologies integrating compliant mechanisms, variable stiffness, and advanced control strategies. Your research will contribute to the development of adaptable robotic systems capable of performing complex physical operations in challenging and uncertain environments. The PhD position is part of RESSORT, a European research project aimed at advancing soft and adaptive robotics through the integration of innovative materials, compliant structures, sensing, and intelligent control. The project addresses the limitations of conventional rigid robotic systems by developing solutions capable of adapting their mechanical behaviour to different tasks and operating conditions. Your research will focus on the design, modelling, and control of robotic systems incorporating soft and variable-stiffness mechanisms. Particular attention will be given to the integration of mechanical adaptability and control to improve physical interaction, operational stability, and performance. The developed methods will be implemented and experimentally validated on robotic platforms, including adaptive and morphing aerial systems. Responsibilities And Qualifications Your main responsibility will be to investigate and develop mechatronic and control solutions for soft and adaptive robotic systems. The research will combine mechanical design, dynamic modelling, control development, and experimental validation, addressing the challenges associated with integrating compliant structures into robotic platforms. Your primary tasks will include: Design and develop compliant and variable-stiffness mechanisms for robotic applications. Develop mathematical and dynamic models of robotic systems incorporating flexible and adaptive mechanical structures. Investigate control strategies to manage changes in mechanical configuration, stiffness, and interaction forces. Integrate actuators, sensors, and embedded control systems into experimental robotic platforms. Develop methods for stable and efficient robotic operation under varying mechanical and environmental conditions. Implement and validate the developed technologies through simulations and experiments on real robotic systems. Collaborate with international research and industrial partners and disseminate research results through scientific publications and conferences. We expect you to have a strong background in mechatronics, robotics, mechanical engineering, control engineering, or a closely related field. Solid competences in mechanical design, dynamic modelling, and control of robotic systems are particularly important. Experience with CAD tools, actuators, embedded systems, and experimental prototyping will be considered an advantage. Good programming skills in MATLAB/Simulink, C++, and/or Python are expected. Familiarity with compliant mechanisms, soft robotics, variable-stiffness systems, or aerial robotics will be beneficial. We are particularly interested in candidates who enjoy combining theoretical developments with practical implementation and experimental work. You should be motivated to develop innovative solutions, work independently, and contribute actively to a multidisciplinary and international research environment. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. linkedin:4482865374.title: PhD position in Development and Implementation of Advanced HIV-1 reservoir diagnostics for a Biomedical laboratory scientist
linkedin:4482865374.desc: Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required. The research group The project is based within the research team of Maarten van De Klundert, which is part of senior professor Anders Sönnerborgs activities at the department of Medicine, Huddinge, Centrum of Infectious Medicine – Clinical Infectious Disease. The team has a strong research focus on HIV-1. The PhD position is based at ANA Futura Laboratory, Campus Flemingsberg, a modern and international research environment with access to advanced infrastructure and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration. The position will be closely integrated with the clinical microbiology laboratory at Karolinska University Laboratory, the National Reference Laboratory for HIV-1 and Retroviruses. You will work in a collaborative environment involving researchers with complementary expertise in molecular virology, HIV-1 immunology, and bioinformatics. The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student The PhD position is part of the national Graduate School: Biomedical Laboratory Scientists for Excellence – Future Educators in Health and Medical Care, (BioLabX). Therefore, only graduated Biomedical laboratory scientists are eligible to apply for the position In this doctoral project, you will investigate the HIV-1 reservoir in clinical samples from people living with HIV-1. It is closely connected to an ongoing clinical cohort at Department of Infectious Diseases, Karolinska University Hospital, and combines established clinical sampling with molecular and bioinformatic analyses of HIV-1 proviruses. You will establish and optimise workflows for the analysis of HIV-1 proviral DNA to characterise HIV-1 proviral sequences with respect to genetic diversity, viral subtype, drug-resistance mutations, hypermutation, and other sequence features. For data analysis, you will use advanced bioinformatics and phylogenetic analysis. You will also be involved in biobanking of all incoming samples, and later characterise immunological characteristics of selected study participants, for instance by FACS analysis, ELIspot assays, assessing HIV reactivation and more. In addition to mandatory courses specific to the PhD education at Karolinska Institutet, the BioLabX program includes a shared course package consisting of two subject-specific doctoral courses. The program also comprises a seminar series, workshops, and annual retreats that are mandatory for the doctoral students. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment full of expertise and curiosity. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. As a doctoral student you are offered an individual research project, a well-educated supervisor, a vast range of elective courses and the opportunity to work in a leading research group. Karolinska Institutet collaborates with prominent universities from all around the world, which ensures opportunities for international exchanges. You will be employed on a doctoral studentship which means that you receive a contractual salary. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care. Submission of false documents is a violation of Swedish law and is considered grounds for legal action. (A) and (B) can only be certified by the documentation requirement for doctoral education. Skills and personal qualities The successful candidate is required to have: A strong interest in HIV research, molecular virology and translational biomedical research. Good analytical skills and an ability to interpret experimental and quantitative data. Excellent ability to speak, read and write in English. A degree in Biomedical Laboratory Science or an equivalent degree The following qualifications are desirable: Experience of experimental laboratory work in molecular biology, microbiology, virology or a related field. Experience with DNA and RNA sequencing, especially NGS and phylogeny. Basic programming and/or bioinformatic experience, for example in R, Python or related tools, and working in linux environments. Experience working with immunological methods and assays, such as PBMC isolation, FACS, ELIspot, intracellular cytokine staining (ICS) etc. Particular emphasis will be placed on the applicant's motivation for doctoral studies, scientific curiosity and analytical ability. Terms and conditions The doctoral student will be employed on a doctoral studentship maximum 4 years full-time. Application process Submit your application and supporting documents through the Varbi recruitment system. Use the button in the top right corner and follow the instructions. We prefer that your application is written in English, but you can also apply in Swedish. Your application must contain the following documents: - A personal letter and a curriculum vitae - Degree projects and previous publications, if any - Any other documentation showing the desirable skills and personal qualities described above - Documents certifying your general eligibility (see A above) - Documents certifying your specific eligibility (see B above) Selection A selection will be made among eligible applicants on the basis of the ability to benefit from doctoral education. The qualifications of the applicants will be evaluated on an overall basis. Karolinska Institutet uses the following bases of assessment: - Documented subject knowledge of relevance to the area of research - Analytical skill - Other documented knowledge or experience that may be relevant to doctoral studies in the subject.
