linkedin:4482889565.title: PhD position in the field of nonlinear vibrational metamaterials
linkedin:4482889565.desc: Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain. The Laboratory for Acoustics/Noise Control is an international team of scientists and engineers active in the fields of vibroacoustics, environmental acoustics, and psychoacoustics. The diverse research topics rely on extensive numerical models and a broad range of experimental equipment for noise and vibration measurements. Mechanical waves and vibrations are traditionally controlled using linear devices with fixed properties. In this PhD project, the student will explore a new generation of nonlinear resonators whose dynamic behaviour changes with vibration amplitude, enabling functionalities that are not achievable with conventional designs. The research will combine mechanical modelling, finite-element simulations, prototype development, and experimental testing. The goal is to develop efficient models and design rules for nonlinear metamaterials capable of adaptive vibration isolation, frequency conversion, and non-reciprocal wave propagation. The successful candidate will work within a collaborative Swiss-French project involving Empa, ETH Zurich, and LAUM. Your tasks As doctoral candidate within this project you will work on highly nonlinear building blocks for vibrational metamaterials. Specific tasks to achieve the challenging results include Develop analytical and numerical models for strongly nonlinear resonators exhibiting nonlinear stiffness, damping, and inertia effects. Design, simulate, and optimize novel resonator concepts based on inertia amplification, bilinear stiffness, and multi-degree-of-freedom dynamics. Manufacture and experimentally characterize resonator prototypes using vibration testing, laser vibrometry, and modal analysis techniques. Investigate nonlinear phenomena such as internal resonances, frequency conversion, bifurcations, and nonlinear energy transfer. Create reduced-order models and efficient simulation tools for the design of nonlinear metamaterials and wave-control devices. Disseminate research results through publications in leading journals, presentations at international conferences, and collaboration with project partners at ETH Zurich and the Université du Mans. Your profile If you recognize yourself in the story below, then you have the profile that fits the project and the research group: I have a master degree in engineering, physics or mathematics, obtained no longer than four years ago and performed above average in comparison to my peers. I am proficient in written and spoken English. During my courses or prior professional activities, I have gathered some experience with at least one of the following: structural and/or nonlinear dynamics, numerical modelling techniques (finite element method), or experimental methods in acoustics. I have a profound interest for these topics. As a researcher I perform research in a structured and scientifically sound manner. I read technical papers, understand the nuances between different theories and implement and improve methodologies myself. In frequent reporting, varying between weekly to monthly, I show the results that I have obtained and I give a well-founded interpretation of those results. I iterate on my work and my approach based on the feedback of my supervisors which steer the direction of my research. It's important for me to work as an active team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and being inspired by my colleagues. During my PhD I want to grow towards more independence, e.g. representing the research group on project meetings and conferences. I see these events as an occasion to disseminate my work to an audience of international experts and research colleagues, and to learn about the larger context of my research and the research project. Our offer We offer a fully funded 4-year PhD position at Empa. The candidate will also be enrolled as a PhD student at the ETH Zürich, co-supervised by Dr. Paolo Tiso. The core of the PhD project will be conducted at Empa with at least one research secondment in Le Mans and intense collaboration with the Chair in Nonlinear Dynamics at ETHZ. Besides ample occasions to develop yourself in a scientific and/or industrial direction offered by the research group, further doctoral training for PhD candidates is provided in the framework of the Doctoral School . Starting date is February 2027 or upon mutual agreement. You stay in a vibrant environment centrally in Europe. Empa has its main campus in Dübendorf, located close to Zürich and 20 minutes by tram from Zurich International Airport. Zurich is one of the cities with the highest quality of life worldwide, welcoming to non-German speaking people and with ample opportunities for social, cultural, and outdoor activities. We foster a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

linkedin:4482897176.title: PhD Position: Safe Planning and Decision-Making under Uncertainty for Long-Horizon Robot Autonomy
linkedin:4482897176.desc: Join TU Delft and the EU-funded OPERA consortium. Push the frontier of general-purpose AI for robotics and tackle the fundamental tension between long-horizon reasoning and real-time safety guarantees. Job Description Robots that operate for long periods among people must plan beyond the next few seconds while staying safe. They need to predict how their surroundings and the people in them will evolve, know how reliable these predictions are, and adapt their plans when the predictions fail. In the EU-funded OPERA project, TU Delft contributes to General-Purpose AI for robotics by developing methods that combine fast, reactive behavior with more deliberate reasoning, planning, and decision-making. In this PhD position, you will develop planning and decision-making methods that let robots act safely and reliably over long time horizons when their knowledge of the environment and of the people around them is incomplete. The research sits at the intersection of model-based planning and control and learning-based models, and addresses the trade-off between safety, performance, and real-time computation. You will formulate the methods and analyze their guarantees and failure modes. This research is connected to OPERA's tasks on GPAI-powered planning and decision-making, on long-term reasoning in human-centered environments, and on adaptive human-robot and robot-environment interaction. Depending on your background, the work may draw on optimal control and model predictive control, motion planning, probabilistic modeling and estimation, or learning-based methods. The emphasis is on methods with a clear formulation and well-understood failure modes, validated in simulation and on real robots. You will work in the Cognitive Robotics Department at TU Delft under the supervision of Prof. Robert Babuška and Dr. Laura Ferranti, and you will be embedded in the Reliable Robot Control Lab (https://r2clab.com/). You will collaborate with OPERA partners across Europe on simulation, perception, and the OPERA open-source toolbox. Job Requirements The ideal candidate for this PhD position has a strong background in control, optimization, or motion planning and is motivated by the question of how robots can plan safely and reliably over long time horizons. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds who want to work at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. You have: An MSc degree in Systems and Control, Robotics, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. A strong interest in safe planning and decision-making for robots, at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. A passion for rigorous, theoretically grounded research, combined with an eagerness to validate ideas in simulation and on real robots. Strong analytical and mathematical skills, in particular in optimization, probability and statistics, and dynamical systems. Excellent communication skills and proficiency in English (written and verbal), as required for academic publication and international collaboration. You are particularly encouraged to apply if you have experience in one or more of the following areas: Hands-on experience implementing optimization-based planners or controllers (e.g., model predictive control with acados or CasADi) in C++ or Python. Safe or robust control and planning under uncertainty. Learned dynamics or prediction models, model-based reinforcement learning. Uncertainty quantification, probabilistic or Bayesian modeling, state estimation. Long-horizon or hierarchical planning, prediction of human or multi-agent behavior. Real-robot deployment with ROS or ROS 2. As part of OPERA, you will travel to meet and collaborate with the project’s European partners and attend regular consortium meetings. We particularly encourage applications from women and other underrepresented groups, as we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive research environment. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Mechanical Engineering From chip to ship. From machine to human being. From idea to solution. Driven by a deep-rooted desire to understand our environment and discover its underlying mechanisms, research and education at the ME faculty focusses on fundamental understanding, design, production including application and product improvement, materials, processes and (mechanical) systems. ME is a dynamic and innovative faculty with high-tech lab facilities and international reach. It’s a large faculty but also versatile, so we can often make unique connections by combining different disciplines. This is reflected in ME’s outstanding, state-of-the-art education, which trains students to become responsible and socially engaged engineers and scientists. We translate our knowledge and insights into solutions to societal issues, contributing to a sustainable society and to the development of prosperity and well-being. That is what unites us in pioneering research, inspiring education and (inter)national cooperation. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. Do you want to experience working at our faculty? These videos will introduce you to some of our researchers and their work. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3059 - €3881 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information For more information, please reach out to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska [l.ferranti@tudelft.nl, r.babuska@tudelft.nl] Please do not use LinkedIn and other channels for applications or inquiries. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 15 November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: A letter of motivation explaining why you are the right candidate for this project An updated cv Exam transcipts from your Bachelor and Master A copy of your MSc thesis, or draft MSc thesis (or a link to access it) You can address your application to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska. linkedin:4482849819.desc: Your function When a proton meets a hydrogen atom, the pair can emit a photon and stay together as H₂⁺. This is how the first molecules formed after the Big Bang, and it is one of the proposed routes to the first antimatter molecule, yet it has never been measured. In the NWO Vidi project SAMURAI, you will study these collisions one quantum state at a time: instead of colliding atoms, we use lasers to prepare a hydrogen molecule at the moment of a collision and watch it fall apart. You will be part of a small group in which experiment and theory go hand in hand. Your duties excite H₂ with two tunable extreme-ultraviolet lasers (60–205 nm), built in our lab and unique in the Netherlands, and image the fragments with velocity-map imaging aim for the first spectroscopic observation of the excited electronic states of H₂⁺, calculated by Edward Teller in his PhD thesis in 1930 and never seen since trap H₂⁺ ions and use millimetre waves and magnetic fields to control how they come apart work towards the first measurement of radiative association: joining a cold proton and a cold hydrogen atom with light, next to a crystal of laser-cooled Be⁺ ions compare your data with multichannel quantum-defect theory and scattering calculations, and contribute to the theory yourself if you like develop your skills in lasers and nonlinear optics, ultrahigh vacuum, electronics, CAD design and scientific programming present your results at international conferences and publish them in peer-reviewed journals Your profile an MSc degree (or close to completing one) in physics, physical chemistry or a related field affinity with quantum mechanics and atomic, molecular and optical physics, and an interest in lasers and electronics good command of spoken and written English most important: you are curious, enjoy building things that work, like working in a team, and want to spend four years on a question nobody has answered yet As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements. What do we offer? Education A challenging position in a socially engaged organisation. At VU Amsterdam, you contribute to education, research and service for a better world. And that is valuable. So in return for your efforts, we offer you: a salary of minimum € 3.204,00 (PhD) and maximum € 4.051,00 (PhD) gross per month, on a full-time basis. This is based on UFO profile PhD candidate. The group carries out precision measurements on atoms and molecules, using advanced laser techniques and methods to cool their motion. It shares the infrastructure of LaserLaB Amsterdam, with lasers ranging from ultrastable to ultrafast, connected to atomic clocks and frequency combs. The aims are to test fundamental theories such as quantum electrodynamics, to determine fundamental constants such as the proton-to-electron mass ratio, and to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. linkedin:4480658123.desc: Hjem Karriere i SINTEF Ledige stillinger Ledig stilling PhD Candidate (MSCA) in multiscale ejector design and optimization within high temperature heat pumps About the position SINTEF Energy is announcing two PhD candidate positions within the field of thermal engineering and industrial heat supply utilizing High Temperature Heat Pumps (HTHPs). Both positions are within the frame of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN). The candidate will be employed by the Energy Use Department to carry out the doctoral project described below, enrolled by the doctoral program at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), and have supervisors at both SINTEF and DTU Construct. About the project The activity is coordinated within the HeatMinds MSCA-DN by Brunel University in London, UK. The HeatMinds project is officially launched in October 2026 and holds a consortium of 18 partners across Europe. This integrated project aims to conduct collaborative research while training fifteen doctoral candidates to make a step change in accelerating the development and deployment of industrial HTHPs to support the decarbonization of heat supply in the process industry. Supported by leading universities, research centres, and industrial actors, advanced models and design tools will be developed that contribute to the advancement of these efforts. HeatMinds will tackle highly connected research questions, namely what are the optimum and sustainable cycle arrangements, component designs, and supporting energy policy frameworks? HeatMinds will establish a roadmap for deploying IHTHP technology to support the decarbonisation of several key industries. The other project partners recruiting PhD students are Brunel University (UK), City St. Georges University (UK), University of Seville (Spain), Technical University of Denmark, and SINTEF Industry. One of the PhD projects hosted by SINTEF Energy is titled “Multiscale design and optimization of ejectors integrated within novel IHTHP architectures” and addresses the potential for improved energy efficiency achieved by using ejectors. The project also addresses the coupled and multiscale challenges associated with optimal design and integration, and focuses on the use of natural working fluids. On the one hand, the analysis and design of optimal heat pump cycles is typically carried out using simple lumped or one-dimensional models. On the other hand, accurate component performance and design requires more detailed analysis methods, such as CFD, that present a challenge for how complex and coupled systems should be designed. This Project Includes Elements Of Evaluation of two-phase ejector component integration strategies within high temperature heat pump applications, considering system constraints and ejector performance trade-offs. Component design and optimization using computational fluid dynamics. Exploration of multi-fidelity and multiscale modelling methods that may include surrogate modelling approaches for coupled cycle analyses. Evaluation of proposed efficient reduced-order ejector performance models that could be directly implemented to ejector dimensioning tools and/or automation algorithms. Comparison to experimental test results. SINTEF Energy, along with the partners in HeatMinds, hold significant experience and expertise in the analysis, design, and experimental testing of two-phase ejectors integrated in refrigeration and heat pump applications. DTU Construct additionally has an extensive track record working with two-phase flow, turbomachinery, and design optimization. The work will be conducted in close collaboration with SINTEF colleagues as well as with HeatMinds partners. The project includes an international secondment to Danfoss (Denmark), to gain practical insight into industrial R&D for ejector components and systems. Duties of the position Publish scientific articles and contribute to dissemination activities. Engage in collaboration and secondment with HeatMinds partners. Participate in relevant conferences, workshops, and training activities. Be flexible and prepare to adjust to activities and project focus as the PhD project progresses if needed. Complete the doctoral education. Participate actively in the relevant SINTEF Energy research groups’ activities. Required Selection Criteria You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree[JD1.1]. Master’s students in their final year can apply, but the degree must be completed and documented before 1 January 2027. Strong academic record (average grade B or better) or demonstrated research potential Must meet the admission requirements for the PhD program at DTU Construct. Please see https://www.dtu.dk/english/education/phd for more information for specific requirements for the PhD program at DTU Construct. Excellent written and spoken English. MSCA Mobility Rule: At the time of employment, the candidate must not have lived, worked, or studied in Norway for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date of the position. The appointment is to be made in accordance with SINTEF’s guidelines for recruitment positions and the academic regulations set by DTU Construct. Background (mandatory) Strong mechanical engineering fundamentals with a focus on thermal and fluid flow phenomena Foundations of computational fluid dynamics, numerical methods, and heat and mass transfer Thermodynamic cycle analysis Fundamentals of programming Additional background that will be valued in the selection process: Optimisation methods and/or surrogate modeling for component and system design Multiphase flow and phase change modelling Familiarity with experimental methods and model validation Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently and take initiative. Plan and carry out research systematically. Collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Show strong motivation and curiosity for the subject. Communicate clearly and constructively with colleagues. Emphasis will be placed on personal suitability and motivation for the position. We offer An exciting and challenging research project within an international MSCA Doctoral Network with excellent opportunities to collaborate within international research groups and industry. A dynamic, creative, and inclusive working environment. Access to cutting edge facilities and interdisciplinary training. Career development and mentoring through the HeatMinds network. Salary and conditions The employment period is three years, funded through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network Grant HeatMinds. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. About The Application The Application Must Include A letter motivating the application (cover letter). Curriculum vitae. Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale. Names and contact information of two references. Applications without the required documentation will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, disability, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. linkedin:4480684722.desc: Für unser Forschungsprojekt SOUND suchen wir eine:n PhD-Doktorand:in, die/der anhand neuester neurobildgebender Verfahren sowie klinischer Daten untersucht, wie sich das Sprachverstehen nach einer Cochlea-Implantation besser vorhersagen lässt (*Predicting Speech Perception Outcomes in Cochlear Implant Candidates Using Neuroimaging Data*). Das Projekt wird vom Forschungsteam «Auditory Pathway» am Hearing Research Laboratory des ARTORG Centers for Biomedical Engineering Research der Universität Bern in enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Universitätsklinik für Hals-, Nasen- und Ohrenkrankheiten am Inselspital durchgeführt. Cochlea-Implantate sind hochwirksame Neuroprothesen, die Menschen mit hochgradigem Hörverlust ermöglichen, wieder Klänge wahrzunehmen und Sprache zu verstehen. Wie gut das Sprachverstehen nach der Implantation gelingt, ist individuell sehr unterschiedlich: Bei rund einem Viertel der Patientinnen und Patienten bleiben die Ergebnisse hinter den Erwartungen zurück, und verlässliche Prognosen zum individuellen Nutzen eines Cochlea-Implantats vor der Operation fehlen bislang. Hinweise deuten darauf hin, dass neben dem Hörorgan auch die Verarbeitung und Vernetzung im Gehirn eine wichtige Rolle spielen. Die SOUND Study untersucht, wie sich diese Erkenntnisse für individuellere Prognosen nutzen lassen. Das erwartet Sie Im Rahmen der SOUND Study untersuchen Sie die zentralen Hörbahnen mithilfe neuester bildgebender Verfahren. Im Fokus stehen die funktionelle Nahinfrarotspektroskopie (fNIRS) und spezialisierte Magnetresonanztomografie-Sequenzen (MRT) Sie führen neurobildgebende, audiologische und klinische Daten zusammen und wenden statistische Verfahren sowie Machine Learning an, um Muster zu erkennen, die mit dem späteren Sprachverstehen zusammenhängen Ihre Ergebnisse diskutieren und interpretieren Sie gemeinsam mit Fachpersonen aus der Neuroradiologie sowie mit klinischen und technischen Expertinnen und Experten Das bringen Sie mit Masterabschluss in Elektrotechnik, biomedizinischer Technik, Physik oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet Praktische Erfahrung in der Signalverarbeitung Erfahrung in der medizinischen Bildanalyse oder Interesse, sich in dieses Gebiet einzuarbeiten; Kenntnisse in Datenanalyse oder Machine Learning sind von Vorteil Interesse an klinischer Forschung und an der Arbeit mit Patientinnen und Patienten sowie Freude an der interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

linkedin:4480681551.desc: Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter, Doktorand (m/w/d) im Bereich Robotik & KI: Fertigung nachhaltiger Faserverbundbauteile Robotisch gefertigte Faserverbundstrukturen eröffnen große Potenziale für ressourceneffiziente und nachhaltige Baukomponenten, insbesondere beim Einsatz biobasierter Naturfasern wie Flachs. In der Praxis ist der Weg zur reproduzierbaren, serientauglichen Fertigung jedoch anspruchsvoll: Naturfasern zeigen chargen- und umgebungsbedingte Schwankungen, die zu Abweichungen im Faserverlauf, Qualitätsstreuungen und erhöhter Nacharbeit führen können. Für robuste Prozesse braucht es daher eine durchgängige, digitale Prozessüberwachung, die Abweichungen während der Fertigung erkennt und der Robotik eine schnelle, zielgerichtete Reaktion ermöglicht. Am ISW erforschen und entwickeln wir dafür Algorithmen und Softwarebausteine, die kamerabasierte Inline-Bildverarbeitung, KI-gestützte Anomalieerkennung und Echtzeit-Integration in die Robotersteuerung verbinden. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf der intelligenten Auswertung von Sensordaten und der Online-Anpassung des Wickelpfads bzw. robotischer Bewegungs-/Ablageparameter, um Material- und Prozessschwankungen automatisch zu kompensieren. Ziel ist ein robustes, selbstüberwachendes robotisches Wickelverfahren mit stabiler Bauteilqualität, als Grundlage für wirtschaftliche und nachhaltige Faserverbundbauteile. indeed:8a1199a98b7d82a7.desc: Job description About the project MERIT (MEtabolic Reprogramming in viral pathogenesis: from Infection to Therapeutic innovations) is an EU-funded MSCA training programme aimed at better understanding how viruses affect the human body. Coordinated by Dr. Adithya Sridhar, Assistant Professor, and Prof. Dr. Dasja Pajkrt, Professor of Pediatric Infectious diseases, from the OrganoVIR Labs at Amsterdam UMC (location AMC), this project brings together 7 academic institutions and 12 associated partners from across Europe. Within MERIT, researchers will take a new, holistic approach that focuses on infections and host metabolism to unravel virus-induced metabolic reprogramming and its impact on human health. The project’s objective lies in understanding the complex interplay between viruses and host cells, focusing on metabolic reprogramming, and long-term consequences of infection. This will be achieved by combining three methodological pillars: human organoids, integrative and spatial omics, and advanced microscopy. About the role Despite effective combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), individuals living with HIV experience neurocognitive impairments, collectively known as HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND). The neuropathological changes observed in HAND are also found in neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), such as Alzheimer’s disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, and Parkinson’s disease. A common link between HAND and NDDs is disrupted lipid metabolism, with HAND patients exhibiting increased amyloid-beta deposition. Clinical data suggest that TDP-43 proteinopathy may contribute to HAND, further linking it to NDDs. This project aims to explore these connections using iPSC-derived microglia-embedded brain organoids. By characterising lipid profile changes following HIV infections and investigating TDP-43 proteinopathy, we seek to identify potential mechanisms underlying HAND. At the Amsterdam UMC in the Netherlands, MERIT is looking for a Doctoral Candidate (DC) to work on Work Packages 1 and 2. As DC7, your objectives are: to characterise lipidomic profiles of HIV-infected brain organoids compared to healthy organoids; to assess and alter TDP-43 proteinopathy in HIV-infected organoids. You will be guided during your research project by Prof. Dr. Dasja Pajkrt and Dr. Renata Vieira de Sá at the OrganoVIR Labs at the Amsterdam UMC, Netherlands. You can apply for this position until 30 October 2026 . Applications submitted after this date will not be considered. Profile a motivated PhD candidate with an academic qualification (MSc or MD, or close to completion) in one of these disciplines: in (bio)medical sciences, biology, cell biology, biotechnology, or a closely related field and has a solid foundation in molecular and cellular biology as well as immunology expertise in one or more of the following fields: virology, (3D) cell culture, tissue engineering. experience with experimental laboratory techniques relevant to the field, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research team. excellent oral and written communication skills in English (minimum C1/C2 CEFR level) have not resided/carried out work or studies in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before 1 April 2027 (transnational mobility rule). Our offer A contract with Amsterdam UMC for 36 hours per week for 4 years (probation of 6 months). The opportunity to work on large-scale and in-house research with motivated colleagues from all over the world. Planned secondments in International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB) & Leiden University Medical Center (LUMC). Training in safety and biosecurity aligned with international best practices. You will be trained in hazard identification, containment, incident reporting, and dual-use/gain-of-function issues. An opportunity to take part in a tailor-made pre-MBA programme to develop entrepreneurial and commercial skills and other network-wide training opportunities including conferences and courses, a Personal Development Plan, non-academic coaching, and workshops on topics including ethics and sustainability and AI/LLM. Classification in salary scale OIO: € 3,217 to € 4,077 gross for full-time employment (depending on experience). In addition to a good basic salary, we offer 8.3% end-of-year bonus. Calculate your net salary here. 100% reimbursement for public transport travel costs and, for private transport, €0.18 per km up to a maximum of 40 km each. Do you prefer walking or cycling? Take advantage of our good bike scheme. About the workplace Amsterdam UMC, location AMC, houses the university hospital and the medical faculty of the University of Amsterdam, as well as several research institutes. The OrganoVIR Labs is uniquely embedded within both the Department of Medical Microbiology and Infection Prevention (MMI) and the Department of Pediatrics and is affiliated with the Amsterdam Immunity and Infection Institute (AIII), Amsterdam Reproduction and Development (AR&D), and Emma Centre for Personalized Medicine (Emma CPM). This multidisciplinary positioning fosters close collaboration between fundamental, translational, and clinical research. OrganoVIR Labs has access to various advanced facilities including level 3, state-of-the-art molecular biology and culture facilities and access to high-throughput sequencing. Through its integration with the Department of Pediatrics, OrganoVIR Labs also benefits from extensive clinical expertise in the care of children with a broad spectrum of acute and chronic conditions. The department’s multidisciplinary approach and extensive clinical expertise support the translation of research findings into improved outcomes for pediatric patients. indeed:3ad62b52e9ce8528.desc: Für unser Forschungsprojekt SOUND suchen wir eine:n PhD-Doktorand:in, die/der anhand neuester neurobildgebender Verfahren sowie klinischer Daten untersucht, wie sich das Sprachverstehen nach einer Cochlea-Implantation besser vorhersagen lässt (*Predicting Speech Perception Outcomes in Cochlear Implant Candidates Using Neuroimaging Data*). Das Projekt wird vom Forschungsteam «Auditory Pathway» am Hearing Research Laboratory des ARTORG Centers for Biomedical Engineering Research der Universität Bern in enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Universitätsklinik für Hals-, Nasen- und Ohrenkrankheiten am Inselspital durchgeführt. Cochlea-Implantate sind hochwirksame Neuroprothesen, die Menschen mit hochgradigem Hörverlust ermöglichen, wieder Klänge wahrzunehmen und Sprache zu verstehen. Wie gut das Sprachverstehen nach der Implantation gelingt, ist individuell sehr unterschiedlich: Bei rund einem Viertel der Patientinnen und Patienten bleiben die Ergebnisse hinter den Erwartungen zurück, und verlässliche Prognosen zum individuellen Nutzen eines Cochlea-Implantats vor der Operation fehlen bislang. Hinweise deuten darauf hin, dass neben dem Hörorgan auch die Verarbeitung und Vernetzung im Gehirn eine wichtige Rolle spielen. Die SOUND Study untersucht, wie sich diese Erkenntnisse für individuellere Prognosen nutzen lassen. linkedin:4480692746.desc: Scientist Jena Developmental and Evolutionary Biology & Genetics Immunobiology and Infection Biology & Medicine Earth Sciences and Climate Research Social Sciences Linguistics Job Offer from October 23, 2026 The Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (MPI-GEA) was founded in summer 2022 and is a dynamically growing, highly-interdisciplinary and international research institution. The research focuses on modeling and analyzing the interrelationships between biophysical and human-made systems, looking from the deep past to the future. The institute examines how humanity has driven the emergence of the Anthropocene – the period in which human activities began significantly impacting our planet’s climate and ecosystems – and identifying potential intervention points towards a more sustainable future. Remuneration will follow the standard PhD salaries given in the Max Planck Society which correspond to 65% of EG 13 TvöD (Bund). The position includes 31 days of annual leave. The successful candidate can apply for admission to our graduate school “International Max Planck Research School for Modeling the Anthropocene”. linkedin:4482649226.title: SD-26142 PhD CANDIDATE IN SOCIAL CRITERIA DRIVEN ABSOLUTE ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY ASSESSMENT
linkedin:4482649226.desc: Fixed term contract | Belvaux | 48 months Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact. The Environmental Sustainability Assessment and Circularity (SUSTAIN) Unit conducts cross‑disciplinary research to support the transition toward a more sustainable, resilient, and healthy society. SUSTAIN combines expertise in environmental sciences, circular economy, risk and safety assessment, and sustainable innovation to address complex challenges related to human and environmental health, climate change, and resource efficiency, developing knowledge, methods, and transferable software for the simulation and comprehensive sustainability assessment of socio-economic systems. Its purpose is to foster sustainable eco-innovation, through products and technologies, as well as support sustainability-oriented policy implementation and behavioural change to promote decarbonisation transitions. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? The world faces a convergence of crises that are transforming the conditions for human development. Climate instability, ecosystem degradation, and the overuse of natural resources have reached critical levels, while social inequality, political fragmentation, and technological disruption are reshaping societies. Traditional notions of economic competitiveness, centred on growth and productivity, are being redefined to include social resilience, inclusiveness, and ecological integrity. Responding to this “polycrisis” requires new pathways that reconcile prosperity with planetary and social limits. Luxembourg offers a particularly illustrative example of these tensions. The country enjoys one of the highest income levels globally and a dynamic financial and business environment that sustains its reputation for economic success. Yet this prosperity depends strongly on cross-border commuting, which creates mobility challenges and environmental stress. Escalating housing prices have made access to affordable living increasingly difficult, displacing a significant share of the workforce beyond national borders. The reliance on imported energy leaves households and firms vulnerable to external shocks. Although Luxembourg’s welfare model and social dialogue remain robust, they are under pressure from rising costs of living, widening inequalities, and growing demands on public services. Environmentally, Luxembourg’s footprint per inhabitant ranks among the largest worldwide, driven by high consumption and land-use pressures that push the country beyond sustainable limits. Meeting these intertwined challenges calls for coordinated transformations that bridge sectors, disciplines, and scales. Economic and social progress must be reframed within the concept of a Safe Operating Space—an area in which human well-being is achieved without breaching environmental boundaries. The objective is to steer innovation, governance, and everyday practices toward forms of competitiveness that are compatible with sustainability, rather than in conflict with it. The Doctoral Training Unit C-SOS (Competitiveness within a Safe Operating Space) is designed to cultivate researchers capable of analysing and fostering such transformations. It brings together an interdisciplinary consortium to train 12 PhD candidates in the assessment and design of inclusive and sustainable development trajectories. The programme equips them with conceptual and methodological tools to connect environmental sustainability, social well-being, and economic dynamics into integrated frameworks for decision-making. Its ambition is to inform socio-economic policies, encourage responsible industrial and technological innovation, and contribute to more equitable and resilient societies. Luxembourg provides an ideal environment for this initiative, combining strong expertise in sustainability science and policy analysis. The DTU is a collaboration between researchers at the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), the University of Luxembourg (UL) and the Urban Development and Mobility Department at the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research (LISER). The consortium also includes the National Statistics Office (STATEC). In this DTU, 12 scientists will train 12 PhD students over six years (from January 2027), each obtaining a PhD from UL’s doctoral schools. As part of the C-SOS Doctoral Training Unit, in this PhD you will integrate concepts from Post-Growth, Sufficiency and Doughnut Economics into the downscaling of planetary boundaries, leveraging good examples of application to territories and cities. Possible research questions include: how to couple ecological limits and social foundation as an interdependent system? How to define social foundation? How to allocate the carrying capacity based on social foundation?. You will be embedded in the SUSTAIN unit at LIST and enrolled as a doctoral candidate at the University of Luxembourg. You will work closely with a diverse cohort of 12 PhD researchers across the social, economic, and environmental sciences, contributing to a shared research agenda on how Luxembourg can thrive within its fair share of planetary limits You will be mainly in charge of: Conducting a systematic review and critical assessment of existing carrying capacity allocation and planetary boundary downscaling approaches, spanning economic and emission based allocation methods, sufficiency based approaches, and Doughnut Economics frameworks Developing a methodological framework for coupling ecological limits and social foundation as an interdependent system, integrating Post-Growth, Sufficiency, and Doughnut Economics concepts into the downscaling of planetary boundaries Applying the framework to Luxembourg and comparable small territories under a range of allocation scenarios, drawing on Green Deal technology targets, context specific Decent Living Standards, and provisioning systems, producing environmental ceiling estimates grounded in social foundation thresholds Building and maintaining a dynamic system model enabling the testing of individual and combined allocation approaches, valuing social outcome generation per unit of environmental impact across relevant planetary boundary dimensions Collaborating with other C-SOS doctoral researchers, in particular those working on social foundation, Quality of Life, and economic systems, to ensure that allocation approaches rest on socially realistic and empirically coherent definitions of social foundation Publishing results in peer reviewed journals and presenting at international conferences Contributing to C-SOS training activities, workshops, and stakeholder engagement events Is Your profile described below? Are you our future colleague? Apply now! Your mission Help create engineering tools that combine mechanics, computation and AI to make the design of complex optomechatronic systems faster, more rigorous and more reusable. CSEM and the Engineering Design and Computing Laboratory of ETH Zurich are seeking a doctoral researcher to investigate how AI and advanced computational methods can support the design of high-performance optomechatronic systems. The research will be anchored in compliant mechanisms, where performance emerges from tightly coupled geometry, material behaviour, actuation, sensing, manufacturing and verification constraints. The ambition is not to treat AI as a black box. You will develop scientifically grounded methods that combine physics-based models, simulation data and engineering knowledge, and make their predictions traceable, testable and useful to engineers. Research focus The project will build on the outcomes of Guilain Lang’s doctoral thesis, “CAM2S2: Compliant AM Mechanisms Systematic Synthesizer” [link to the online thesis], which established a systematic framework for translating requirements into compliant mechanism designs. The new research will critically assess and selectively reuse, adapt or extend the methods and tools developed in CAM2S2, without being constrained to retain the complete existing framework. From this foundation, it will develop and validate AI-assisted methods to derive engineering insight from requirements, explore broader solution spaces and generate reusable models for mechanism and optomechatronic system design. The exact thesis plan will be refined with the selected candidate and the supervisors. Expected research directions include: AI-assisted interpretation of requirements to identify critical design drivers, sensitive parameters, conflicts and uncertainty. Traceable use of scientific literature and CSEM engineering knowledge, including models, test results and lessons learned. Inverse and multi-objective design methods that connect required performance to geometry, material choices and manufacturing constraints. Extension of mechanism synthesis beyond a limited set of topologies, including variable cross-sections and alternative manufacturing routes. Physics-informed surrogate or reduced-order models for nonlinear stiffness, stress, buckling, parasitic motion and other key mechanism properties. Automated generation of design-of-experiment campaigns using finite element models and computational methods. Implementation and validation on representative compliant optomechatronic demonstrators. Your responsibilities Formulate focused research questions and establish robust benchmarks against existing analytical, numerical and engineering workflows. Develop computational models, algorithms and research software with reproducible data and version control practices. Design numerical experiments, critically assess model validity and quantify uncertainty. Work closely with specialists in mechanics, systems engineering, AI, manufacturing and testing at CSEM and ETH Zurich. Validate selected methods against higher-fidelity simulations and experimental evidence. Publish in leading peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences. Transfer useful methods into engineering tools and document them so that they can be understood, challenged and reused. Your profile Know-how Essential Master's degree in microtechnology or mechanical engineering, computational science and engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, robotics, or a closely related field. Strong foundation in computational mechanics and numerical modelling, including finite element analysis. Understanding of the architecture and development of multidisciplinary optomechatronic or mechatronic systems. Ability to develop and assess computational methods beyond routine use of commercial FEM software. Solid programming skills, preferably in Python and/or a compiled scientific-computing language. Rigorous scientific reasoning, independence, creativity and the ability to communicate clearly in written and spoken English. Strong assets Background in machine learning, artificial intelligence or data-driven modelling, with the ability to connect these methods to physical systems. Experience with surrogate modelling, optimisation, uncertainty quantification, reduced-order modelling, differentiable simulation or scientific machine learning. Knowledge of compliant mechanisms, nonlinear structural mechanics, mechanism synthesis or topology optimisation. Experience in design for additive manufacturing. DfAM is a major advantage, although the project will not be limited to DfAM. Experience with CAD, parametric modelling, experimental validation or the development of engineering software. What we offer A doctoral project at the intersection of fundamental methods and demanding real-world engineering applications. Joint supervision by CSEM and Prof. Kristina Shea's Engineering Design and Computing Laboratory at ETH Zurich. Access to CSEM expertise, engineering heritage, simulation and test capabilities in precision mechanisms and optomechatronic systems. A multidisciplinary and international environment with close interaction between researchers and engineers. The opportunity to publish scientific results while translating research into methods with direct engineering value. Attractive employment conditions and access to the ETH Zurich doctoral ecosystem, subject to the applicable admission and approval requirements. Since 1984, our purpose has remained constant: to harness science and technology for the benefit of society. Today, with over 650 people across Switzerland, we remain committed to our mission: to develop and transfer world-class solutions in digital technologies, precision manufacturing, and sustainable energy systems. In doing so, we empower Swiss industry to innovate and remain competitive. Our strength is the excellence of our people. We believe that strong values support the successful development of our organization as well as the harmonious and balanced development of all our employees. We are A unique place between research and industry at the cutting edge of new technologies An innovative, non-profit, and employee-driven company A dynamic, multidisciplinary, and multicultural environment A solar team focused on enabling solutions to energy challenges for a sustainable world Working@CSEM means Being part of a passionate community Flexibility, attractive working conditions, and opportunities of development Benefit from a management style based on trust & feedback Please submit: A concise motivation letter explaining why this research question fits your background and ambitions. Contact details for at least two academic or professional referees. Applications will be evaluated on scientific potential, depth of fundamentals, evidence of independent problem solving and alignment with the interdisciplinary nature of the project. linkedin:4483101644.title: CDD - Doctorant CIFRE (H/F/X) - Tribologie & Science des Matériaux : Durabilité des tribofilms vers une meilleure prédiction des performances des lubrifiants
linkedin:4483101644.desc: Contexte et environnement Rejoignez TotalEnergies et participez à un projet de recherche innovant mené en partenariat avec le Laboratoire de Tribologie et Dynamique des Systèmes (LTDS) de l'École Centrale de Lyon. Dans un contexte d'amélioration continue des performances énergétiques et environnementales, la compréhension des mécanismes de frottement et d'usure constitue un enjeu majeur pour le développement des futures générations de lubrifiants. En conditions sévères de lubrification, certains additifs contenus dans le lubrifiant réagissent avec les surfaces frottantes pour former un tribofilm permettant de contrôler le frottement et l'usure de l’interface. Cette thèse CIFRE a pour objectif d'identifier des descripteurs mécaniques, physico-chimiques et interfaciaux robustes permettant de relier les propriétés et la durabilité des tribofilms aux performances tribologiques observées. Les résultats contribueront à améliorer la discrimination des formulations et la prédictivité des méthodes d'évaluation des lubrifiants, afin d'accélérer le développement de formulations innovantes. Le doctorant évoluera au sein d'un environnement mêlant recherche académique et recherche industrielle, avec une présence répartie entre le Centre de Recherche de Solaize et le LTDS à Écully. Activités À ce titre, vos principales missions consistent à : Contribuer scientifiquement à la diminution de la consommation énergétique ; Définir et mettre en œuvre les protocoles expérimentaux nécessaires pour générer des tribofilms dans des conditions contrôlées ; Réaliser des essais tribologiques sur différentes formulations et différents matériaux ; Caractériser les surfaces, interfaces et tribofilms à l'aide de techniques avancées de caractérisation ; Exploiter, analyser et interpréter les résultats expérimentaux obtenus ; Étudier la robustesse, la variabilité et l'évolution des propriétés des tribofilms au cours des sollicitations tribologiques, afin de mieux comprendre les mécanismes qui gouvernent leur durabilité et les performances associées ; Développer des descripteurs robustes et exploitables permettant d'améliorer la discrimination des formulations et la prédiction des performances des lubrifiants ; Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de TotalEnergies et du LTDS ; Présenter l'avancement de vos travaux lors de réunions scientifiques et techniques ; Valoriser les résultats au travers de publications et de participations à des conférences nationales et internationales ; Rédiger et soutenir une thèse de doctorat à l'issue des travaux de recherche. Profil du candidat Titulaire ou prochainement diplômé d' un Master 2 ou d'un Diplôme d'Ingénieur en tribologie, science des matériaux, mécanique, physico-chimie ou dans un domaine lié aux surfaces et aux interfaces , vous souhaitez vous engager dans un projet de recherche appliquée au sein d'un environnement combinant excellence académique et recherche industrielle. Vous justifiez idéalement d' une première expérience en laboratoire de recherche ou en R&D (stage de fin d'études, projet de recherche, année de césure), au cours de laquelle vous avez réalisé des travaux expérimentaux et participé à l' analyse de résultats scientifiques . Vous avez : Une bonne connaissance de la science des matériaux et des phénomènes liés aux surfaces et interfaces ; Un intérêt marqué pour la tribologie, les phénomènes de frottement, d'usure et de lubrification ; Une expérience pratique des manipulations expérimentales en laboratoire ; Des compétences en analyse et traitement de données scientifiques ; Une bonne maîtrise de l'anglais scientifique, à l'écrit comme à l'oral ; Idéalement, une expérience en techniques de caractérisation des matériaux ou des surfaces (AFM, Raman, XPS, nanoindentation ou techniques similaires). Vous appréciez le travail expérimental et le travail en équipe. Vous êtes capable d'évoluer dans un environnement multidisciplinaire à l'interface entre mécanique, matériaux et physico-chimie et souhaitez contribuer à des travaux de recherche à fort impact industriel.

Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact. The Environmental Sustainability Assessment and Circularity (SUSTAIN) Unit conducts cross‑disciplinary research to support the transition toward a more sustainable, resilient, and healthy society. SUSTAIN combines expertise in environmental sciences, circular economy, risk and safety assessment, and sustainable innovation to address complex challenges related to human and environmental health, climate change, and resource efficiency, developing knowledge, methods, and transferable software for the simulation and comprehensive sustainability assessment of socio-economic systems. Its purpose is to foster sustainable eco-innovation, through products and technologies, as well as support sustainability-oriented policy implementation and behavioural change to promote decarbonisation transitions. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? The world faces a convergence of crises that are transforming the conditions for human development. Climate instability, ecosystem degradation, and the overuse of natural resources have reached critical levels, while social inequality, political fragmentation, and technological disruption are reshaping societies. Traditional notions of economic competitiveness, centred on growth and productivity, are being redefined to include social resilience, inclusiveness, and ecological integrity. Responding to this “polycrisis” requires new pathways that reconcile prosperity with planetary and social limits. Luxembourg offers a particularly illustrative example of these tensions. The country enjoys one of the highest income levels globally and a dynamic financial and business environment that sustains its reputation for economic success. Yet this prosperity depends strongly on cross-border commuting, which creates mobility challenges and environmental stress. Escalating housing prices have made access to affordable living increasingly difficult, displacing a significant share of the workforce beyond national borders. The reliance on imported energy leaves households and firms vulnerable to external shocks. Although Luxembourg’s welfare model and social dialogue remain robust, they are under pressure from rising costs of living, widening inequalities, and growing demands on public services. Environmentally, Luxembourg’s footprint per inhabitant ranks among the largest worldwide, driven by high consumption and land-use pressures that push the country beyond sustainable limits. Meeting these intertwined challenges calls for coordinated transformations that bridge sectors, disciplines, and scales. Economic and social progress must be reframed within the concept of a Safe Operating Space—an area in which human well-being is achieved without breaching environmental boundaries. The objective is to steer innovation, governance, and everyday practices toward forms of competitiveness that are compatible with sustainability, rather than in conflict with it. The Doctoral Training Unit C-SOS (Competitiveness within a Safe Operating Space) is designed to cultivate researchers capable of analysing and fostering such transformations. It brings together an interdisciplinary consortium to train 12 PhD candidates in the assessment and design of inclusive and sustainable development trajectories. The programme equips them with conceptual and methodological tools to connect environmental sustainability, social well-being, and economic dynamics into integrated frameworks for decision-making. Its ambition is to inform socio-economic policies, encourage responsible industrial and technological innovation, and contribute to more equitable and resilient societies. Luxembourg provides an ideal environment for this initiative, combining strong expertise in sustainability science and policy analysis. The DTU is a collaboration between researchers at the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), the University of Luxembourg (UL) and the Urban Development and Mobility Department at the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research (LISER). The consortium also includes the National Statistics Office (STATEC). In this DTU, 12 scientists will train 12 PhD students over six years (from January 2027), each obtaining a PhD from UL’s doctoral schools. As part of the C-SOS Doctoral Training Unit, in this PhD you will develop a quantitative policy toolbox that estimates, across multiple planetary boundary dimensions (e.g. climate change, water and land use, biodiversity), what a given policy measure actually delivers — individually and in combination — for Luxembourg and the Greater Region. You will be embedded in the SUSTAIN unit at LIST and enrolled as a doctoral candidate at the University of Luxembourg. You will work closely with a diverse cohort of 12 PhD researchers across the social, economic, and environmental sciences, contributing to a shared research agenda on how Luxembourg can thrive within its fair share of planetary limits You will be mainly in charge of: Conducting a systematic review and critical assessment of existing multiregional input-output (MRIO) analysis based projection methods and demand-side modelling approaches (taxation/subsidies, bans, income elasticities, rebound effects) Developing a methodological framework for the prospective quantification of environmental impacts of policy scenarios, integrating input-output analysis, scenario modelling, and micro-economic methods Applying the framework to Luxembourg and the Greater Region under a range of beyond-growth and climate policy scenarios (e.g. carbon fee-and-dividend schemes, ICE phase-out, 4-day workweek, housing construction codes, mobility subsidies), producing quantitative footprint estimates at territorial scale Building and maintaining an open, modular, Python-based policy toolbox enabling the testing of individual and combined policy measures and their environmental outcomes across all relevant planetary boundary dimensions Collaborating with other C-SOS doctoral researchers — in particular those working on social foundation and economic systems — to ensure that policy scenarios are grounded in socially realistic and economically coherent assumptions Publishing results in peer-reviewed journals and presenting at international conferences Contributing to C-SOS training activities, workshops, and stakeholder engagement events Is Your profile described below? linkedin:4481011007.title: PhD Student (m/f/d) |Community ecology, stone tool use and social behavior in gracile capuchin monkeys
linkedin:4481011007.desc: Young Researchers Radolfzell / Konstanz Developmental and Evolutionary Biology & Genetics Behavioral Sciences Microbiology & Ecology Job Offer from October 23, 2026 The Max Planck Institut of Animal Behavior at its sites in Konstanz and Radolfzell offers an international, interdisciplinary, and collaborative enviroment that opens up unique research opportunities. The goal of our basic research is to develop a quantitative and predictive understanding of the decisions and movements of animals in their natural environment. The Ecology of Animal Societies at the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior would like to fill PhD Student (m/f/d) 100 % - Community ecology, stone tool use and social behavior in gracile capuchin monkeys with a flexible starting date in summer / autumn 2027 . This position is fully funded for a period of 4 years. The workplace will be in Konstanz, Germany. Our Group The Inheritance and Social Learning across Scales (ISLaS) group investigates how extragenetic modes of inheritance– namely cultural transmission via social learning and the ecological inheritance of home ranges and territories— affect and are affected by social behavior, ecology, and genetic evolution. We aim to integrate quantitative theory with reproducible Bayesian statistical modeling grounded in an appreciation for natural history. Our work integrates theory and tools from cultural evolution, animal behavior, population biology, spatial ecology, and the quantitative social sciences. We are based out of Konstanz, Germany, but our group does field research in Panama, Costa Rica, Colombia, Mozambique, and California. Our current group has projects focused on the adaptive significance of tool use, parasitology, social behavior and ecology in capuchin monkeys, methods development in social network analysis, and computer vision tools for studying longitudinal behavior and population demography using camera traps. We prioritize theoretical and methodological rigor and embracing uncertainty over prestige, and are sympatheticto many social and methodological calls for science reform (i.e. reproducible, open science and in-country field-partnerships and collaboration). Project Details We will hire one student for one of two possible projects: [A] Community Ecology of Stone Tool Use in Gracile Capuchins This project will focus on combining field experimentation and data collection, analyzing existing data, and analytical or agent-based modeling to tackle varying questions related to stone tool use by white-faced capuchin monkeys (Cebus imitator) living in the archipelago of Coiba National Park, Panama. Most of these groups are unhabituated and highly terrestrial, so camera trapping is central to our research. Field work may consist of a few 2 week trips or longer multi-month stays in Panama depending on the nature of the project. Linking Tool-Use Behavior to Below-ground Ecological Processes Promises and Pitfalls of Capuchin Tool-use to Heterospeciﬁcs The Metapopulation Ecology of Stone Tool Sites [B] Multi-site comparisons of the social behavior, ecology, and/or movement of gracile capuchin monkeys (genus Cebus) This project is opened up to a motivated and independent PhD student with systems expertise in Cebus trying to answer broad scale questions about the social behavior, population demography, community ecology, movement ecology or any other aspect of Cebus behavior, evolution, and ecology. A desire to develop indirect approaches to measure these biological or environmental traits (camera trapping, remote sensing, biological samples) is a plus. Potential students may work within our study systems in Panama, or foster collaboration between long-term studies where they have previous research experience and support from senior collaborators. The project should dovetail with long-term research goals of our group and yield within group collaborations. Qualifications REQUIRED: Applicants are required to have a Masters degree in any scientific discipline including biology, ecology, anthropology, archaeology, or the quantitative sciences and have some previous field research experience. DESIRED: The candidate should be enthusiastic about integrating observational and/or experimental field collected data with quantitative approaches in Bayesian data analysis, causal inference, or theoretical modelling. Broad thinking and a desire to link fields and questions across disciplines is a plus. Previous field research experience in remote environments, the desire to conduct field research in the tropical Americas, and the ability to work and communicate in a cross-cultural context is highly desirable. Prior experience with programming (e.g. in R, Python, Julia, Mathematica, NetLogo, etc.) and an enthusiasm for tackling challenging problems is also highly desirable.Researchers with systems expertise, who feel they may be lacking in quantitative skills are encouraged to apply as well if they are willing to put in considerable effort to develop them with the group’s guidance. The student will be expected to proactively co-develop and implement research ideas to move the project forward, thus a high degree of independence, and ability to know when to ask for help if needed, is crucial. The working language of the group is English, the ability to speak Spanish is desirable, and German language skills are not a requirement. Applicants who are shortlisted for interviews are strongly encouraged to talk to current lab members and alumni to feel out if a PhD position in the group is a mutually beneficial fit. Our Offer The student will join the Inheritance and Social Learning across Scales (ISLaS) research group led by Dr. Brendan Barrett (he/him) and integrated within the Department for the Ecology of Animal Societies. They will work closely with a team of collaborators both within the department, outside of the department and at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute in Panama. The University of Konstanz and the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior together form a thriving research community representing a global hotspot for behavioral ecology, collective behavior, and animal movement research, including the Centre for the Advanced Study of Collective Behavior. The student will join the International Max Planck Research School for Quantitative Behaviour, Ecology and Evolution from lab to field (IMPRS-QBEE), a cooperative doctoral program between the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior and the University of Konstanz. The successful candidate will join a supportive, international, and interdisciplinary research team, with access to strong academic and career mentorship, the ability to participate in coursework and conferences, and opportunities for growth as both a computational and field biologist. The position is fully funded for 4 years (TVöD salary scale E-13, 65%). The Max Planck Society endeavors to employ more severely disabled people. Applications of severely disabled persons are expressly welcome. The Max Planck Society strives for gender and diversity equality. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. How to apply Are you interested? Then we are looking forward to receiving your application by December 1, 2026 through IMPRS Online portal. Please Include The Following Application Materials Curriculum vitae (CV) Contact information for 2 references Letter of motivation Research Statement (2 pages, excluding references) Research interests: Describe your main research interests, how they developed, and how they relate to the research we do in our group. (½ page) Research proposal: Spend some time exploring our groups prior publications or relevant literature. Then, choose one of the potential project directions listed above (A or B) and describe 1-2 specific biological questions you would like to ask or hypotheses you would like to test within the scope of the project. Explain the theoretical framework and/or analytical approach(es) you would use to address your question(s). Include a mock figure (can be hand drawn) of what your results might look like, and an interpretation of your potential findings (1-2 pages). ( NOTE: this section is an opportunity for you to develop your ideas and demonstrate how you would address scientific questions with quantitative approaches. It is not meant as a full-fledged PhD proposal, and you will not be expected to carry out the exact project you propose should you join our team!) Code example: If possible please provide an example of some code you have written, with a brief explanation of what it does (you can also link to publicly-accessible repository). The code does not have to relate to animal behavior, but it should be written by you and be something you can explain to others if needed. AI Declaration: For transparency (and not penalization), indicate if you used AI in drafting your application, and if so describe briefly how you used it. Academic transcripts for your BSc and MSc degrees. Transcripts can be unofficial at this stage – official records will be required before acceptance. Questions about this position should be addressed to Dr. Brendan Barrett (bbarrett@ab.mpg.de).

linkedin:4481067227.desc: Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon The Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon conducts cutting-edge international research for a changing world: Around 1,000 employees contribute to the tackling of climate change, the sustainable use of the world's coastal systems and the resource-compatible enhancement of the quality of life. From fundamental research to practical applications, the interdisciplinary research spectrum covers a unique range. Institute of Material and Process Design The Institute of Material and Process Design is dedicated to the sustainable and ecological development of innovative materials and manufacturing processes, especially for the transportation sector and medical technology. To this end, materials are tailored and manufacturing processes are designed to conserve resources – from the modeling of material behavior to the development of the material to the finished component. PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys Reference code: 1057 - 2026/WD 1 Commencement date: as soon as possible Work location: Geesthacht Application deadline: November 12th, 2026 The Institute of Material and Process Design at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon is offering a 4-year PhD position in the field of computational materials engineering, machine learning, and digital twins for advanced lightweight materials. The focus of the PhD project will be the development of a physics-guided digital twin framework for magnesium alloys by integrating experimental characterization, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, precipitation modeling, and machine learning approaches to establish quantitative composition-process-structure-property relationships. Building upon recently developed machine-learning approaches for structure-property prediction in extruded magnesium alloys, the project aims to advance toward a next-generation Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework capable of predicting microstructure evolution and resulting mechanical properties across previously unseen processing conditions and material states. The candidate will work closely with interdisciplinary teams combining expertise in magnesium alloy development, thermomechanical processing, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, machine learning, and advanced experimental characterization. The objective of the project is to bridge the gap between purely data-driven materials modeling and mechanistic microstructure simulations by combining crystal plasticity, dynamic recrystallization, precipitation kinetics, and machine learning into a unified digital-twin framework. The resulting methodologies shall enable accelerated alloy and process design by leveraging experimentally validated physics-guided surrogate models with improved extrapolation capabilities beyond the limits of conventional machine-learning approaches. This work directly contributes to the digital transformation of materials development and manufacturing technologies for future lightweight engineering applications. fully-funded PhD programme Full Time Edinburgh Posted 4 days ago Website CDT in Machine Learning Systems, University of Edinburgh About The CDT Machine Learning has a dramatic impact on our daily lives built on the back of improved computer systems. Systems research and ML research are symbiotic. Modern systems research targets the ubiquitous need for efficient ML. ML research, conversely, is directly affected by how methods will be deployed. Furthermore, systems research increasingly explores ML methods to improve systems, and ML research develops such methods. Major gains are made when the development of ML and systems are symbiotic and co-optimized. This is relevant across a broad spectrum of industries: in-car systems, medical devices, phones, sensor networks, condition monitoring systems, high-performance compute, and high-frequency trading. This CDT develops researchers with expertise across the systems-ML stack. This makes a cohort-based programme vital, treating ML Systems as a holistic discipline. Cohort interaction, and integration, give students real experience across multiple systems, approaches and methodologies. Company engagement is an integral part of the programme with built-in internships alongside entrepreneurship training. The PhD programme in Machine Learning Systems positions students for strong, ethically aware technical careers, developing the next generation of leaders. Students will develop foundational research skills in Computer Systems, Machine Learning, Hardware, Sensors and Control, Programming and Integrated Machine Learning Environments, AI Ethics, and Leadership and Entrepreneurship. At the end, all students will have extensive experience of real-world deployment and optimization of machine learning methods. Candidate’s profile An Ideal Candidate Would Typically Have a strong degree or higher qualification in a relevant field (e.g. computer science, mathematics, engineering, physical sciences, economics or any other field where evidence is provided of sufficient computing and mathematical background) solid experience of programming, machine learning methods and ideally deep learning environments (e.g. pytorch) or a computer systems background CDT studentships The CDT has a minimum of 10 fully-funded studentships available for September 2027 entry. Studentships include stipend, fees and research costs for 4 years. Home students will receive an enhanced stipend thanks to the Government TechFirst Scheme, in return of some additional requirements around widening participation and wider engagement with the TechFirst programme. As a UKRI-funded CDT, application is open to all UK/EU/non-EU citizens providing they meet the University PhD entry requirements. However, the number of students with international fees status that can be recruited is restricted (about 3 per year). An indication of the fees status categories, entry requirements and further details on eligibility criteria can be found on our website. Why Edinburgh? The University of Edinburgh is one of the best research-intense Universities in the world. The School of Informatics that hosts the CDT is consistently ranked among the world’s top 30 computer science departments. In 2026 QS World University Ranking by Subject, it is ranked 22nd for Computer Science and Information System, and 30th for Data Science and AI. The CDT students will be hosted in the state-of-the-art Informatics Forum in the heart of Scotland’s capital, consistently considered one of the most desirable places to live in the world. How To Apply The deadline for first-stage applications is 14th December 2026, 23:59. We accept applications from Home applicants until 15th March 2027, pending studentships availability.
