linkedin:4481066383.desc: Life is always about becoming… Im Leben geht es darum, sich auf eine Reise zu begeben, um die beste Version unseres zukünftigen Selbst zu werden. Während wir Neues entdecken, stellen wir uns Herausforderungen, meistern sie und wachsen über uns hinaus. Bewerben Sie sich bei Mercedes-Benz und finden Sie den Aufgabenbereich, in dem Sie Ihre Talente individuell entfalten können. Dabei werden Sie von visionären Kolleginnen und Kollegen unterstützt, die Ihren Pioniergeist teilen. Bei uns einzusteigen bedeutet, Teil eines globalen Teams zu werden, dessen Ziel es ist, die begehrenswertesten Automobile der Welt zu bauen. Together for excellence. Stellennummer: MER00049OI Aufgaben Du hast ein ingenieur- oder naturwissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium abgeschlossen und möchtest kunststofftechnische Verarbeitungsverfahren für automobile Elektroantriebe weiterentwickeln? Du arbeitest gerne an der Schnittstelle zwischen Vorentwicklung, Produktion, Werkstofftechnik und Qualität? Dann erwartet Dich ein Promotionsvorhaben zu kunststofftechnischen Fertigungsprozessen für den Stator eines Elektromotors. Wir vom Team der Prozessentwicklung für elektrische Antriebe sind Teil des Planungs- und Produktionstechnologiezentrums für den Antriebsstrang am Standort Untertürkheim. Wir stellen in Zusammenarbeit mit den anderen Teams die neuesten und innovativsten Technologien im Produktionsumfeld zur Verfügung und sichern den Reifegrad bis zur Serieneinführung ab. In unserem Team werden neben vielen fertigungstechnischen und messtechnischen, auch weiterführende Fragestellungen aus dem Entwicklungs- und Qualitätsbereich bearbeitet. Zudem entwickeln wir innovative Fertigungsverfahren und Prozesse für hochwertige Powertrain-Anwendungen. Im Rahmen eines Technologieprojektes für zukünftige Antriebssysteme suchen wir eine*n Doktorand*in mit dem Fokus der Weiterentwicklung von Fertigungstechnologien in der Kunststofftechnik. Deine Aufgaben umfassen unter anderem: Stand der Technik zu polymerbasierten Stator Baugruppen und Isolationskonzepten analysieren Fertigungsprozesse wie Spritzgießen, Extrusion, Imprägnieren und Pressen entwickeln Thermoplaste, Duroplaste und Faserverbundwerkstoffe werkstoff- und prozessgerecht auslegen Versuchsreihen mittels Design of Experiments planen, durchführen und auswerten Prozess-, Werkzeug- und Qualitätsdaten korrelieren sowie robuste Prozessfenster ableiten Werkstoffe mittels DSC, TGA, DMA, TMA und Rheometrie charakterisieren Prozessinduzierte Defekte und Schädigungsmechanismen analysieren Bauteilqualität, Zykluszeit, Materialeffizienz und Industrialisierbarkeit optimieren Ergebnisse dokumentieren, publizieren und mit Fachbereichen sowie Universität abstimmen Die Tätigkeit kann ab Februar 2027 beginnen. Einstellungsvoraussetzung ist die Betreuung des Promotionsvorhabens durch einen Hochschullehrenden. Die Auswahl einer entsprechenden Betreuungsperson obliegt dem Promovierenden. Profil Studium: Sehr gut abgeschlossenes Master- oder Diplomstudium der Kunststofftechnik, Polymertechnik, Leichtbau, Maschinenbau oder vergleichbar mit kunststofftechnischem Schwerpunkt sowie erfüllte Promotionsvoraussetzungen Fachkenntnisse: Fundierte Kenntnisse und praktische Erfahrung in der Kunststoffverarbeitung, insbesondere Spritzgießen; Erfahrung mit Extrusion, Duroplasten, Insert-Molding, Verguss- oder Faserverbundverfahren ist von Vorteil Analytik: Praktische Erfahrung mit DSC, TGA, DMA, TMA und Rheometrie; Kenntnisse in Mikroskopie oder mechanischer Prüfung sind wünschenswert Methoden und IT: Erfahrung mit DoE und statistischer Datenanalyse; sicherer Umgang mit MS Office, Kenntnisse in CAD, Python oder Prozesssimulation sind von Vorteil Sprachen: Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Persönliches: Analytische, selbstständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise, Labororientierung, Qualitätsbewusstsein, Kommunikationsstärke und Teamfähigkeit Sonstiges: Bereitschaft zur Arbeit im Technikum und Labor sowie Führerschein Klasse B Zusätzliche Informationen: Promoviere im Mercedes-Benz Konzern! Profitiere von unserem Know-how, einem internationalen Expertise-Netzwerk, Forschungsmaterialien, Arbeitseinblicken und einer persönlichen Betreuung durch Mentorinnen und Mentoren – zusätzlich zu Deiner Hochschule. thehub:6adbf55a6c9d8e36c1fccfe6.title: Junior Quantum Engineer (PhD candidate)
thehub:6adbf55a6c9d8e36c1fccfe6.desc:
At IQM, we build world-leading quantum computers for the well-being of humankind. We design systems to tackle computational challenges beyond the practical limits of classical machines. Our work sits at the edge of science and engineering. It's complex, demanding, and deeply collaborative. We turn deep research into reliable, full-stack systems that drive discoveries in fields like medicine, energy, and technology, reshaping how the world computes.
 This position is part of QuBriC , the first European Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network dedicated entirely to QEC. You will join an international cohort of doctoral researchers and collaborate with leading academic and industrial partners, including research visits at Chalmers (Gothenburg) and INRA (Paris) .
 Join the team that gives quantum a heartbeat.
 The work 
 The PhD project focus on successfully implementing and testing quantum error correction (QEC) protocols on hardware efficient quantum processors (QPU). You will have access to IQM co-design architecture QPU to benchmark QEC codes efficiency on those QPUs.
 Joining our QEC Operations team, you will combine Python development, experiments on superconducting quantum processors and data analysis to improve and demonstrate QEC performance. You will develop calibration procedure and fundamental operations such as qubit reset and leakage reduction units. Working with quantum and software engineering teams, you will also contribute to the control software that makes these experiments possible.
 Your IQM Team Leader will guide your engineering work, while your PhD supervisor will guide your academic research. Alongside your contributions to IQM’s QEC roadmap, you will write scientific publications, present your findings and complete the activities required by your host university.
 What you’ll actually do 
 Implement, run and analyze experiments for fundamental QEC operations, including qubit reset and leakage reduction.
 Execute QEC capability benchmarks and demonstration experiments, and report findings clearly and accurately.
 Develop features in our quantum computer control software in collaboration with quantum and software engineering teams.
 Support QEC calibration of research and customer quantum processors under guidance, working with calibration and service teams to establish useful workflows.
 Keep up with relevant scientific developments and bring new knowledge into the team’s experimental work.
 Write publications, prepare conference presentations and contribute to university activities, grant reporting and research outreach as part of your PhD.
 What we’re looking for 
 A master’s degree, or equivalent skills, in a field relevant to quantum computing research and development, with excellent academic grades.
 A solid understanding of quantum information processing and quantum computing, including the basic concepts of quantum error correction.
 An understanding of superconducting qubits and quantum processing units.
 Python software engineering skills, including language features, environments, testing, documentation and version control.
 Experience conducting laboratory experiments in quantum science or technology through your studies, research projects or equivalent experience.
 An ability to solve problems with guidance and turn your work into documented code, methods and results that others can use.
 Clear written and spoken communication, a collaborative approach and a commitment to reporting technical results accurately.
 No prior professional experience beyond your university education is required.
 The applicant cannot be in possession of a doctoral degree at the date of the recruitment. 
 Additional information 
 Mobility rule: To fulfil the Marie Skłodowska-Curie mobility rules, you must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Germany for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your date of recruitment.
 The applicant cannot be in possession of a doctoral degree at the date of the recruitment.
 Duration : The position is funded for three years with expecting starting date in January.
 Gross monthly salary range: 5000 € - 5833 €.
 Work location: Munich, Germany.
 Why IQM? 
 Full-stack quantum computing: From quantum hardware to software layers and beyond, we build across the full-stack.
 High-performance playground: We aim high, and we know sustainable performance only works when life outside work does too—hybrid setups, flexible hours.
 Never the smartest: You won’t always be the smartest person in the room. Neither will we. Expect to learn constantly - from each other and beyond with IQM’s Learning Hub, LinkedIn Learning, and a team-based L&D budget.
 Approachable leadership: Flat hierarchy, direct access. Feel free to approach any leaders. They're friendlier than they look!
 The sweet spot: Big enough to matter. Small enough to move fast. Growing between a startup and a corporation. We’re in the phase where top performers get noticed.
 Bigger than IQM: Our people build know-how for the entire quantum ecosystem. We publish papers, run hackathons, and help shape a market that's still being defined.
 The future of computing won’t build itself. You might be one of the few who do. 
 Meet our people and learn more about IQM on our stories page.
 Explore our scientific publications.
 We'll start interviews and move forward with hiring as soon as we meet strong candidates. Please submit your application soon.
 600M€+ Total Funding | 400+ Team Members | 30+ Quantum Computers Built | 300+ Patents Filed | 10 Location Globally 
 IQM is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and gender balance. We evaluate all applicants on merit, regardless of gender, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or disability. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and underrepresented groups."

indeed:5e072f7239ba2a47.desc: registration number: fb17-0028-wmz-2026 Entry date: 2027-02-01 Application deadline: 2026-11-29 Salary: E 13 TV-H Duration: 3 years Volume of employment: part-time (65%) The University of Marburg, founded in 1527, offers a variety of excellent programs of study for around 22,000 students and confronts the important topics of our time through excellent research across a broad spectrum of sciences. The Department of Biology, research group “Animal Ecology” led by Prof. Dr. Anne Mupepele, is currently accepting applications for a position offered in collaboration with Dr. Felix Fornoff, Chair of Nature Conservation and Landscape Ecology, Faculty of Environment and Natural Resources, University of Freiburg. The position is a third-party-funded part-time position (65% of the regular working hours) as Research Assistant (Doctoral Researcher/PhD) is available from 1 February 2027, subject to the approval of funding, for a fixed term of three years. The position will be classified in pay grade E 13 of the Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the State of Hesse (TV-H). The ‘BeeConn’ project (Bee Genetic Connectivity Across Landscapes: Insect Translocation and Population Establishment for Ecological Restoration), funded under the Biodiversa+ call ‘BiodivConnect’, addresses three key challenges in pollinator restoration: 1. the successful translocation and establishment of pollinator species, 2. the restoration of genetic diversity and gene flow through connected stepping-stone habitats and 3. the development of stakeholder-supported strategies for long-term restoration. The project includes additional partners in Sweden and Poland. The PhD project will contribute to all three objectives, with a primary focus on the successful translocation of ground-nesting bees and assessing genetic connectivity across different landscapes in collaboration with the Polish partners. Deviations from this scenario, for example, due to personal preference for one of the two locations or to better balanced work and family life, are possible upon agreement. Further the question of how habitat connectivity affects genetic exchange between populations of cavity-nesting wild bees Academic services in the field of research, including the drafting and publication of peer-reviewed academic articles, as well as the presentation of research findings at working group seminars and at academic conferences The position is limited to a time period deemed adequate for the completion of a doctoral degree. indeed:a7f444bd30951135.title: PhD Position Bayesian Modeling and Counterfactual Methods for Nanoparticle Transport in Human Tissue
indeed:a7f444bd30951135.desc: PhD Position Bayesian Modeling and Counterfactual Methods for Nanoparticle Transport in Human Tissue Shape the future of nanoparticle safety and design. Join TU Delft as a PhD researcher using Bayesian and counterfactual modelling to predict nanoparticle transport in human tissue. Job description We are looking for a PhD candidate to build the computational model at the center of a European project on nanoparticle transport in human tissue. You will join the research group of Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, working within the SYNERGIE project (Horizon Europe), a consortium of thirteen partners including Fraunhofer, Roche, the Karolinska Institute, University Hospital Aachen, Mimetas, Ruhr University Bochum and Maastricht University. Small particles from the environment have been detected in human blood, placenta and brain tissue, but it is still not clear what they do there. Dose-response data for humans does not exist and animal studies have not transferred well, and as a result there is no exposure limit for these particles. Part of the reason prediction is so hard is that a particle changes as it moves through the body. It acquires a layer of proteins, it aggregates with other particles, and depending on the material it may partly degrade, so that the particle reaching a given tissue is not the same object that was administered or characterised at the start. Most transport models do not account for this. They treat the particle as fixed, which means they are predicting the fate of something that has already changed. The same difficulty affects engineered nanoparticles for drug delivery, and it is one of the reasons so few of them reach their intended target. SYNERGIE is building a platform of nine human tissue-on-chip models that can be connected to follow a particle through uptake, circulation and storage. TU Delft leads the in silico work package. As a PhD candidate, you will: Build a mechanistic model of how particles move between nine human tissues, and calibrate it against experimental data using Bayesian inference. Work out which physical and chemical properties of a particle decide where it ends up. Develop methods that go beyond prediction: for a particle that behaves badly, what is the smallest change that would fix it, and when should that answer not be trusted. Release the model as open-source software and support its use in regulatory dialogue. You will also contribute to teaching in the department and to the supervision of BSc projects. You will work alongside a postdoctoral researcher and PhD candidates on related problems, and interact with experimental partners across the SYNERGIE consortium. You will have access to the DelftBlue high-performance computing cluster. The intended start date is January 2027. Job requirements MSc in applied mathematics, computational science, physics, systems biology, or a closely related quantitative field. Demonstrated experience building and solving ODE or dynamical systems models. Demonstrated experience with Bayesian inference in a probabilistic programming framework such as PyMC, Stan or NumPyro. Strong scientific programming in Python. Please point us to a repository. Excellent written and spoken English. Preferred qualifications: Continuous optimization or optimal control. Causal inference or counterfactual reasoning. Surrogate modelling, Gaussian processes, or emulation. Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling or systems pharmacology. Experience packaging and documenting scientific software. No background in toxicology, nanomaterials, chemistry or biology is required. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Technology, Policy & Management The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments. . Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, via s.azimirashti@tudelft.nl. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 29 November 2026 upload your CV, a brief cover letter, a one-page research statement, and a link to a code repository you have built. If the applicants are selected for an interview, they will be asked to provide contact details of two referees with their consent. You can address your application to Dr. Sepinoud Azimi. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. The position is a part of the FME SecurEL center, and it is funded by the Research Council of Norway and USN. The position is located at the Department of Electrical Engineering, Information Technology, and Cybernetics and reports to the Head of Department. The position will be working in the research group, “Electrical Power Systems” (EPS). The place of employment is Porsgrunn. The employment period will be four years full time, and there is a premise for employment that the PhD Research Fellow is enrolled in USN’s PhD-program in PhD in Technology within three months of accession in the position. The four-year full-time period will consist of 75 % research duties and 25 % teaching duties. About the PhD-project and SecurEL This PhD position “The role of hydropower generators in securing electricity supply and enhancing grid resilience” will be associated with Work Package 1 (WP1) on Security of Electricity Supply in SecurEL. The overall objective for the PhD work is to investigate the role of hydropower generators in managing the security of electricity supply in evolving regional distribution grids. The work of the PhD candidate will be integrated with the ongoing work being carried out by the research partners in WP1. In the initial phase, the supervisors, the candidate (based on the candidate's profile), and research partners in SecurEL will work together to identify the comprehensive research questions to be addressed to meet the overall objective of the PhD work. Some potential specific research objectives: Model the coordination and interactions between power producers and system operators (DSOs and TSO) in scenarios for the transition of distribution grids. Quantify the importance of hydropower production and its interoperability in managing security of supply and grid stability. Explore the interplay between different aspects of security of supply (energy availability, power capacity, reliability of supply and voltage quality), as well as power flow balancing, and dynamic system integration) in regional distribution grids. Investigate how generator characteristics such as capabilities for fault-ride through, island mode transition, and black start impact the vulnerability and resilience of the grid, in particular considering islanded grid operation. Develop vulnerability indicators related to power production and control for increasing situational awareness. indeed:31d9bbba44b69dca.desc: ICFO is offering a PhD position to highly motivated student who wish to start their scientific career in a friendly and stimulating environment. The successful candidate will be joining the Macroscopic Quantum Optics Theory group led by Prof. Dr. Oriol Romero-Isart . Our PhD-program brings together top-level training and teaching for young scientists , benefiting from the extensive course offerings of local universities and focused instruction by ICFO professors, in a stimulating, international and interdisciplinary environment . PhD-students have the opportunity to take advantage of our network of excellence , consisting in partners of national and international research institutes and universities, as well as industrial partners in the field. The successful candidate will join a research project funded by a “la Caixa” Junior Leader Fellowship at ICFO. The project, “Tabletop Tests of Fundamental Physics with Levitated Nanoparticles,” will be carried out within the Macroscopic Quantum Optics Theory group Macroscopic Quantum Optics Theory group led by Prof. Dr. Oriol Romero Isart and aims to explore how levitated quantum optomechanical systems can be used to investigate fundamental questions in physics, including the search for new fundamental interactions, dark matter, and signatures of the quantum nature of gravity. Main Tasks and Responsibilities The candidate will conduct theoretical research at the intersection of quantum optics, quantum information, and fundamental physics. Their work will involve developing analytical and numerical tools to model quantum systems and designing experimentally feasible protocols for precision sensing and tests of fundamental physics. Eligibility To be eligible for the position, candidates must: Have an internationally-recognized Master-equivalent degree, The degree must be completed by the start of your prospective PhD at ICFO, at the latest, and must be in a field of science and engineering related to the ICFO research activities. Degrees issued within the European Higher Education Area (EHEA) must have an equivalent to 300 ECTS, out of which a minimum of 60 ECTS must have been obtained in postgraduate studies. Please, if in doubt regarding your academic eligibility, contact us at jobs@icfo.eu Candidates who have already been awarded a PhD are not eligible to apply. Have an excellent academic record, previous research experience and a strong commitment for scientific research. Have a high working knowledge of English. ICFO is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates are selected exclusively on merit and potential on the basis of submitted application material. No restrictions related to disabilities, citizenship or gender apply to ICFO positions. ICFO abides by the principles of openness, efficiency, transparency, supportiveness, and international comparability as stated in the European Charter for Researchers and the European Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers. Candidates with disabilities or other special needs are strongly encouraged to apply to the program. ICFO will provide all possible assistance to ensure the candidate’s application is fairly assessed. Such information may include details of family obligations, severe illness or disability, refugee situation, etc. If the selection panel decides to shortlist a candidate based in part on such extenuating circumstances, it may require the candidate to provide reasonable supporting documentation. Conditions ICFO PhD positions are offered for a period of 4.5 years. The conditions of the positions awarded in the scope of the ICFO PhD fellowship program are as follows: Initial contract for a period of up to 6 months (referred to as the “initial trainee period”), while being pre-admitted to the PhD program, with an explicit follow-up/ renewal procedure at the end of this first stage. Note that in certain circumstances the initial trainee period might be shortened or not offered. During this period, students already take part in the ICFO working environment, join a research group, and work with their supervisor to define a research project. After the initial training period, students are formally enrolled in a PhD Program with a local university (as a general rule, the UPC PhD in Photonics program administered by ICFO), and the full PhD Fellowship activated. Fellowships are offered for periods of three years, renewable for an additional fourth year, and are formalized via a PhD-contract. Continuity and renewal are subject to satisfactory performance in the PhD studies and related research activities, evaluated annually by the Thesis Director and the ICFO PhD Committee. ICFO offers a standard salary level for PhD Students of €27.257,83 gross annual salary. This applies to both the 6-months Trainee Period and the 4-years PhD Period. As part of the fellowship, ICFO will provide budget as deemed necessary and with the corresponding approval from the corresponding Group/Team Leader to enable the PhD fellow to complete his/her assigned research project. This budget is managed by the Group/Team leader, and will include consumables and other materials, training and other related costs, such as registration fees, travel and subsistence costs for participation in national or international events, conference, meetings, schools, and/or other training activities. Additionally, a family allowance is also available on request and after corresponding approval for people with family charges in the terms described in the corresponding policy. To apply , suitable candidates are requested to submit (in English) online the following material: A Cover Letter addressing research interests and motivation for application, as well as specific indication of ICFO research group of interest, A Curriculum Vitae, including contact details, Scanned copies of the complete (Bachelor and Master equivalent) official academic transcripts in English or Spanish, Scanned copies of the degree certificates, if available at the time of application, Holders of degrees issued within European Higher Education Area outside Spain shall also submit the European Diploma supplement, if available. If not submitted during the application, this will be compulsory to be submitted in further steps of the selection process. Holders of degrees issued in outside European Higher Education Area shall submit documentation that explicitly indicate equivalence of degree and/or admissibility in a PhD program in the country where it was issued. If not submitted during the application, this will be compulsory to be submitted in further steps of the selection process. Examples of documents we accept are: Official document or website from the degree granting university Academic transcript including this explicit description Letter or certificate from faculty, school or department, addressed to ICFO on official letter-head, signed by a person responsible for admissions into the PhD program If available, scanned copy of standardized test results (GRE, TOEFL, etc.). Note that submission of test results is optional, but they can be particularly helpful for evaluating candidates with degrees obtained outside the European Higher Education Area. The names and contact details of 2 referees. Extenuating circumstances (optional; 1-page max). Candidates may submit a statement regarding any career interruptions (care of dependents, birth of children, etc.) or any other aspects, which will be taken-into-account in evaluating their applications. Candidates may contact jobs@icfo.eu for formal enquiries regarding the application. Selection process All students admitted into the ICFO PhD program must pass through a selection process involving the evaluation of submitted documents, an eligibility and admissibility check and an interview with a selection committee. ICFO Selection Committees are appointed in line with the recommendations of European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers, in terms of gender balance, diversity of discipline, expertise and necessary competence for a proper evaluation and assessment of the candidates. Candidates may explain their experience, highlight their achievements, and describe their career aspirations and relevant personal or professional details. Candidates invited to the interviews receive detailed guidelines about the selection process and the interview day. At all stages of the process, candidates may contact the Talent Attraction Team via jobs@icfo.eu; for complete information about the PhD Admissions process at ICFO, please see https://www.icfo.eu/studies/phd-program/ Data Protection In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and Organic Law 3/2018, ICFO informs applicants that their personal data will be processed exclusively for recruitment purposes. indeed:a496bd394be54f45.desc: Doctoral Position in Environmental Microbiology 100%, Zurich, fixed-term The Environmental Microbiology group led by Prof. Marie Schölmerich at the Department of Environmental Systems Science, ETH Zurich, invites applications for a fully funded 4 year Doctoral Position. Our group explores the fascinating world of anaerobic microbiology from the global to the microscopic scale. This project investigates the physiology and bioenergetics of alkaliphilic methanogenic archaea. Project background The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect reliable traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress. Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website. NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups. Job description Alkaline environments such as soda lakes and serpentinising vents are candidate sites for the emergence of life on Earth and potential habitats on ocean worlds like Enceladus Methanogenic archaea are the main biological source of the greenhouse gas methane Some methanogenic archaea can thrive under alkaliphilic conditions where conventional energy conservation reaches its limits This Doctoral project seeks to investigate what limits the growth of alkaliphilic methanogens, how they conserve energy and acquire carbon at high pH, and which signatures distinguish their methane from abiotic methane The work combines anaerobic cultivation, physiology and biochemistry Profile MSc (or equivalent) in microbiology, environmental sciences or a related field Experience in anaerobic cultivation and/or protein biochemistry is an advantage Curiosity about fundamental questions and enthusiasm for experimental work and excellent communication skills in English Workplace Workplace We offer Opportunities to engage in cutting-edge research with the potential for high impact in the field of environmental microbiology Encouraging and collaborative research environment A Doctoral Position in a national, interdisciplinary network linking microbiology with geochemistry, planetary science and origin-of-life research Training in anaerobic microbiology, bioenergetics, and omics A fundamental research question with direct relevance to astrobiology and the methane cycle Support for career goals through conference travel and workshops Exciting working environment, cultural diversity and attractive offers and benefits We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values, ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future. Curious? So are we. Questions regarding the position should be directed to Prof. Marie Schölmerich, marie.schoelmerich@usys.ethz.ch (no applications). Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered. The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026. We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

linkedin:4483550632.title: PhD Position in Neuroimaging, LLM, Genetics and Cross-species comparison
linkedin:4483550632.desc: Your function Do you enjoy working with complex neuroimaging data, large datasets and computational methods? Do you want to work at the intersection of genetics, neuroimaging, neuroscience, neurodiversity and cross-species analyses? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the Connectome Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam The Connectome Lab at the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR), Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, is seeking a PhD candidate in Neuroimaging, Genetics and Cross-species comparison. The project aims to understand how variation in brain anatomy and connectivity contributes to the remarkable diversity of the human brain, and how these features relate to principles of brain evolution. We will combine large-scale human neuroimaging datasets with comparative datasets across species to investigate variation in brain structure, connectivity and functional organization. A central goal is to understand which aspects of brain organization are highly conserved, which show substantial variation between individuals, and which features may have emerged or expanded during human brain evolution. The project therefore brings together neuroimaging, connectomics, neurodiversity, comparative neuroscience and computational neuroscience . You will work with large structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets and develop and apply computational approaches to quantify variation in brain organization across individuals, populations and species. There is particularly attention for the use of LLM in data mining. You will be part of the computational neuroimaging Lab led by Prof. Martijn van den Heuvel and work in an interdisciplinary environment with researchers from neuroimaging, computational neuroscience, genetics, psychology, psychiatry and artificial intelligence. Your duties analyse large-scale structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets develop and apply pipelines for cortical reconstruction, tractography, functional connectivity and connectome analysis investigate individual variation and neurodiversity in brain structure and connectivity integrate genetics with neuroimaging perform comparative analyses of human and non-human brain organization in the context of brain evolution integrate findings across different neuroimaging datasets and imaging modalities develop and apply computational and statistical approaches for analysing brain networks contribute to reproducible and open neuroimaging workflows collaborate with researchers within the Connectome Lab, CNCR and international research networks present your findings at national and international scientific meetings write scientific manuscripts contribute to teaching activities where appropriate Your profile MSc degree in neuroscience, neuroimaging, genetics, biomedical engineering, physics, computer science, artificial intelligence, mathematics, psychology, biology, or a related quantitative discipline. Hands-on experience with computational analysis is important. Ideally, you have experience with several of the following: structural MRI and cortical reconstruction, including FreeSurfer Genetics (GWAS) diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI), tractography and structural connectivity resting-state fMRI and functional connectivity analysis FSL and other commonly used neuroimaging software packages Experience with AI / LLM processing and quality control of neuroimaging datasets connectome and network neuroscience analyses Strong interest in and experience with scientific programming is essential. You should have experience with Python, MATLAB, R, Bash and/or comparable languages , and be comfortable working with computational analysis pipelines. Experience with one or more of the following would be an advantage: large-scale neuroimaging datasets such as UK Biobank, HCP or comparable resources comparative or cross-species neuroimaging brain atlases, surface-based analysis and registration machine learning or multivariate statistics high-performance computing version control and reproducible research workflows network science and computational modelling We are particularly interested in candidates who enjoy working with complex data, think critically about methodology, and are motivated to develop strong computational and neuroimaging expertise. You should also: have a strong interest in neurodiversity and/or evolution be able to work independently while enjoying collaboration within a multidisciplinary team have good analytical and problem-solving skills have a good command of written and spoken English be motivated to learn new neuroimaging and computational techniques support open and reproducible science and be willing to share tools and data with the wider scientific community As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. So in return for your efforts, we offer you: a salary of minimum € 3.204,00 (PhD year 1) and maximum € 4.051 (PhD year 4) gross per month, on a full-time basis. Our research focuses on understanding the architecture of the human brain and how its network organization relates to cognition, individual variation, brain disorders and evolution. You will work in a multidisciplinary team of PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers and students with backgrounds spanning neuroimaging, network neuroscience, genetics, artificial intelligence, computational neuroscience and psychology. The project is embedded within the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR) , providing a highly interdisciplinary research environment and opportunities for collaboration within VU Amsterdam and with national and international research groups. Faculty of Science Working at the Faculty of Science means collaborating with students, lecturers and researchers who are focused on their field, yet have a broad view of the world. linkedin:4482949202.title: Doctoral researcher in computational genomics for predictive medicine
linkedin:4482949202.desc: The Barrett lab at the University of Helsinki is recruiting a doctoral researcher (PhD student) in computational genomics for predictive medicine. We are jointly affiliated with the ELLIS Institute Finland , the Institute for Molecular Medicine Finland (FIMM) , and the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Helsinki. We analyze multiomic data to discover, understand, and measure mechanistically meaningful subtypes of complex human diseases. We believe that characterizing diseases not by their observed clinical phenotype, but by their molecular and biological endotype, will enable better treatment for patients. This long-held ambition in biomedicine is now poised to be realized due to: National research biobanks that collectively include millions of individuals with matched biosamples and detailed electronic health records. Large and growing multiomic data sets in samples from these biobanks, including genomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and transcriptomics. New machine learning and AI methods to build multiomic models that stratify disease risk, progression, and treatment response by molecular endotypes. Find examples of research areas and possible projects on our website. Responsibilities Design and implement a PhD research project on a topic related to computational genomics for predictive medicine. Carry out the research project: propose hypotheses, write code, think about and discuss results, and interpret findings. Collaborate closely with other members of the team, other researchers at the ELLIS Institute and University of Helsinki, and international partners. Share scientific results via publications and presentations at local and international conferences, and contribute more broadly to open science (e.g. via pre-prints and open source software). Contribute to mentoring and training the next generation of scientists. Qualifications, Experience, And Skills These items are most important for this role. We expect candidates to fulfill most of these: Motivation to work collaboratively on hard scientific problems with a pragmatic focus on getting things done. Master’s degree in computational biology, data science, bioinformatics, or a related discipline (exceptional candidates may be considered coming straight from a bachelor’s). Proficiency in programming for data analysis in either Python or R. Research experience in computational biology and/or data science. Excellent written and spoken English. Any of the following are nice experience to have, but not essential. Please don’t be put off if you don’t have these: Working in high-performance or cloud compute environments. Working on machine learning problems (e.g. with frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow). Research with health care and/or genomics data. Developing software in a small team environment with code review and version control. Using agentic AI tools (e.g. from Anthropic and OpenAI) while still retaining your own thinking process (see here for more about how we use AI). What We Offer This is an opportunity to be one of the first members of a newly established laboratory led by Professor Jeffrey Barrett, who has over 20 years’ experience leading genomics research teams. You will benefit from hands-on supervision from Professor Barrett as well as active participation in the intellectual environments at both FIMM (genomics and molecular medicine) and the ELLIS Institute (fundamentals of applied AI). Our team has access to biobank data sets which cumulatively include 2 million individuals (FinnGen, UK Biobank, All of Us, Estonian Biobank). We have access to both local supercomputer facilities as well as extensive cloud computing resources. We also routinely generate new ’omics data in samples available from the Finnish biobank network. The position is for a fixed term, with a maximum duration of four years. A trial period of six months will be applied. The salary is based on the salary system of the Finnish universities . The starting salary is typically around 2600-2850 EUR per month, depending on the appointees’ qualifications and experience, and rises gradually as the PhD work progresses. The University of Helsinki offers comprehensive services to its employees, including occupational health care, support in access to high quality sports facilities, and many opportunities for professional development. Standard Finnish pension benefits are provided for university employees. How To Apply Please submit your application through the University of Helsinki recruitment system by November 19 , 2026. Your application should include: A one-page cover letter describing why you’re interested in this role. Please don’t use AI for this! It’s important to explain in your own voice. CV, including publications and github link if applicable Contact information for two references For more information regarding the position or the research goals of the group, please contact Jeff at jeffrey.c.barrett(at)helsinki.fi. More information A diverse and equitable study and work culture is important to us. That is why we do our best to promote an inclusive university community. We encourage all qualified applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply for our positions. Click this link to read about accessibility and inclusivity at our University. JOIN US TO BUILD A BETTER WORLD – TOGETHER! #HelsinkiUniCareers The Institute for Molecular Medicine Finland (FIMM) is an international research unit focusing on human genomics and personalized medicine at the Helsinki Institute of Life Science (HiLIFE) of the University of Helsinki - a leading Nordic university with a strong commitment to life science research. As part of Academic Medical Center Helsinki in Meilahti campus FIMM collaborates locally with the Faculty of Medicine, Helsinki University Hospital and National Institute for Health and Welfare. FIMM is part of the Nordic EMBL Partnership for Molecular Medicine, composed of the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL) and the centres for molecular medicine in Norway, Sweden and Denmark, and the EU-LIFE Community. ELLIS (European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems) is a major European initiative in AI with a mission to strengthen Europe’s AI landscape by connecting top researchers, attracting talent, and fostering strategic collaborations. ELLIS unites leading machine learning researchers in Europe and operates as a multi-centric, pan-European AI Lab, currently spanning 47 research sites. ELLIS Institute Finland was launched in 2025 and is the second institute in the ELLIS network , partnering with Finnish universities. We develop machine learning through fundamental research, with a particular focus on the fundamentals of applied AI: making machine learning more widely and effectively applicable, and better at working with people. AI for Research is one part of this focus. Our faculty works across a broad range of areas, including data-efficient probabilistic machine learning, generative modelling, amortized inference, interactive and cooperative machine learning, and transformative multidisciplinary collaboration. The institute will have a small number of strategic focus areas and the first one is AI for Health, spearheaded by a project to build a nationwide foundation model to support better decision-making in healthcare.

linkedin:4477194495.title: PhD position 6G-Native Distributed Intelligence for Physical AI
linkedin:4477194495.desc: Join the Dutch 6G flagship project to help shape the future of communications. Job Description Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge. How can 6G enable resource-constrained Physical AI by dynamically distributing and adapting AI workloads across embedded devices, the edge, and the cloud, while jointly orchestrating communication, computation, and sensing under strict latency, reliability, and resource constraints? The project will investigate resource-aware 6G-native distributed AI techniques such as collaborative and split inference, adaptive model partitioning and selection, computation offloading, and cross-layer resource orchestration. A particular focus will be on how 6G can enable Physical AI systems to adapt to changing network, compute, sensor, and energy conditions while maintaining predictable performance. You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. Fostering a highly collaborative and friendly atmosphere, we will give you all the support you need to develop and grow. Moreover, as a valued member of the FNS consortium, you can collaborate with various partners in pursuit of integrating your AI/ML techniques into the various 6G PoCs and demos. Job requerements Become part of an expansive ecosystem shaping the development of 6G. You will benefit from training in 5G and beyond networks, AI, and software development. Plus, you will gain exclusive access to (1) a state-of-the-art testbed where theory meets real-world application, and (2) an ecosystem that cultivates entrepreneurial endeavours. Are you ready to challenge yourself? We're seeking candidates who have, or are about to receive, a Master-of-Science degree in a relevant computer science discipline and who like to combine theory with practice. Proficiency in English is essential, as you'll collaborate within a diverse, international community. For more details on our admission requirements, please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/opleidingen/phd/admission. We’ll evaluate based on your academic record, interviews, and possibly assignments. While a strong background in the field is crucial, what matters as well is your creative flair, motivation, and above all, your passion for comprehensive research! TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context. Join TU Delft as a PhD researcher using Bayesian and counterfactual modelling to predict nanoparticle transport in human tissue. Job Description We are looking for a PhD candidate to build the computational model at the center of a European project on nanoparticle transport in human tissue. You will join the research group of Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, working within the SYNERGIE project (Horizon Europe), a consortium of thirteen partners including Fraunhofer, Roche, the Karolinska Institute, University Hospital Aachen, Mimetas, Ruhr University Bochum and Maastricht University. Small particles from the environment have been detected in human blood, placenta and brain tissue, but it is still not clear what they do there. Dose-response data for humans does not exist and animal studies have not transferred well, and as a result there is no exposure limit for these particles. Part of the reason prediction is so hard is that a particle changes as it moves through the body. It acquires a layer of proteins, it aggregates with other particles, and depending on the material it may partly degrade, so that the particle reaching a given tissue is not the same object that was administered or characterised at the start. Most transport models do not account for this. They treat the particle as fixed, which means they are predicting the fate of something that has already changed. The same difficulty affects engineered nanoparticles for drug delivery, and it is one of the reasons so few of them reach their intended target. SYNERGIE is building a platform of nine human tissue-on-chip models that can be connected to follow a particle through uptake, circulation and storage. TU Delft leads the in silico work package. As a PhD candidate, you will: Build a mechanistic model of how particles move between nine human tissues, and calibrate it against experimental data using Bayesian inference. Work out which physical and chemical properties of a particle decide where it ends up. Develop methods that go beyond prediction: for a particle that behaves badly, what is the smallest change that would fix it, and when should that answer not be trusted. Release the model as open-source software and support its use in regulatory dialogue. You will also contribute to teaching in the department and to the supervision of BSc projects. You will work alongside a postdoctoral researcher and PhD candidates on related problems, and interact with experimental partners across the SYNERGIE consortium. You will have access to the DelftBlue high-performance computing cluster. The intended start date is January 2027. The diverse research topics rely on extensive numerical models and a broad range of experimental equipment for noise and vibration measurements. The research will combine mechanical modelling, finite-element simulations, prototype development, and experimental testing. linkedin:4481466420.title: PhD In-flight aeroelastic measurements & modelling for scaled experimental a/c (m/v/x)
linkedin:4481466420.desc: Functieomschrijving Join a cutting-edge PhD in experimental flight testing and advanced optical measurement technology to help shape the future of sustainable flight! Background Recently, the use of scaled flight testing has received interest at NLR and multiple other research institutions in Europe to fill the gap between ground testing and full-scale flight testing. Scaled flight tests of radically new aircraft concepts can provide early stage validation data of flight dynamics and complex interdisciplinary topics such as aero(servo)elasticity . Because these topics are very challenging to address in ground testing, validation data would typically only be obtained at the later stages of a design processes when large prototypes are flown. Insights into these topics stemming from scaled flight tests at earlier design stages can be critical enablers to accelerate innovation in aerospace. Currently, a gap exists between the highly sophisticated measurement instruments focused on producing a maximal amount of information that are used in ground testing and the specialized equipment with a focus on reliability and accuracy in difficult measurement circumstances that has been developed for large-scale flight testing. Previous projects that were focused on advanced in-flight measurement techniques have made large steps towards making modern measurement instruments, often optical and/or laser-based measurement techniques, applicable in-flight. However, existing research work focused on large-scale industrial flight testing. The recent interest on the topic of scaled flight testing results in a need to develop advanced measurement techniques specifically for smaller scale experimental flight testing. This type application is of high interest for advanced measurement techniques because the uncertainties are larger than in industrial testing, creating a more urgent need for more comprehensive and detailed measurement data. Furthermore, understanding the possibilities and limitations of scaled flight testing for aeroelastic phenomena and the application of digital twins can improve the value of the results. Project Description Ultra-high aspect ratio wings, with or without truss, are often featured on novel aircraft configurations for future sustainable aircraft. Such wings exhibit different structural characteristics than wings on current aircraft types. The differences become even more pronounced when the fuel source is switched to hydrogen because the hydrogen fuel tanks cannot be carried in the wing. This means that the development of such new wings will have considerable consequences for the entire aircraft design, resulting in novel configurations. Novel configurations are also envisioned for other aircraft concept ideas, such as wings carrying batteries, distributed propulsion on wings, etc. Addressing the design challenges of these novel aircraft designs can be supported by scaled flight testing. Among the tests performed with such scaled experimental aircraft, the complex topic of aeroservoelasticity at the intersection of aerodynamics, flight dynamics, structural dynamics and control, stands out as highly relevant and challenging. It requires efficient and robust measurement techniques applied in flight and a detailed understanding of the validity of results for characterizing the multi-disciplinary problems addressed, such as aeroelastic aircraft state estimation, gust sensing, and load alleviation, where state-of-the art pointwise measurements encounter limitations that could be overcome by global optical measurement techniques. Optical measurement techniques promise to improve in-flight capabilities significantly but require further maturation in the relevant test environment, which is targeted in this PhD project. Furthermore, the assessment of the scaling possibilities and limitations is supported with a simulation environment in which digital twins of the scaled and full-scale aircraft provide substantiation of accuracies and validity of results. The maturation is achieved in a combination of ground tests (e.g. the wind tunnel) for developing and refining the envisioned measurement approach and flight testing (e.g. the Diana 2 scaled glider platform) for validating its performance. Your profile Master’s degree in aerospace engineering or an equivalent study; Hands-on experience with complex measurement technology; Experience or affinity with (experimental) flight testing; Strong background in programming, using MATLAB and/or Python or other relevant programming languages; Collaborative and self-directed, and receptive to constructive feedback; Good communication skills for spoken and written English. Knowledge of Dutch is desirable but not mandatory; Ability to learn independently and passion for research. What we offer you You will receive a 4-year research contract from NLR Amsterdam and will join the Flight Test and Certification department. In addition, you will be enrolled in the Doctoral Education programme of the Graduate School at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), i.e. an excellent team of supervisors and academic staff. At the start of your assignment your working week will ideally be divided into: 4 days in Amsterdam, 1 days in Delft. In Addition To All This, We Offer No fewer than 45 days off (with full-time employment) so that you can also fully enjoy your free time in addition to your challenging job; A fixed end-of-year bonus of 8%; A contribution towards your healthcare costs; Extra paid parental leave; The possibility to work from home. Working at NLR? Royal NLR has been a knowledge organization with the will and ambition to innovate for over 100 years. Based on that motivation, we make the world of aviation and space travel safer, more sustainable, more efficient and effective and stand for groundbreaking innovations. We employ more than 1000 passionate professionals, from aircraft engineers to psychologists and from mathematicians to application experts. NLR stands for an inclusive and diverse organization where everyone feels welcome, safe, valued and respected. Would you like to know more? linkedin:4483531128.title: Doktorand i numerisk simulering av turbulent värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor
linkedin:4483531128.desc: Om arbetsplatsen Doktoranden kommer att vara anställd vid Institutionen för Energivetenskaper vid Lunds tekniska högskola (LTH), Lunds universitet, och tillhöra avdelningen för värmeöverföring. Forskningsmiljön bedriver forskning inom strömningsmekanik, värmeöverföring och beräkningsströmningsmekanik, med särskilt fokus på numerisk modellering och simulering av turbulenta strömmar och tekniska tillämpningar. Doktoranden kommer att arbeta i en forskningsmiljö som förenar grundforskning med tillämpningar av direkt relevans för industrin. Projektet genomförs i nära samarbete med Siemens Energy AB, Ericsson AB, TRATON AB och RISE. Det ger möjlighet att arbeta i gränslandet mellan grundforskning, avancerade numeriska metoder och industriellt relevanta problem. Doktoranden får tillgång till expertis inom beräkningsströmningsmekanik (CFD), turbulens, värmeöverföring, numeriska metoder och högprestandaberäkningar. Arbetet innebär omfattande användning av högprestandaberäkningsresurser, både GPU- och CPU-baserade. Att vara doktorand Som doktorand är du både antagen som student och anställd vid Lunds universitet. Som doktorand får du vetenskaplig skolning. Du tränas i att tänka kritiskt och analytiskt, lösa problem självständigt med lämpliga metoder och utveckla en medvetenhet om forskningsetik. Du får också möjlighet att arbeta i projekt och utveckla ditt ledarskap och din pedagogiska förmåga. Under hela utbildningen får du handledning. Doktorandutbildningen avslutas med en avhandling och doktorsexamen. Ämnes- och projektbeskrivning Ytråhet påverkar turbulent strömning, väggfriktion och värmeöverföring i många tekniska system. Det är viktigt att förstå och kunna förutsäga dessa effekter inom en rad tillämpningar, bland annat energisystem, termisk hantering och transporter. Trots den praktiska betydelsen är det fortfarande en utmaning att förutsäga turbulent värmeöverföring över realistiska skrovliga ytor med god noggrannhet, särskilt när arbetsmediets egenskaper och de relativa tjocklekarna hos impuls- och värmegränsskikten varierar. Målet med doktorandprojektet är att fördjupa den fysikaliska förståelsen av samspelet mellan ytråhet, turbulens och värmeöverföring samt omsätta förståelsen i förbättrade tekniska modeller. Forskningen kommer främst att använda högupplösta numeriska simuleringar, däribland direkt numerisk simulering (DNS) och storvirvelsimulering (LES). Olika CFD-program kommer att användas beroende på problem och önskad noggrannhet, bland annat OpenFOAM, CaNS och nekRS. Simuleringarna kommer i stor utsträckning att använda moderna högprestandaberäkningsresurser med både GPU:er och CPU:er. Projektet undersöker hur ytråhet påverkar turbulent strömning och värmeöverföring för olika fluider och termiska förhållanden. Särskild uppmärksamhet ägnas åt samspelet mellan råhetsgeometri, turbulenta strukturer samt impuls- och värmegränsskikt, även när de termiska gränsskiktens och impulsgränsskiktens relativa tjocklek skiljer sig åt. Data från de högupplösta simuleringarna ska användas för att identifiera relevanta fysikaliska mekanismer och skalningssamband samt stödja utvecklingen av reducerade modeller och tekniska modeller för värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor. Det omfattar förbättrade modeller och korrelationer som lämpar sig för Reynoldsmedelvärdesbaserade Navier–Stokes-simuleringar (RANS). Det övergripande målet är att knyta samman grundläggande turbulensfysik, högupplösta numeriska simuleringar och beräkningsmodeller som kan användas vid teknisk konstruktion. Projektet genomförs i nära samarbete med Siemens Energy AB, Ericsson AB, TRATON AB och RISE. Samarbetet ger möjligheter till vetenskapligt utbyte och kontakt med forskare och ingenjörer som arbetar med industriella tillämpningar av turbulent strömning och värmeöverföring. Arbetsuppgifter Du ägnar huvuddelen av din arbetstid åt forskarutbildningen, som omfattar deltagande i forskningsprojekt samt forskarutbildningskurser, seminarier och vetenskapliga konferenser. En central del av arbetet är att genomföra och analysera högupplösta numeriska simuleringar av turbulent strömning och värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor. Du använder CFD- och högprestandaberäkningsramverk, exempelvis OpenFOAM, CaNS och nekRS, på CPU- och GPU-baserade system. Du ska ha erfarenhet av jämförbara simuleringsverktyg och högprestandaberäkningssystem (HPC); erfarenhet av de specifika program som används i projektet är meriterande. Arbetsuppgifterna omfattar Genomföra DNS- och LES-simuleringar av turbulent strömning och värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor med OpenFOAM, CaNS, nekRS eller jämförbara ramverk för CFD och vetenskapliga beräkningar. Förbereda, köra, validera och analysera simuleringar på GPU- och CPU-baserade högprestandaberäkningssystem. Undersöka hur ytråhetens geometri och egenskaper påverkar turbulent impuls- och värmeöverföring. Undersöka effekterna av fluidernas egenskaper och termiska förhållanden, inklusive olika förhållanden mellan impuls- och värmegränsskiktens tjocklek. Bearbeta, analysera och visualisera stora datamängder, identifiera fysikaliska mekanismer och ta fram skalningssamband utifrån DNS- och LES-data. Utveckla reducerade modeller, korrelationer och förbättrade RANS-modeller för turbulent värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor. Bedöma och validera de utvecklade modellerna mot högupplösta numeriska data och, när sådana finns, experimentella data. Samarbeta med forskare vid Lunds universitet och med projektets industri- och forskningspartner. Presentera forskningsresultat vid projektmöten, vetenskapliga konferenser och internationella workshoppar. Skriva vetenskapliga artiklar för publicering i internationella sakkunniggranskade tidskrifter och bidra till doktorsavhandlingen. Arbetet kan innebära resor inom Sverige och internationellt för projektmöten, besök hos forsknings- och industripartner, konferenser och forskningssamarbeten. Arbetsuppgifterna kan även omfatta undervisning och annat institutionsarbete, dock högst 20% av arbetstiden. Behörighetskrav En sökande uppfyller de allmänna behörighetskraven till utbildning på forskarnivå om personen: har avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller på något annat sätt, i Sverige eller utomlands, har förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. Särskilda krav För att kunna genomföra den aktuella forskarutbildningen krävs även följande: Masterexamen eller motsvarande inom maskinteknik, teknisk fysik, flygteknik, energiteknik, tillämpad matematik, beräkningsvetenskap eller ett annat ämne som är relevant för projektet. Goda kunskaper i strömningsmekanik, CFD och turbulenta strömmar samt relevanta kunskaper i värmeöverföring. Ett omfattande forskningsprojekt eller examensarbete inom CFD, turbulens, värmeöverföring eller ett närliggande område. Dokumenterad förmåga att självständigt sätta upp, genomföra, felsöka, validera och analysera numeriska simuleringar. Förmågan ska styrkas genom forskningserfarenhet och inte enbart genom kursarbete. Erfarenhet av vetenskaplig programmering i ett relevant språk, till exempel C/C++, Fortran och Python eller Matlab. Praktisk erfarenhet av att köra beräkningssimuleringar på HPC-system. Förmåga att planera och genomföra forskningsuppgifter med begränsad löpande handledning, kritiskt analysera resultat och tydligt kommunicera slutsatser. Mycket goda kunskaper i engelska, både i tal och skrift. Meriterande kvalifikationer Följande kvalifikationer är meriterande för den aktuella forskarutbildningen: Erfarenhet av DNS eller LES, väggbegränsad turbulens, turbulent värmeöverföring, ytråhet eller konvektiv värmeöverföring. Erfarenhet av CFD eller ett ramverk för högupplösta simuleringar, till exempel OpenFOAM, CaNS, nekRS eller motsvarande forskningskod. Erfarenhet av parallellberäkningar eller GPU-accelererade vetenskapliga beräkningar. Kunskaper i RANS, väggmodellering eller termisk turbulensmodellering. Forskningserfarenhet utöver masterexamensarbetet, till exempel som forskningsassistent eller forskningsingenjör. Erfarenhet av att presentera eller publicera forskningsresultat eller av att samarbeta med industrin. Du behöver inte ha erfarenhet av alla program som används i projektet. Däremot ska du ha visat att du självständigt kan bedriva beräkningsforskning med ett jämförbart ramverk för CFD eller vetenskapliga beräkningar. Du förväntas kunna bidra från ett tidigt skede med stöd av tidigare erfarenhet av numeriska simuleringar och HPC. Vi erbjuder Lunds universitet är en statlig myndighet. Som anställd får du särskilda förmåner, generös semester och fördelaktiga tjänstepensionsvillkor. Läs mer om att arbeta på Lunds universitet. Anställningsvillkor Anställningen är en tidsbegränsad heltidsanställning med start så snart som möjligt. Forskarutbildningen vid LTH omfattar fyra års heltidsstudier. Om du har undervisning eller andra arbetsuppgifter vid institutionen förlängs anställningen i motsvarande omfattning. Doktorandanställningar regleras i högskoleförordningen (1993:100), 5 kap. 1–7 . Läs mer om att vara anställd som doktorand på Lunds universitet. Övrigt Doktoranden förväntas ha regelbunden kontakt med projektets akademiska partner och industripartner. Tjänsten kan därför omfatta besök hos partnerorganisationer och deltagande i projektmöten, workshoppar och konferenser i Sverige och utomlands. Ansökan Ansökan ska vara skriven på engelska och innehålla: CV och personligt brev där du beskriver varför du söker forskarutbildningen och det aktuella forskningsprojektet samt hur din utbildningsbakgrund, forskningserfarenhet och dina intressen anknyter till CFD, turbulens och värmeöverföring. Kopior av utfärdade studieintyg och/eller examensbevis. Handlingarna ska styrka att du uppfyller de allmänna och särskilda behörighetskraven till forskarutbildningen och har de ämneskunskaper som krävs för doktorandprojektet. Studieutdrag med genomförda kurser och betyg. En kopia av masterexamensarbetet eller, om arbetet inte är färdigt, en sammanfattning av det pågående arbetet och beräknat datum för färdigställande. Övriga handlingar som du vill åberopa, till exempel vetenskapliga publikationer, tekniska rapporter, konferensbidrag, rekommendationsbrev eller annat material som visar relevant forskningserfarenhet. Kontaktuppgifter till minst två referenspersoner som kan kontaktas under rekryteringsprocessen. Välkommen med din ansökan.

linkedin:4483713875.title: CIFRE - Panel Level Package (PLP) development : interfaces characterization - H/F
linkedin:4483713875.desc: Chez STMicroelectronics, nous sommes convaincus que la technologie est un moteur d’innovation et a un impact positif pour les entreprises, les personnes et la société. En tant qu’acteur mondial des semiconducteurs, nos technologies de pointe et nos composants électroniques sont invisibles mais au cœur du monde d’aujourd’hui. Rejoindre ST, c’est intégrer une entreprise internationale riche de plus de 115 nationalités, présente dans 40 pays, et rassemblant plus de 50 000 talents passionnés et engagés, tous unis par la volonté de créer et d’inventer la technologie de demain. Innover demande bien plus que des compétences techniques : cela nécessite des personnes inspirantes, qui savent collaborer avec respect et enthousiasme. Des collaborateurs animés par la passion, prêts à remettre en question le statu quo, à faire avancer l’innovation et à révéler leur plein potentiel. Venez vivre cette aventure avec nous et contribuez à construire un futur plus intelligent et plus durable, en alliant responsabilité et innovation. Notre technologie commence avec vous. A propos de vos missions En microélectronique, la technologie Panel-Level Packaging (PLP) repose sur la réalisation d'empilements complexes associant différentes couches fonctionnelles, notamment organiques, métalliques et d'encapsulation. La fiabilité de ces architectures dépend non seulement des propriétés de chaque matériau, mais également de la qualité des interfaces qui les séparent. Celle-ci dépend des choix réalisés lors de la fabrication : température de dépôt, préparation de surface, rugosité des couches, utilisation de promoteurs d’adhérence… Néanmoins, à ce jour, les mécanismes physiques et mécaniques à l'origine de l'adhérence entre ces matériaux restent à préciser, tout comme leur évolution sous sollicitation mécanique ou thermomécanique. De fait, des défauts d'interface, une adhérence insuffisante ou l'apparition de contraintes locales sont autant de paramètres pouvant favoriser l'amorçage et la propagation de délaminations, susceptibles de compromettre l'intégrité de l'empilement. Une meilleure compréhension des relations entre les caractéristiques des interfaces, les propriétés mécaniques des couches et les mécanismes d'endommagement apparaît donc essentielle pour fiabiliser les procédés et orienter la conception des empilements. Cette thèse vise à développer une approche expérimentale et numérique permettant de caractériser les interfaces des empilements PLP, de comprendre leur comportement mécanique et d'identifier les paramètres gouvernant leur tenue et leur endommagement. Il s'agira notamment de dépasser la seule mesure de l'adhérence pour étudier le rôle de la morphologie des interfaces, des propriétés mécaniques locales et des mécanismes de déformation et de rupture dans la réponse globale de l'empilement. Une première partie portera sur la caractérisation des interfaces et de leur état initial, notamment par tomographie aux rayons X, Microscopie Électronique à Balayage (MEB) et, lorsque cela sera pertinent, microscopie à force atomique (AFM). Une attention particulière sera accordée à la morphologie des interfaces, à la présence de défauts et à l'influence des traitements de surface. Une seconde partie sera consacrée au développement et à l'adaptation d'essais mécaniques permettant de solliciter spécifiquement les interfaces. Parmi les essais envisagés, les essais DBC (Double Cantilever Beam) et les essais de flexion 4 points sur éprouvette entaillée semblent être particulièrement adaptés. Le couplage des sollicitations mécaniques à des observations in situ sous MEB ou tomographe permettra de relier les réponses mécaniques mesurées aux mécanismes d'endommagement observés. Une approche multi-échelle sera développée afin de relier les propriétés mécaniques des constituants au comportement des interfaces. L'indentation instrumentée pourra être utilisée pour caractériser localement les propriétés mécaniques des couches, en tenant compte des effets de l'épaisseur, du substrat et de la proximité des interfaces. Grâce à cette technique il est également envisagé d’estimer l’adhérence et la résistance à la délamination par la technique d’indentation par supercouche (superlayer indentation technique). Enfin, la confrontation des caractérisations structurales et des essais mécaniques permettra d'établir des relations entre les paramètres de procédé, l'état initial des interfaces, les modes de rupture et la résistance à la délamination. Les résultats attendus contribueront à établir une méthodologie expérimentale de caractérisation de la tenue des interfaces et à proposer des critères permettant d'orienter le choix des traitements de surface et des architectures multicouches. Ce sujet de thèse est le fruit d’une collaboration entre le laboratoire de mécanique Gabriel Lamé et STMicroelectronics et pourra bénéficier des outils expérimentaux et des compétences de deux plateformes de l’Université de Tours : le CERMEL et le CERTeM. A propos de vous Bac +5 en Physique/Matériaux / chimie, connaissance des procédés de la microélectronique, connaissance en physique des semi-conducteurs, rigueur scientifique, autonomie, persévérance. ST est fière d’être certifiée parmi les 17 entreprises mondiales « Global Top Employers 2025 » et d’être la première et unique entreprise de semi-conducteurs à recevoir cette distinction. ST a été distinguée dans ce classement grâce à sa démarche d’amélioration continue, se démarquant notamment par son engagement en matière d’éthique et d’intégrité, de sens et de valeurs, d’organisation et de gestion du changement, ainsi que par sa stratégie commerciale et ses performances. En France, ST a également obtenu la labélisation Happy Trainee 2025. Nous cultivons un environnement de travail inclusif et diversifié, où la discrimination n’a pas sa place. Notre ambition est de recruter et de fidéliser des talents reflétant la richesse des sociétés dans lesquelles nous évoluons. Nous nous engageons à l’équité dans le développement des carrières, les opportunités professionnelles et la rémunération. Chez ST, nous encourageons les candidats qui ne remplissent pas forcément tous les critères à postuler, car nous croyons en la richesse des parcours variés et offrons de réelles opportunités d’apprentissage et d’évolution. La diversité, l’équité et l’inclusion sont des valeurs fondamentales qui façonnent notre culture d’entreprise. Pour découvrir toutes nos opportunités, rendez-vous sur st.com/careers.
