L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Physique des lasers, atomes et molécules Type de Contrat CDD Doctorant Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 59658 VILLENEUVE D ASCQ Durée du contrat 36 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration La rémunération est d'un minimum de 2300,00 € mensuel Postuler Date limite de candidature : lundi 16 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Sujet De Thèse Sonde micro-endoscopique pour l’histologie Raman stimulée Votre Environnement de Travail Les techniques d'endoscopie sont essentielles pour le diagnostic, la stadification et le traitement des cancers épithéliaux. Pour de nombreux cancers, elles sont souvent le seul moyen d'accéder directement au site tumoral. Cependant, les tissus précancéreux présentent parfois des modifications subtiles indétectables visuellement. La détection endoscopique du cancer souffre de deux principales faiblesses : (1) la sensibilité limitée des marqueurs fluorescents couramment utilisés et (2) le besoin de biopsies et d'analyses histologiques, qui retardent la chirurgie et la prise de décisions. Le projet de thèse vise à développer une sonde optique miniature pour l'histologie Raman stimulée capable de fournir des images tissulaires en temps réel, en concordance étroite avec l'histologie classique (coloration H&E). Cette approche ambitionne de permettre une détection précoce et moins invasive des cancers gastro-entérologiques, ainsi que d'explorer son potentiel pour la détection des cancers urologiques et l'évaluation peropératoire des marges tumorales. Nous proposons une approche novatrice combinant la microscopie Raman stimulée (SRS), des fibres à cœur creux de dernière génération et avec les technologies les plus avancées d'assemblage de sondes miniatures micro-endoscopiques fibrées. L'objectif est de développer une sonde endoscopique SRS permettant de réaliser une histologie Raman stimulée en temps réel. Les développements viseront des applications en cancers gastro-entérologiques et urologiques, avec une validation sur des tissus biologiques pertinents en lien avec des partenaires cliniciens. La thèse se déroulera au laboratoire PhLAM de l'Université de Lille, sous la direction d'Alexandre Kudlinski, en étroite collaboration avec Hervé Rigneault (Institut Fresnel, Aix-Marseille Université) et la société Lightcore Technologies (basée à Lille et Marseille). Le sujet de thèse est à forte dominante expérimentale dans le domaine de l’optique, des fibres optiques et des lasers ultra-brefs. Des compétences en pilotage d’instruments, en électronique, en conception optique (notamment avec des logiciels tels que Zemax) et en traitement d’images seront appréciées. Le candidat devra manifester un réel intérêt pour l’optique expérimentale, faire preuve d’autonomie, d’initiative et d’une bonne capacité à résoudre des problèmes pratiques. linkedin:4481422565.desc: PhD position (m/w/d) on the Natural ecology and evolution of C. elegans at Kiel University, Germany Well-motivated and highly-qualified students from all countries are welcome to apply. We are looking forward to your application for a PhD position to join the Schulenburg group in Kiel in the beautiful landscape of Northern Germany. Application deadline: 4 November 2026 . The PhD position is for 3,5 years with a possible extension for another 6 months. It is based in the Schulenburg group (https://evoecogen-kiel.de/). The PhD project aims at understanding how the model nematode C. elegans interacts with other organisms in its natural environment, ranging from the interaction with microbes up to predators and parasites. C. elegans is one of the best studied model organisms in the life sciences, yet there is still very little understanding of its natural ecology, and especially the interaction with other organisms, even though this natural context sets the stage for full appreciation of the nematode’s gene functions. Based on the observation of such interactions in nature, the project will then further study selected interaction types in the lab, taking advantage of the tools available for this model organism, thereby allowing us to generate new insights on the evolution as well as the genetic basis of ecologically relevant biotic interactions. The position will be integrated within the graduate school on Translational Evolutionary Research (https://transevo.de/), providing numerous opportunities for exchange with colleagues working on related topics. indeed:e60873546e9c68c2.title: Thèse CIFRE: Réduction de modèle par deep learning pour la plasticité cristalline F/H
indeed:e60873546e9c68c2.desc: Mise en ligne le 2026-10-27 Type de contrat : Thèse Niveau de formation : BAC +8 Expérience : Débutant Spécialité(s) : Ingénierie / Expertise / Recherche Pays / Région : France / Ile-de-France Département : Seine et Marne (77) Ville : Moret-sur-Loing Description de l'offre EDF R&D, avec ses 2000 chercheurs, a pour missions principales de contribuer à l'amélioration de la performance des unités opérationnelles du groupe EDF, d'identifier et de préparer les relais de croissance à moyen et long termes. EDF R&D met en œuvre une politique volontariste de partenariat en France et à l’international notamment dans les pays où le Groupe est présent. Vous souhaitez associer mécanique des matériaux, simulation numérique et intelligence artificielle pour répondre à des enjeux industriels ? -> Rejoignez EDF Recherche et Développement dans le cadre d’une thèse CIFRE consacrée à la réduction de modèle par apprentissage profond pour les calculs en plasticité cristalline. La poursuite de l’exploitation des centrales nucléaires au-delà de 60 ans nécessite des outils avancés pour justifier la tenue mécanique des composants. Pour les matériaux métalliques, leur comportement dépend notamment de la microstructure, c’est-à-dire de l’organisation des grains qui les constituent. Les simulations en plasticité cristalline permettent de représenter ces grains et leurs interactions pour mieux comprendre les déformations et les mécanismes de rupture. Elles restent toutefois coûteuses en temps de calcul, ce qui limite l’étude de microstructures et de sollicitations variées. L’objectif de cette thèse est de développer des modèles réduits fondés sur l’apprentissage profond pour accélérer ces simulations, tout en conservant une précision adaptée aux grandeurs étudiées et en respectant les lois physiques. Vos principales missions seront les suivantes : Étudier les méthodes de réduction de modèle et d’apprentissage profond adaptées à la plasticité cristalline. Constituer et exploiter des jeux de données issus de simulations de référence, couvrant différentes microstructures, propriétés des matériaux et sollicitations mécaniques. Développer des modèles capables de prédire les grandeurs mécaniques recherchées, en intégrant des contraintes physiques pour améliorer leur fiabilité. Comparer les approches en matière de précision, de coût de calcul et de capacité à traiter des configurations non utilisées pendant l’apprentissage. Appliquer les méthodes à des cas représentatifs des besoins industriels et valoriser les résultats dans des publications scientifiques. Deux pistes seront particulièrement explorées : des réseaux de neurones apprenant directement la relation entre les données du problème et la réponse mécanique, et des approches hybrides associant réduction par projection et corrections non linéaires apprises. Principalement numérique, cette thèse se situe à l’interface entre mécanique des matériaux, mathématiques appliquées et apprentissage automatique. Elle contribuera au développement d’outils plus rapides pour comprendre le comportement des matériaux à l’échelle de leur microstructure. Poste basé sur le site EDF Lab Les Renardières à Moret sur Loing (77). Profil souhaité Vous êtes titulaire, ou prochainement titulaire, d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master bac +5 en mécanique, mathématiques appliquées ou calcul scientifique. Vous disposez de bonnes bases en méthodes numériques et en programmation scientifique, notamment en Python. Vous avez un intérêt marqué pour la mécanique des matériaux et l’apprentissage automatique. Une première expérience en simulation mécanique ou en apprentissage profond serait appréciée. Qualités attendues pour mener les travaux de thèse : Curiosité scientifique, Rigueur, Autonomie, Goût du travail en équipe, Sens de l'organisation (la thèse étant un projet de 3 ans). Vous savez présenter clairement vos résultats et disposez d’un niveau d’anglais vous permettant de lire et de rédiger des publications scientifiques. Le dossier de candidature doit comporter : un curriculum vitae détaillé ; une lettre de motivation ; relevés de notes de votre diplôme de master ou d’ingénieur des années n, n-1 et n2 ; lettres de recommandations et les noms, les coordonnées d’au moins deux personnes pouvant être contactées pour recommandation. Les avantages : Vous pourrez bénéficier des activités sociales de l’entreprise. Vous aurez une prime d’intéressement et une couverture sociale. Vous serez remboursé(e) de 75% de votre abonnement de transport en Ile de France. La diversité alimente notre performance. Dans le groupe EDF, accueillir des personnes en situation de handicap fait partie de notre ADN. Notre objectif est d’ouvrir nos portes à toutes les compétences, toutes les énergies et toutes les personnalités sans exclusion. Le poste proposé est donc ouvert à toutes et à tous.

indeed:60ac88896c2424b5.desc: Your function Do you enjoy working with complex neuroimaging data, large datasets and computational methods? Do you want to work at the intersection of genetics, neuroimaging, neuroscience, neurodiversity and cross-species analyses? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the Connectome Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam The Connectome Lab at the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR), Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, is seeking a PhD candidate in Neuroimaging, Genetics and Cross-species comparison. The project aims to understand how variation in brain anatomy and connectivity contributes to the remarkable diversity of the human brain, and how these features relate to principles of brain evolution. We will combine large-scale human neuroimaging datasets with comparative datasets across species to investigate variation in brain structure, connectivity and functional organization. A central goal is to understand which aspects of brain organization are highly conserved, which show substantial variation between individuals, and which features may have emerged or expanded during human brain evolution. The project therefore brings together neuroimaging, connectomics, neurodiversity, comparative neuroscience and computational neuroscience . You will work with large structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets and develop and apply computational approaches to quantify variation in brain organization across individuals, populations and species. There is particularly attention for the use of LLM in data mining. You will be part of the computational neuroimaging Lab led by Prof. Martijn van den Heuvel and work in an interdisciplinary environment with researchers from neuroimaging, computational neuroscience, genetics, psychology, psychiatry and artificial intelligence. Your duties analyse large-scale structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets develop and apply pipelines for cortical reconstruction, tractography, functional connectivity and connectome analysis investigate individual variation and neurodiversity in brain structure and connectivity integrate genetics with neuroimaging perform comparative analyses of human and non-human brain organization in the context of brain evolution integrate findings across different neuroimaging datasets and imaging modalities develop and apply computational and statistical approaches for analysing brain networks contribute to reproducible and open neuroimaging workflows collaborate with researchers within the Connectome Lab, CNCR and international research networks present your findings at national and international scientific meetings write scientific manuscripts contribute to teaching activities where appropriate Your profile MSc degree in neuroscience, neuroimaging, genetics, biomedical engineering, physics, computer science, artificial intelligence, mathematics, psychology, biology, or a related quantitative discipline. Hands-on experience with computational analysis is important. Ideally, you have experience with several of the following: structural MRI and cortical reconstruction, including FreeSurfer Genetics (GWAS) diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI), tractography and structural connectivity resting-state fMRI and functional connectivity analysis FSL and other commonly used neuroimaging software packages Experience with AI / LLM processing and quality control of neuroimaging datasets connectome and network neuroscience analyses Strong interest in and experience with scientific programming is essential. You should have experience with Python, MATLAB, R, Bash and/or comparable languages , and be comfortable working with computational analysis pipelines. Experience with one or more of the following would be an advantage: large-scale neuroimaging datasets such as UK Biobank, HCP or comparable resources comparative or cross-species neuroimaging brain atlases, surface-based analysis and registration machine learning or multivariate statistics high-performance computing version control and reproducible research workflows network science and computational modelling We are particularly interested in candidates who enjoy working with complex data, think critically about methodology, and are motivated to develop strong computational and neuroimaging expertise. You should also: have a strong interest in neurodiversity and/or evolution be able to work independently while enjoying collaboration within a multidisciplinary team have good analytical and problem-solving skills have a good command of written and spoken English be motivated to learn new neuroimaging and computational techniques support open and reproducible science and be willing to share tools and data with the wider scientific community As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. indeed:ec4198d72a0d944a.title: PhD Assessing Social Sustainability in Short Food Supply Chains
indeed:ec4198d72a0d944a.desc: Your job Are you interested in how law and policy can make agri-food systems fairer and more socially sustainable? Do you enjoy combining legal analysis with empirical research and engaging with farmers and other food-system actors? Join the Law Group at Wageningen University & Research as a PhD candidate in the Horizon Europe project SOCIAL AGRI. Social issues such as working conditions, farmer wellbeing, migrant worker integration and gender equality remain insufficiently captured in EU agricultural data and policy frameworks. This makes social costs and inequalities difficult to assess and address. SOCIAL AGRI aims to close this gap by collecting evidence on social conditions in agriculture, assessing their economic implications, and translating the findings into practical legal and policy instruments to make social sustainability a measurable and actionable dimension of European agricultural policy. You will contribute to this objective through an in-depth socio-legal study of short food supply chains (SFSCs) in the Netherlands. You will investigate how different SFSC models operate, how EU and Dutch law and policy shape their development, and how their organisation affects social sustainability, including working conditions, inclusion, community relationships and the distribution of value. Combining legal analysis with empirical research, you will use methods such as semi-structured interviews and stakeholder engagement activities, depending on the research design. You will identify legal and regulatory barriers to socially sustainable practices and explore how law and policy could better support their development. Working with other project partners, you will also contribute to developing and assessing SOCIAL AGRI’s social-sustainability indicators. Your findings will inform the project’s comparative analysis and help translate evidence on social performance into feasible policy recommendations and legal instruments, including potential regulatory approaches and contractual provisions. Your duties and responsibilities include: Develop and carry out a PhD research plan aligned with SOCIAL AGRI, with a clear focus on the Dutch short food supply chain case study and its contribution to the project’s evidence-to-policy pathway. Analyse relevant EU and Dutch legal and policy frameworks affecting short food supply chains and social sustainability in agriculture. Collect and analyse empirical evidence on the social conditions and relationships within Dutch short food supply chains, using appropriate qualitative methods. Contribute to the development actionable legal and policy instruments, including policy recommendations and model regulatory or contractual provisions, in collaboration with the wider consortium and relevant stakeholders, and of social-sustainability indicators. Contribute to comparative research, collaboration and dissemination within SOCIAL AGRI, interdisciplinary teamwork, project meetings, workshops and academic publications, while actively participating in the academic life of the Law Group. You will work here The research is embedded within the chair Law Group.The Law Group is a vibrant, dynamic, intercultural research community that is closely integrated into the Department of Social Sciences. It has a critical, socio-legal orientation, and excels in interdisciplinary research. It collaborates closely with a range of global partners. The focus of the group’s work is detailed in its most recent Chair Plan. You will work under the supervision of Dr Mirta Alessandrini, who is responsible for the SOCIAL AGRI Dutch case study, Dr Edwin Albals, and Dr Inga Winkler. You will also collaborate with colleagues and researchers from the wider SOCIAL AGRI consortium. Your qualities You are curious, analytically minded and motivated to conduct independent research on the legal and social dimensions of agri-food systems. You are comfortable working across disciplines, engaging with people outside academia, and managing your research independently. You have excellent organisational and time-management skills and can balance different tasks and priorities effectively. To meet the requirements of the role, you have: A completed Master level degree in law, agricultural economics, food studies, rural sociology, social sciences or a closely related discipline. Candidates from various disciplinary backgrounds are welcome to apply, provided they demonstrate affinity with the legal and policy dimensions of agri-food systems. A good understanding of the EU legal and policy context. Experience with qualitative research methods, such as semi-structured interviews or focus groups and with multi-stakeholder processes or clear evidence of the ability to develop these skills. Strong analytical, academic writing and communication skills, with fluency in both Dutch and English. The ability to work independently and collaborate effectively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment. For this position your command of the English and Dutch language is expected to be at C1 level. Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here. We offer Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment. A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: Partially paid parental leave; working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%; excellent pension scheme. In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team. The gross salary for the first year is € 3.204,- per month rising to € 4.051,- in the fourth year in according to the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (scale P). This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help. You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment. Coming from abroad Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees. indeed:d309c535dda25f2a.desc: University of South-Eastern Norway Kjølnes Ring 56, 3918 Porsgrunn Om jobben Lagre favoritt Stillingstittel PhD Research Fellow in Hydropower generators securing electricity supply and grid resilience Type ansettelse Åremål, heltid 100% Antall stillinger 1 Arbeidsspråk Engelsk Søk senest mandag 9. november Welcome to USN The University of Southeastern Norway (USN) ranks as the country's fourth largest higher education institution. We are a vibrant community of approximately 18,000 students and 1,900 employees. Video: https://vimeo.com/898549899/60305e2540 About the position The Faculty of Technology, Natural Sciences and Maritime Sciences (TNM) has a vacancy for a temporary 100 % position as PhD Research Fellow in “The role of hydropower generators in securing electricity supply and enhancing grid resilience” from January 1st 2027. The position is a part of the FME SecurEL center, and it is funded by the Research Council of Norway and USN. The position is located at the Department of Electrical Engineering, Information Technology, and Cybernetics and reports to the Head of Department. The position will be working in the research group, “Electrical Power Systems” (EPS). The place of employment is Porsgrunn. The employment period will be four years full time, and there is a premise for employment that the PhD Research Fellow is enrolled in USN’s PhD-program in PhD in Technology within three months of accession in the position. The four-year full-time period will consist of 75 % research duties and 25 % teaching duties. About the PhD-project and SecurEL This PhD position “The role of hydropower generators in securing electricity supply and enhancing grid resilience” will be associated with Work Package 1 (WP1) on Security of Electricity Supply in SecurEL. The overall objective for the PhD work is to investigate the role of hydropower generators in managing the security of electricity supply in evolving regional distribution grids. The work of the PhD candidate will be integrated with the ongoing work being carried out by the research partners in WP1. In the initial phase, the supervisors, the candidate (based on the candidate's profile), and research partners in SecurEL will work together to identify the comprehensive research questions to be addressed to meet the overall objective of the PhD work. Some potential specific research objectives: Model the coordination and interactions between power producers and system operators (DSOs and TSO) in scenarios for the transition of distribution grids. Quantify the importance of hydropower production and its interoperability in managing security of supply and grid stability. Explore the interplay between different aspects of security of supply (energy availability, power capacity, reliability of supply and voltage quality), as well as power flow balancing, and dynamic system integration) in regional distribution grids. Investigate how generator characteristics such as capabilities for fault-ride through, island mode transition, and black start impact the vulnerability and resilience of the grid, in particular considering islanded grid operation. Develop vulnerability indicators related to power production and control for increasing situational awareness. Read more about the Centre and its research at the website https://www.securel.no Qualifications Eligibility Requirements: A master’s degree equivalent to a Norwegian master’s degree (120 ECTS). Documented proficiency in English (Nordic applicants may submit their high school diploma as documentation). Applicants with a strong background in STEM fields (e.g., electrical power engineering, control system engineering, physics or environmental engineering, mathematics (Operations research) or computer science or machine learning). The master’s thesis must be included in the application. Some of the teaching duties are in Norwegian language. Documented level of Norwegian or Scandinavian language skills at minimum B2 level are required. Ideal Candidate: Ability to collaborate and work effectively in an international and interdisciplinary research environment. Demonstrates experience or strong interest in modelling, programming, systems thinking, and qualitative/quantitative research methods. Documented programming experience for example GitHub project on MATLAB, Python, Julia, Javascript. Experience in mathematical modeling, control engineering, and optimization is a distinctive advantage. Possesses a strong academic record, with relevant experience in either industry or academia. Has prior professional experience and a solid understanding of workplace responsibilities and expectations, which will be considered a key advantage. Shows a deep interest in interdisciplinary research, is capable of independent work, and actively engages with the supervision team to foster collaborative research. The applicant must have gained the degree within the start date of the position, so applicants in the last semester of their master’s degree are also encouraged to apply. indeed:97893c9c906e048d.title: PhD Research Fellow in AI Native Networking for Healthcare
indeed:97893c9c906e048d.desc: About the position We seek a PhD Research Fellow for a 3-year position in the SYNAPSE project. The successful candidate will have a solid background in computer networking and an interest in developing machine-learning methods for network control and network-aware distributed learning. Section for Medical Information and Communication Technology (Medical ICT Research), The Intervention Centre (see: http://www.ivs.no), at Oslo University Hospital offers a full-time PhD Fellowship. The recruited PhD Fellow will be part of the Wireless Sensor Network Research Group of Professor Ilangko Balasingham and will be enrolled in the PhD program at the University of Oslo Oslo University Hospital is a workplace with great diversity. We believe this is crucial for solving our tasks in the best possible way. We want this diversity to be reflected among the applicants for our positions, and we encourage all qualified candidates, regardless of background, to apply! Key information Application deadline: 15.11.2026 Employer: Oslo universitetssykehus HF Town/city: Oslo Title: PhD Research Fellow in AI Native Networking for Healthcare Positions: 1 Full-time/part-time: Full-time Employment type: Contract Percentage of full-time: 100 Webcruiter ID: 5199969633 Start date: 01.01.2027 End date: 31.12.2029 Social sharing : Share on x Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook Share by email About SYNAPSE SYNAPSE, funded by the Research Council of Norway, develops networks that adapt their decisions to network conditions and the clinical urgency of the information they carry. Learning is integrated into network control to support decisions about scheduling, routing and resource allocation. For example, an urgent clinical alert should reach its destination promptly even when links are congested and patients are moving. The project also develops distributed and federated learning methods that adapt to connectivity, available resources and clinical priorities. Network control and distributed learning are designed together, so that the network supports learning and learning remains effective when communication is constrained. The methods are evaluated in remote patient monitoring and hospital-at-home scenarios. This position focuses on network protocols and their control at the MAC, network, transport and cross-layer levels, combined with machine learning. It does not cover hardware, antennas, circuits or physical-layer signal processing, and is not a general data-science position. Applicants must document relevant computer-networking knowledge and experience. Research areas Learning-based network control, including scheduling, link selection, routing and resource allocation in wireless and edge networks. Reinforcement learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning for distributed network decision-making. Graph and hypergraph representation learning of network state, including temporal graph neural networks. Network- and urgency-aware distributed and federated learning, adapting the exchange of data and model updates to network conditions and clinical priorities. Evaluation through network simulation and emulation, and with real remote patient monitoring data. Resonsibilities Develop and evaluate learning-based methods for urgency-aware network control and network-aware distributed learning. Implement and test the methods using network simulation or emulation and real monitoring data. Publish in leading networking and machine-learning venues and complete a PhD at the University of Oslo, Faculty of Medicine. Required qualifications A master’s degree (120 ECTS), including a thesis, in computer science, network or communication engineering, electrical engineering or equivalent. A relevant bachelor’s degree (180 ECTS), with a total of five years of higher education. A solid foundation in computer networking, demonstrated through relevant coursework and a substantial project, thesis or research experience involving network protocols, wireless or mobile networks, routing or network performance. Coursework or project experience in machine learning, and good programming skills in Python. A weighted average grade of B or better on the master’s degree, as required by the University of Oslo. A master’s thesis graded B or better (Norwegian grading scale or equivalent). Preferred qualifications Experience with reinforcement learning or graph neural networks. Experience with network simulation or emulation tools, such as ns-3, OMNeT++ or Mininet. Publications or a master’s thesis combining networking and machine learning. Language Requirements Applicants who are not proficient in a Scandinavian language must document English proficiency through one of the following: TOEFL: at least 600 (paper-based) or 92 (internet-based); IELTS Academic: at least 6.5, with no section below 5.5; Cambridge CAE/CPE: grade A or B. Personal Qualities Ability to work independently and collaboratively. A structured, precise and adaptable working style. Strong communication and teamwork skills. A positive attitude and ability to manage a dynamic work environment. A high level of professionalism and work ethic. We offer A fully funded, full-time three-year PhD position. Salary according to the Norwegian state salary scale (approximately NOK 550,800–587,000 per year). Supervision by Dr Roufaida Laidi (PI), Prof. Ilangko Balasingham and Dr Hemin Ali Qadir, in collaboration with Prof. Tarik Taleb (Ruhr University Bochum). A clinical research environment at The Intervention Centre, Oslo University Hospital. Access to high-performance computing infrastructure at OUS and national e-infrastructure services. An inclusive, interdisciplinary research environment at the Intervention Centre, OUS. Pension, insurance and welfare schemes through the Norwegian public sector. Family-friendly surroundings with cultural and outdoor opportunities in Oslo. Your application Submit a cover letter of at most one page explaining your interest in SYNAPSE and your fit with the position. Identify: Your computer-networking background, naming relevant coursework, a thesis, substantial projects or publications and explaining your own contribution. Your experience implementing machine-learning methods and using network simulation, emulation or testbeds. The research area or areas above that best match your background and interests. Supporting documents A CV. Transcripts for your bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with the grading scale or diploma supplement. Copies of your diplomas. Documented English proficiency. Names and contact details of two referees, at least one academic. Referees must not be family members. Documents not in English or a Scandinavian language must be accompanied by a certified translation. Applications without transcripts and diplomas will not be assessed. Submit your application electronically through Webcruiter Address: Sognsvannsveien 20, 0372 Oslo, Norway Open directions (in new tab) Contacts Dr. Roufaida Laidi Project leader, PI Email: roufaida.laidi@ous-hf.no Prof. Ilangko Balasingham Section leader Email: ilangko.balasingham@ous-research.no About the employer Oslo University Hospital is a highly specialised hospital in charge of extensive regional and local hospital assignments and the provision of high quality services for the citizens of Oslo. The hospital also has a nationwide responsibility for a number of national and multi-regional assignments and has several national centres of competence. The hospital is Scandinavia's largest and we each year carry out more than 1.2 million patient treatments. Oslo University Hospital is responsible for approximately 50 percent of all medical and healthcare research conducted at Norwegian hospitals and is a significant role player within the education of a large variety of health care personnel. We are an emergency hospital for East and Southern Norway and have national emergency assignments. The hospital has a total budget of NOK 17 billion. More than 20,000 employees are engaged with activities at more than 40 different locations. The University of Oslo is Norway's oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 28 000 students and 7000 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. The Faculty of Medicine was established in 1814 and is the oldest medical faculty in Norway. The Faculty is organized into three basic units and has approximately 1,500 employees and about 2000 students. The Institute of Clinical Medicine (Klinmed) is one of three institutes under the Faculty. Klinmed is responsible for the Faculty's educational and research activities at Oslo University Hospital and Akershus University Hospital. With about 800 employees spread over approximately 425 man-labour years, Klinmed is the university's largest institute.

indeed:177b239b6dc2b9c7.title: Marie Sklodowska-Curie Doctoral Researcher - Mechanical Engineering - 108121 - Grade 8
indeed:177b239b6dc2b9c7.desc: Position Details Department of Mechanical Engineering Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK Fixed salary of £49,747, additional allowances may be applicable depending on circumstances Grade: 8 (Spot) Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to 31 December 2029 4 x Positions available Closing date: 15th November 2026 This role is also open as an internal secondment opportunity which would need to be agreed by your current line manager. Background To create and disseminate knowledge through initiating and conducting original research and through publication, as appropriate to the disciplinary area. The posts are part of SurPhase, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network funded under Horizon Europe (Grant Agreement No. 101311533) and coordinated by the University of Birmingham. SurPhase is an international, interdisciplinary and intersectoral doctoral training programme addressing fundamental and applied challenges in phase-change heat transfer. It brings together expertise in thermal sciences, surface engineering, advanced manufacturing, computational modelling, data-driven methods, durability and sustainability. The University of Birmingham will recruit four Doctoral Candidates, each appointed as a Research Fellow I for 36 months and undertaking an individual doctoral research project within the SurPhase programme. The four University of Birmingham projects broadly cover: advanced surface engineering for enhanced flow boiling; molecular modelling of phase change at engineered interfaces; data-driven design of surfaces for enhanced boiling; and durability and sustainability of engineered heat-transfer surfaces. The postholders will also participate in the network-wide research and training programme and undertake planned research secondments with SurPhase academic and industrial partners. Role Summary Initiate and conduct original research which has measurable outcomes and is reflected in a growing national and often incipient international reputation Plan, design and co-ordinate research activities and programmes Contribute to the development of research strategies Publish results of own research Supervise PhD students Contribute to the Department/School through management/leadership Develop and make substantial contributions to knowledge transfer, enterprise, business engagement, public engagement activities, widening participation, schools outreach or similar activities at Department/School level or further within the University Additional SurPhase-specific responsibilities: Undertake an individual doctoral research project within the SurPhase MSCA Doctoral Network. Design, conduct and analyse research appropriate to the appointed project. Contribute to the scientific objectives, milestones and deliverables of SurPhase. Work collaboratively with researchers across the academic and industrial consortium. Participate in network-wide scientific, transferable-skills and professional-development training. Undertake planned international and intersectoral research secondments. Disseminate research through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, network activities and appropriate public-engagement activities. Main Duties To plan and carry out research, using appropriate methodology and techniques. This may include, where appropriate to the discipline: Pursue personal research including developing research ideas and winning support, including financial support Plan, publish and/or execute high quality research Project manage research activities, and/or supervise other research staff Present high quality findings in publications and conference proceedings Develop novel methodologies and techniques appropriate to the type of research being pursued Supervise and examine PhD students, both within and out with the University Provide expert advice to colleagues and students within discipline Contribute to the administration/management of research across the Department/School Develop and make substantial contributions to knowledge transfer, enterprise, business engagement, , and public engagement activities of manifest benefit to the College and the University Contribute to some administrative activities within the University, typically relating to research Apply knowledge in a way that develops new intellectual understanding * Actively manages equality, diversity and inclusion through monitoring and evaluation and actively challenging unacceptable behaviour This indicative responsibility may also be included in a research role at a lower grade. Additional SurPhase-specific duties: Undertake research within one of the four University of Birmingham SurPhase Doctoral Candidate projects. Plan and execute experimental, computational or data-driven research, as appropriate to the specific project. Maintain accurate and reproducible research records and contribute to appropriate research data management and open-science practices. Work with SurPhase supervisors, Doctoral Candidates and academic and industrial partners across the network. Participate in regular project meetings, network meetings, training schools, workshops and conferences. Undertake research secondments at partner organisations in accordance with the SurPhase training programme. Prepare research outputs including journal papers, conference contributions, technical reports and project deliverables. Complete the academic and research requirements associated with registration for a doctoral degree at the University of Birmingham. Contribute to the wider research environment of the School of Engineering. Person Specification Normally, a higher degree relevant to the research area (normally PhD or near completion) or equivalent qualifications Extensive research experience and scholarship within subject specialism Experience and achievement reflected in a growing reputation Extensive experience and demonstrated success in planning, undertaking and project managing research to deliver high quality results Extensive experience of applying and/or developing and devising successful models, techniques and methods Extensive experience and achievement in knowledge transfer, enterprise and similar activity Experience of championing Equality, Diversity and Inclusion in own work area Ability to monitor and evaluate the extent to which equality and diversity legislation, policies, procedures are applied Ability to identify issues with the potential to impact on protected groups and take appropriate action Informal enquiries to Ali Sadaghiani a.sadaghiani@bham.ac.uk View our staff values and behaviours here Use of AI in applications: We want to understand your genuine interest in the role and for the written elements of your application to accurately reflect your own communication style. Applications that rely too heavily on AI tools can appear generic and lack the detail we need to assess your skills and experience. Such applications will unlikely be progressed to interview. We believe there is no such thing as a 'typical' member of University of Birmingham staff and that diversity in its many forms is a strength that underpins the exchange of ideas, innovation and debate at the heart of University life. We are committed to proactively addressing the barriers experienced by some groups in our community and are proud to hold Athena SWAN, Race Equality Charter and Disability Confident accreditations. We have an Equality Diversity and Inclusion Centre that focuses on continuously improving the University as a fair and inclusive place to work where everyone has the opportunity to succeed. linkedin:4484038099.title: PhD Student/ Research Assistant (f/m/d)
linkedin:4484038099.desc: The Chair for Embedded Systems (CES) at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) invites applications for a Doctoral Researcher (f/m/d) position on Adaptive, Secure, and Energy-Efficient Edge AI Processors . The position aims to develop an adaptive Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and to integrate it into a complete System-on-Chip (SoC) platform for efficient, reliable, and secure edge AI. A central challenge is to exploit runtime-configurable precision, approximate computing, and early-exit inference to meet strict energy, performance, real-time, and security requirements. The research spans hardware architecture, FPGA prototyping, ASIC implementation, hardware/software co-design, and system-level execution. Research Focus The successful candidate will contribute to research in the following interconnected areas: Adaptive NPU architectures – runtime-configurable processing elements, systolic arrays, mixed-precision data paths, approximate arithmetic, and reliability monitoring. SoC integration, FPGA and ASIC design – RISC-V-based SoC integration, RTL design and verification, FPGA prototyping, system bring-up, PPA evaluation, technology-aware optimization, and post-silicon validation. Cross-layer hardware/software optimization – joint exploration of hardware and neural-network parameters, dynamic precision and approximation, early-exit execution, workload mapping, scheduling, and energy-aware runtime management. Hardware security and trusted execution – security monitoring, hardware roots of trust, measured boot, platform attestation, memory isolation, and protection against side-channel attacks. Personal Qualifications A very good Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. A background or strong interest in FPGA/ASIC design and hardware/software co-design , ideally complemented by knowledge of computer architecture, embedded systems, edge AI, real-time systems, or hardware security. Experience with C/C++, Python, RTL design (Verilog/VHDL/SystemVerilog), Linux, or hardware design and simulation tools is advantageous. Strong motivation for independent research, teamwork, and fluent written and spoken English. Starting Date Expected from January 2027. Application Process Please send your application, including a cover letter, CV, and copies of relevant certificates and academic transcripts, to henkel@kit.edu with the following email subject line: Application for NPU Researcher Position – Last Name, First Name We encourage applications from candidates of diverse backgrounds. Recognized severely disabled applicants will be given preference if equally qualified.

linkedin:4484027233.title: Doctoral student in equitable AI for breast cancer screening and risk prediction
linkedin:4484027233.desc: Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required. The research group The doctoral student will be based at the Department of Oncology-Pathology, Karolinska Institutet, within the Computational Breast Imaging Group led by Associate Professor Fredrik Strand. The group is internationally recognized for the development and evaluation of AI for breast cancer imaging and precision medicine, combining expertise in radiology, machine learning, and biostatistics. It comprises PhD students, research engineers, research assistants, postdoctoral researchers, and collaborating senior clinicians in radiology, pathology, oncology, and surgery. The group has active national collaborations (KTH, Lund University, the Institute for Future Studies, and several groups at KI) and international collaborations (among others UC Berkeley, UCSF, University of Hawaii, and University of Barcelona). Available infrastructure includes high-performance computing, GDPR-compliant secure storage, and the VAI.B platform, which holds multi-region Swedish screening mammography data linked to cancer outcomes. The doctoral student will be supervised by Apostolia Tsirikoglou, PhD, research specialist and lead AI scientist in the group, as main supervisor, together with Associate Professor Fredrik Strand, head of the group and principal investigator of the project, as co-supervisor. The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student This PhD project investigates whether AI systems used in population-based mammography screening perform equitably across population groups, and how inequities can be reduced. AI is entering breast cancer screening both as detection support and as risk prediction to guide screening intervals and supplemental imaging. Systems developed on specific populations may perform differently for groups that were underrepresented in their development, and screening outcomes already differ by country of birth and socioeconomic status. Evidence on equitable performance is therefore needed before AI is adopted at scale. The project uses a large multi-region Swedish screening dataset with radiologist assessments, cancer outcomes from the National Quality Register for Breast Cancer, and demographic and socioeconomic data from Statistics Sweden. The doctoral student will evaluate commercial and in-house AI cancer detection systems and AI risk prediction models across subgroups defined by country of birth and socioeconomic status, compare AI with radiologist performance in the same groups, and, in a later phase, develop and evaluate fairness-aware models that reduce identified disparities while maintaining clinical performance. The doctoral student is expected to take an active and increasingly independent role in study design, cohort construction and register linkage, statistical analysis, running and evaluating AI systems on imaging data, model development, writing scientific publications, and presenting results at international conferences. The doctoral education includes courses in epidemiology, biostatistics, machine learning, and AI fairness. Where needed, competence in deep learning model development will be built during the project under supervision. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment full of expertise and curiosity. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. As a doctoral student you are offered an individual research project, a well-educated supervisor, a vast range of elective courses and the opportunity to work in a leading research group. Karolinska Institutet collaborates with prominent universities from all around the world, which ensures opportunities for international exchanges. You will be employed on a doctoral studentship which means that you receive a contractual salary. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care. B) Specific eligibility requirement You meet the specific eligibility requirement for doctoral/third-cycle/PhD education if you: - Show proficiency in English equivalent to the course English B/English 6 at Swedish upper secondary school. Follow the instructions on the web page English language requirements for doctoral education. Verification of your documents Karolinska Institutet checks the authenticity of your documents. Karolinska Institutet reserves the right to revoke admission if supporting documents are discovered to be fraudulent. Submission of false documents is a violation of Swedish law and is considered grounds for legal action. (A) and (B) can only be certified by the documentation requirement for doctoral education. Skills and personal qualities Necessary: A master's degree (or equivalent) in bioinformatics, biostatistics, or a related quantitative field Programming skills for data processing and analysis Knowledge of statistical and epidemiological methods Strong analytical ability and interest in interdisciplinary research at the intersection of AI, medicine, and health equity Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team Excellent written and spoken English Desirable/advantageous: Experience with population-based register data and record linkage, preferably Swedish national registers Experience with cohort construction and subgroup analyses in large health datasets Experience with large-scale processing of medical imaging data or evaluation of AI systems on clinical data Interest in health equity, fairness in AI, and responsible implementation of AI in healthcare Terms and conditions The doctoral student will be employed on a doctoral studentship maximum 4 years full-time. Application process Submit your application and supporting documents through the Varbi recruitment system. Use the button in the top right corner and follow the instructions. We prefer that your application is written in English, but you can also apply in Swedish. Your application must contain the following documents: - A personal letter and a curriculum vitae - Degree projects and previous publications, if any - Any other documentation showing the desirable skills and personal qualities described above - Documents certifying your general eligibility (see A above) - Documents certifying your specific eligibility (see B above) Selection A selection will be made among eligible applicants on the basis of the ability to benefit from doctoral education. The qualifications of the applicants will be evaluated on an overall basis. Karolinska Institutet uses the following bases of assessment: - Documented subject knowledge of relevance to the area of research - Analytical skill - Other documented knowledge or experience that may be relevant to doctoral studies in the subject. linkedin:4484030512.desc: Job Description Are you fascinated by how the food we eat shapes our microbiome and metabolic health? Excited by the prospect of determining how nutritious are microbial foods? Eager to work in a cutting-edge, interdisciplinary research environment tackling major food-system challenges? Then join us as our new PhD Student in computational modelling of protein and nutrient bioavailability of microbial foods! This position sits within BRIGHT’s Microbial Foods mission. You will help developing computational tools to predict the nutritional value of alternative proteins and nutrients. Our goal is to predict how well a protein or microbial food is digested, absorbed and assimilated in humans, so that foodstuffs can be tailored for a nutritious and sustainable diet without compromising taste and texture. You will build the computational model at the heart of our mission, combining protein language model embeddings with nutritional composition, proteomics and metabolomics data into a multi-modal AI/ML system that predicts digestibility and bioavailability of proteins as well as the bioavailability of micronutrients and food-derived bioactives. The position is fully computational, and you will work with a talented team of scientists generating the in vitro and clinical data that will train and validate your model. Responsibilities And Qualifications Responsibilities: Review the state-of-the-art in protein bioavailability, covering digestion, absorption and assimilation, with a focus on microbial foods Build a multi-modal AI/ML model that predicts protein digestibility and bioavailability, combining protein language model embeddings with nutritional composition data and benchmarking against DIAAS and ileal digestibility datasets Create and curate a database of selected microbial foods, for example, Yarrowia lipolytica and Aspergillus spp. Model proteolytic digestion and the absorption of peptides and amino acids and small molecules including transporter-mediated uptake Test and refine the model against proteomics and metabolomics data for single microbial proteins and whole microbial cells Retrain the model with in vitro digestion data and with clinical trial data generated by our experimental partners Apply the model to the computational redesign of microbial foods for improved bioavailability, and release it as an open-source tool Report your research results in peer-reviewed scientific publications and international conferences Collaborate within BRIGHT as well as our local, national and international networks Disseminate your results through scientific publications, public engagement and social media Teach and supervise MSc and BSc students Qualifications: MSc in bioinformatics, computational biology, machine learning, computer science, food science or a related area Advanced programming experience in Python Experience with machine learning, including deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch Excellent English proficiency in written and oral form Excellent communication and social skills for working within an interdisciplinary research team Strong analytical skills and ability to work independently Preferred qualifications but not mandatory: Experience with protein language models or other sequence-based representation learning Familiarity with protein digestion, nutrition or food science, including metrics like DIAAS and PDCAAS Experience working with proteomics or metabolomics data Experience with data curation and building structured databases, and an interest in open-source software development You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures The period of employment is 3 years. The position is full time. The preferred starting date is 1st April 2027 (or sooner according to mutual agreement). You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Carlos Acevedo-Rocha: cargac@dtu.dk More information about BRIGHT: https://bright.dtu.dk/ If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale One letter of reference, with referee’s email and phone number You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. BRIGHT Mission 2: Microbial Foods BRIGHT Mission 2 aims to build an AI-powered framework for the rational design of microbial foods that meet four targets: consumer acceptance, health, sustainability and scalability. The first phase focuses on two fungal chassis, Aspergillus and Yarrowia, characterizing more than 500 prototypes through multi-omics, sensory analysis, life-cycle assessment and safety testing. Predictive models for flavor, texture, nutrition and process scale-up are trained iteratively through active learning. The scientific scope spans strain engineering, adaptive laboratory evolution, solid- and liquid-state fermentation, sensory and consumer research, and pre-clinical and clinical evaluation of safety, bioavailability and cardiometabolic health, in collaboration with national and international partners. BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions. DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. linkedin:4483796912.title: Thèse CIFRE: Réduction de modèle par deep learning pour la plasticité cristalline F/H
linkedin:4483796912.desc: EDF R&D, avec ses 2000 chercheurs, a pour missions principales de contribuer à l'amélioration de la performance des unités opérationnelles du groupe EDF, d'identifier et de préparer les relais de croissance à moyen et long termes. EDF R&D met en œuvre une politique volontariste de partenariat en France et à l’international notamment dans les pays où le Groupe est présent. Vous souhaitez associer mécanique des matériaux, simulation numérique et intelligence artificielle pour répondre à des enjeux industriels ? > Rejoignez EDF Recherche et Développement dans le cadre d’une thèse CIFRE consacrée à la réduction de modèle par apprentissage profond pour les calculs en plasticité cristalline. La poursuite de l’exploitation des centrales nucléaires au-delà de 60 ans nécessite des outils avancés pour justifier la tenue mécanique des composants. Pour les matériaux métalliques, leur comportement dépend notamment de la microstructure, c’est-à-dire de l’organisation des grains qui les constituent. Les simulations en plasticité cristalline permettent de représenter ces grains et leurs interactions pour mieux comprendre les déformations et les mécanismes de rupture. Elles restent toutefois coûteuses en temps de calcul, ce qui limite l’étude de microstructures et de sollicitations variées. L’objectif de cette thèse est de développer des modèles réduits fondés sur l’apprentissage profond pour accélérer ces simulations, tout en conservant une précision adaptée aux grandeurs étudiées et en respectant les lois physiques. Vos principales missions seront les suivantes : Étudier les méthodes de réduction de modèle et d’apprentissage profond adaptées à la plasticité cristalline. Constituer et exploiter des jeux de données issus de simulations de référence, couvrant différentes microstructures, propriétés des matériaux et sollicitations mécaniques. Développer des modèles capables de prédire les grandeurs mécaniques recherchées, en intégrant des contraintes physiques pour améliorer leur fiabilité. Comparer les approches en matière de précision, de coût de calcul et de capacité à traiter des configurations non utilisées pendant l’apprentissage. Appliquer les méthodes à des cas représentatifs des besoins industriels et valoriser les résultats dans des publications scientifiques. Deux pistes seront particulièrement explorées : des réseaux de neurones apprenant directement la relation entre les données du problème et la réponse mécanique, et des approches hybrides associant réduction par projection et corrections non linéaires apprises. Principalement numérique, cette thèse se situe à l’interface entre mécanique des matériaux, mathématiques appliquées et apprentissage automatique. Elle contribuera au développement d’outils plus rapides pour comprendre le comportement des matériaux à l’échelle de leur microstructure. Poste basé sur le site EDF Lab Les Renardières à Moret sur Loing (77). Vous êtes titulaire, ou prochainement titulaire, d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master bac +5 en mécanique, mathématiques appliquées ou calcul scientifique. Vous disposez de bonnes bases en méthodes numériques et en programmation scientifique, notamment en Python. Vous avez un intérêt marqué pour la mécanique des matériaux et l’apprentissage automatique. linkedin:4483269556.desc: About The Position Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia. The position will specifically focus on Reinforcement Learning for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP). The Ph.D. candidate will be a member of the group of Civil Engineering and Geomatics at NTNU and will tightly cooperate with other Ph.D./post-docs in projects (such as HEU-CIRCULess) and research groups at the department. The Ph.D. position will offer opportunities to develop high-quality research within the field of digitalization of circular construction. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. Duties of the position Develop learning-based algorithms or methods for deterministic scheduling optimization problems with the aim of achieving competitive performance against state-of-the-art approaches. Extend the developed framework to scheduling under uncertainty. Investigate how the proposed learning-based methods can be extended to uncertain and dynamic project environments. Improve the scalability of learning-based scheduling methods and evaluate generalization, robustness, and computational performance. Disseminate research outcomes. Publications in relevant high quality peer-reviewed journals are needed. Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above Academic publications and popular science dissemination Participate in the research group Civil Engineering and Geomatics Research group Civil Engineering and Geomatics - NTNU Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must have a relevant master’s degree in Computer Science and technology, computer system engineering or equivalent. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Experience in reinforcement learning, GNN, etc. You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education. You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme https://www.ntnu.edu/studies/phiv Applicants must have fluent skills in both written and oral English. Non-English native speaker applicants who do not have master in Europe must provide evidence of good English language skills, written and spoken. The following tests can be used as such documentation: TOEFL, IELTS or Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) or Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE). Minimum scores are: TOEFL: 600 (paper-based test), 92 (Internet-based test); IELTS: 6.5, with no section lower than 5.5 (only Academic IELTS test accepted); CAE/CPE: grade B or A. In extraordinary circumstances, formal documentation of language skills can be relinquished. In such cases, the candidate’s language skills will be assessed in a personal interview. PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”. The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria Academic publication in relevant field. Experience in programming skills, and artificial intelligence. Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently The applicant must be motivated to work closely with teams and external partners Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity Show curiosity and strong motivation for the subject Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities. We offer An exciting job with an important mission in society Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Working capital that can be used to implement the project Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering https://www.ntnu.edu/studies/phiv within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed. About The Application The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English. Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request. The Application Must Include Transcripts for Bachelor's and Master's degrees Diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees Copy of Master's thesis Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages) Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page) Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work Possibly certificates CV Names and contact information of three relevant referees If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education.
