linkedin:4484094509.title: PhD Position in Agentic AI for Autonomous Materials Discovery in Next-Generation Energy Devices
linkedin:4484094509.desc: Company Description IREC – Institut de Recerca en Energia de Catalunya – is the public Catalonia Institute for Energy Research, attached to the Department of Territory, Housing and Ecological Transition, with participation from the Department of Research and Universities. As a CERCA and TECNIO-accredited center created in 2008, IREC focuses on sustainable development and strengthening industrial competitiveness in the energy sector. The institute conducts medium- and long-term research, driving innovation and new technological products in key energy domains. IREC also promotes knowledge transfer and public dissemination of research outcomes, working closely with government, universities, and industry. Its research departments cover areas such as solar energy materials and systems, nanoionics and fuel cells, functional nanomaterials, energy storage and catalysis, power systems, energy systems analytics, and climate-neutral buildings and communities. Role Description The PhD Position in Agentic AI for Autonomous Materials Discovery in Next-Generation Energy Devices is a full-time, on-site role based in Barcelona. The PhD candidate will develop and implement agentic AI and machine learning methods to autonomously explore, design, and optimize materials for advanced energy devices. Day-to-day tasks include building computational workflows, integrating experimental and simulation data, and collaborating with materials scientists and engineers to validate AI-driven discoveries. The role involves publishing research in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at conferences, and contributing to project reports and proposals. The candidate will work within IREC’s interdisciplinary research environment, participate in group meetings, and support the development of open, reproducible research tools and datasets. Qualifications Strong background in artificial intelligence and machine learning, preferably with experience in agent-based systems and autonomous experimentation. Knowledge of computational materials science, chemistry, physics, or related fields, including modeling and simulation of materials and energy devices. Proficiency in scientific programming (e.g., Python, Julia, or similar) and experience with data analysis, model development, and workflow automation. Ability to design and conduct rigorous research, interpret complex results, and communicate findings clearly in written and oral form. Master’s degree (or equivalent) in engineering, physics, chemistry, computer science, materials science, or a closely related discipline, qualifying for PhD enrollment. Interest in sustainable energy technologies and interdisciplinary collaboration with experimental and theoretical teams. Fluency in English for research communication; knowledge of Catalan or Spanish is an asset but not mandatory. Capacity to work independently and as part of a diverse team, demonstrating initiative, critical thinking, and strong organizational skills.

linkedin:4462954683.title: Thèse CIFRE pour Estimation Probabiliste De Franchibilité Pour Des Plateformes Terrestres Non Habitées Résilientes En Environnements Non Structurés. ( H/F)
linkedin:4462954683.desc: L'industrie automobile est en pleine mutation, face à des défis majeurs et des opportunités considérables. La transition vers les véhicules électriques, la pression réglementaire pour réduire les émissions de CO2, et la concurrence accrue des nouveaux acteurs du secteur (constructeurs chinois, entreprises technologiques) forcent les fabricants à repenser leur modèle. La robotisation et l'intelligence artificielle, incarnées par le développement de robots industriels intelligents, deviennent des éléments cruciaux pour répondre à ces enjeux. L’objectif de cette thèse est de contribuer aux développements de nouvelles techniques d’IA embarquées pour transformer et démocratiser l’usage de la robotique industrielle. Vous devrez définir, tester et expérimenter les nouvelles solutions d'IA dans la robotique comme le Reiforcement Learning, le VLA, l'imitation learning... Par l'usage de ces nouvelles technologies, vous définirez les architectures et les solutions logicielles pour simplifier l'usage de la robotique industrielle et réduire les compétences requises pour programmer les robots. Vous serez intégré à l'équipe innovation et standards industriels en charge de la transformation numérique des usines Renault et des nouvelles solutions Robotique et IA physique. Contexte Les véhicules autonomes et les plateformes robotiques terrestres évoluent désormais dans des environnements de plus en plus ouverts, incertains et dégradés. Au-delà des réseaux routiers structurés, la capacité d’un système mobile à comprendre le terrain, à estimer sa franchibilité et à décider de manière sûre devient un enjeu scientifique, industriel et stratégique majeur. Dans ce contexte, AMPERE souhaite renforcer ses compétences en intelligence artificielle, perception, sûreté de fonctionnement et architectures de véhicules définis par logiciel, afin de contribuer au développement de solutions autonomes robustes, maîtrisées et compatibles avec les exigences de souveraineté technologique. Votre environnement La Direction de l’Ingénierie d’AMPERE recherche un doctorant CIFRE pour travailler sur l’estimation probabiliste de la franchibilité de plateformes terrestres non habitées résilientes en environnements non structurés, en s’appuyant sur les avancées récentes en perception fondée sur l’IA, fusion de capteurs, modélisation de l’incertitude et assurance sécurité. Vous évoluerez dans un environnement pluridisciplinaire associant recherche industrielle, expertise système et encadrement académique, avec une attention particulière portée à la discrétion, à la protection des savoir-faire et à la valorisation de capacités technologiques européennes maîtrisées. les experts ADAS/AD, architecture logicielle, perception, sûreté de fonctionnement, validation et robotique mobile d’AMPERE ; les partenaires académiques de l’ENSTA / Institut Polytechnique de Paris, ainsi que les doctorants et équipes de recherche travaillant sur les systèmes autonomes, la perception et la robotique de terrain. Vos missions Dans le cadre de cette thèse CIFRE, vous contribuerez à la conception d’une couche de perception et d’estimation de franchibilité destinée à préparer des plateformes mobiles à évoluer dans des environnements non structurés, incertains ou dégradés. Vos travaux viseront à combiner compréhension sémantique du terrain, fusion de capteurs, informations proprioceptives du véhicule et modélisation probabiliste de l’incertitude afin d’aider le système à décider s’il peut poursuivre sa trajectoire, ralentir, s’arrêter ou déclencher une stratégie de repli. réaliser un état de l’art sur la franchibilité des véhicules terrestres non habités, la perception pour environnements non structurés, les modèles fondateurs, la fusion de capteurs et l’estimation de l’incertitude ; développer un module d’estimation probabiliste de la franchibilité pouvant s’interfacer avec des architectures de conduite autonome existantes ; étudier l’apport des modèles d’IA, notamment les modèles de perception avancés, pour qualifier les propriétés du terrain au-delà de la seule géométrie ; intégrer des indicateurs d’état du véhicule, tels que glissement, effort, adhérence ou marge dynamique, afin de rapprocher la perception de la réalité physique du terrain ; définir des métriques de confiance, des seuils de décision et des mécanismes de repli compatibles avec une démarche d’assurance sécurité ; valider les approches proposées par simulation, jumeau numérique, jeux de données et, lorsque possible, expérimentations sur prototype ; contribuer aux publications scientifiques, aux livrables de thèse, aux échanges avec les experts internes et à la capitalisation des résultats pour de futurs développements industriels. Votre profil Vous êtes diplômé(e) d’une grande école d’ingénieurs, d’un master recherche de haut niveau ou d’un programme international équivalent, avec une spécialisation en robotique, intelligence artificielle, systèmes autonomes, perception ou ingénierie des systèmes. Une première expérience de recherche ou d’ingénierie appliquée à l’IA pour les plateformes robotiques mobiles, les véhicules intelligents ou les systèmes embarqués constituera un atout important. Vous disposez de solides connaissances dans plusieurs des domaines suivants : robotique mobile, intelligence artificielle, systèmes autonomes, ADAS/AD ou systèmes de conduite automatisée ; perception embarquée, capteurs caméra, LiDAR ou radar, et algorithmes de fusion de données appliqués à la compréhension de scènes complexes ; simulation, modélisation ou validation de plateformes mobiles évoluant dans des environnements complexes, incertains ou non structurés. Des connaissances en ingénierie système, architecture véhicule, sûreté de fonctionnement, validation ou technologies embarquées constitueront également des atouts appréciés. Vous êtes curieux(se), rigoureux(se), autonome et force de proposition, avec le goût des sujets scientifiques exigeants et des problématiques industrielles à forts enjeux. Vous savez structurer votre raisonnement, expliquer clairement vos choix techniques et interagir efficacement avec des interlocuteurs de niveaux d’expertise variés, dans un environnement où la discrétion et la maîtrise de l’information sont essentielles. Vous disposez d’un très bon niveau d’anglais écrit et oral, nécessaire pour évoluer dans un environnement scientifique international, contribuer à des publications et échanger avec des partenaires académiques et industriels. Métier Transverse

linkedin:4484221266.title: PhD position on Quantitative evaluation of battery cells using X-ray computed tomography
linkedin:4484221266.desc: The Manufacturing Metrology research group of the KU Leuven Department of Mechanical Engineering investigates, develops, optimises and implements measurement solutions for manufacturing quality control. Our expertise covers surface and 3D coordinate metrology using tactile and optical probes as well as X-ray Computed Tomography (XCT). We target Industry 4.0 readiness of measurement solutions by increasing speed, reducing measurement errors, and establishing traceability to realise in-line and in-process capabilities that intelligently feedback inspection results for first-time-right and zero-waste manufacturing. We put our expertise and state-of-the-art equipment at the disposal of manufacturing companies to address complex metrology challenges and to improve manufacturing process understanding and performance. Responsibilities X-ray computed tomography (XCT) is a non-destructive volumetric imaging technology that can image both external and internal structures of parts. The technology has been increasingly used for industrial applications. However, the cost and time consumed to conduct XCT scans are significant for industrial use in the uptake of the technology. Hence, most XCTs are used for research rather than for production purposes. Recent developments have demonstrated the potential of using XCT to assess the quality of battery cells. However, there is currently no guidance on how to perform dimensional evaluation for such specialised applications, and the impact of systematic influence factors and measurement errors remains largely unknown. This project aims to develop a robust data analysis workflow that converts XCT measurement outputs into reliable, interpretable quality metrics. As part of this project, you will join a supportive team of research scientists working together to advance battery quality evaluation using XCT. You’ll have the chance to learn new skills, contribute your own ideas, and grow your expertise while shaping your future career path. Profile Candidate Must Hold a Master's degree in Maths, Computer Science, Physics, Engineering, or the equivalent. Has distinction in Master degree. Be knowledgeable in areas such as statistical analysis, imaging processing and analysis, machine learning Experience in X-ray computed tomography or instrument calibration is considered an asset. Other General Requirement Has a scientific curiosity and interest in research. Has strong mathematical and computational skills. Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Has the necessary skills to design and implement experiments, undertake computational tasks, and analyse measurement results. Has adequate English communication skills and can present results competently and comprehensively in research team meetings, conferences and peer-reviewed journal papers. Is flexible and has good time management skills. Can work independently and have good interactions with the co/supervisors and peers. Frequently report the progress of the conducted research to the co/supervisors. Is willing to help organise workshops and other events. Is willing to engage in teaching assignments. Is willing to travel nationally or internationally to visit collaborators to conduct work. Offer The opportunity to pursue a PhD degree that is fully supported for 4 years. The project can start immediately following the completion of recruitment. Interested? The applicant should provide the following information in the application: An academic CV Bachelor degree (Bachelor specification, University + Country, Year obtained), score Master degree (Master specification, University + Country, Year obtained), Master thesis if any (Title, Year, Supervisor), score A one-paragraph (maximum one page) statement explaining the motivation for applying for this PhD position. Two academic references For more information please contact Prof. dr. Wenjuan Sun, mail: wenjuan.sun@kuleuven.be or dr. Maryam Ramezani, mail: maryam.ramezani@kuleuven.be. You can apply for this job no later than December 18, 2026 via the online application tool KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. linkedin:4483676432.title: Doctoral student in AI-powered Asset Health Indices for Smart Maintenance
linkedin:4483676432.desc: How can artificial intelligence help predict equipment degradation and enable smarter maintenance decisions? At Chalmers University of Technology, you will explore this question by developing AI-powered methods for assessing and predicting the health of industrial assets. We are looking for a Doctoral student to become part of our team at the Division of Production Systems in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. Please join our innovative team and contribute to exciting research on Production systems, AI-supported condition assessment, and maintenance decision-making in a collaborative and dynamic environment. About Us The Division of Production Systems works with the sustainability and competitiveness of industrial production systems. The research area is system-oriented and requires knowledge about both the system as a whole and its separate components, for example humans, automation, and processes. The research highlights the different stages of a production system’s life cycle, i.e. planning, design, commissioning, operation, maintenance and reuse. Methods and research findings are generic, with applications within various industries, such as automotive, aerospace, processing and mining industries. The people in the division form an internationally diverse, gender-balanced, and inclusive team of more than 30 cross-disciplinary researchers and support staff. Our strong international collaborative networks and advanced research infrastructure, Stena Industry Innovation Lab, make us a competitive international actor. The Production Systems Division is part of Chalmers largest unit, the Department of Mechanical Engineering, where we unite the power of technology, people, and society to drive the transition toward a sustainable future. The department is highly ranked internationally. Through research, education, and collaboration, we create solutions that connect materials to mobility, ideas to impact – shaping a resilient and sustainable world. About The Research Project The research will develop and evaluate AI-powered Asset Health Index models that combine heterogeneous condition data, maintenance information, operational data, and expert knowledge into transparent indicators of asset condition and degradation. The work will investigate how artificial intelligence can strengthen model development, support prognostics and Remaining Useful Life estimation, and turn complex data into useful information for maintenance and asset-management decisions. Through close academic and industrial collaboration, the project will validate the models in a real-world pilot environment, with emphasis on general methods for condition assessment, risk analysis, maintenance prioritisation, and lifecycle-oriented decision support for complex technical assets. Who We Are Looking For The following requirements are mandatory: To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree (masterexamen) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree (magisterexamen) of 60 credits* in Mechanical Engineering, Production Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Automation, Data Science, Computer Science, or another relevant field. Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. You should have a strong interest in maintenance, asset management, data-driven engineering, artificial intelligence, or prognostics and health management. A strong candidate is highly motivated, self-driven and curious, with excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative research environment. for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted. The Following Experience Will Strengthen Your Application Prior expertise and experience in Asset Health Index (AHI) Data analysis, machine learning, statistical modelling, or optimisation Maintenance engineering, reliability, condition monitoring, prognostics, or asset management Working with heterogeneous industrial data, including structured and unstructured information Programming and development of decision-support or simulation models Academic or industrial collaboration in multidisciplinary environments What You Will Do Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Product and Production Development (Product and production development | Chalmers) Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing Develop and validate Asset Health Index models by combining condition data, maintenance information, operational data, and expert knowledge Explore AI-supported methods for prognostics, Remaining Useful Life estimation, transparent model interpretation, and maintenance decision support Implement, test, and demonstrate models and decision-support concepts together with other researchers and industry participants in laboratory and real-world pilot environments The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours Contract terms The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start. The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years. A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026). Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn. What We Offer As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about working at Chalmers and our benefits for employees. A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg. Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg. Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence. We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities. If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in. Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here. Application procedure The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files. CV Personal letter A brief introduction about yourself. A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position. Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts. Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form. A background check may be conducted as part of the application process. Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview. We welcome your application no later than November 30th, 2026. For Questions, Please Contact Johan Stahre Professor of Production Systems, Division manager johan.stahre@chalmers.se Anders Skoogh Professor of Maintenance Engineering anders.skoogh@chalmers.se We look forward to your application! linkedin:4483687354.desc: About The Position Are you motivated to pursue a doctoral degree and explore how mobile networks can work together to keep critical services running when facing failures or congestion? The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU has a vacancy for a PhD Candidate in Resilient Service Continuity Across Mobile Networks. As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a range of leading positions in business, administration, higher education and research. The position is fully funded and will run for 4 years (100 % employment), including teaching duties. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Discipline, and the workplace will be in Trondheim. About The Project Mobile networks increasingly support critical services in emergency response, industry, transport, and maritime operations. Access to several networks can improve resilience, but sustaining a service requires more than restoring connectivity. Independently operated networks must coordinate resources and priorities while managing dependencies and commitments to existing users. They may also depend on shared infrastructure or capacity leased from one another, limiting the resilience gained from access to multiple operators. Norway’s plans for a new emergency network (Nødnett) over commercial mobile infrastructure illustrate the relevance of these broader challenges. About As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how mobile networks can cooperate to maintain critical services during failures, congestion, and recovery. Your research will address networks that retain their own operational policies and exchange limited information about capacity and internal state, developing insights applicable across public and private networks. A specific focus will be on the networked systems mechanisms, data paths, and open interfaces needed to support resilient service continuity in multi-operator mobile network systems, addressing research questions such as: What information must networks exchange to make effective admission and resource-allocation decisions without requiring full visibility into each other’s infrastructure? How can service priorities and resource policies be coordinated across heterogeneous networks, including during congestion and large bursts of registration requests? How can network selection, traffic steering, and recovery mechanisms maintain application continuity while avoiding repeated switching and overload cascades? How do shared infrastructure, leased capacity, and dependencies between operators affect failure propagation and the resilience gained from alternative network access? With the Beyond 5G lab at the department, the project will emphasize experimental systems research: you will have the opportunity to conduct your research in both commercial and open-source mobile network deployments and test your ideas under realistic conditions. To explore conditions beyond the scale of the physical deployments, methods including simulation and analytical modeling can be a complementary building block. Duties of the position Complete doctoral education and obtain a doctorate Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above Academic publications and popular science dissemination Participate in the Networking research group Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions Teaching in courses related to networking Other career-enhancing work Some changes to your work duties may occur after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in Information Security and Communication Technology, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information. You must have a relevant master's degree in communication networks, wireless and mobile communications, information security and distributed systems, or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis. Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and preferably within August 2027. You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. If you are in your master’s program, integrated PhD could be an option. Your MSc grades after your fourth year need to be completed with a grade B or better, in addition the IE-faculty require that your bachelor degree is completed with a grade C or better. Integrated PhD - Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering - NTNU. Excellent oral and written presentation skills in English. The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria Practical experience with 5G radio access and core deployments. Hands-on experience with communication networks including multi-vendor and softwarized environments. Exposure to resilience and dependability topics in the context of communication networks as part of the master’s curriculum. Teaching experience, preferably at master’s level. Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language. Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are Highly motivated by fundamental scientific research with practical relevance. Able to work independently. Able to work in a structured way, set goals, and make plans to achieve them. Eager to disseminate research results both locally as well as through publications and presentations at international conferences. In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal suitability, as well as motivation, in terms of the qualifications specified in the advertisement. We offer An exciting job with an important mission in society Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. The successful candidate will be granted conditional admission to the relevant doctoral programme when employed in the PhD position. It is a prerequisite for continued employment that the requirements for full admission are met within three months, and that you continue to participate in the organized doctoral programme for the remainder of the employment period. For more information about the requirements for full admission, please see Section 6 of the PhD regulations. As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps and thermal energy storage. Your project will develop new Carnot Battery technologies: systems that combine heat pumps based on high temperature thermodynamic cycles together with high-temperature thermal energy storage, such as molten salts and dual-media packed beds. These systems will deliver clean process heat while also giving industry flexibility on the electricity market. Supervision: Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli and Prof. Anders Christiansen Erlandsson with industrial secondments. You will work with fellow doctoral candidates across the network and with industrial partners in Denmark and abroad. Your main tasks will be: Develop and Design new architectures comprising cycles using natural working fluids and thermal energy storage, optimised for efficiency, cost, and fast response to electricity price signals Carry out multi-objective optimisation and dynamic system analysis of alternative layouts Validate results by carrying out experiments and data comparison during industrial secondments, turning the results into innovations with real-world impact (e.g. patents, future commercial solutions) Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach. Are you passionate about advancing renewable energy technologies? Do you want to develop cutting-edge computational frameworks that shape the future of sustainable energy? Join us in solving key challenges in decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors. You will work on ensuring these pathways operate within planetary boundaries while meeting stringent criteria for cost-effectiveness, safety, and operational resilience. Key Research Questions: How can the intermittent nature of renewable electricity production be economically decoupled from further chemical processing of eFuels and eChemicals? How can the technical, economic, and environmental feasibility of the PtX value chain be maximized under operational and market uncertainty? You will be directly supervised by Prof. Rofice Dickson and work alongside a vibrant, multidisciplinary team of PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and industrial partners. The unique competitive edge of the Department of Chemical and Metallurgical Engineering in the School of Chemical Engineering is based on sustainable utilization of raw materials, designing more efficient processes, and developing new materials and products. linkedin:4484059870.desc: At AAU Energy, a PhD stipend is available within the general study programme in Electrical and Electronic Engineering. The stipend is open for appointment from 1 December 2026 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years and the position is full-time. Your work tasks The position is offered in relation to the GreenMag project, and you will be positioned in the Section of Power Electronics Systems and Materials within the research programme Sustainable Power Electronics and Electrification (SPELL) at AAU Energy, Aalborg University. You will be based at the Aalborg campus in a highly international research environment with close collaboration with academic and industrial partners in the field of power electronics and energy systems. The increasing electrification of transport, industry and renewable energy systems is driving the development of high-power-density power converters operating at megawatt levels. Advanced planar magnetic components are emerging as a key technology for achieving higher power density, manufacturability and integration in such converters. However, thermal management remains one of the major challenges that limit the performance, reliability and scalability of planar magnetic solutions, especially at high power and high frequency. In this PhD project, you will work on the development of innovative thermal management technologies for megawatt planar magnetics used in future electrification systems. Your research will combine advanced modelling, experimental validation and prototype development to improve heat dissipation and thermal reliability while maintaining the required electrical and magnetic performance. You will analyse thermal behaviour and heat transfer mechanisms in high-power planar magnetic components, design and evaluate cooling concepts and contribute to the integration of these solutions in realistic converter systems. You will conduct cutting-edge research on thermal behaviour and heat transfer mechanisms in megawatt-class planar magnetic components and use this knowledge to propose and evaluate new design strategies. You will develop multiphysics simulation models using finite element modelling tools to investigate the thermal performance of planar magnetics and to study alternative cooling concepts and material choices. You will design, manufacture and experimentally validate novel thermal management solutions for planar magnetic structures, and you will explore advanced materials and cooling technologies that can be applied in megawatt-class magnetic components. As part of the GreenMag project, you will collaborate with academic and industrial partners, disseminate your research results through publications in international journals and conferences, and contribute to teaching and supervision activities within the department as part of the PhD education programme. Your competencies You have a relevant educational background within Power Electronics, Electrical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, Energy Engineering or a closely related field, and you hold a Master’s degree that qualifies you for enrolment in the PhD programme. You are motivated to work at the interface between thermal science, electromagnetics and power electronics, and you are interested in both theoretical and experimental research. You bring strong analytical skills and a structured approach to modelling and problem solving, and you are comfortable working with numerical tools for thermal and multiphysics analysis. Experience with thermal analysis, power electronics or magnetic component design will be considered an advantage, as will experience with finite element analysis tools such as COMSOL Multiphysics or ANSYS. It is beneficial if you have worked with experimental testing, prototype development or laboratory work in previous projects and if you are prepared to work with both simulation and hands-on experiments in this PhD. As a person, you are curious and creative, and you are motivated by addressing challenging research questions in collaboration with others. Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, are required, as you will present your results in scientific publications, at international conferences and in meetings with project partners. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. At AAU Energy, you will be part of a highly international environment where research, innovation and collaboration are used to develop solutions to global challenges associated with electrification and the green transition. The department has campuses in Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs approximately 300 staff members from a broad range of nationalities and disciplinary backgrounds, creating a vibrant international research environment with extensive opportunities for collaboration and professional growth. The department offers world-class laboratory and workshop facilities, and maintains close collaboration with industrial partners. As a PhD student, you will have access to advanced facilities for the design, manufacturing and testing of high-power magnetic components and power electronic systems, and you will be part of an active research community in Sustainable Power Electronics and Electrification. With significant committed Irish government support, Tyndall will grow to be 1,000 people by 2030, with approximately 750 researchers, including 250 PhD students. A new 17,000 m2 research building is under development adjacent to the Cork headquarters and there are developing plans to expand Tyndall’s existing Dublin research labs and to establish other research sites within Ireland. Tyndall’s expansion is also supported by recent national and EU funding wins for significant (M€10’s) additional research equipment across a range of areas such as semiconductor processing, microscopy, quantum technologies, heterogeneous integration, ultra-high speed optical communications and RF through THz characterisation. About Rinn Semiconductor Rinn Semiconductors is part of a constellation of seven major new centres which collectively represent an investment of €460M in advanced research by the Government of Ireland. Rinn Semiconductors aims to lead Ireland’s response to the end of Moore’s Law scaling, the point where traditional improvements in computer chips slows down or ends, by pioneering modular integrated circuit-based (chiplet-based) semiconductor design and integration. With deep expertise in the areas of Heterogeneous Integration and Advanced Packaging, the Rinn Semiconductors team propose to enable transformative advances in these technologies and to apply them in three main application areas: Future Internet, Sustainable Energy and Environment, and Digital Healthcare. A key objective of the Rinn is to foster deep collaboration across the seven universities and institutions involved, by leveraging the semiconductor fabrication facilities at Tyndall, ultimately creating a cohesive “atom to systems” value chain in Ireland, connecting everything from basic materials research through to complete technology solutions. The Rinn will operate in close collaboration with Ireland’s vibrant semiconductor industry sector which supports 20,000 high skilled jobs and includes world leading multinational companies, small and medium sized enterprises and start-ups. The successful applicant will: Join a world-class and highly diverse community of more than 100 PhD students, more than a 100 Postdoctoral Researchers and around 35 experienced PIs and Research Fellows Engage with over 30 industry partners to learn about their work and future career opportunities Become an in-house entrepreneur and explore the opportunity to commercialise your research through a Spin-Out company Follow in the footsteps of our current trainees where over 86% of PhDs have transitioned into industry with some of the world’s leading semiconductor companies, in Ireland and the EU. If you aspire to be a future PI and academic research leader our programme will support you to build your research track record and vision, equipping you to take the next steps on your career journey. About the Role The CARE (Digital Healthcare) theme at Rinn Semiconductor, Ireland’s Centre for Semiconductor Innovation, hosted at Tyndall National Institute (a research flagship of University College Cork, UCC), is offering a fully funded PhD position focused on the design of photonic integrated circuits (PICs) for Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging (FLIM) in next-generation endoscopy. This research sits within CARE 1, which aims to develop a compact, single-use multimodal photonic integrated circuit endoscope for colorectal inflammation and early-stage cancer diagnostics. Antimicrobial resistance and cross-contamination from reusable endoscopes are major global health burdens, while current gastrointestinal endoscopes remain bulky, costly, and limited to surface-level RGB imaging. By combining innovations in integrated silicon photonics and heterogeneous semiconductor integration, CARE 1 will deliver a low-cost, ultra-compact, single-use endoscope that adds FLIM-based molecular and metabolic imaging to conventional RGB imaging, giving clinicians transformative diagnostic insight in vivo, with clinical demonstration in the advanced endoscopy unit at Cork University Hospital. This PhD will tackle the photonic heart of that system: the design of a foundry-compatible PIC and pulsing scheme for a UV/violet (375–400 nm) source capable of the low repetition rate and pulse characteristics required for nanosecond-scale lifetime measurements. The work spans simulation, design, and experimental validation of pulsed laser architectures, culminating in a packaging-ready PIC design for FLIM biophotonics. Key Duties & Responsibilities Explore mode-locking strategies for a UV 375–400 nm laser, including long Al₂O₃ spiral cavity design, pulse picking with amplification, and gain-switching with amplification (HCSEL) schemes. Design a first-generation, foundry-compatible full-system PIC for FLIM. Experimentally test and benchmark the optimal pulsing scheme (at the Tyndall fabrication facility or with an external foundry partner). Develop a second-generation, foundry-compatible PIC incorporating experimental feedback, optimised toward a packaging-ready design. Participate in Education and Public Engagement activities. Ensure compliance with Tyndall’s Quality Management Systems, Health and Safety standards, and other regulations. Essential Criteria Must hold a master's degree, or an equivalent qualifying degree in Physics, Semiconductor, Photonics or a related discipline to enroll in the PhD programme. Strong academic background in photonics, optics, electronic engineering, or a related discipline. Solid grounding in integrated photonics and/or laser physics (waveguides, cavities, laser operation). Proficiency in a relevant programming/simulation language (e.g., Python, MATLAB, C++). Must meet UCC's postgraduate English language requirements through a recognized test qualification or an approved institution exemption. Desirable Criteria Experience with photonic simulation and design tools (e.g., Lumerical, COMSOL, or PIC design/layout environments). Familiarity with pulsed laser sources (mode-locking, gain-switching) and PIC foundry design flows / PDKs. Interest in semiconductor fabrication and heterogeneous integration. Enthusiasm for translational, application-driven research with real clinical impact in digital healthcare. Demonstrate a strong desire to innovate and pursue advanced research through relevant skills and project experience. What We Offer Full PhD funding, including tuition fees and a tax-free stipend. A position within Rinn Semiconductor — Ireland’s Centre for Semiconductor Innovation, working at the interface of photonics, semiconductors, and digital healthcare. Access to world-class fabrication and characterisation facilities at Tyndall National Institute / UCC. Cross-theme collaboration with the HET (heterogeneous integration), NET, and PACK (packaging) themes, alongside an extensive network of industry and clinical partners. The opportunity to contribute to a next-generation medical diagnostic platform with direct clinical translation. Supervision Supervisor: HET (Heterogeneous Integration) theme. Co-supervisor: Biophotonics team (design focus). Cross-theme links: HET, PACK. Terms of Studentship The annual stipend is €25,000.00. In addition, annual tuition fees will be paid by the Tyndall National Institute. Duration of Study: 4 years Informal enquiries can be made in confidence to supervisor Zhi Li The closing date for applications is Tuesday 24th November at 1pm. Application Instructions Please make sure to attach an up-to-date CV/Resume AND a brief motivation letter outlining how you meet the ‘Essential Criteria’ for this role. Postgraduate applicants whose first language is not English must provide evidence of English language proficiency as per UCC regulations (https://www.ucc.ie/en/study/comparison/english/postgraduate/). Certificates should be valid (usually less than 2 years old) and should be uploaded with their application.

indeed:fc289a8280ab6ba8.title: PhD Student in Aptamer-Enabled, Animal-Free Bioanalysis
indeed:fc289a8280ab6ba8.desc: Category: Education Location: Måløv, Capital Region of Denmark, DK Department: CMC Development & Scaling, Global Manufacturing & Supply Location: Måløv, Denmark Your impact begins here Take scientific ownership of a new analytical technology built on aptamers: functional DNA or RNA binders. As PhD Student in Aptamer-Enabled, Animal-Free Bioanalysis, you will turn aptamer discovery into automated, reproducible methods and test them against established assays. Your work could help reduce reliance on animal-derived reagents in the assays that support clinical drug candidates, and bring new science into pharmaceutical practice. What you’ll bring You are a curious, self-driven scientist who is excited by applied research between academia and industry. You have: A relevant MSc degree, supported by BSc-level training, in molecular biology, molecular medicine, chemistry, biochemistry, nanoscience or a closely related discipline. Recent graduates and candidates expecting to complete their MSc by the end of Q1 2027 are welcome to apply. A strong interest or experience in nucleic acid research, aptamer development, bioanalysis and laboratory work. An organised, flexible approach to complex experimental work, and the confidence to drive a project independently while using academic and industrial supervision. Strong collaboration and communication skills across disciplines and organisations, and fluent written and spoken English. Useful, but not essential: Experience with in vitro selection, enzymatic nucleic acid synthesis and purification, biophysical characterisation and/or next-generation sequencing analysis. Experience with bioanalytical assay development, laboratory automation or liquid handlers, or knowledge of protein–protein interactions and protein purification. What you’ll do You will own the scientific direction of the project within the agreed scope, supported by your supervisors. You will: Generate, select and characterise DNA- and/or RNA-based aptamers using nucleic acid chemistry, in vitro evolution and nanotechnology tools. Develop and optimise fit-for-purpose bioanalysis methods, assessing specificity, robustness, reproducibility, throughput and transferability. Automate aptamer generation, screening and assay workflows on liquid-handling platforms. Benchmark new assay formats against established analytical methods. Assess how novel assays could be introduced in pharmaceutical development and quality control, including GxP and regulatory expectations. Document and publish your results, complete your PhD requirements and share your learning across Aarhus University and Novo. Who you’ll work with In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain from drug and device development to marketed Novo products. You will join CMC Bioanalysis in Måløv, part of CMC Development & Scaling, which develops assays for cell banks, in-process samples, drug substance and drug product across the global clinical project portfolio. Your future team has 18 colleagues with deep biological-assay expertise, a can-do mindset and strong team spirit. You will be enrolled in the Graduate School of Natural Sciences at Aarhus University, joining a nucleic acid research environment working across DNA, RNA and XNA. Academic and industrial supervisors will support you throughout, and supervision meetings continue whether you are in Aarhus or Måløv. This project moves between two research environments. You will start in Aarhus, then spend a substantial period in Måløv. The order and length of each period may change as the science progresses. What you can expect here You will be trusted to own your project and supported to do it well. Expect interdisciplinary training, access to expertise across Aarhus University and Novo, and relevant courses, seminars and research meetings. You will gain first-hand insight into the pharmaceutical product life cycle and the quality and regulatory framework for biological and recombinant products. Salary: For this role, the Monthly Base Salary is 40.145,48 DKK, corresponding to the years of employment as PhD Student. Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here. Start now Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn aptamer science into methods that move pharmaceutical bioanalysis forward, apply by 8 November 2026. Please include a letter of motivation, your CV with any publications and research experience, reference letter(s) from previous academic supervisors if available, and documentation of your completed MSc degree with BSc and MSc transcripts (including weighted grade averages and English translations where applicable). For further information, please contact Senior Research Scientist Ali Shahrokhtash at axoj@novonordisk.com or Scientific Director Jan Amstrup at jaam@novonordisk.com. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

indeed:04d8260632a3005a.title: Doctoral Student in Magnetic Resonance for the Study of Granular Systems
indeed:04d8260632a3005a.desc: Doctoral Student in Magnetic Resonance for the Study of Granular Systems 100%, Zurich, fixed-term ETH Zurich is one of the leading universities worldwide and renowned for its excellence in education, fundamental and applied research, and technology transfer. At the Institute for Biomedical Engineering, one research focus is on nuclear magnetic resonance. The team of Prof. Klaas Prüssmann drives innovation in magnetic resonance from physical and mathematical principles all the way to novel imaging, sensing, and tracking technology. In close collaboration with academic and industrial partners, we pursue applications in the biomedical realm, process engineering, and materials science. One recent focus of interest is on the use of magnetic resonance for particle tracking in granular systems. We are looking for a Physicist or Engineer to join us on this frontier as a Doctoral Student. Project background Granular systems are ubiquitous in nature and of fundamental importance to industry, from food and pharma to material conversion. However, despite their widespread occurence and use, many important phenomena such as the transition between flowing and solid states, mixing, segregation, or surface instabilities, are poorly understood. Magnetic resonance has proven a powerful means of studying granular physics, permitting both dynamic imaging and, newly, the tracking of particle swarms. The focus is now on further expanding the tracking strategies and, in the applied realm, on exploring the role of the shape of particles and how granular dynamics change when particles are soft and deform upon stress. The project is a shared effort with ETH colleagues in process engineering and encompasses two Doctoral Student positions, one each at the Institute for Biomedical Engineering (Prof. Prüssmann) and the Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering (Prof. Müller). The two Doctoral Researchers will benefit from immersion in both environments and are foreseen to collaborate closely. Job description The objective of the Doctoral Student hired by the Institute for Biomedical Engineering is to advance magnetic resonance technology and methods towards the study of granular systems made up of arbitrarily shaped and soft particles. This will include work on principles of particle tracking and imaging, creation of new methods, implementation on magnetic resonance equipment, all the way to experimental exploration and use in granular systems. The collaborative effort with the partner Doctoral Student will particularly target the fabrication of tailored and soft particles, applied studies in granular systems science, and the creation of experimental setups to this end. Profile Applicants for this position are expected to have a Master’s degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering, or from another program with substantial coverage of Physics and Mathematics. The position also requires a good command of English, both oral and written. We highly value: Analytical strength Intellectual rigor Creativity Passion for both abstract thought and practical implementation Intrinsic motivation Team orientation Previous experience with magnetic resonance or granular systems is a benefit but not a requirement. Workplace Workplace We offer An opportunity to do leading research Membership in a dynamic, collegial team of diverse backgrounds An exciting academic environment Excellent infrastructure Excellent perspectives for career development A competitive salary We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values, ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future. Curious? So are we. We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents: A brief motivation letter (up to half a page) CV Transcripts (Bachelor and Master) Names of two potential reference providers Further information about the Department and Institute can be found on the following websites: D-ITET and Institute for Biomedical Engineering. Questions regarding the position should be directed to Klaas Prüssmann at pruesmann@biomed.ee.ethz.ch (no applications). Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered. The position is to be filled at the earliest mutually convenient date.

indeed:d4ca4422bae9aaa1.title: Doctoral Positions in Exoplanet Atmosphere Characterisation and the Search for Life
indeed:d4ca4422bae9aaa1.desc: Doctoral Positions in Exoplanet Atmosphere Characterisation and the Search for Life 100%, Zurich, fixed-term We are looking for one or two Doctoral Students to work on the atmospheric characterisation of temperate terrestrial exoplanets and the search for life within the Exoplanets and Habitability Group led by Prof. Sascha P. Quanz at ETH Zurich. The positions is closely connected to the ETH-led LIFE space mission. LIFE is a space-based mid-infrared nulling interferometer to directly detect and spectroscopically characterise dozens of temperate terrestrial exoplanets around nearby stars. The successful candidates will join the LIFE Science Team and work closely with researchers and students at ETH Zurich and across the wider LIFE collaboration. Project background A central goal of LIFE is to characterise the atmospheres of temperate terrestrial exoplanets and ultimately assess their habitability and possible signs of life. Understanding which atmospheric properties can be robustly inferred from mid-infrared observations is also essential for translating LIFE's science goals into science requirements and corresponding instrument-performance requirements. Our group has developed the atmospheric retrieval framework pyRetLIFE and has so far investigated mainly Earth-like planets and classical atmospheric biosignature gases. An important next step is to broaden this work towards the diversity of potentially habitable and inhabited worlds: different atmospheric compositions and climates, non-Earth-like biospheres, non-standard biosignatures, and the abiotic scenarios against which potential signs of life need to be interpreted. Possible research directions for the successful Doctoral students include The modelling and characterisation of non-Earth-like atmospheres and biospheres, using physically motivated atmospheric models and retrievals to understand which properties and potential biosignatures future missions like LIFE can robustly constrain The exploration of alternative inference approaches, including machine learning and AI, for atmospheric characterisation and the interpretation of potential signs of life, this could include investigating where such methods provide additional information compared with conventional retrievals, and assessing their robustness, interpretability and sensitivity to modelling assumptions Job description Develop and pursue research on the characterisation of temperate terrestrial exoplanet atmospheres and the search for signs of life in the context of the LIFE mission Investigate atmospheric scenarios beyond modern Earth analogues; this may include non-Earth-like biospheres, non-standard biosignatures and/or relevant abiotic alternatives Use and further develop atmospheric retrieval and/or complementary modelling and inference approaches Explore, where relevant, ML/AI approaches for atmospheric inference and interpretation Investigate the robustness and limitations of atmospheric characterisation methods and compare complementary approaches where scientifically useful In close collaboration with the LIFE Science Team and LIFE Instrument Science Team, translate atmospheric characterisation results into science requirements and related instrument-performance requirements for LIFE Contribute new scientific ideas to the development of the LIFE science case and interact with the broader LIFE collaboration Profile Master's degree (or equivalent degree) in astrophysics, planetary science, atmospheric science, physics or a closely related field, completed by the start date Strong interest in exoplanet science, atmospheres, habitability, biosignatures and the search for life Experience in one or more of the following is welcome, but not required: atmospheric modelling, atmospheric retrievals, radiative transfer, photochemical or climate modelling, statistical inference, machine-learning/AI methods, or related numerical approaches Strong scientific programming skills, preferably in Python; experience with AI and machine learning tools is an asset Ability and interest to work in a team and across disciplinary boundaries Ability to interact with the broader exoplanet, atmospheric science and astrobiology communities Scientific curiosity, independence and a collaborative approach to research Very good command of English (spoken and written) Workplace Workplace We offer A collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment within the Exoplanets and Habitability Group and the LIFE Space Mission team at ETH Zurich, with close links to the international LIFE collaboration A fully funded four-year Doctoral Position with competitive salary and benefits according to ETH regulations, including support for conference travel, computing and career development We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values, ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future. Curious? So are we. We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents: CV University transcripts and, if already available, diploma A statement of research interests (max. 2 pages), indicating which of the research directions described above you would be particularly interested in pursuing. Names and contact details of three referees The application deadline is November 25, 2026. The start date is flexible, but we envision to start in spring / early summer 2027. Further information about the group can be found on our website. Questions regarding the position and informal enquiries are welcome and should be directed to Prof. Sascha P. Quanz, sascha.quanz@phys.ethz.ch. Please note that applications must be submitted exclusively through our online application portal; applications sent by email or post will not be considered. We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

indeed:84789c8209f4163b.title: AstraZeneca funded Non-clinical PhD Studentship in Improved 2A peptides for co-translational separation of a polyprotein
indeed:84789c8209f4163b.desc: Applications are invited for a 4-year PhD studentship starting on 1 October 2027 and based in the Department of Pathology, University of Cambridge, and the AstraZeneca Discovery Centre at Cambridge. The student will be working on a collaborative project jointly supervised by Prof. Andrew Firth at the University of Cambridge and Dr Giovanni Ciotta at AstraZeneca and will have the opportunity to work across the two sites. The project focuses on manipulating peptide-bond skipping sequences to aid protein engineering. 2A peptides mediate co-translational separation of a polyprotein via a mechanism known as "ribosome skipping" or "StopGo". These ~20 amino acid peptides adopt an unusual conformation within the translating ribosome that prevents peptide bond formation at a specific site, but instead promotes release of the nascent peptide followed by continuation of translation. These sequences have proved to be exceptionally useful in biotechnology because they allow the introduction of all components of a pathway or multi-subunit complex in a single step, with stable stoichiometric co-expression from a single promoter. However, 2A peptides have some caveats ¿ including ribosome drop-off, ribosome pausing/stalling, and some amount of separation failure ¿ which constrain their functional utility. We have identified new classes of 2A sequences, some of which have improved properties compared to traditional 2A peptides. This PhD project will contribute to our work investigating these new 2A sequences and optimising them for biotechnological applications. The UCam team has expertise in molecular biology including ribosome profiling, ribosome structure and function, cell biology, cryo-electron microscopy, and bioinformatics. The AZ team has expertise in cell therapy, CRISPR/Cas9 technologies, and viral vectors. The PhD project will focus on molecular biology techniques but there will also be opportunity for bioinformatic skill development and there may be scope to obtain structural biology experience. At the AstraZeneca site, the student will focus on implementing optimised sequences in specific biotechnological applications, e.g. in cell therapy. Candidate We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic individual capable of thinking and working independently. Applicants should have or shortly expect to obtain a first or upper second-class degree from a UK university, or an equivalent standard from an overseas university, in a relevant subject such as Biochemistry, Microbiology, Cell Biology or Genetics. These positions are open to UK citizens or overseas students who meet the UK residency requirements (home fees) or are able to augment the funds to cover the extra costs associated with international student fees through scholarships or funding schemes. Students will not be allowed to supplement fees via self funding. Full details of the University's entrance requirements and scholarships are specified on the following link: https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/ Additionally, the Department requires that by the time of interview all potential students must have fulfilled the language requirements for admission: http://www.graduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/blpapdpth/requirements Please check for further eligibility details using this website: https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/finance/fees/what-my-fee-status Application Process All applications should be made online via the University's Applicant Portal for a PhD in Pathology (BLPA22). A completed application must be submitted by the closing date below. Please also explain your motivation why you wish to pursue a PhD in this area, outline your research interests and background, and describe the qualities and experience you will bring to the role. Please also download our equal opportunities monitoring form from this link and return the completed form by email to postgrad@path.cam.ac.uk An application is only complete when all supporting documents, including the equal opportunities monitoring form, and the two academic references, are submitted. It is the applicant's responsibility to ensure their referees submit their references before the closing date of the studentship. Funding Full funding covering Maintenance fees (expected to start at approx. £23,805 p.a.) and the University Composition Fee is provided for the studentship, with effect from 1 October 2027. Student support and training As a graduate student at Cambridge, you will have access to a wide range of training opportunities. During their PhD, there is no taught or examined coursework, but students are encouraged to attend the wide variety of lectures and training courses available to them across the Department and wider University. This includes a centrally run Statistics course and the University Core Skills Training Programme, which includes sessions on Time Management, Presentation and Performance and Scientific Writing. linkedin:4484425686.title: PhD Student in Artificial Intelligence: Causal Modelling and Multi-Agent Systems
linkedin:4484425686.desc: The University of Applied Sciences and Arts of Southern Switzerland (SUPSI) invites applications for a PhD Student in Artificial Intelligence: Causal Modelling and Multi-Agent Systems , at the Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence (IDSIA USI-SUPSI) within the Department of Innovative Technologies (DTI), located in Lugano. The degree of employment is 100%, with a contract starting on 01.02.2027, or on a mutually agreed date. Scope and purpose of the position The position is part of the research project Formal Epistemology of Human-AI Interactions, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). The project studies the conditions under which interactions between humans and artificial intelligence (AI) systems are epistemically reliable. The project aims to develop formal methods to represent, analyse and mathematically optimise human–AI interaction protocols. It takes into account factors such as how disagreements are handled, human oversight, interaction costs, and epistemic and governance constraints. The work includes developing causal-probabilistic models and evaluating them through multi-agent simulations in two application domains: neurological intensive care and cybersecurity. The project involves an interdisciplinary team with expertise in mathematics, logic, formal epistemology and artificial intelligence. It works with IDSIA research groups specialising in causal-probabilistic modelling and computational methods. It is also carried out in collaboration with Delft University of Technology and the University Hospital Zurich Duties and responsibilities Developing causal-probabilistic models to represent and analyse human–AI interaction protocols. Studying and implementing mathematical optimisation methods for protocols, taking into account performance, costs, and epistemic and governance constraints. Developing multi-agent simulation environments to evaluate protocols in the project’s two application domains (neurological intensive care and cybersecurity). Contributing to the project’s interdisciplinary activities and to the evaluation of results with domain experts. Writing scientific publications and presenting results at leading international conferences and journals in artificial intelligence, computer science and philosophy (e.g. NeurIPS, AAAI, FAccT, Synthese and Minds & Machines). Requirements Technical background and skills Master’s degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, mathematics, data science or a related field. Strong mathematical knowledge, particularly in probability and statistics, and knowledge of artificial intelligence and machine learning methods. Basic knowledge in at least one of: probabilistic modelling, causal inference, mathematical optimisation, or multi-agent systems. Good programming skills, preferably in Python, and experience implementing and evaluating computational models. Interest in the epistemological and ethical aspects of AI and in interdisciplinary research on human–AI interaction. Aptitude for original scientific research, ability to work both in a team and independently, scientific curiosity and strong motivation for research. Excellent command of English, spoken and written. Employment is conditional on admission to and enrolment in the PhD in Informatics at the Università della Svizzera italiana (USI) or the USI-SUPSI PhD programme in Applied Data Science and Artificial Intelligence Desirable but not strictly required Advanced knowledge of, or project or research experience in, at least one of: causal and probabilistic modelling, multi-agent systems, mathematical optimisation, or simulation of intelligent systems. Prior research experience, documented through academic projects, a Master’s thesis or other scientific activities. Scientific publications or preprints in international conferences and journals, preferably in areas relevant to the project. Experience with libraries and frameworks for probabilistic modelling, causal inference, mathematical optimisation or multi-agent simulation (e.g. pgmpy, PyMC, CVXPY, Google ADK or equivalent). What SUPSI Offers Fixed-term contract. Fully funded PhD. The opportunity to carry out original doctoral research with a significant degree of scientific autonomy, at the intersection of artificial intelligence, mathematics and formal epistemology. An international, interdisciplinary research environment, with scientific supervision by experts in AI, mathematical modelling and epistemology, and collaborations with Delft University of Technology and the University Hospital Zurich. Opportunities for international research mobility, participation in conferences and workshops, and publication in leading venues. Advanced training and professional development opportunities within the PhD programme. We value diversity In all its activities, SUPSI ensures an inclusive, accessible, and respectful study and work environment that values diversity, with the aim of providing high-quality higher education for all. Application Process Applications will only be considered if submitted electronically by 22.11.2026, through the dedicated application form. The following documents, written in English, must be included: Motivation letter (1–2 pages). Curriculum vitae including a list of publications (if available) and a link to the Master’s thesis. Copies of academic transcripts with grades from Bachelor’s and Master’s programs. List of three referees (with email addresses). For further information, please contact Alessandro Facchini. Incomplete applications, those submitted to incorrect addresses, or those received after the deadline will not be considered. In addition to the required application documents, further documentation (such as a criminal record certificate or a copy of an identity document) may be requested at a later stage.
